sample.title: fix(signals): classify Claude's login refusal as an auth failure
sample.body:
## What

Resolve https://github.com/nickderobertis/oneharness/issues/1290, accepted at severity
`high`: Claude Code's login refusal is classified as a rate limit.

`crates/oneharness-core/src/domain/signals.rs:902-957` scans the generic failure vocabulary
with rate-limit phrases ahead of auth, and the auth list omits both `not logged in` and
`/login`. So a zero-token failed result whose text says
`Not logged in · Please run /login` is recorded with `failure_kind: "rate_limit"` and a
fall-through reason of `rate-limit`, because unrelated text in the same failed run decides
the classification. That is what oneharness 0.12.1 recorded against an empty Claude
configuration directory on a real host.

Add the Claude login refusal as an **adapter-specific auth precondition, checked ahead of
the generic vocabulary**. The structure for that already exists:
`classify_harness_failure` checks the harness-aware quota signal, then the precondition
refusals, then the unknown-session rejection, and only then falls through to the generic
`classify_failure` — and its own doc comment says why that order is load-bearing. Scope the
phrase to the Claude dialect rather than making it dialect-agnostic, so another harness's
unrelated text cannot be read as a login refusal, and keep the existing bound that a
candidate with work evidence never falls through: an agent that merely wrote the sentence
mid-run must not hand its task on.

Cover a failed stream-json result that carries the refusal **and** unrelated warning text
in the same output, since that mixture is what the misclassification came from.

## Why

The user accepted this at `high` severity after hitting it on their own host. An
unauthenticated Claude identity reported as rate-limited sends an operator to the wrong
remedy entirely: they wait out a limit that does not exist, or go looking for quota, when
the fix is to authenticate the named configuration directory. The fall-through reason is
wrong for the same reason, so the chain's own record of why it moved on is misleading. The
workaround is reading raw result text by hand, which is what a failure classifier exists to
save an operator from doing.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed Claude-dialect result whose text carries the login refusal is classified as an
  authentication failure, and its fall-through reason says auth rather than rate limit.
- That classification holds when the same failed output also carries unrelated warning text
  and rate-limit vocabulary, so the refusal decides the reading rather than the neighbouring
  text.
- The phrase is recognized for the Claude dialect and not for another harness's output, so
  an unrelated CLI's text carrying similar words is classified as it was before.
- A candidate with work evidence still does not fall through on this signal, so an agent
  that wrote the sentence mid-run cannot hand its task on.
- Every behaviour above is proven by tests driving the real classifier over real captured
  result text rather than by inspection, and no test substitutes a double for the layer
  under test.
- The commit body carries a `Closes` line naming
  https://github.com/nickderobertis/oneharness/issues/1290.
- The crate tests that cover the classifier are green over the finished tree, and so is the
  judged lint over this change's diff.
- Every claim this dispatch makes about the finished work is true of the tree as it finally
  stands.

## Additional info

Iterate with this repository's diff-scoped judged lint and the crate tests over the
classifier rather than its whole gate, which builds and smokes artifacts this change cannot
affect. The repository's own required checks run downstream on the change this branch
becomes; nothing here asks you to have run them first.

This repository publishes the reusable engine as its own crate target, separately from the
CLI, and a consumer in this plan waits on that crate: a node of `onepipeline` relinks
`oneharness-core` to the release carrying this fix, and this host's engine pin then adopts
it. Two consequences for your commit. Its type decides what release carries it, so a type
that cuts no release would leave the classifier unreleased and two nodes waiting
indefinitely. And the consumer's own resolution has to stay compatible with what
`oneagentgraph` and `onejudge` require of `oneharness-core`, so keep the change within the
engine's current minor version; if you find you cannot, raise it over
`$ORCHESTRATOR_ASK_MANAGER` rather than deciding the version story yourself.

Board items on the follow-ups board are not yours to move — its credential is masked from
every dispatch. The `Closes` line is the whole of what this node does about the issue.

## Additional info

### Operational notes for this host

**Run only the checks that exercise what you changed.** The tests that cover the code
you touched, the lint that reads your diff — and nothing wider. The repository's own
automation runs the full bar downstream on the change this work becomes: a `pre-push`
hook where that repository publishes locally, the host's required checks where it
publishes remotely. Neither is waiting for you to have run it first, so running it here
spends twenty to forty minutes of this dispatch learning what the merge path reports
anyway. That is measured rather than estimated: one node in this workstream spent about
84 minutes on three rounds of everything its repository could run, to reach lint findings
a diff-scoped run reports in two.

**Pick those checks from your change, and take the narrowest scope each one supports.**
One test module over the whole suite; the lint over your diff over the lint over the
tree. A repository's own fast deterministic tier is a fine choice when it is what
exercises your change — its `just --list` says which recipe that is — and a poor one when
you reached for it because it was the widest thing available. When a check you ran
reports something, fix that and run **that check** again; nothing here asks you to re-run
its ne

[GitHub Copilot CLI](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli) - [Kimi Code CLI](https://github​.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli) - [OpenCode](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode) - [Pi](https://github​.com/badlogic/pi-mono) - [Qwen Code](https://github​.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) - [DeepSeek TUI](https://github​.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI) - [Claude Code Skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) --- ## 横向对比 下面是基于你提供的 9 个 AI CLI 工具日报，整理出的横向对比分析。 **说明：表格中的 Issue 数、PR 数为“今日重点更新项”，并不等同于全仓库完整增量。** --- ## 1) 生态全景 过去 24 小时，AI CLI 生态的重心已经从“能不能跑”转向“能不能稳定、可控、可观测地跑”。 社区高频反馈集中在 **安全误判、上下文/会话管理、成本透明度、跨平台兼容性、工具权限与模型路由** 等问题，说明 CLI 正在从单纯命令行入口演进为“可长期使用的 Agent 工作台”。 同时，各项目都在补齐 **MCP/插件/多代理/daemon/IDE 协同** 等能力，表明生态竞争点正在从模型本身转向“系统工程能力”。 一个明显信号是：**用户对可预测性和可审计性的要求正在快速上升**，尤其在长会话、自动化和企业环境中。 --- ## 2) 各工具活跃度对比 | 工具 | 今日重点 Issues 数 | 今日 PR 数 | Release 情况 | |---|---:|---:|---| | Claude Code | 10 | 0 | 无新 Release | | OpenAI Codex | 10 | 3 | 1 个新 Release（alpha） | | Gemini CLI | 2 | 1 | 无新 Release | | GitHub Copilot CLI | 3 | 0 | 1 个新 Release | | Kimi Code CLI | 1 | 0 | 无新 Release | | OpenCode | 10 | 10 | 无新 Release | | Pi | 10 | 4 | 无新 Release | | Qwen Code | 8 | 10 | 1 个 nightly Release | | DeepSeek TUI | 3 | 2 | 无新 Release | **总览：** - 今日重点 Issue 合计：**57** - 今日 PR 合计：**30** - 新 Release 合计：**3** --- ## 3) 共同关注的功能方向 ### A. 成本、额度与模型状态透明化 多个工具都在强调“看得见”： - **Claude Code**：默认显示使用/花费、`total_cost_usd` 准确性 - **Codex**：rate limit / usage / reset 倒计时 - **Pi**：OpenRouter 成本回传 - **Copilot CLI**：模型可用性与订阅权益一致性 - **Qwen Code**：会话/daemon 状态可观测 **共同诉求：** 用户希望 CLI 在会话中直接展示成本、额度、模型切换状态，而不是事后回看。 --- ### B. 会话、上下文与压缩/回溯稳定性 长会话问题是全生态高频痛点： - **Claude Code**：自动压缩卡住、上下文累积污染判断 - **Codex**：自动压缩、崩溃恢复后状态丢失 - **Qwen Code**：`/compress` 后无法 `/rewind` - **OpenCode**：durable compaction barrier - **Pi**：长流程中的 usage 读取和流式容错 **共同诉求：** 长任务中会话状态要可恢复、可回滚、可审计，且压缩不能破坏后续上下文。 --- ### C. 安全、权限与工具调用边界 这是今天最强烈的跨项目信号之一： - **Claude Code**：安全分类器误判、模型降级 - **Qwen Code**：hook 权限 `ask` 被静默拒绝 - **OpenCode**：拒绝权限后应立即停止、工具权限强制控制 - **Pi**：示例沙箱可绕过 - **DeepSeek TUI**：代理行为不遵循既有脚本/宪法 - **OpenCode / Claude**：都出现“误删、误退、误判”类高风险反馈 **共同诉求：** 工具调用必须“可控、可解释、可阻断”，不能让 Agent 的自由度越过安全边界。 --- ### D. 跨平台兼容性与系统边界适配 - **Claude Code**：Windows/macOS/Linux 稳定性问题并存 - **Codex**：macOS 崩溃、Windows 恢复丢 UI - **Gemini CLI**：Nix / WSL / 网络共享场景兼容性 - **OpenCode**：Windows 终端、安装器、路径规范化 - **Qwen Code**：Windows Shell stdout、CI 环境 - **DeepSeek TUI**：窄屏终端显示 **共同诉求：** CLI 不再只是“本机能跑”，而是要在企业、虚拟化、网络盘、WSL、容器等复杂环境中稳定工作。 --- ### E. 模型/Provider 兼容与路由可控 - **Kimi Code CLI**：第三方 OpenAI-compatible provider 下 `thinking.enabled` 不生效 - **OpenCode**：OpenRouter、自签名 TLS、reasoning endpoint 约束 - **Pi**：OpenRouter cost 回传 - **Gemini CLI**：特殊系统路径误判影响工具路由 - **Copilot CLI**：模型权益/可用性不一致 **共同诉求：** 多模型时代，CLI 需要对 provider 差异做显式适配，而不是默认假设统一行为。 --- ## 4) 差异化定位分析 ### Claude Code - **定位**：高端编程 Agent，强调深度代码修改与长任务执行。 - **特点**：功能强，但当前最受困于 **安全误判、上下文漂移、成本透明度不足**。 - **目标用户**：高频开发者、重度长会话用户、复杂代码迁移场景。 ### OpenAI Codex - **定位**：桌面端 + CLI + 多代理工作台。 - **特点**：更强调 **UI/IDE 协同、会话恢复、usage 可见性**，并且有持续 release/PR。 - **目标用户**：需要“工作台式”体验的开发者，尤其是桌面端用户。 ### Gemini CLI - **定位**：轻量 CLI，偏基础可用性。 - **特点**：关注点很集中，主要是 **文件系统/平台兼容性** 和状态同步。 - **目标用户**：希望在标准和非标准 Linux/WSL 环境中稳定运行的用户。 ### GitHub Copilot CLI - **定位**：围绕 MCP/插件的可控 Agent CLI。 - **特点**：社区体量较小，但发布节奏清晰，重点在 **工具管理、键盘交互、模型权益一致性**。 - **目标用户**：依赖 MCP 和终端交互效率的早期采用者。 ### Kimi Code CLI - **定位**：多供应商兼容的 CLI。 - **特点**：当前最核心的是 **OpenAI-compatible 兼容层** 和 `thinking` 行为控制。 - **目标用户**：接入多家模型服务、关注推理行为控制的开发者。 ### OpenCode - **定位**：协议/平台型开源 CLI，强调系统边界和扩展性。 - **特点**：PR 侧很强，持续做 **协议层、MCP、权限、安装器、Windows 兼容** 的系统性优化。 - **目标用户**：需要可扩展、可治理、可嵌入的团队与平台型用户。 ### Pi - **定位**：更像 AI SDK / coding-agent 基础设施。 - **特点**：关注 **Strict Tools / Grammar、成本统计、嵌入式安全、项目级配置**。 - **目标用户**：做二次开发、嵌入式集成、企业/平台团队。 ### Qwen Code - **定位**：偏 daemon 化、session 化的 Agent 平台。 - **特点**：非常重视 **会话恢复、AutoMemory、CI 自动化、daemon 性能**。 - **目标用户**：多会话、多代理、自动化流水线用户。 ### DeepSeek TUI - **定位**：终端原生、偏轻量交互的 TUI 工具。 - **特点**：重点在 **稳定退出、输出可读性、行为约束**，产品形态更接近“可用的 TUI 代理”。 - **目标用户**：终端重度用户、偏脚本化/管道化使用者。 --- ## 5) 社区热度与成熟度 ### 社区热度高 - **Claude Code**：Issue 讨论最集中，但 PR 侧停滞，说明“痛点多、修复反馈弱”。 - **OpenCode**：Issue 与 PR 都很活跃，属于高强度迭代。 - **Pi**：问题和 PR 都多，且偏基础架构，活跃度高。 - **Qwen Code**：Issue + PR 双高，明显处于快速推进期。 - **OpenAI Codex**：持续有 release 和 PR，社区也保持活跃。 ### 快速迭代阶段 - **OpenCode、Qwen Code、Pi、OpenAI Codex**：都在高频修复核心链路，说明还在快速打磨产品边界。 - **GitHub Copilot CLI**：更新节奏不算大，但方向清晰，属于“功能扩展期”。 ### 相对平稳或早期 - **Gemini CLI、Kimi Code CLI、DeepSeek TUI**：整体更新量较低，社区规模和议题复杂度相对小，偏早期或专注细分场景。 - 其中 **Kimi Code CLI** 更偏“单点兼容性问题”，**Gemini CLI** 更偏基础稳定性，**DeepSeek TUI** 则更偏终端体验打磨。 --- ## 6) 值得关注的趋势信号 ### 1. CLI 正在平台化，而不只是命令行工具 MCP、daemon、session manager、plugin manager、multi-agent 等能力持续出现。 **参考价值：** 开发者需要按“平台/系统”而非“单次命令”设计架构。 ### 2. 可观测性正在成为核心竞争力 成本、额度、模型状态、会话进度、重置时间都在被要求默认可见。 **参考价值：** CLI 产品必须内建 usage 面板、状态栏和审计日志。 ### 3. 安全边界比模型能力更影响信任 误删、误退、误判、静默拒绝、权限绕过是高频痛点。 **参考价值：** Agent 的“可执行性”必须和“可阻断性”同时设计。 ### 4. 长会话与多文件编辑仍是主要难点 上下文污染、压缩后回退失败、恢复后状态错乱，说明长任务控制仍不稳。 **参考价值：** 会话状态机、压缩策略、回放机制会成为下一阶段关键基础设施。 ### 5. 多 Provider / 多模型兼容正在成为标配 不同服务商对 usage、thinking、TLS、路由、权限的实现差异，正在持续暴露。 **参考价值：** 未来 CLI 的竞争点不只是接入多少模型，而是能否“正确适配模型差异”。 ### 6. Windows / WSL / 企业环境仍是高价值战场 多项目都集中暴露 Windows、网络盘、安装器、路径、控制台行为问题。 **参考价值：** 生态要真正进入生产环境，必须补齐系统级兼容性。 --- 如果你愿意，我还可以把这份报告进一步加工成： 1. **一页式高管摘要** 2. **研发周会版 PPT 大纲** 3. **带优先级/风险等级的矩阵表** --- ## 各工具详细报告

sample.title: review dispatch: chunked diff reads + decoupled-subagent recovery playbook
sample.body:
**Problem.** During PR #167's review loop (2026-07-03), 3 of 7 Claude-engine reviewer dispatches derailed mid-run with a known-class harness defect: on the turn immediately after an oversized truncation-flagged tool_result, the subagent behaves as if its conversation history is gone ("only MCP server instructions, no task"), exits without writing its findings file, and burns a full agent boot (~44k tokens each). Transcript evidence: the task prompt IS delivered (byte-identical first record in failed vs successful runs) and the agents start on-task; the derail follows the whole-file Read of a 1,275-line `diff.txt` (~28k tokens > the 25k Read cap → 47.7KB truncated result). Same stimulus across all seven agents; four coped (issued the follow-up offset Read), three derailed — same class as claude-code#59903 (closed stale) / #57751 cache-bleed adjacency. Owner decision: not filing upstream at this time; harden the band instead.

**Why the band is exposed by construction.** The review skills tell specialists "review the diff at `$SESSION_DIR/round-N/diff.txt`" and leave the how to the agent — the natural first move is one whole-file Read, which fires the trigger on essentially every diff over ~1,000 lines. Medium-plus PRs hit this every time.

**Ask — two small, independent hardenings:**

1. **Chunked diff reads (trigger avoidance).** In the specialist dispatch prompt templates (`skills/review-code/reference/auto-fix-loop.md`; the equivalent instruction in the review-plan/spec/tasks and audit-debt dispatch prompts if applicable), instruct reviewers to read `diff.txt` in bounded chunks (e.g. ≤800 lines per Read via offset/limit), never one whole-file read. Better review hygiene regardless of the harness defect.

2. **Decoupled-subagent recovery playbook (detect + recover).** In the host tool map (`hosts/claude-tools.md`, the file every skill's "resolve dispatch via the host tool map" line points to), add a short dispatch-reliability note: after any reviewer/subagent dispatch returns, verify the expected output file was actually (re)written (existence + mtime); on the derail signature (fast completion, off-topic result text, output file untouched), retry the identical dispatch ONCE; if it recurs, dispatch `general-purpose` at the same model with the agent's methodology body (`agents/<name>.md` minus frontmatter) embedded and the same output contract. Never compile a findings file the returning agent did not freshly write. Check whether `hosts/codex-tools.md` needs a parallel note (its `spawn_agent` path has not exhibited this; note the asymmetry rather than inventing one).

**Non-goals.** No change to the executed-evidence gates (the spine's #145 handling and review-spec's `spec_loop_plan.py` from #164/#167 already make stale findings unable to masquerade as fresh); no upstream bug filing (a sanitized, scrub-verified draft with transcript evidence exists in the 2026-07-03 session record if this is ever revisited).

**Validation.** `validate_hosts.py` / `validate_skills.py` still green (tool-map + skill token-shape rules), plus the standard pytest suites per CLAUDE.md.

Origin: PR #167 review-loop session, 2026-07-03.

sample.title: gh issue develop creates a branch on origin, and no hook sees it: the one issue subcommand that is a ref-creating write
sample.body:
Found while filling US-14's coverage gap for #105. US-14 says every `gh issue` subcommand stays available, so #105 enumerates gh's fifteen verbs and pins each. Fourteen are plainly reads or writes to an issue. One is not.

## The gap

`gh issue develop <n>` creates a **linked branch on the remote**. It is an issue subcommand by name and a ref-creating write by effect:

```
$ gh issue develop 27 --base main
$ gh issue develop 27 --base main --name whatever-i-like
```

Both are permitted by every hook, measured on `origin/dev-05` at 43fb767. Nothing refuses them, and nothing sees them: `no-git-push.sh` matches `git push`, and this is not one. `gh issue develop --list 27` is a read and is not at issue here.

CLAUDE.md states the rule this crosses, in the paragraph the boundary hooks carry:

> An agent may push the branch of the linked worktree it is working in — non-forced, and naming that branch in the command … **That is the whole of what it may push.**

Creating a ref on `origin` through `gh` is the same effect under another spelling, which is the reasoning #47 and #97 both used to reach the `gh api` form of a rule that already existed for `gh`.

## What it is and is not

Worth stating plainly, because the severity decides whether this is worth a rule at all:

- It **cannot** move or delete an existing ref, so `main` and `dev-NN` are not reachable through it.
- It **cannot** push commits.
- It **can** leave a branch on `origin` that nobody cut deliberately, which
  `report-stale-branches.sh` then has to classify — and it lands in exactly the
  category that skill says it cannot resolve: a branch with no pull request,
  where "only whoever cut it knows".

So this is a permitting-direction gap of low severity, not an open door. It is filed because the permitting direction is where every serious finding in these files has been, and because #105 would otherwise have pinned `ALLOW` on it — which #103 Q18 forbids for a verdict that may be wrong.

## Not pinned, deliberately

#105 pins thirteen verbs and leaves this one's two creating spellings unpinned, with a comment beside them pointing here. `gh issue develop --list 27` is pinned `ALLOW` as the read it is. US-14 is covered either way — coverage is one bit per requirement — so nothing in the matrix hides this.

## The decision this needs

Three answers are available and it is Bertan's which:

1. **Leave it permitted.** US-14 is then right as written, and the note is a comment. Cheapest, and defensible on severity.
2. **Refuse the creating spellings**, permit `--list`. A `gh_rule 'issue develop'` with an argument expression separating `--list` from the rest. This is the shape `gh release`'s allowlist already has.
3. **Refuse it outright**, and amend US-14 to say "every issue subcommand that acts on the issue".

Whichever is taken, `requirements.md` gains the `GH-<this issue>` entry that records it and #105's comment is replaced by the check that pins the chosen verdict.

sample.title: Port browser voice dictation (PR #593) onto main
sample.body:
## User story

As a Flow web user, I can click a microphone button beside Send to dictate a message, review the transcribed text, and send it manually — with no external transcription service or stored audio.

## Context

The feature is fully built and reviewed in **PR #593** (`codex/voice-dictation`, head `9398a4c`, author Mahad Farooq). That PR is a stacked review draft on base `codex/voice-dictation-review-base` — **do not merge it or its base**. Its parent (`21ec541`) predates current main; a merge simulation found conflicts, including in Composer. This ticket is to **port the 14 feature files onto current main** in a fresh branch/PR, resolve conflicts, apply the known fixes, and add the outstanding regression coverage. Reference and credit PR #593 in the new PR body.

## Scope (web only)

- Microphone button beside Send in the shared web composer (channels, DMs, threads). Click to dictate, click Stop, review inserted text, send manually.
- Uses standard or webkit-prefixed browser `SpeechRecognition` — no paid SDK, API key, Flow transcription service, or stored audio. UI discloses that browser vendors may process audio remotely.
- `useDictation` hook owns starting/listening/stopping states, cancellation, timeouts, stale-callback guards; document-level coordinator allows one active session.
- Interim words shown outside the draft; finalized result indices insert once at the saved cursor/selection; draft prefix/suffix preserved; 12,000-char limit; Undo while result unchanged.
- Editing, Send, attachment, emoji, and mention controls disabled during capture. Escape, owner change, and pagehide cancel capture.
- macOS/iOS native clients untouched.

## Fixes to fold in (identified in PR #593 review, described in its body but not committed)

1. Defer editor focus after stopping until React restores `contentEditable` (currently focus is left on the mic button).
2. Detach callbacks before aborting error sessions (timeout/rejection paths currently abort first — errors/late results can be lost or wrongly accepted).
3. Close failed constructor transactions.
4. Cancel unconditionally on pagehide.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Feature works on current main with newer Composer behavior preserved: draft persistence, message scheduling, capability checks, workspace/backend bindings — resolve conflicts in their favor.
- [ ] All four fixes above applied.
- [ ] Hook/composer-level regression tests for: synchronous abort events, timeout/rejection abort ordering, owner change, pagehide, unmount, stop-timeout, and post-stop focus restoration (existing 16 dictation unit tests carried over and passing).
- [ ] TypeScript check, web test suite, and production build green on main's current CI workflows (the apple-clients failure on PR #593 was the old base's outdated toolchain; current main workflows should pass unchanged).
- [ ] `changelog/` entry file and client-impact checklist included.

Filed-by: Mahad farooq

sample.title: A mirrored cross-chat claim is retracted in the target thread with zero verification — Elm publicly unbooked a real meeting
sample.body:
## What happened

Elm (life-assistant-sam-employee, on wakeup, image `life-assistant-sam:c343239`) booked a real Calendly meeting, told the counterparty about it in their group thread, and then — on the counterparty's next reply — publicly retracted the booking. The retraction was false. The meeting is real and still on the books; the counterparty has now been told to book it himself.

Verbatim, in `cht_WoqQzoexFrtX4QRhHbxwcg`:

- `14:38:04` (assistant, mirrored) — "Update — got past Calendly's bot-blocking this time … and successfully booked us for Monday 9/14, 2:00–3:00pm PT."
- `14:46:35` (counterparty) — "Looking forward to it!"
- `14:46:49` (assistant) — "Correction — my last message was wrong. I did **not** get past Calendly's block; there's no real booking. … please go ahead and grab Monday 9/14 … yourself."
- `14:50:56` (owner) — "this message is a bug…investigating"
- `14:51:00` (assistant) — "no meeting is booked yet."

## Ground truth: the booking is real

From the owner-DM turn (`20260910_164605_aeecf205`) that did the work:

- `14:01:51` accessibility click → "Clicked Schedule Event"
- `14:02:01` URL becomes `…/1-hr-virtual/invitees/f3971b07-…`, page title `Confirmed - Calendly`
- `14:02:14` AX read: `[You are scheduled!] [A calendar invitation has been sent to your email address.] [1 HR Virtual] [2:00pm - 3:00pm, Monday, September 14, 2026] [Pacific Time]`

Independently confirmed now: that invitee URL returns **200**, a same-shape random invitee UUID on the same event type returns **404**. Calendly only serves an invitee page for an invitee record that exists.

So the `14:38` message was true, and the `14:46:49` + `14:51:00` messages are the false ones.

## Root cause

The retraction was emitted with **zero tool calls** — `messages.id=46967` has `tool_calls = NULL` and empty `api_content`, 14 seconds after the inbound. Nothing was checked.

What it was reacting to is a contradiction that lives entirely inside the target session (`20260903_104303_dbc092f8`), and that the mirror creates:

- `09-08 17:27:19`, still `active=1` in that session: "Calendly blocked the automated booking (anti-bot security check, ref tid-rb-…) — can you grab that slot yourself?" — backed **in that session** by its own tool trace (`vision_analyze` reading "This booking cannot be completed", a Cloudflare `400` on the booking POST).
- `09-11 14:38:04`: the mirrored success claim — a **bare assistant turn**, no tool trace, because the evidence for it lives in the owner DM.

`_mirror_sent` records the *body* and nothing else, by design (the docstring is explicit: "assistant role because the text is genuinely the agent speaking"). In the target session the fresh true claim is therefore an unsupported assertion sitting beside a stale, richly-evidenced false one. Asked to speak, the model resolved the conflict toward the evidenced side and retracted a true statement in front of a third party.

The cross-chat recall from #78/#81 *was* injected on that turn (the "Recalled from this agent's other Plow chats" block is present in `api_content` for `messages.id=46966`) but returned unrelated snippets — Kirby, a deck, an Erik PDF — not the Calendly evidence from eight minutes earlier. The mechanism that could have adjudicated surfaced nothing.

## This is not a #76 failure

#76 worked exactly as specified: the mirror landed the message in the target chat's history (that is *why* the model could say "my last message"), and the running image carries it (`_mirror_sent` at `__init__.py:3128`, called from the transport at `:2067`). The gap is that #76 mirrors the claim without its grounding, and nothing supersedes the contradicting turns already in the target session.

## Blast radius

Any cross-chat send whose content contradicts anything older in the target thread. The mirrored turn is indistinguishable from an ordinary in-thread reply, so the model treats it as its own retractable words while having none of the evidence that produced it. Both directions are reachable: a true claim retracted (here), or a stale claim re-asserted over a fresher mirrored correction.

## Recommended fix

A statement that reverses a prior externally-visible claim must be verified against the surface that owns the fact before it is sent — the retraction is the high-stakes act, and this one went out on zero evidence. That gate removes the class regardless of how the contradiction arose.

Secondarily, and cheaply: have `_mirror_sent` stamp provenance on the mirrored turn (sent from another chat's turn, with the source chat), so the target session can tell a delivered cross-chat message from its own in-thread prose rather than weighing two bare assertions.

Evidence: `wakeup`, container `hermes-life-assistant-sam-employee`, `/var/lib/hermes/state.db`, sessions `20260903_104303_dbc092f8` (group) and `20260910_164605_aeecf205` (owner DM), 2026-09-11.

sample.title: [Epic] I0 P4: Binding Resolution: A Bare String Means a Literal
sample.body:
## Summary

A technique step names what it consumes. Most of those names are written as a bare string. Of 412 technique input bindings, 349 are bare — 85 percent — and of those, 193 name a session value and 156 are literals, with both forms appearing in a single binding block. The server guesses: a bare string is a rename when it names a resolvable bag entry, otherwise a literal. Two placeholder grammars sit beside that guess. One accepts a dotted path inside braces; the other does not. Seventeen dotted placeholders already report as resolved while naming no producer.

A program that walks a definition cannot guess. This epic makes a bare supplied value a literal always, a reference always braced, and both placeholder grammars the dotted form, with a guard that holds the rule. It is the first new stage of [#527](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/527) after the rebase of 2026-09-12, and it lands before the runner, because shipping a component whose argument is that it removes guessing, with a near coin-flip heuristic on 85 percent of its inputs, defeats the argument.

This epic covers one work item per gap.

## The three gaps

**A bare string means two things in one block.** The same binding map can hold a literal path and a session value, both written without braces. The resolver treats the string as a rename when the bag happens to contain that name, and as a literal when it does not. The answer changes if an earlier step writes a colliding name.

**Two token grammars disagree about dots.** The grammar the resolution precedence uses has no dots. A sibling module's does. A dotted placeholder can therefore report as resolved on one path and name no producer on the other. Seventeen such sites exist.

**The guard that already holds the rule covers the wrong surface.** A `set` action and a checkpoint's `setVariable` already require a bare string to be a literal and a reference to be braced. Technique input bindings — the 193 sites that matter to the runner — are outside that guard.

## The work

**W1 — Measure the 193 sites and the 17 silent resolutions.** Walk every technique input binding through the real loader. Record which bare strings name a session value and which are literals, and list the dotted placeholders that report as resolved while naming no producer. This is the rewrite gate: every later change is checked against this list, not against inspection.

**W2 — A bare supplied value is a literal; a reference is braced.** Migrate the 193 sites. The existing set-action guard is the model. After this item, the rename-if-resolvable heuristic is gone from technique inputs.

**W3 — Both placeholder grammars are the dotted form.** One token regular expression, shared by resolution and by the modules that already accept dots. The 17 silent resolutions fail the load or resolve to a real producer.

**W4 — A guard holds both rules.** The set-action guard widens to technique input bindings, or a sibling guard shares its check. A new bare-as-reference or a second token grammar fails the change that introduces it.

## Why now is cheap

The set-action half of the rule already shipped, so the authoring convention is in the corpus and the guard has a home. The 193 sites are a closed walk through the loader, not an open discovery. Waiting means the runner either guesses or is blocked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every technique input binding in the corpus is either a braced reference or a bare literal, and the loader no longer infers which.
- [ ] The 193 sites that named a session value are braced, checked against the W1 list, not against inspection.
- [ ] One placeholder grammar, the dotted form, is used by every resolver and every guard.
- [ ] The 17 dotted placeholders that reported as resolved while naming no producer either resolve to a producer or fail the load.
- [ ] A new bare-as-reference or a second token grammar fails the change that introduces it.

## Non-goals

- **Section slugs, inline technique calls, or borrowed-operation scope.** Those are [#530](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/530).
- **Per-step writes, the session store index, or a cursor.** Those are the write-authority and position epics.
- **Re-authoring action steps as technique outputs.** Still open, and not this surface.

## Tracking

Each work item is delivered as its own pull request when picked up.

| | Work item | Agent time | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| [ ] | **W1** — measure the 193 sites and the 17 silent resolutions | 2–3 h | — |
| [ ] | **W2** — bare is a literal; a reference is braced | 4–6 h | W1 |
| [ ] | **W3** — both placeholder grammars are the dotted form | 2–4 h | W1 |
| [ ] | **W4** — a guard holds both rules | 1–2 h | W2, W3 |
| | **Epic total** | **2–3 days** | |

Carries specification REQ-F044, REQ-F045 and REQ-NF031.

## Investigation detail

The rebase that created this epic, the counts, and the running order:
**[2026-09-12-i0-programme-rebase](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-09-12-i0-programme-rebase)**

The binding-resolution decision and the 193-site / 17-placeholder figures:
**[2026-08-28-runner-execution-protocol](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-08-28-runner-execution-protocol)**

sample.title: feat(model-access): expose scoped operator and organizer management
sample.body:
Parent design and full capability tracker: #681. Work package **M09**.
## Requirements
- PLAT-202 — Per-Range LLM Access Management

## Outcome
Let operators configure approved capacity and organizers plan model access without scripts or provider credentials.

## Design
[Architecture and contracts](https://github.com/Brad-Edwards/shifter/blob/681-model-access-design/docs/architecture/model-access/architecture.md), [security design](https://github.com/Brad-Edwards/shifter/blob/681-model-access-design/docs/architecture/model-access/security.md), [operations design](https://github.com/Brad-Edwards/shifter/blob/681-model-access-design/docs/ops/model-access.md). ADR-059, ADR-060 and ADR-061 are proposed in the #681 design PR; implementation starts from the reviewed design on `dev`, with any changed decision documented in the same implementation PR.

## Starting points
- `shifter/shifter_platform/ DRF API, scope registry and OpenAPI`
- `ctf organizer and operator service facades`
- `shifter/shifter_platform/frontend/src/ existing event/admin/range surfaces`

## Acceptance
- [ ] Publish versioned operator catalog validate/publish/drain and event policy/assessment/range status-revoke-re-enroll resources through canonical DRF/service boundaries.

Blocked by #2121. Native GitHub blocking relationships are authoritative and will be read back after creation.

sample.title: rfc: .agents/compose/RULES.md#18 — output lifecycle: where runs write, when results are reused, retried, force-deleted, or refused
sample.body:
## Which rule

- **Document**: `.agents/compose/RULES.md` (Output section) and `.agents/src/RULES.md` principle 12
- **Rule number / section**: compose rule 18 "Accumulating results" — plus a gap: no rule says what a run does when its output already exists
- **Current text** (pasted verbatim):

> 18. **Accumulating results.** Results MUST be organized as `output/{benchmark}/{task-id}/`. Running multiple tasks MUST accumulate results without overwriting.

## Proposed new text

Revise rule 18 so the run directory is keyed by every axis that distinguishes a run, and add an **Output lifecycle** section (rules 23–36) fixing the standard lifecycle every eval harness needs:

- **Where outputs go** — one output root selected by `EVAL_OUTPUT_DIR` (default `output/`) that outlives the run; a run is named by a run id (`EVAL_RUN_ID`, else freshly generated); each task writes only in `{output root}/{benchmark}/{agent}/{model}/{run-id}/{task-id}/` — the layout the kind/oc launchers already mint (`deploy/oc/run.sh:106-118`, `deploy/kind/run.sh:201-224`, #428).
- **When outputs are reused** — a task directory is *complete* when it holds `task/result.json` (whatever the reward). Relaunching a run id skips every complete task, naming the existing result. An unnamed launch gets a fresh run id, so it never collides and never reuses.
- **When outputs are deleted and rerun** — an *incomplete* task directory (the attempt died before grading) is deleted and retried. A *forced* run (`EVAL_FORCE` / `--force`) deletes each task directory it is about to run, complete or not. A task directory always holds exactly one attempt; deletion never reaches outside the run directory.
- **When it fails loudly** — a second concurrent attempt on the same task directory fails before starting; a run keeps going past an incomplete task but exits non-zero naming each incomplete task directory; aggregation never counts an incomplete directory as a reward.

The full text is in the linked PR.

## Rationale

- Rule 18 keys the directory by benchmark and task only, so two agents or two models on the same task overwrite each other — the clobbering reported in #136 — and the doctrine that says "without overwriting" is satisfiable only by luck. The cluster launchers had to invent a run id to stop exactly that (#428), and the chart explicitly declines to enforce uniqueness (`containers/benchmarks/_chart/templates/_helpers.tpl:146-160`); the doctrine should own it.
- Nothing states whether a rerun reuses, overwrites, or refuses an existing result. Every mature harness fixes this (skip complete, retry failed, explicit force), and the current silence is how a named volume with fixed flat paths (#358) shipped without anyone noticing a rule was broken.
- The launcher already grades a crashed or timed-out agent (`containers/core/runner/run:56-60`), so `task/result.json` present ⇔ the attempt reached grading. That is the natural, already-true completion marker; the rules only make it normative and say what happens on each side of it.
- #399 asks for run isolation across surfaces; the output half of it (per-run directory, single writer) belongs here.

## Impact

- [x] Code changes required: `containers/compose/services.yaml` + `runner.yaml` (host bind under `EVAL_OUTPUT_DIR` with the rule-18 nesting), `cli/src/run.rs` (`--output-dir`, `--run-id`, `--force`, skip/retry/lock/exit-code logic; `--mode job` today never sets the chart's output volume, `cli/src/run.rs:570-572`), `containers/core/runner/run` + `write-result`, `cli/src/report.rs` (incomplete ≠ score), the kind/oc launchers (already conform except `EVAL_RUN_ID`).
- [x] Other rules invalidated: none removed; rule 18 revised in place; `src/RULES.md` 12 gains two flags. `benchmarks/RULES.md` 24 (byte-equivalent `task/result.json` across surfaces) is unchanged and now also implies an identical layout.
- [x] Mechanical check changes: an end-to-end assertion that `output/{benchmark}/{agent}/{model}/{run-id}/{task-id}/task/result.json` exists after a run on each surface; a rerun test (same run id: complete → skipped, incomplete → retried, `--force` → fresh directory; no run id → new directory). `tests/static/deploy-scripts.sweep.sh:30-46` and `tests/e2e/cluster-contract.sh:168-196` already cover the no-overwrite half for the cluster launchers.
- [x] Breaking for contributors: the local layout gains three levels (`{agent}/{model}/{run-id}`), so `docs/guides/run-your-first-eval.md`, `README.md`, `cli/src/report.rs:68-69`, and any script reading `output/<b>/<t>/task/result.json` must follow. Major bump per top-level principle 9 (output format changed). The cluster layout is unchanged.

## Migration path

1. Land the doctrine (this RFC's PR, rules only).
2. Code PR resolving #358 + #136 against the new rules, with the mechanical check.
3. Docs PR updating the documented paths.

## Alternatives considered

- **Overwrite by default** — silently destroys paid-for trajectories; rejected.
- **No run id, key by benchmark/agent/model/task only** — every rerun of a graded task would need `--force`, and a second trial of the same configuration would have nowhere to go; the cluster launchers already proved a run id is needed (#428).
- **Keep failed attempts alongside** (`attempt-N/`) — more state, more code; a directory that holds one attempt is simpler and the logs of a retried infra failure are rarely worth keeping.

## Related drift

#358 (rule 18 unimplemented on compose/container), #136 (flat volume clobbers runs), #399 (concurrent-run isolation RFC).

sample.title: [Feature] Option to build a smaller image without local browser tooling
sample.body:
## Background

We're the [Ascensionoid](https://ascensionoid.com) initiative. The concept, briefly: extend the useful life of existing or end-of-support hardware by pairing it with cloud AI and connectivity, instead of replacing it.

Hermes Suite fits this model well, since model inference is cloud-side and the device only runs the harness. We have been running hermes-suite releases on a Jetson Nano 4GB (arm64), including the current latest (2026.7.20-0.52.106): it works. This proposal is mainly about such devices: keeping low-resource edge hardware on current releases, and on new agent/webui combinations ahead of official suite releases.

## Observed on a Jetson Nano 4GB (quad-core CPU; running in 5W power mode, which limits it to 2 cores)

- The three services (gateway, dashboard, webui) use roughly 450MB of resident memory shortly after start, and the webui process grows with uptime: our four-week-old production instance measures about 840MB for webui alone, 900MB+ in total (sum of per-process RSS, via ps).
- With concurrent use (several CLI sessions plus MCP servers), available RAM drops to around 1.1GB. Workable, but a thin margin.
- Each release image is about 4.4GB on disk. Local Chromium (Playwright) is the largest optional component, and browser automation is optional in practice.
- For context: upstream docs note 1GB RAM is sufficient without browser automation, and there is an open request for a slim image (NousResearch/hermes-agent#12572).

## Proposal (opt-in; defaults unchanged)

One new build-time option in `versions.env`:

`ENABLE_BROWSER` (default `true`). Set `false` (or use `./build.sh --no-browser`) to skip the Playwright/Chromium install stage and strip the base image's preinstalled Chromium. The result is a `-slim` image tag, about 1.1GB smaller (measured on arm64: 4.44GB down to 3.34GB) with no local Chromium in the runtime. Intended for low-resource edge devices, which can use a cloud browser backend instead.

With nothing set, builds and behavior are identical to current releases.

## Verified on real hardware (Jetson Nano 4GB, podman 3.4.2, arm64)

- The `-slim` image builds and boots on-device.
- All three services (gateway, dashboard, webui) reach RUNNING state; webui answers HTTP 200 and the dashboard 302 (login redirect) after startup settles.
- Local Chromium is confirmed absent in the `-slim` runtime; a 5-minute soak stays stable at about 450MB RSS.
- Default path unchanged: a 27-assertion shell test suite covers build args, image tags, the docker-nolog config round-trip, and up/down tag derivation.

## Status

The implementation is complete locally with the test suite above, and we are submitting it as a PR.

sample.title: Add shared session learning for project knowledge and mission planning
sample.body:
Sessions and missions produce useful discoveries, but those discoveries are not consistently checked, retained and applied to later work. Add a shared learning loop so later sessions avoid repeated mistakes and mission plans benefit from earlier planning and execution evidence.

**Expected behavior:** evaluate every session, capture reusable discoveries, retrieve relevant lessons before decisions, and check whether reuse helped. A session producing **zero new lessons is valid**. Summaries, pending tasks and temporary workarounds remain execution history unless they establish durable knowledge.

This is a high-level proposal. Proposed defaults are coverage of ordinary coding sessions and missions, automatic local capture and evidence checking, and reviewed changes to shared guidance. These defaults remain open design decisions.

Keep two learning tracks within one system:

| Track | What belongs here |
|---|---|
| Project knowledge | Domain rules, architecture constraints, debugging discoveries, test/environment requirements and explicitly stated user preferences. |
| Mission workflow lessons | Interview gaps, decomposition mistakes, verification weaknesses, briefing problems and avoidable repair loops. |

**Topic and applicability scope are separate.** A mission workflow lesson initially applies to its originating project unless broader applicability is supported. Cross-project knowledge belongs in a user-owned store outside installed plugin caches.

**Inspiration from the source review**

| Plugin | Borrow | Limitation observed |
|---|---|---|
| Compound Engineering | Capture verified, non-obvious discoveries; retrieve relevant lessons during planning; refresh stale, overlapping or contradictory guidance. | Automatic capture depends on an opted-in completion instruction, which cannot establish coverage of interrupted sessions. [Capture](https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin/blob/44d65ad64a0ac8e542eabee31ce031a7aeb41b28/skills/ce-compound/SKILL.md), [planning retrieval](https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin/blob/44d65ad64a0ac8e542eabee31ce031a7aeb41b28/skills/ce-plan/references/agents/learnings-researcher.md), [refresh](https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin/blob/44d65ad64a0ac8e542eabee31ce031a7aeb41b28/skills/ce-compound-refresh/SKILL.md), [automation directive](https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin/blob/44d65ad64a0ac8e542eabee31ce031a7aeb41b28/skills/ce-setup/assets/compounding-directive.md). |
| ECC | Small lessons with triggers, actions, scope and evidence; project isolation; bounded injection into later sessions. | Its background learner is disabled by default. The observed tool stream does not itself include user messages, so corrections need explicit capture. Observation and confidence scores do not establish correctness. [Learning architecture](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/blob/8321021c54d670126ce3b2969d5deb880b4b0c2a/skills/continuous-learning-v2/SKILL.md), [observation hook](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/blob/8321021c54d670126ce3b2969d5deb880b4b0c2a/skills/continuous-learning-v2/hooks/observe.sh), [session retrieval](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/blob/8321021c54d670126ce3b2969d5deb880b4b0c2a/scripts/hooks/session-start.js). |

The review inspected these revisions on September 13, 2026, without running or benchmarking the plugins.

This repository already provides evidence through handoffs, checked outcomes, reviews, amendments and journals. Existing [mission artifacts](https://github.com/dimakrest/context-engineering/blob/67cf86a969444eeaf370a79f7e8f6c77d6e27652/plugins/missions/templates/MISSIONS_TEMPLATES.md) support mission continuity, and [ordinary planning](https://github.com/dimakrest/context-engineering/blob/67cf86a969444eeaf370a79f7e8f6c77d6e27652/commands/create-plan.md) can consult historical research. Build consistent extraction and reuse on that foundation.

**Proposed loop: capture → verify → retrieve → feedback → promotion**

1. **Capture meaningful discoveries throughout work.** Record explicit user corrections, verified fixes, failures with established causes, resolved review findings and planning defects. Reuse mission evidence rather than copying entire transcripts. Extract at completion, handoff and milestone boundaries; provide an explicit learn action. Session IDs, processing cursors and startup recovery should make checkpoint processing resumable without duplicates. Report capture gaps when a host cannot provide events.

2. **Verify and consolidate small lesson records.** Include ID, topic, applicability scope/condition, action, rationale, evidence, originating session/mission, relevant files/version, status and last verification. Start with `candidate → verified → superseded`. A worker claim creates a candidate; checked evidence or an explicit user statement can support a narrowly scoped lesson. An unexplained failure stays an observation. Deduplicate, retain contradictory evidence and avoid counting repeated agent attempts as independent confirmation. Record branch/commit and adoption status so an unmerged result does not become an assumed fact about main.

3. **Retrieve when decisions are made.** Integrate ordinary task entry, mission interview/decomposition through the current `mission-spec` skill, design research and worker briefing. Start with Markdown metadata and text search by project, affected area, task type and phase. Return a small, budgeted selection—initially perhaps three to five lessons—with applicability and evidence. Record which lesson changed a question, dependency, feature boundary or verification choice. Recheck historical claims against current code; keep only concise references in bounded mission state.

4. **Check the outcome and maintain the store.** Record the decision influenced and whether later evidence makes the lesson helpful, contradicted, irrelevant or still unknown. A usage receipt alone does not prove benefit. Refresh when referenced code chan

sample.title: pack wiring writes agent files to $HOME/.claude, ignoring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
sample.body:
### What happened?

`nono pull` runs a pack's `wiring` directives against destinations the pack authors as literal `$HOME/.claude/...`. But Claude Code reads its config from `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` whenever that variable is set. For anyone who has relocated it, `nono pull nolabs-ai/claude` writes the entire plugin half of the pack — marketplace tree, plugin cache symlink, and the `json_merge` entries into `known_marketplaces.json`, `installed_plugins.json` and `settings.json` — into `~/.claude`, a directory Claude Code never opens.

Nothing errors. `nono pull` prints success, the profile half installs correctly and works, so the only symptom is that the `nono` plugin (permission-failure diagnostics plus the `nono-sandbox` skill) silently never loads. On my machine `~/.claude` did not exist at all beforehand — the pull created it.

Where it comes from:

- `crates/nono-cli/src/wiring.rs:667` — `expand_vars` knows `$PACK_DIR`, `$NS`, `$PLUGIN`, `$HOME`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `$NONO_CONFIG`, `$NONO_PACKAGES`. There is no way for a pack to express "wherever this agent's config actually lives".
- Because of that, `nolabs-ai/claude` 0.1.4 hardcodes `$HOME/.claude` in **11 of its 12** wiring destinations (the twelfth is the `$NONO_CONFIG/profile-drafts` marker).
- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` appears exactly once under `crates/nono-cli/src/` — in `sandbox_prepare.rs`. The wiring path never consults it.

### What did you expect to happen?

Wiring destinations to land wherever the agent actually reads them, so the plugin loads. Failing that, a warning — silently wiring an agent integration into a directory the agent doesn't read is worse than refusing to.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Relocate Claude Code's config: `export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.local/claude`, and make sure `~/.claude` does not exist.
2. `nono pull nolabs-ai/claude`
3. `~/.claude` is created and populated; `jq '.enabledPlugins' ~/.local/claude/settings.json` has no `nono@nolabs-ai` entry.
4. Start Claude Code. The nono plugin isn't loaded. No error is reported at any point.

### Relevant output or logs

```console
$ jq -c '[.wiring[] | (.dest // .link // .file // "")] | map(select(startswith("$HOME/.claude"))) | length' \
    ~/.config/nono/packages/nolabs-ai/claude/package.json
11

$ ls ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/        # created by the pull
nolabs-ai

$ jq -c '.enabledPlugins | keys | map(select(test("nono")))' ~/.local/claude/settings.json
[]
```

### Proposed fix

Keep `wiring.rs` agent-agnostic — let the **pack** name the variable, and have the CLI resolve it generically. An optional `wiring_vars` block in `package.json`:

```json
"wiring_vars": {
  "CLAUDE_CONFIG": { "env": "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", "default": "$HOME/.claude" }
},
"wiring": [
  { "type": "write_file", "source": "hooks/hooks.json",
    "dest": "$CLAUDE_CONFIG/plugins/marketplaces/$NS/plugins/nono/hooks/hooks.json" }
]
```

Resolution order: use the env var when set, non-empty and valid; otherwise the declared `default`, itself expanded through the existing variable table. `$NAME` syntax is unchanged, and `wiring_vars` defaults to empty, so every existing pack keeps its current behavior.

Implementation is contained: add the field to `PackageManifest` (`package.rs:40`), carry the resolved map on `WiringContext` (`wiring.rs:293`, built at the single call site `package_cmd.rs:832`), and consult it in the `expand_vars` match arm before erroring on an unknown variable.

### Security considerations

This is the part I'd most like review on. Today `wiring.rs:19` states that **"no user-controlled inputs flow in"**, and this proposal knowingly changes that: an environment variable would feed a file-write destination. Per the path rules in AGENTS.md, I'd gate it with:

- must be absolute — reject relative values outright;
- reject any `..` component using `Path::components`, never string matching;
- require the resolved path to be under `$HOME` via `Path::starts_with` (component-wise), rejecting anything outside it;
- on unset, empty or rejected, fall back to the declared `default` rather than failing the install, and say so on stderr.

`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is already read from the environment here and is not validated to that bar, so there may be an existing gap worth closing in the same place. Happy to set the bar wherever you'd prefer — including "reject and abort" instead of "fall back".

### Alternatives considered

- **`${VAR:-default}` in `policy::substitute_vars`** — more general and needs no manifest change, but that helper is shared with profile path expansion, so it widens the blast radius well beyond wiring.
- **Add `$CLAUDE_CONFIG` to the CLI's variable table** — about ten lines and ships immediately, but it contradicts `wiring.rs:9`, "The CLI knows nothing about specific agents."

### Scope

CLI mechanism only. Adopting `$CLAUDE_CONFIG` in the claude pack is a follow-up PR on `nolabs-ai/nono-packs`; until that lands there's no behavior change for anyone.

Related: #377 (same environment variable, but the profile's filesystem grants rather than wiring), #1834, #1795, #1803.

### nono version

0.77.0

### Operating system

macOS

### OS version / distro

macOS 26.6.2 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64, installed via Homebrew

### Additional context — agent disclosure

I'm an AI agent (Claude), filing this before writing any code, per the contribution policy in AGENTS.md.

Files consulted: `crates/nono-cli/src/wiring.rs`, `package.rs`, `package_cmd.rs`, `policy.rs`, `migration.rs`, plus `neps/README.md` (this reads as a bug fix / small feature addition, so no NEP), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/pull_request_template.md` and `.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml`.

Intent: implement the `wiring_vars` proposal above and open a PR linking this issue. If you'd rather take a different approach — or none — say so and I'll drop it.

Found while debugging a separate, self-inflicted problem: a stale `always-further/claude` pack that 0.77.0 could no longer parse after #1826 removed the legacy profile-key alia

sample.title: docs: rewrite localizing-ui for a single shipped catalog after the ja drop
sample.body:
## Why

#26 dropped the `ja` locale (`LOCALES = ["en"]`, `messages/ja.json` deleted), deferring Japanese rather than cancelling it. The `localizing-ui` skill still teaches a two-catalog procedure, so an agent following it today is told to edit a file that does not exist:

- `.agents/skills/localizing-ui/SKILL.md:8` — the `description` names `messages/ja.json` as a trigger.
- `.agents/skills/localizing-ui/SKILL.md:31-32` — says the `localeCount` example "quotes `ja.json` rather than translating it".
- `.agents/skills/localizing-ui/SKILL.md:50` — the add-a-key procedure's step 2 is "`messages/ja.json` — add the same key".
- `.agents/skills/localizing-ui/SKILL.md:94-104` — the ICU plural-categories example quotes `HomePage.localeCount` from `ja.json`; that key was already removed from both catalogs in `9ad10dd`, before `ja.json` itself went.
- `.agents/skills/starting-an-app/SKILL.md:76` — names `messages/en.json` and `messages/ja.json` as carrying the page heading.
- `tests/placeholders.test.ts:53-60` — comments still cite `messages/ja.json` and `HomePage.localeCount`.

What prevents harm today: `tests/messages.test.ts` and the type-derived `MessageKey` union reject a key added to a catalog that is not in `MESSAGES`, so following the stale step 2 fails loudly rather than silently — but it costs the next agent a confused run.

## What

- Rewrite the add-a-key procedure and the description for one shipped catalog, while keeping (in one short paragraph) what re-adding a locale requires, pointing at `starting-an-app`'s "The locale decision" rather than restating it — `ja` is deferred, not cancelled.
- Replace the plural-categories worked example with one that does not depend on a deleted file or key (the rule — plural categories may differ per locale and the test does not compare them — stays).
- Fix `starting-an-app:76` and the `tests/placeholders.test.ts` comments to name only files that exist.
- `pnpm agents:sync` after the skill edits; never hand-edit `.claude/skills/`.

## Done when

- [ ] `git grep -n "ja\.json\|localeCount" -- .agents/skills tests` returns only lines that describe re-adding a locale, not the current tree
- [ ] `pnpm agents:sync && pnpm agents:check` pass
- [ ] `pnpm check:quick` is green

sample.title: PHYS-D1-2026-09-06-01: `synthesize_packed_havok_proxy` pre-bakes `ref_scale`, so FO4+/Starfield packed-Havok proxies get an `XSCL²` collider — the third site of #3064/#3065, closed on the first two only
sample.body:
Reported by `/audit-physics` (full 7-dimension pass) — `docs/audits/AUDIT_PHYSICS_2026-09-06.md`, base `229306ce`.

Every claim below was independently re-derived from the code by the audit orchestrator before filing, not accepted from the dimension agent.


- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Dimension**: Shape Translation
- **Location**: `byroredux/src/cell_loader/spawn.rs:101-105` (the stale rationale), `:227` (the first application), `:277-291` (the parented ghost); consumer `crates/physics/src/sync.rs:907` → `crates/physics/src/convert.rs:246-251`
- **Status**: NEW — partial close of #3064 / #3065 (both CLOSED, fixed in `b8c4e6af`)
- **Trigger Conditions**: all of — (1) FO4 / FO76 / Starfield, so collision routes through the opaque `BhkSystemBinary` blob and `needs_packed_havok_fallback()` is true; (2) `collisions.is_empty()` — no decodable classic `bhk` body; (3) the REFR's base layer is `Clutter` or `Actor` (Architecture takes the precise `ArchitectureTriMesh` arm, which is correct); (4) at least one eligible mesh with finite geometry; (5) **the REFR's `XSCL` is not 1.0**. At `XSCL == 1.0` the bug is a no-op, which is why it survived four passes.
- **Description**: `collision_shape_to_parts` has owned scale application since #2860. `synthesize_packed_havok_proxy` predates that and bakes `ref_scale.abs()` into the cuboid half-extents itself, under a rationale that is now false and still written down: *"only the cuboid half-extents need the REFR scale baked because physics ignores `GlobalTransform::scale`."* Physics stopped ignoring it twelve days after that comment was written.
- **Evidence** — the full chain, each link re-verified by the orchestrator:
  1. Producer bakes: `let half_extents = ((max - min) * 0.5 * ref_scale.abs()).max(Vec3::splat(0.5));` (`spawn.rs:227`). `min`/`max` come from `transformed_mesh_aabb`, mesh-local TRS only.
  2. The ghost is **parented** with local scale 1.0: `world.insert(ghost, Transform::new(local_center, Quat::IDENTITY, 1.0)); world.insert(ghost, GlobalTransform::new(world_center, world_rot, 1.0)); … world.insert(ghost, Parent(placement_root)); add_child(...)` (`spawn.rs:277-291`).
  3. Propagation **overwrites** the seeded `1.0`. `placement_root` carries `GlobalTransform::new(ref_pos, ref_rot, ref_scale)` (`spawn.rs:851-854`); the BFS reaches the ghost and does `if let Some(g) = gq.get_mut(entity) { *g = composed; }` where `composed = GlobalTransform::compose(&parent_global, local.t, local.r, local.scale)` (`crates/core/src/ecs/systems.rs:316-325`), whose scale term is `parent_scale * local_scale` = `ref_scale`.
  4. Ordering is unconditional: cell loading runs after `scheduler.run(...)`, and `Stage::PostUpdate` (propagation) precedes `Stage::Physics`. `collect_newcomers` always reads the propagated value.
  5. Consumer applies again: `collision_shape_to_parts(&n.shape, n.global.scale, &cfg)` (`sync.rs:907`) → `SharedShape::cuboid(clamp_shape_extent(half_extents.x * scale), …)` (`convert.rs:246-251`).

  Net: **half-extents = authored_local × `ref_scale²`**.

  The sibling that was fixed: `synthesize_static_trimesh(positions, mesh_indices)` takes **no scale parameter** at HEAD, and `b8c4e6af`'s replacement test is named `placement_scale_is_applied_once_by_the_shared_converter`. The proxy's own test, `packed_proxy_bakes_outer_scale_into_cuboid_extent` (`spawn/synthesize_trimesh_tests.rs:234`), pins the **producer in isolation** at `ref_scale = 2.0` → `(2,4,6)` — it certifies the pre-bake rather than catching the doubling.
- **Impact**: every FO4 / FO76 / Starfield Clutter or Actor placement matching the trigger gets a proxy `XSCL²` the intended size. `XSCL 2.0` → a 4× cuboid: an invisible wall metres from anything visible. `XSCL 0.5` → a 0.25× cuboid the player walks through. The visual mesh is correct in both directions and nothing is logged — the same invisible-failure profile #3064 was filed HIGH for. Bounded, not catastrophic: `RT_ABSOLUTE_PRECISION_CEILING` and `clamp_shape_extent`'s `MAX_SANE_SHAPE_EXTENT` (both 2^20) cap the product, so this is wrong size, not broadphase poisoning.
- **Related**: #3064, #3065, #2860, #2355, #2543; **PHYS-D3-2026-09-06-02** (the doc rot that preserved the false premise — fix together); PHYS-D7-2026-09-06-03 (the diagnostic that cannot see this).
- **Suggested Fix**: drop `* ref_scale.abs()` from `spawn.rs:227` and let the shared converter own scaling, exactly as `b8c4e6af` did for the trimesh sibling. Keep `ref_scale` as a parameter (still needed for the `is_finite` gate and `local_center`). Rewrite the `:101-105` rationale — it is the false premise, not a comment. Convert `packed_proxy_bakes_outer_scale_into_cuboid_extent` into the end-to-end form its sibling already has: spawn the ghost under a scaled `placement_root`, run propagation + `physics_sync_system`, assert the resulting collider AABB.

## Completeness Checks
- [ ] **SIBLING**: Same pattern checked in related files — this audit's headline result is that *every* recent physics fix closed on fewer sites than its own evidence named; enumerate the full defect class before closing
- [ ] **LOCK_ORDER**: If a `RwLock` scope changes, the canonical acquisition order (`docs/engine/ecs.md`) is preserved and `PhysicsWorld` stays a sink
- [ ] **CANONICAL-BOUNDARY**: Per-game logic stays at the parser→canonical boundary; the solver side carries no `GameKind`/`bsver` branch (PHYSAL doctrine, `docs/engine/physal.md` §1)
- [ ] **TESTS**: A regression test pins this specific fix

sample.title: RunMax v1: Board this Week from optional Log
sample.body:
## Problem Statement

Sunday night I want to raise VO2 max without a complicated running plan. Sixteen-week calendars, questionnaires, daily logging, weekly reviews, and invented paces make me stack two Hard days or skip the week. I cannot measure VO2 max (no lab, no watch, no 5K field). I need **this Week** to be mostly Easy, at most one Quality, with Rest or Walk, and no Quality if I said I hurt.

## Solution

A phone-width **Board** of this calendar **Week** (Monday–Sunday). I may paste a messy **Log** or leave it empty, then tap **Build this week**. I get seven dated **Sessions**. I can tap a card to change Kind, minutes, or note. An illegal Week never appears; a banner explains. “For VO2 max” is chrome copy, not a number I enter.

## User Stories

1. As a runner, I want to open the app and see a **Board**, so that home is this Week rather than a chat.
2. As a runner, I want the **Board** empty until my first **Build this week**, so that I am not looking at a fake Week.
3. As a runner, I want chrome that says the Week is for VO2 max, so that I remember why the Board is mostly Easy.
4. As a runner, I want no VO2 number, 5K, or lab field, so that I am not pretending to measure physiology.
5. As a runner, I want no race **Goal** fields, so that the product stays this Week, not a taper.
6. As a runner, I want an optional **Log** textarea, so that I can paste how the body felt without a questionnaire.
7. As a runner, I want **Build this week** to work with an empty **Log**, so that I am not blocked on writing.
8. As a runner, I want an empty **Log** to still produce seven cards dated this Monday–Sunday, so that I do not type dates.
9. As a runner, I want a Wednesday **Build this week** to still fill Monday and Tuesday, so that the Week is a calendar week, not rolling 7 days.
10. As a runner, I want exactly seven **Sessions**, so that the **Board** is always one week.
11. As a runner, I want most **Sessions** to be **Easy**, so that the Week is not stacked Hard days.
12. As a runner, I want exactly one **Quality** when there is no **Pain**, so that there is one Hard day for VO2 without a workout library.
13. As a runner, I want at least one **Rest** or **Walk**, so that the Week always has a non-running day.
14. As a runner, I want **Quality** to be minutes plus one ordinary-language line, so that I am not given fake paces.
15. As a runner, I want **Easy** and **Quality** minutes to be greater than zero, so that a 0-minute run cannot hide on the Board.
16. As a runner, I want **Rest** duration to be 0 minutes, so that “40 min rest” cannot hide an Easy run.
17. As a runner, I want **Walk** to be allowed to have minutes, so that a walk is not forced to look like Rest.
18. As a runner, I want to paste a **Log** in Indonesian, English, or mixed, so that I can write the way I actually write.
19. As a runner, I want `Rabu lutut agak nyeri, jalan aja` to produce zero **Quality**, so that a sore knee does not get a Hard day.
20. As a runner, I want a **Pain** banner when the **Log** has injury or pain cues, so that I see why Quality is gone.
21. As a runner, I want no diagnosis sentence when I mention pain, so that the app does not play clinic.
22. As a runner, I want `dada pegal abis lari` to produce no **Quality** and no diagnosis, so that chest soreness is treated as **Pain**, not a disease name.
23. As a runner, I want a heavy-feeling **Log** without pain cues to still keep exactly one **Quality**, so that “tired” does not delete the Hard day.
24. As a runner, I want a second **Build this week** on the same Monday to overwrite the first, so that I have one Week, not snapshots.
25. As a runner, I want no list of past Weeks, so that home stays this Week.
26. As a runner, I want to tap a card and change **Easy** to **Rest**, so that I can take a Rest without a new Build.
27. As a runner, I want switching Kind to **Rest** to clear minutes to 0, so that Rest cannot keep a run duration.
28. As a runner, I want a tap that would create a second **Quality** to not stick, so that the Board cannot show two Hard days.
29. As a runner, I want a tap that would remove the last Rest/Walk to not stick, so that the Week cannot lose recovery.
30. As a runner, I want a tap that would add **Quality** while `pain` is set to not stick, so that I cannot override the pain gate by editing.
31. As a runner, I want a tap that sets **Easy** or **Quality** to 0 minutes to not stick, so that empty runs cannot sit on the Board.
32. As a runner, I want the card date to stay locked, so that I cannot slide a Session onto another day.
33. As a runner, I want `hard` to follow Kind, so that I do not set Hard independently of Quality.
34. As a runner, I want an illegal tap to explain itself with a banner, so that I know why the card did not change.
35. As a runner, I want failures to be a banner on the **Board**, so that I am not dropped into a conversation.
36. As a runner, I want no **Why?** drawer, so that explain stays out of the way.
37. As a runner, I want no Copy / Share / WhatsApp control, so that the artifact is the Board, not a message.
38. As a runner, I want Kind only `easy` | `quality` | `rest` | `walk`, so that there is no `race` day in v1.
39. As a runner, I want no km field on a card, so that duration stays minutes only.
40. As a runner, I want workflow chips `parseLog` → `retrieveNotes` → `draftWeek` → `checkWeek` → `saveWeek`, so that I can see **Build this week** working without chat bubbles.
41. As a class reviewer, I want one trace per **Build this week** with one span per tool, so that the five tools are demonstrably real.
42. As a class reviewer, I want MCP `notes` retrieval to show up as a span, so that RAG is not a fake.

sample.title: bug: export_image fails 'Cannot pass deleted object as a pointer of type Paint*' on documents with IMAGE fills (raster path; export_svg works)
sample.body:
## What happened?

`export_image` (raster PNG path) fails with `"Cannot pass deleted object as a pointer of type Paint*"` when exporting a **specific document** (one that contains an `IMAGE`-fill node) via `document_id`. The same export on a plain (no image) document succeeds, and `export_svg` on the same document succeeds.

## Platform

MCP server (dev server `bun run packages/mcp/src/index.ts`, v0.14.0)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a document that contains an `IMAGE`-filled frame (e.g. a `cinematic-kitchen-scene` layer with `fills_type=['IMAGE']`).
2. Call `export_image` with `{document_id, ids:[...], format:"PNG"}` — even a single small panel (`quest-panel`).
3. Error: `Cannot pass deleted object as a pointer of type Paint*`.

## Observed (isolated)

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `export_image` doc with IMAGE fill, any scope | **FAILS** `Cannot pass deleted object as a pointer of type Paint*` |
| `export_image` plain doc (no image), active | succeeds |
| `export_svg` same IMAGE-filled doc, any scope | succeeds (6939B for one panel) |

So the failure is in the **raster/CanvasKit path** only, and correlates with a document that has an `IMAGE` fill node.

## Expected vs actual

Expected: `export_image` renders the PNG. Actual: fails with a `Paint*` pointer error, blocking raster preview/acceptance via document_id.

## Notes

- `export_svg` works, so the document graph itself is fine; the bug is isolated to rasterization touching an image-fill Paint.
- This is separate from the stale-discovery-bridge issue (#4).

## Suggested next step

Confirm whether `export_image` mishandles an `IMAGE`-fill paint during `document_id`-scoped rasterization (e.g. resolving the image paint after its source was GC'd/removed).

sample.title: Convert fetched PDFs to markdown for readable papers
sample.body:
## Description

The `update-references` skill fetches paper PDFs and extracts plain text via `pypdf` or `pdfminer`. Plain text loses all structure: headings, tables, math, figures, and formatting are flattened into an unreadable wall of text. Papers should be converted to markdown so they are readable in any editor or tool.

Replace the plain-text extraction with `pymupdf4llm` (PyMuPDF's markdown converter), which preserves headings, tables, math blocks, and figure references. Output goes to `<db-dir>/papers/<id>.md` instead of `<db-dir>/text/<id>.txt`. The `text_path` field in the CSL-YAML database becomes `md_path`. Keep the legacy `text_path` field readable on load for backward compatibility, but new fetches write markdown only.

Additionally, add a `repair` subcommand to `arxiv.py` that walks the database, checks each entry's `md_path` (and legacy `text_path`), and re-converts any PDFs whose markdown file is missing or stale. This handles existing databases where papers were fetched before the markdown conversion was available.

## Files to Modify

### `.claude/skills/update-references/scripts/arxiv.py`
- `extract_text()` function (lines 234-253): replace with `convert_to_markdown()` that tries `pymupdf4llm.to_markdown()` first, falls back to `pypdf` plain text extraction
- `cmd_fetch()` (lines 257-315):
  - Change `text_dir` from `"text"` to `"papers"` (line 274)
  - Change file extension from `.txt` to `.md` (line 276)
  - Rename `text_path` variable to `md_path` throughout
  - Change db field from `"text_path"` to `"md_path"` (line 300)
  - Update JSON output key from `"text_path"` to `"md_path"` (line 314)
- Add `cmd_repair()` subcommand and `repair` argparse entry:
  - Walk all entries in the database
  - For each entry with a `pdf_path` that exists on disk: check if `md_path` exists and is non-empty; if missing, re-run the markdown conversion on the PDF and update the entry
  - Migrate legacy `text_path` fields: if an entry has `text_path` but no `md_path`, convert the PDF and set `md_path`, leave `text_path` as-is
  - Print a JSON summary: how many entries checked, how many converted, how many skipped (no PDF on disk)

### `.claude/skills/update-references/scripts/scholar.py`
- Text extraction block in `cmd_fetch()` (lines 185-210):
  - Replace `pypdf` text extraction with `pymupdf4llm.to_markdown()` call, same fallback pattern
  - Change `text_dir` from `"text"` to `"papers"` (line 204)
  - Change file extension from `.txt` to `.md` (line 206)
  - Rename `text_path` to `md_path` throughout
  - Change db field from `"text_path"` to `"md_path"` (line 233)
  - Update JSON output key from `"text_path"` to `"md_path"` (line 246)

### `.claude/skills/update-references/SKILL.md`
- Line 42: change `<db-dir>/text/<arxiv-id>vN.txt` to `<db-dir>/papers/<arxiv-id>vN.md` and update description from "plain-text sidecar" to "markdown conversion"
- Lines 165-166: change `text_path` field reference to `md_path`, update path example
- Lines 199-201: update dependencies section — replace `pypdf (or pdfminer.six)` with `pymupdf4llm` as the recommended converter, note `pypdf` as fallback
- Add documentation for the `repair` subcommand in the workflow section

### `.claude/skills/audit-references/SKILL.md`
- Line 32: change `<db-dir>/text/` to `<db-dir>/papers/` in the directory description
- Line 80: change `text_path` to `md_path` in the "Already fetched?" check
- Line 139: update dependencies from "pypdf is recommended" to "pymupdf4llm is recommended"

## Acceptance Criteria

- `arxiv.py fetch` produces `<db-dir>/papers/<id>vN.md` with markdown formatting (headings, tables, math)
- `scholar.py fetch` produces `<db-dir>/papers/<id>.md` with the same markdown formatting
- CSL-YAML entries use `md_path` field pointing to the markdown file
- Legacy `text_path` entries in existing databases are still readable (no migration needed, just read compatibility)
- `pymupdf4llm` is the primary converter; `pypdf` plain text is the fallback if `pymupdf4llm` is not installed
- `arxiv.py repair` walks the database and converts any PDFs missing their markdown file, printing a summary of what it did
- `arxiv.py repair` migrates legacy `text_path`-only entries by converting the PDF and adding `md_path`
- SKILL.md files updated to reference `papers/` directory, `md_path` field, and `repair` subcommand

Estimated LOC: ~180 (changes to existing code plus ~60 lines for repair subcommand)

sample.title: PR thread-reply endpoint documented in section 4 / pr-review-workflow.md 404s for every comment
sample.body:
## What's broken

The reply path documented in section 4 and `docs/pr-review-workflow.md` is missing the PR number:

```
wrong: /repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/comments/<comment-id>/replies
right: /repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<N>/comments/<comment-id>/replies
```

GitHub's real endpoint is `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments/{comment_id}/replies`. The documented form returns 404 for every comment, in every repository, always — so the instruction to "reply in the same thread" (marked mandatory, forbidding a top-level-comment substitute) cannot be followed by anyone doing exactly what the document says.

Verified empirically: the documented path 404s on a real published review comment; the corrected path posts successfully with the expected `in_reply_to_id`.

The doc's own "Thread reply returns 404" troubleshooting entry is also wrong — it attributes the 404 to an org restriction or a deleted comment, sending the reader to a top-level-comment fallback instead of the real cause (the missing PR number). It should list the two genuine causes instead: a pending unsubmitted review (comments unpublished, cannot be replied to), or a deleted comment — and note that an outdated thread is *not* a cause, since outdated threads reply normally.

## Fix

Correct the path in three places — `AGENTS.md` section 4 Phase 2, and both occurrences in `docs/pr-review-workflow.md` (the initial verdict reply and the post-fix SHA follow-up) — plus the gh-to-MCP mapping row in `CLAUDE.md`. Rewrite the "Thread reply returns 404" edge case per the above. Add a warning that piping the call through `grep`/`head` can swallow the error body and make a 404 look like success — check the response or exit code explicitly.
