| Cloud API key and `/login <provider>` | Preserve env-key setup and Codex login; verify which supported provider authorizations already exist. API-key prompts are not new subscription OAuth. |
| Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM and sglang | Run existing setup journeys first; identify missing preset, optional-key, discovery/manual-model, connection/version hint or recovery behavior. |
| `--local`, detection, default model, pull/load | A proposed shortcut, not implemented or authorized by this issue. Decide explicit endpoint/probe and download/load consent, resource bounds and offline behavior before changing existing no-scanning defaults. Do not promise one model is available on every server. |
| Unknown local/custom model IDs | Confirm actual behavior. Support explicit user-selected models with conservative, visible fallback metadata where appropriate; do not make up capabilities or silently change built-in catalog resolution. |
| `/llama` router management | Load/unload/download, gated-repository authorization, router state and loaded-model filtering are distinct new scope. No silent unload/delete or ambient credential discovery. |
| Model naming and picker resolution | One documented user ID vs wire ID contract; exact → unique prefix → unambiguous fuzzy/provider-qualified selection. Ambiguity must not silently choose the wrong route. |
| Compatibility and sampling escape hatches | Inventory existing overrides, then scope bounded typed/per-model additions. Review protected request/auth/tool fields; a sampling escape hatch must not override ownership or admission invariants. |
| Small custom-provider file and picker reread | Document the minimal supported local config, then verify edit-and-switch without restart. Reload transactionally; malformed or concurrently edited config must not destroy the working catalog or expose secrets. |
| Local-model guide and connection hints | Update existing #275 guide for verified journeys; example commands/configs must be runnable against the accepted candidate, not copied from Pi/Codex claims. |
| Optional keychain storage | Separate migration/fallback/security design if retained; do not silently migrate existing credentials. |

## Required decisions and evidence

- [ ] For each row classify **already implemented / acceptance incomplete / confirmed bug / new proposal / deferred**, with exact source and tests.
- [ ] Keep build-time catalog determinism, explicit runtime discovery, offline behavior, no per-model system prompts, and protocol choices based on verified server support. Do not force Responses on all local servers.
- [ ] Exercise env-key, existing custom-file, guided setup, disconnected server, unknown explicit local model, refresh and rollback paths with sanitized fixtures; record unavailable real-server tests.
- [ ] Publish only remaining independently landable issues under the existing setup ownership. Separate consensual download/server-management and credential-store changes from presentation polish.
- [ ] Record shared-file conflicts with TUI and provider refactors and obtain fresh execution approval. No new swarm, installation change or release is authorized here.

sample.title: (dev-flow-stats): count promotion in isStale's activity check
sample.body:
## Problem

`isStale`'s activity union — already fixed once in #663's own review round 2
to include `stage_transitions`/`interventions`/`settlements`/
`evidence_registrations`/`pr_bindings`/`outcome_transitions` — still never
includes `promotion.promoted_at`. A run that has been promoted (reached
ready-for-review) but whose corresponding `outcome_transitions[]` entry
falls outside an `--as-of` cutoff can be wrongly terminalized as
"abandoned" by staleness alone.

## Current violation (observed 2026-09-05)

`isStale` (`scripts/dev-flow-stats.mjs:1409-1422`):

```js
function isStale(state, staleAfterDays, asOfEpoch) {
  if (state.outcome !== null) return false; // already terminal
  ...
  const allEntries = [
    ...state.stage_transitions, ...state.interventions, ...state.settlements,
    ...state.evidence_registrations, ...state.pr_bindings, ...state.outcome_transitions,
  ];
```

Nothing here reads `state.promotion`. The schema does not guarantee
`promotion` and its corresponding `outcome_transitions` entry are posted
atomically (only that this repo's own writer keeps them in sync in
practice), so an `--as-of` cutoff can legitimately fall between the two: at
that cutoff, `reconstructAsOf` derives `state.promotion` present but
`state.outcome === null` (the outcome_transitions entry is still
cutoff-filtered out). `isStale`'s early return
(`if (state.outcome !== null) return false`) does not apply, so the run
falls through to the activity union above — which never sees the
promotion event — and can be terminalized as abandoned if the run's other
chain entries are stale enough as of that cutoff, even though it was
promoted recently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] [CI] `isStale`'s activity union includes `state.promotion.promoted_at`
      when `state.promotion` is non-null
- [ ] [CI] A regression fixture with an `--as-of` cutoff strictly between
      a run's `promotion.promoted_at` and its `outcome_transitions[]`
      entry, with every other chain array stale as of that cutoff, proves
      the run is no longer terminalized as abandoned

## Verify

```sh
task test -- dev-flow-stats
```

## Provenance

Codex cloud review, PR #751 (#663), shepherd round 6's own re-review
(round 7 of the PR's shepherd stage), P2 — confirmed accurate: a gap in
the same activity union review round 2 already patched once for a
different omission (see the union's own comment citing that round).
Declared the PR's final round by the maintainer; disposed of as a
follow-up rather than fixed in place, per that round's
no-further-code-changes constraint.

sample.title: Adopt three guard patterns the sibling repos already have
sample.body:
While porting the security setup from #223 into MitFahrBar, FWApp and DurecMix, three patterns turned up that those repos have and this one does not. All three are the same class of thing this repo already believes in — a convention that CLAUDE.md states, with nothing enforcing it. Listed cheapest first.

## 1. `release.yml` has the same trap MitFahrBar was bitten by, unguarded

`MitFahrBar/test/release_workflow_test.dart` exists because of a concrete failure, and its header records it:

> Der v0.34.1-Lauf starb NACH dem Taggen (25.07.2026): `cp` erzeugte `mitfahrbar-*.apk`, `upload-artifact` suchte noch `fahrgemeinschaft-*.apk` — sauber kompiliert, grün in jeder PR-CI, gescheitert erst im echten Release. Zurück blieb ein Tag ohne Release, den die Tag-Entscheidung fortan als „schon veröffentlicht" wertete.

`release.yml` here has the identical shape — the artifact name is written in four independent places and nothing checks they agree:

```
128:  run: cp build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk "pilzbuddy-${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}.apk"
132:  path: pilzbuddy-${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}.apk
143:  run: cp build/app/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab "pilzbuddy-${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}.aab"
187:  files: pilzbuddy-*.apk
```

A green PR CI proves nothing about this path: it only runs in a real release, and it fails *after* tagging. Same reasoning as `android_manifest_test.dart`, which this repo already has.

MitFahrBar has five such workflow tests (release, backup, notify, fuel_history, report); this repo has zero. `release_workflow_test.dart` is the one that has already cost someone a manual tag deletion.

**Effort:** small. Port the test, adapt the stem.

## 2. Generated assets have no staleness check

CLAUDE.md says of `assets/map_style/protomaps_light_de.json`:

> ist generiert (npm `@protomaps/basemaps`, Flavor LIGHT, lang de) — nicht von Hand editieren, sondern neu generieren

Nothing enforces that. A hand-edit survives every check and ships.

DurecMix solves exactly this for its Rust licence notices (`tool/gen_rust_licenses.py`): the generated asset carries a **hash of its input** in the header, and `--check` fails CI when the input moved without regeneration. Its docstring is worth reading for *why* it hashes the input rather than the output — everything else is environment-dependent.

Applies here to the map style and arguably to `assets/offline_maps/overview_dach.pmtiles` (generated with `pmtiles extract`).

**Effort:** small, and `tool/` is Version-Guard-exempt so it costs no release.

## 3. `analysis_options.yaml` is bare

Current file, comments stripped:

```yaml
include: package:flutter_lints/flutter.yaml
linter:
  rules:
```

That is stock `flutter_lints` and an empty list. MitFahrBar:

```yaml
include: package:flutter_lints/flutter.yaml
analyzer:
  language:
    strict-casts: true
    strict-raw-types: true
  errors:
    avoid_print: error
    use_build_context_synchronously: error
linter:
  rules:
    - unawaited_futures
    - prefer_const_constructors
    - prefer_final_locals
```

— guarded by `test/analysis_options_test.dart`, so a rule cannot vanish silently while `flutter analyze` stays green.

The one that matters here is **`use_build_context_synchronously: error`**. CLAUDE.md states "`mounted`/`context.mounted` nach jedem `await` prüfen" as a convention; under stock lints that is a *warning*, so it is enforced by attention alone. `avoid_print` would be free (`print(` appears 0 times in `lib/`), and `strict-casts`/`unawaited_futures` are where the real work would be.

**Effort: unknown, and that is the point.** Turning these on could surface anything from five findings to two hundred, and some `strict-casts` fixes touch real logic. This needs a measured run first — install the pinned SDK, enable them one at a time, count. It deliberately did **not** ride along with the security work in #223: a lint sweep across `lib/` has no business inside a licence fix.

Suggested order: enable the free ones (`avoid_print`, `use_build_context_synchronously`) plus the guard test in one PR; treat `strict-casts` / `strict-raw-types` / `unawaited_futures` as separate, measured PRs.

---

Working templates for all three: `MitFahrBar/test/release_workflow_test.dart`, `MitFahrBar/test/analysis_options_test.dart`, `durec-multichannel-mixdown/tool/gen_rust_licenses.py`.

sample.title: Abuse limits AB1 — Duplicate-booking guard on both public write paths
sample.body:
**Stub** — rank 2 of the pilot roadmap decided in [#71](https://github.com/Dapta-Tech/dapta-calendars-slate/issues/71) (**wave 3** in its schedule). Not yet ready for an agent: run `/to-spec` on this ticket to fill it out, then label `ready-for-agent`.

- **Rank 2** — a host wants it, but the pilot can open without it.
- **Lanes: BOTH.** AB1 adds a toggle to `event-type-form.tsx` (EVT) *and* a 409 state to `booking-flow.tsx` (PUB), so per #71's rule it **consumes both lane slots and runs alone against them**; the third slot still goes to a lane-free unit.
- **Blocked by:** [#80](https://github.com/Dapta-Tech/dapta-calendars-slate/issues/80) (F), shipped, and by its lane predecessors [#83](https://github.com/Dapta-Tech/dapta-calendars-slate/issues/83) (C1), shipped, and `R` in the EVT lane.
- **Blocks:** `E` and `B2` in the PUB lane; `H2` and `AB2` in the EVT lane.
- **Source decision:** [#69](https://github.com/Dapta-Tech/dapta-calendars-slate/issues/69).

## Scope

The cheaper half of #69 — and **not a security control**: the per-IP limiter already is one. This is a host-facing product feature.

1. **A per-event-type boolean, off by default.**
2. **Counts `accepted` + `pending` bookings with `end_ms > now`** for the invitee's email, matched **lowercased and trimmed with `+tags` intact**.
3. **Both public write paths instrumented** — `createBooking` *and* `createTeamBooking`. Missing the team path is the obvious way to ship this half-built.
4. **`onBehalf` and API-key writes are exempt.**
5. **A blocked booker gets `409 DUPLICATE_BOOKING` with no slot detail** — the error must not disclose the existing booking. Re-sending the manage link to that booker is deferred (#69: it breaks the single-active-token invariant).
6. A configurable N stays out: without email verification, N > 1 defends no better than 1.

## Conventions

Migration numbers may collide with concurrent units — see #71 → *Mechanical conventions*. i18n keys append as a namespaced block in each locale object.

sample.title: Fix gsd_validate_milestone deadlock where UAT evidence is both required and rejected
sample.body:
## Summary

`gsd_validate_milestone` cannot be satisfied when planning includes a UAT verification class. The two validation paths contradict each other, so the verdict can never persist:

- **Omit** the UAT row from `verificationEvidence` → `planned UAT verification requires current structured database evidence; verificationClasses prose cannot authorize Milestone validation`
- **Include** the UAT row → `technical verdict requires the current criterion and matching settled attempt`

There is no third option.

## Repro

Milestone M003 in `entity-services-entity-service`, 7/7 slices complete, every slice ASSESSMENT `verdict: PASS`, all four verification tiers independently re-verified green (cold build 0 warnings/0 errors, unit 2764, integration 243/243, functional 1918/1918).

1. Call `gsd_validate_milestone` with all four planned classes (`Contract`, `Integration`, `Operational`, `UAT`) and a 4-row `verificationEvidence` array → **error B**.
2. Call `gsd_prepare_milestone_subjective_uat`; present the returned options to the user; call `gsd_answer_milestone_subjective_uat` with the returned `criterionId` / `questionId` / `interactionId`. Tool confirms success: *"Recorded the authenticated subjective UAT response as accepted"* and returns a `humanAcceptanceId`.
3. Re-call `gsd_validate_milestone` → **error B again**, despite a settled acceptance.
4. Drop the UAT row from `verificationEvidence` and re-submit → **error A**.
5. Re-prepare the criterion (issues a fresh `questionId` / `interactionId`), answer again, re-submit → **error B again**.

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** a settled subjective-UAT acceptance satisfies the "current criterion and matching settled attempt" requirement for the UAT verification class.

**Actual:** two settled acceptances now exist against the same `criterionId` (differing `questionId`s), and neither is accepted as the "matching settled attempt". The lookup appears keyed on state that a fresh prepare/answer cycle does not refresh — possibly a stale binding left behind by an interrupted prior session. Both acceptances were recorded by the tool as successful, so the write path and the read path disagree about which attempt is current.

## Four earlier objections were cleared first

The payload shape is otherwise valid — each of these was raised once and fixed, in sequence, before the deadlock was reached:

1. `Contract verification evidence must use one evidence class` — fixed by consolidating two Contract rows into one.
2. `Contract verification evidence was tested against <git-sha>+8-uncommitted…, but the current source revision is sha256:520ada17…` — fixed by using the sha256 fingerprint as `testedSourceRevision`.
3. `command evidence requires an exit code` — fixed by adding `exitCode: 0`.
4. `technical verdict requires the current criterion and matching settled attempt` — **not fixable**; see repro above.

## Collateral findings (same unit, same incident)

- **Auto-mode overwrote the validation artifact with a placeholder.** `.gsd/phases/03-new-milestone-m003/03-VALIDATION.md` contains `# BLOCKER — auto-mode recovery failed` ("hard recovery exhausted 1 attempts without producing the artifact"). It reads like a real artifact and will mislead anyone who greps for the verdict.
- **The `workflow-only` tools policy makes the failure unrecoverable from inside the unit.** `validate-milestone` blocks both `write` and `report_gsd_bug`. An agent that completes validation but cannot persist it therefore also cannot leave resume notes *or* file the defect. Attempting either returns a HARD BLOCK whose wording forbids retrying or working around it, which is correct as a gate but leaves no sanctioned escape path. Filing this issue required starting a separate quick task.

## Impact

A fully validated milestone with all four tiers green cannot be closed. The only on-disk artifact is a misleading blocker placeholder, and the analysis (three parallel reviewers, four independently re-run verification tiers, a settled human acceptance) is stranded in session context rather than persisted.

## Suggested direction

Make the UAT-class evidence check accept the most recent settled acceptance for the `criterionId`, rather than requiring a match against an attempt record that a fresh prepare/answer cycle does not update. Failing that, surface *which* attempt the validator considers current in the error message, so the mismatch is diagnosable rather than opaque.


_Area: gsd_validate_milestone / subjective-UAT binding_

```
--- environment ---
gsd-pi: 1.18.0
commit: c085cdfb
platform: darwin arm64
node: v24.20.0
cwd project: entity-services-entity-service
```

_Filed via gsd-pi self-report._

sample.title: no CI: add a GitHub Actions workflow running the test suites, and fix the 2 pre-existing agent-icons failures
sample.body:
This repo has **no CI at all** — there is no `.github/workflows/` directory, so every
PR reports `checks=0` and the only verification any change ever gets is an agent
reporting its own local test run. That is the single weakest link in the apex
workflow right now: a linked review pair can sign off at 0 findings and nothing
independent has executed a line of the code.

It is also free to fix. `Wred/tmux-delta` is public, and GitHub Actions has
unlimited minutes on standard GitHub-hosted runners for public repositories.

## scope

### 1. add `.github/workflows/tests.yml`

Run the suites on `ubuntu-latest` on `push` and `pull_request`:

```
tests/apex-send.test.sh        91 tests
tests/apex-pair.test.sh       154 tests   (slow — several minutes)
tests/apex-recover.test.sh    101 tests
tests/apex-delivery.test.sh    65 tests
tests/agent-icons.test.sh      56 tests   (2 currently failing — see below)
tests/apex-watch.test.sh       47 tests
tests/apex-lock.test.sh        27 tests
tests/status-format.test.sh     7 tests
```

Notes for whoever picks this up:

- Runner needs `zsh` and `tmux` (`apt-get install -y zsh tmux`). Every suite is
  `#!/usr/bin/env zsh` and uses zsh-only syntax (`${0:A:h:h}`, `setopt err_return`,
  `${(qqq)…}`, `${(f)…}`), so bash is not a fallback.
- `agent-icons.test.sh` uses a **stub** tmux on `PATH`, so it needs no real tmux.
  The apex suites do drive real panes; verify they tolerate a runner with no TTY
  rather than assuming it. If a suite genuinely needs a pty, `script`/`unbuffer`
  is the escape hatch — but check first, don't add it pre-emptively.
- Prefer a job-per-suite matrix over one sequential job. `apex-pair` alone runs
  minutes; wall-clock matters more than minute count when minutes are free, and a
  matrix names the failing suite directly in the checks UI.
- Do **not** paper over failures with `|| true`, `continue-on-error`, or by
  grepping the tail of the output. Each suite already exits non-zero on failure;
  let it.

### 2. fix the 2 pre-existing `agent-icons` failures

These fail on `main` today, so CI goes red the moment it exists. They look like a
real regression rather than stale tests:

```
FAIL an apex member with no hook events yet still shows
     expected to contain: "󰚩"
     actual             : ""
FAIL a launching apex member shows before its first hook event
```

An apex member renders no robot glyph until its first hook event lands. Prime
suspect is `d457804` ("fix(agent-icons): stop non-agent panes inheriting manager's
apex_role") over-correcting: in excluding panes that only inherited the session's
`apex_role`, it plausibly also excludes a genuine member that has not yet recorded
an event of its own. The visible symptom is a freshly spawned worker showing no
marker in its session pill until it first transitions.

Triage before fixing. If the tests turn out to encode behaviour that was
deliberately dropped, say so on this issue and update the tests instead — but
justify it, do not quarantine them to get CI green.

**Why these two are one issue:** the workflow cannot land green without the icon
fix, so splitting them would produce a PR that is red on arrival and a second PR
that cannot be verified. They are coupled by construction.

## follow-up for the repo owner (not part of this issue)

Adding the workflow does not make it *enforced*. `main`'s protection currently has
`required_approving_review_count: 1` and no required status checks. Once this lands
and is observed stable, the workflow should be added to branch protection as a
required check — that is a repo-settings change only the owner can make, and it is
the precondition for apex being allowed to merge anything on the strength of CI.

sample.title: Dependabot splits devantler-tech/actions bumps across PRs, deadlocking the same-commit pin contract
sample.body:
> 🤖 Generated by the Agentic Engineer

## Problem

`scripts/workflow-caller-pin-contract.test.sh` requires **every** `devantler-tech/actions` caller to
pin the same commit and carry the same version comment. Three workflows call in:

| Workflow | Job | Reusable workflow |
|---|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/cd.yaml` | `publish` | `publish-app.yaml` |
| `.github/workflows/release.yaml` | `release` | `create-release.yaml` |
| `.github/workflows/template-sync.yaml` | `template-sync` | `template-sync.yaml` |

This repository's `.github/dependabot.yml` has **no `groups:` key** on its `github-actions`
ecosystem, so Dependabot opens **one PR per caller**. Each bumps a single file and leaves the other
two behind, so each independently fails:

```
FAIL: every devantler-tech/actions caller must pin the same commit
```

That check is required, so `CI - Required Checks` fails and auto-merge can never complete. The PRs
deadlock each other: no single one can merge, and no merge order rescues it.

## Why this repository still has it

**`devantler-tech/platform-tenant-template` already fixed this.** Its `.github/dependabot.yml`
carries a `devantler-tech-actions` group (plus a `security-updates` companion) with a long comment
recording the identical diagnosis — its own #156/#157/#158 each touched exactly one file.

That fix cannot reach this repository: `.github/dependabot.yml` is listed in
`.templatesyncignore`, because this tenant owns the file so it can add the `npm` and `docker`
ecosystems its stack needs. Template-sync therefore never overwrites it, and the grouping fix has
never arrived. The drift is invisible — nothing compares a sync-ignored file against the template.

## Evidence

The v13.2.3 → v13.3.0 bump produced #219, #221 and #222 on 2026-09-05. All three armed auto-merge,
all three failed `Workflow Caller Pins`, and all three sat unmergeable. Reproduced locally: bumping
one caller alone fails with that exact message; bumping all three together passes.

This recurs on **every** `devantler-tech/actions` release, because the `exclude` cooldown rule
deliberately makes our own actions bump immediately.

## Expected outcome

Dependabot raises a single PR that bumps every `devantler-tech/actions` caller together.

## Acceptance criteria

- This repository's `.github/dependabot.yml` groups all `devantler-tech/*` github-actions updates
  into one pull request.
- A `devantler-tech/actions` release produces exactly one PR touching all three callers, which
  passes `Workflow Caller Pins` without intervention.
- The existing `exclude` cooldown behaviour for `devantler-tech/*` is preserved, as are the `npm`
  and `docker` ecosystems this tenant owns.

## Notes

The current deadlock is cleared separately by #228, which bumps all three pins atomically — the
manual escalation the template's own comment prescribes. This issue is the recurrence fix.

A wider question this raises, not in scope here: no mechanism detects when a sync-ignored tenant
file drifts behind the template's version of the same file.

sample.title: fix(deps): track incompatible AWS Smithy Document releases
sample.body:
## Prerequisites

- [x] I have searched existing issues to verify this bug has not been reported in this repository.

## Bug Description

Fresh dependency resolution for Reinhardt's AWS features selects `aws-smithy-types 1.7.0` together with `aws-smithy-json 0.63.0` from `aws-config 1.12.0`. Those releases are incompatible: the Smithy `Document` representation changed while the older JSON implementation still expects a `HashMap` and an exhaustive enum.

Upstream report: https://github.com/smithy-lang/smithy-rs/issues/4853

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out PR #6301 without an existing `Cargo.lock`.
2. Run `cargo check --workspace --all --all-features`.
3. Observe compilation errors in the registry's `aws-smithy-json 0.63.0`.

The affected AWS features are declared in `crates/reinhardt-conf/Cargo.toml`, `crates/reinhardt-db/Cargo.toml`, `crates/reinhardt-providers/Cargo.toml`, `crates/reinhardt-tasks/Cargo.toml`, and `crates/reinhardt-utils/Cargo.toml`.

## Expected Behavior

AWS-enabled crates compile with a freshly resolved dependency graph, including when consumed independently outside the workspace.

## Actual Behavior

The JSON crate reports two `E0308` errors (`DocumentObject` versus `HashMap<String, Document>`) and an `E0004` non-exhaustive match error. Mixed `aws-smithy-json 0.63/0.64` and `aws-smithy-schema 0.2/0.3` versions also fail the dependency policy check.

## Environment

- Reinhardt revision: `a5a3ed5e0922568e0cf8f8518cebd7bc7381ec92` (`0.4.0-alpha.15` workspace)
- Environment: GitHub Actions Linux CI; local Rust 1.96.0 on macOS with an older lockfile compiles successfully
- Failed CI: https://github.com/kent8192/reinhardt-web/actions/runs/34920506200

## Additional Context

The existing local graph uses `aws-smithy-types 1.6.3`. The upstream report verifies that an exact direct constraint to this version restores a compatible graph, including resolver backtracking of the AWS runtime releases. A workspace-only unused constraint or a library's lockfile does not protect downstream consumers; the relevant optional AWS features must activate the constraint.

Remove any temporary constraint after upstream publishes compatible AWS configuration and service dependency graphs and fresh resolution passes compilation and dependency-policy checks for all five AWS integrations.

Refs #6301.

sample.title: connection 3/4：每备份 DEK —— wrap、unwrap 与作为指令的 erase (per-backup DEKs)
sample.body:
## Parent

[#148](https://github.com/liumingjian/dbx/issues/148) — 规格：connection 的凭据加密. Obligations D16–D19b and the rulings behind them are there, including the ones [#97](https://github.com/liumingjian/dbx/issues/97) settled; [`docs/spec/connection.md`](https://github.com/liumingjian/dbx/blob/main/docs/spec/connection.md) §Slices owns the blocking edges.

## What to build

Backups get their own keys, and erasure becomes something DBX can actually promise. After this ticket `workflow` slice 8 is unblocked: it can encrypt a backup set, read one back after an incident, and destroy a credential for good.

**Each backup gets a key of its own.** Every `wrap` issues a data-encryption key distinct from every one before it, so two backups never share a key and erasing one cannot expose the other. `wrap` returns the wrapped form for `workflow` to store **beside the backup artifact** — never in the append-only tombstone ledger. ADR-0006 is explicit about why: appending means bytes can never be taken back, so a wrapped key in the ledger stays recoverable forever to anyone holding the master key, which defeats erasure outright. The ledger tracks the key by identity and fingerprint only.

**`unwrap` is the only way back into a backup, and its two failures are not interchangeable.** "Master key wrong or missing" means: restore `secrets/` from the copy kept off the machine. "Wrapped form corrupt or erased" means: this backup is gone, choose another. An erased key surfacing as a key problem sends the DBA hunting for a key that was deliberately destroyed — or worse, concluding the key is broken and re-entering every password. Slice 1 declared both types; this is where they acquire behaviour.

**`erase` returns an instruction and performs no erasure.** `connection` persists nothing and owns no bytes; `workflow` shreds the artifact-side material and appends the tombstone. `erase`'s job is to validate that the wrapped form belongs to the present master key and hand back the instruction. It is idempotent, because cleanup is retried.

The property to prove is negative, and a failure code does not prove it: after an erasure instruction is applied, **no** path through `connection.api` returns that DEK — not while holding the master key, not while holding its separately protected backup.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each `wrap` returns a DEK distinct from every DEK issued before it (obligation 16).
- [ ] `wrap` returns the wrapped form for `workflow` to store beside the backup artifact. Nothing in `connection` writes it anywhere, and nothing invites the ledger to hold it (obligation 16; ADR-0006 as amended by #97).
- [ ] `unwrap(wrap(k)) = k` under the same master key (obligation 17).
- [ ] `unwrap` has exactly two typed failures and they stay distinct: **master key wrong or missing**, and **wrapped form corrupt or erased**. An erased key never surfaces as a key problem (obligation 18). These are the types slice 1 declared; they are given behaviour, not redeclared.
- [ ] `erase` returns an erasure instruction and writes nothing. It never touches `backups/` or the ledger, and `connection` holds no state between calls (obligation 19).
- [ ] **Erasure is proven negatively**: after the instruction is applied, no path through `connection.api` returns the DEK, holding the master key and its separately protected backup. A test asserting one method's failure code does not satisfy this (obligation 19a).
- [ ] `erase` is idempotent: producing an instruction for an already-erased DEK succeeds without error (obligation 19b).
- [ ] A GCM nonce is never reused under one key, and an altered or foreign wrapped form never unwraps.
- [ ] The `ConnectionContractTest` cases for D16–D19b, written and disabled in slice 1, are **enabled** — not rewritten, not replaced.
- [ ] The TLS case stays disabled; slice 4 owns it.
- [ ] `connection.api` still exposes exactly six entry points and still references no other DBX module — the slice 1 rules stay green.
- [ ] **Watched to fail**: at least one planted violation per new rule, red output quoted on this ticket before it is made green.
- [ ] L1 (`check`) green on the mac through `rexec`.

## Blocked by

- [#150](https://github.com/liumingjian/dbx/issues/150) — connection 2/4: the master key must load and wrapping must have a key to wrap under.

Independent of [#152](https://github.com/liumingjian/dbx/issues/152) (slice 4): the two share no code path and can run concurrently in separate worktrees.

sample.title: [Feature Request]: Documentation retrieval tools (public API reference + auth-walled product docs)
sample.body:
### Feature Description

falcon-mcp has no documentation-retrieval tool. An agent connected to the server can query the tenant in depth (29 modules today) but cannot look up CrowdStrike's own documentation — it has to fall back on whatever the model memorized, which for a platform that ships API changes continuously is the weakest link in the chain.

I'd like a `docs` module. Concretely, two capabilities, in priority order:

**1. API reference lookup (no credentials required).**
`developer.crowdstrike.com` already publishes an LLM-addressable mirror of the entire API reference:

- `https://developer.crowdstrike.com/llms.txt`
- `https://developer.crowdstrike.com/llms-full.txt` — 1468 operations, each with method, path and required scope (~380 KB)
- a `.md` variant of every reference page, e.g. `https://developer.crowdstrike.com/api-reference/operations/QueryDevicesByFilter.md`, which returns method, path, `**Scope:** Hosts: READ`, the parameter list, and a FalconPy example in under 1 KB
- `https://developer.crowdstrike.com/api-reference/operations-by-collection.md`

All of the above are public, unauthenticated, `200`, and already clean Markdown. Two tools over that surface — search the operation catalogue, fetch one operation page — need no new credentials and no new scopes.

**2. Product documentation search (credentialed).**
The product documentation is a different story, and this is the part I can't solve on my own:

- `https://falcon.<region>.crowdstrike.com/documentation/page/<id>/<slug>` returns the Falcon **login page** to any non-browser client — it's an Ember SPA behind a console session cookie.
- `https://docs.crowdstrike.com` is a Fluid Topics instance (`<meta name="ft-tenant-base-url" content="https://docs.crowdstrike.com/">`). Its REST API is live but gated: `GET /api/users/me` → `401 {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Required Authentication"}`. Fluid Topics documents search/maps/topics endpoints and JWT + SSO auth, so there is a real machine-readable docs API here — just not one a Falcon API client can reach.
- The Falcon API itself has no documentation collection. I went through all 128 collections / 1468 operations in `llms-full.txt`: the only near-miss is `Knowledge Bases` / `Knowledge Base Files` (`/agentic-studio/...`, scope *Charlotte AI Agent Definition*), which is the customer-authored corpus for Charlotte AI agents, not CrowdStrike product docs. FalconPy's 135 endpoint modules confirm the same.
- The regional Swagger spec is not public either — `https://assets.falcon.crowdstrike.com/support/api/swagger.json` returns `403 MissingKey` ("Missing Key-Pair-Id query parameter or cookie value"), i.e. a signed CloudFront URL minted by a console session.

So: **an OAuth2 API client pair — the only credential falcon-mcp holds — cannot retrieve CrowdStrike product documentation today.** If that's something CrowdStrike would consider exposing (a docs search operation under an existing or new scope, or a documented way to use a Fluid Topics token alongside the Falcon creds), it would make part 2 buildable. If not, I'd rather know that than keep guessing, and part 1 still stands on its own.

### Use Case

As a security engineer driving falcon-mcp from an agent, the failures I hit are documentation failures, not API failures:

- **Scope errors.** An agent picks a tool, the call 403s, and the fix is knowing the exact scope string. Today that lives in a hand-maintained mapping inside this repo — which is precisely what #545, #552 and #553 were about. A live lookup against `developer.crowdstrike.com`, where the scope is stated on every operation page, turns that from data this project has to keep correct into data it can read.
- **Reaching past the MCP.** When no tool covers what I need, the next step is a direct FalconPy/REST call. Right now the agent guesses the operation ID, path and parameters from memory. With an API-reference tool it can look up `operations-by-collection.md`, confirm the operation exists, and get the signature — in the same session, without me leaving to open a browser.
- **Product behaviour, not just endpoints.** Half my questions aren't "what's the endpoint" but "what does this prevention-policy setting actually do", "what does this sensor status mean", "what are the documented limits on RTR". Those answers are only in the product docs. That is the auth-walled half above, and it's the half I'd get the most out of.

The distinctive thing here is that the credential is already in the room. I'm authenticated to the tenant; the docs I need are gated by the same subscription I'm authenticated against. Making the server able to read them is a much shorter path than any external docs mirror.

### Related Module/Area

New module needed

### Proposed Solution (Optional)

A `docs` module, with part 1 shippable independently of part 2:

```
falcon_search_api_reference(query, collection=None, limit=20)
    -> [{operation_id, method, path, scope, summary, doc_url}]
    Backed by developer.crowdstrike.com/llms-full.txt (or operations-by-collection.md),
    fetched once and cached. No auth.

falcon_get_api_operation(operation_id)
    -> full operation page (params, scope, example)
    Backed by /api-reference/operations/<OperationId>.md. No auth.

falcon_search_product_docs(query, limit=10)      # part 2, gated
falcon_get_product_doc(doc_id)                   # part 2, gated
    Backed by the docs.crowdstrike.com Fluid Topics API, registered only when a
    docs credential is configured, and absent from tools/list otherwise.
```

Notes on fit with existing conventions:

- Part 1 introduces the server's first outbound call to a host other than the Falcon API. That's a real design decision, not a detail — it wants an opt-out (the module is already opt-in via `--modules`), and it needs to honour the existing proxy configuration from #405.
- Alternatively part 1 could ship as MCP **resources** rather than tools, alongside the existing `falcon_mcp/resources/*.py` FQL guides. Re

sample.title: Android: Media3 (ExoPlayer) producer backend behind the existing AImageReader consumer — scope, design, phases
sample.body:
## Why

Nearly every Android bug in this player's history lived in the hand-written producer layer (extractor + `AMediaCodec` state machine + AAudio): the non-monotonic pacing traps, AAudio power-saving underruns, the audio wedge, and most recently the read-error-is-EOS bug fixed in #70 (v1.9.6). Each one cost a device session to find. AndroidX Media3 (ExoPlayer) has already paid for all of them: `Mp4Extractor`, `DefaultAudioSink` with a latency-corrected position tracker, load-error retry policy, seek/loop state machine, and a decade of per-device codec quirks.

What is genuinely ours and must stay identical: the OpenXR frame loop, the Vulkan `AHardwareBuffer` import and weaving hand-off, display-locked frame selection against the runtime's predicted display time, exact-PTS L/R pairing for dual-track stereo MP4 (LVF v2), the convergence UV shift, and the shared ImGui HUD. None of that touches the producer.

This issue scopes replacing the **producer** (extractor + codec + audio output) with ExoPlayer driven from Kotlin over JNI, while the **consumer** (`AImageReader` onward) stays native. Two research passes went into it: an audit of the current contract in `video_decoder.cpp` / `audio_player.cpp` / `main.cpp`, and a primary-source read of androidx/media `1.10.0`. Findings below cite both.

**Not a rewrite now.** v1.9.6 is robust and device-verified. This is the plan for the next real expansion of the Android player (streaming, subtitles, HDR, DRM, 4K60-per-eye tuning), or when the producer bites again.

## Verdict

Feasible, as **"ExoPlayer + four small custom classes"**. We would not adopt ExoPlayer's rendering model; we use its extractor / codec / audio plumbing and override its frame-release policy so the native consumer keeps owning presentation. Estimated 450–650 LOC Kotlin + ~150 LOC JNI + a ~200 LOC consumer refactor; deletes ~1,400 LOC of native producer code.

| # | Finding (androidx/media 1.10.0) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `MediaCodecVideoRenderer.renderOutputBufferV21` calls `codec.releaseOutputBuffer(index, releaseTimeNs)` with a **vsync-snapped `System.nanoTime()`** (`VideoFrameReleaseHelper.adjustReleaseTime`, 80 % vsync offset). Our consumer reads `AImage_getTimestamp()` as the **media PTS** (today the codec is released with `presentationTimeUs*1000`). As-is this breaks display-locked selection *and* L/R pairing, and trips `validatePtsOnce` into the newest-frame fallback. | **Feasible with a subclass**: override `renderOutputBufferV21` (protected) to release at `presentationTimeUs * 1000`. An `AImageReader` consumer never applies desired-present-time deferral, so the value is pure metadata, exactly as today. Zero consumer change. (`VideoFrameMetadataListener` is the weaker alternative: exact, but per-frame on the playback thread and unavailable on the effects path.) |
| 2 | **Two video renderers on one player**: no stock support. `DefaultTrackSelector.selectAllTracks` yields one definition per track type; `MappingTrackSelector.selectTracks` is `final` and `preferUnassociatedRenderer` is hard-coded to metadata only. | **Feasible with a custom class**: implement `TrackSelector` directly (maintainer-endorsed pattern, google/ExoPlayer#6589, re-confirmed androidx/media#1473) returning two `FixedTrackSelection`s at the two video renderer indices. Engine has no per-type limit; the only constraint (one `MediaClock`) is satisfied because video renderers return `null` from `getMediaClock()`. Surfaces per renderer via `createMessage(renderer).setType(MSG_SET_VIDEO_OUTPUT)`, never `setVideoSurface` (broadcasts). |
| 3 | The two video renderers are **not synchronised to each other**: each owns a `VideoFrameReleaseControl` and independently drops (`earlyUs < -30 ms`), drops-to-keyframe (`< -500 ms`) and force-releases. | **Real hazard, neutralisable**: override `shouldDropOutputBuffer` / `shouldDropBuffersToKeyframe` → `false` in both renderers and let the native pairing queue absorb jitter. ExoPlayer becomes a decode pump driven by one audio clock. |
| 4 | `tkhd` disabled flag is **never read** by `BoxParser.parseTkhd`; both eye tracks appear as `C.TRACK_TYPE_VIDEO`. `hdlr` name is not read; `mdhd` language → `Format.language`, `tkhd` track id → `Format.id`. | **Go.** Discriminate L/R by `Format.language` (`abl`/`abr`), fall back to track order, same rule as the native probe. |
| 5 | The `mett` convergence track is exposed (`parseMetaDataSampleEntry` keeps the MIME verbatim) but needs `MimeTypes.registerCustomMimeType(..., TRACK_TYPE_METADATA)` plus a custom `MetadataDecoderFactory` to be decoded; and `elst` is applied **per track**, so a convergence track without its own edit list is not shifted with the video. | **Keep it native.** The existing probe already parses it once at open into an array indexed by PTS. Routing it through a Java looper callback is strictly more machinery and reintroduces the edit-list trap. |
| 6 | Audio position: `getCurrentPosition()` is ms-granular, app-thread-only, refreshed every ~10 ms. The accurate value (`MediaCodecAudioRenderer.getPositionUs` → `AudioTrackPositionTracker`, `AudioTrack.getTimestamp`, latency-corrected) is playback-thread-only. | **Feasible with a subclass**: `MediaCodecAudioRenderer` override of `getPositionUs()` publishes a `(positionUs, nanoTime)` anchor into atomics on every `doSomeWork`; native extrapolates lock-free. Sub-ms, zero JNI per frame. |
| 7 | Sources: `ContentDataSource` for `content://` (needs `Context` + the persistable grant; pass the URI string to Java), `FileDescriptorDataSource(fd, offset, length)` exists but is single-use (wrap in a factory that dups per `open()`). Loop: `REPEAT_MODE_ONE` rebases PTS to 0 per lap; the two renderers cross the seam independently (a few frames of L/R straddle, which the existing "master jumped → resync" path already handles). Seek: `SeekParameters.EXACT` default; a frame is force-released after a seek while paused. | **Go.** |

## The one change ExoPlayer forces on the consume

sample.title: Images: add an optional FLUX.2 klein 4B fast workflow
sample.body:
## Outcome

Add an optional `flux-fast` text-to-image mode backed by the official distilled **FLUX.2 [klein] 4B FP8** checkpoint. It should provide a second fast, Apache-2.0-licensed image style on the tower without changing the existing `fast` or `quality` modes.

This replaces the rejected 9B proposal in #89. It is independent of #13: either `quality-fast` or `flux-fast` may be implemented first.

## Product decisions

- Mode key: `flux-fast`.
- User-facing label: **FLUX.2 klein 4B (fast, Apache 2.0)**.
- Use the distilled FP8 4B checkpoint and the official four-step ComfyUI text-to-image workflow. Start with `guidance=1.0` and the upstream sampler/scheduler settings; document any deliberate deviation.
- Text-to-image only in this issue. Do not add image-to-image, multi-reference editing, masks, LoRAs, or the base/9B checkpoints. #88 owns masked editing.
- Keep Z-Image-Turbo as the `fast` default. Do not rename or silently redirect any existing mode.
- The mode is optional and disabled until its exact assets and required ComfyUI nodes pass preflight. Never fall back to another model after the user selects it.
- No Hugging Face token or license-acceptance flow: the selected 4B artifacts are public and Apache 2.0.

## Pinned assets and lifecycle

Create a small checked-in manifest for this component. Pin immutable upstream revisions, expected byte sizes, SHA-256 hashes, destination filenames, licenses, and source URLs for:

1. `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4b-fp8` at revision `5b4408e59397a4a37ccb46afe426d8ed86379441`, file `flux-2-klein-4b-fp8.safetensors` (about 4.07 GB);
2. ComfyUI's official `flux2-vae.safetensors` artifact from `Comfy-Org/vae-text-encorder-for-flux-klein-4b` (about 336 MB); and
3. the official `qwen_3_4b.safetensors` encoder from that Comfy-Org repository.

The current Z-Image `fast` workflow already uses a file named `qwen_3_4b.safetensors` (about 7.5 GB). Hash it and reuse it only if it exactly matches the pinned FLUX-compatible artifact. Otherwise install the pinned encoder under a distinct filename and point only the FLUX graph at it; never overwrite a working shared asset based on filename alone.

Add an explicit owner-run component command (for example `ops/images-models.ps1 install|remove|status flux-fast`) rather than downloading on daemon start:

- preflight free space for the full missing payload, temporary files, and a 5 GiB reserve;
- stream to a `.part` file, resume safely when supported, verify size and SHA-256, then atomically promote;
- never log bearer tokens or URL query strings (none are expected for these public artifacts);
- make repeated install/status/remove operations idempotent;
- remove only files owned solely by `flux-fast`; never remove the shared encoder while Z-Image uses it;
- clean stale partial files on explicit removal and report how much space was recovered.

Include Apache 2.0 attribution/model-card links in the documentation and component metadata. Do not commit model weights.

## ComfyUI compatibility and rollback

The tower currently records ComfyUI portable v0.35.0. Upstream's FLUX 4B guide says the workflow requires current core nodes.

- Determine the first stable ComfyUI portable release that contains the official FLUX.2 klein 4B template/nodes, then pin that version or immutable revision. Do not track `latest` or a nightly build.
- Stage the new portable build beside the current one. Validate startup plus `fast`, `quality`, and `flux-fast` graph preflight before changing the configured production path.
- Preserve the previous build and provide a documented one-command rollback. A failed upgrade or FLUX probe must leave the existing image modes on the old build.
- Validate node classes and asset names through ComfyUI's object-info/API before advertising the mode. Missing nodes/assets make only `flux-fast` unavailable with a precise reason and remediation.

Transcribe the official API-format graph into the harness; do not execute an arbitrary downloaded workflow JSON. Record the upstream template/revision used for the transcription.

## Harness and Agent Harness Web behavior

- Extend the image capability/mode response with stable fields for mode key, display name, availability, unavailable reason, license, checkpoint revision/hash, supported resolutions/aspects, steps, and negative-prompt support.
- Show the selector only to users already allowed to generate images. When the component is absent or incompatible, show `flux-fast` disabled with a concise owner-facing install/doctor message; other modes continue working.
- Reuse the existing image queue, exclusive `InferenceGate`, GPU hold, ComfyUI warmup/progress/cancellation, result storage, notifications, and agent `generate_image` tool. Do not create a second scheduler or leave ComfyUI resident on the 16 GB GPU.
- Use the existing `standard` dimensions initially. Reject unsupported dimensions explicitly instead of silently resizing.
- Persist enough provenance with every result to reproduce it: mode, checkpoint revision and SHA-256, encoder/VAE hashes, ComfyUI revision, prompt, dimensions, seed, steps, sampler/scheduler, guidance, and timing. Existing image records remain readable.
- Extend `ops/check-stack.ps1`/doctor output with the component and ComfyUI compatibility status. A missing optional component is a warning, not a stack failure.

## Tests

Add deterministic tests for:

- the exact graph shape, four-step settings, dimensions, seed, and output prefix;
- capability reporting for installed, missing, corrupt, shared-encoder, and missing-node states;
- selection through the HTTP API and `generate_image` tool, including no silent fallback;
- atomic install/hash-failure cleanup, idempotent status/removal, shared-asset preservation, and insufficient-space refusal without downloading;
- staged ComfyUI validation/rollback and regression probes for the existing `fast` and `quality` graphs;
- provenance persistence and reading old image rows; and
- queue/GPU-handoff cleanu

sample.title: APP PRI 4B — Adopt Core custom ingredient IDs for new App pantry ingredients
sample.body:
## Purpose

Continue PRI 4 after the merged P4A identity contract (#38 / PR #39).

Implement the **App-side adoption** of the active Core custom-ingredient identity contract for newly created App custom pantry ingredients.

Current master baseline when this issue was created:
`fd81c463abae7b349b34830aa176c7c9d5b5cc89`

Governing contract:
`docs/development/CORE_CUSTOM_INGREDIENT_IDENTITY_V1.md`

This is an App adapter phase, not a new identity design.

## Current state to preserve

- App currently creates custom pantry ingredient IDs through `modules/pantry.py::_generer_custom_ingredient_id()`.
- Existing App IDs use legacy `custom_<...>` and are permanently grandfathered by the Core contract.
- App's current `.kbhrecipe` importer rejects custom ingredient rows; do **not** change that in this issue.
- App's current `.kbhbrew` snapshot path does not create custom ingredient rows; do **not** add that capability here.
- `pantry_item_id` is row identity and is explicitly OUTSIDE the Core custom-ingredient identity contract. Do not change it.

## Required behavior

For **newly created App custom pantry ingredients only**:

1. Mint IDs in exact canonical format:
   `kbh-custom-<lowercase canonical UUIDv4>`
2. Mint once at creation and keep the same ingredient ID across later pantry-row edits/renames.
3. Do not rewrite, normalize, migrate, or re-save any existing legacy `custom_*` ID.
4. Preserve all existing pantry behavior and UI semantics except the new ID format.
5. Generation-time collision handling must follow Core V1: never overwrite/reuse a colliding ID; mint another ID.
6. The collision check must cover every **current App local storage location that can actually hold custom ingredient IDs today**. Based on the active contract, pantry is currently the exercised App location because App recipe import rejects custom rows and App brew snapshots do not create them. Verify this against current master before implementation. If current code contradicts that assumption, stop and report the exact additional location/scope rather than silently expanding capability.
7. Do not infer ingredient type from the ID string. Type remains structural (`ingredient_type`).
8. Existing legacy IDs remain readable/editable exactly as before.

## Scope

Expected narrow scope:
- `modules/pantry.py`
- directly affected App pantry UI caller(s), only if required to provide current occupied IDs safely
- focused pantry tests
- minimal documentation update if needed to record App adoption status

Do not touch Web in this issue.

## Explicitly out of scope

- No Web changes.
- No migration of existing App data.
- No lazy on-read normalization.
- No change to `pantry_item_id`.
- No new custom-ingredient support in App `.kbhrecipe` import.

sample.title: Hardening (low, defense-in-depth): runner-writable ancestor symlink can redirect worker-privileged clone-tree sinks (CWE-59)
sample.body:
## Summary

Severity: **Low — defense-in-depth / future-proofing.** Not a current
cross-tenant exposure.

The worker-privileged clone-management sinks under `runner/` operate on
`clonePath = runnerRoot/<repoDir>/<key>` with only a **lexical** containment check
(or none at all), so a runner-controlled symlink in an **ancestor** path component
can lexically pass validation and be followed at operation time (CWE-59, link
following). `runnerRoot` is `worker:runner 2775` (setgid, no sticky, per the comment
at `agent/src/git.ts:693-698`), so a runner-uid/group process can rename/unlink
`runnerRoot/<repoDir>` and plant an ancestor symlink.

**Why this is low, not the Major CodeRabbit assigned.** A per-user worker is
**single-tenant**: every run on it shares runner uid 10002 and already has direct
mutation access to every clone under that runner-writable PVC subtree, so a run can
already clobber a sibling clone directly — the symlink trick grants **no
privilege/tenant escalation** over what the runner can already do. There is no
cross-user worker sharing, and worker-only targets would require an `issue-N` entry
the current layout does not create. So this is a valid **pre-existing** mechanism to
harden the worker-privileged filesystem sinks against, not a live cross-tenant hole.

Surfaced by CodeRabbit on PR #1321 (issue #1315). #1315 did **not** introduce it: the
base already performed worker-uid recursive delete + reseed on the same
runner-writable ancestor with no containment; #1315 replaced terminal deletion with a
recoverable rename and added the first (lexical) guard, so it **reduces** rather than
expands the effective capability. Non-blocking for #1315, tracked here.

## Affected sinks (a coherent fix must cover ALL of them, or structurally remove the ancestor write)

- **`retireRunnerClone`** (the #1315 atomic rename to quarantine). Include the new
  **foreign-retire invocation** in the threat model: a run now moves a *different*
  (terminal-owner) run's clone.
- **The reseed `fs.rm(clonePath, {recursive:true})` + `fs.mkdir(dirname(clonePath))`**
  in `runnerCloneForBranch` (`agent/src/git.ts:692` / `:699`) — no containment at all.
- **The `removeRunnerClone` fallback** (`agent/src/git.ts`).
- **Ancestor directory permissions:** `runnerRoot` is `2775` with no sticky bit. A
  structural fix (worker-owned, non-group-writable ancestors so the runner can only
  write *inside* its own clone, or a sticky bit) may be simpler than per-call
  validation — but must be validated across **clone creation and all uid modes**
  (the M4 group-`runner` split and the single-uid `#58` path).

## Why lstat-per-ancestor is NOT the fix

A retire-only `lstat`/`realpath` check is **TOCTOU-prone** (an ancestor can be swapped
between the check and the `rename`/`rm`) and creates false assurance while the sibling
sinks stay open. The coherent fix must be **race-safe** — an
`openat2(RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS)` / dirfd-based resolution, or the structural
permission redesign above — applied across every sink. Do not ship a retire-only
`realpath` check.

## Acceptance

- Every runner-tree clone sink resolves its source race-safely (no TOCTOU), OR the
  runner has no write access to any ancestor of `clonePath`, validated across clone
  creation and all uid modes.
- A test proving an ancestor symlink cannot redirect any sink outside the intended
  canonical clone.

## Not queued

No sweep label — needs a security design decision first (openat2/dirfd availability on
the `node:24-alpine` base, versus the structural permission change).

Refs: PR #1321, #1315, the CodeRabbit CWE-59 finding on `agent/src/git.ts`.

sample.title: Bug: no automatic reconnection when the indiserver TCP connection drops
sample.body:
## Problem

Once `async_setup_entry` in `custom_components/indi_client/__init__.py` calls `client.connect()` and `client.start()`, nothing ever retries the connection again if it is lost.

In `custom_components/indi_client/indi/client.py`, `INDIClient._read_loop()`:

```python
except (ConnectionError, OSError) as err:
    _LOGGER.debug("INDI connection to %s:%s lost: %s", self.host, self.port, err)
finally:
    if self.connected:
        self.connected = False
        if self.on_connection_changed:
            self.on_connection_changed(False)
```

When the socket read raises (indiserver restarted, network blip, USB-triggered driver crash taking indiserver down, etc.), the loop simply exits. `connected` flips to `False`, `binary_sensor.*_server_connected` correctly goes `off`, and every entity's `available` property (in `entity.py`, which checks `self._client.connected`) correctly goes unavailable — but no code path ever calls `client.connect()`/`client.start()` again. The only way to restore the integration is for the user to manually reload/restart the config entry (or Home Assistant) from the UI.

For an integration meant to run unattended controlling telescope hardware overnight, a transient network hiccup or an indiserver restart (common when a driver/USB device is power-cycled) permanently breaks the integration until a human intervenes.

I checked `config_flow.py`, `entity.py`, `binary_sensor.py`, and the rest of `custom_components/indi_client/` — there is no coordinator, backoff loop, or reconnect timer anywhere in the codebase; this isn't just a missed edge case in one file, the capability doesn't exist at all.

## Suggested fix

Add a reconnect loop (e.g. exponential backoff, retried from `_read_loop`'s `finally` block or a small supervisor task started alongside it in `start()`) that keeps trying `connect()` + `start()` (re-sending `getProperties`, since `self.devices` state is likely stale/gone after a drop) until it succeeds or the config entry is unloaded. `disconnect()` already exists and cleanly cancels `_read_task`, so it should be safe to call it before each reconnect attempt to reset state.

## Notes

This is a read-only issue-hunt finding — the version-bump/CHANGELOG CI requirement mentioned in `CLAUDE.md` doesn't apply here since no PR is attached.

This issue was created by an automated issue-hunt routine.

sample.body:
## Purpose
Shared collaboration board for ChatGPT and Claude on the Smart Koi Pond project. Goal: complement each other, review each other's work, and avoid duplicated or conflicting implementation.

## Governing authority
Before substantive changes, both assistants should follow the same authority order:
1. Project Router in Google Drive
2. Canonical ACTIVE Handbook
3. Current State
4. ACTIVE Portable Handoff
5. Relevant Functional / Visual specification
6. Fresh GitHub `main` + CI evidence

Google Drive remains the durable authority. GitHub is the execution/review layer. This issue is coordination only; it is not a second handbook.

## Current accepted software checkpoint
- Repository: `DontAsk3010/smart-koi-pond`
- Repository visibility: PUBLIC for cross-assistant read/review collaboration
- Accepted main after PR #47: `ad8762f27c4827dc29507976ac2527563e3f9b87`
- PR #47: integrated owner operation + guided test values + integrated backwash → water restore → chemistry re-evaluation/verification
- Post-merge CI: PASS on Python 3.11 + 3.12
- Visual Functional Acceptance: PASS
- Deployment Package: PASS
- Windows Package: PASS

## Collaboration rules
- Do not create a second control/state engine, browser calculator, or parallel source of truth.
- Do not infer missing evidence as zero/healthy/success.
- Command ON / feedback ON does not prove process recovery; verify the process response.
- High-risk automatic chemical dosing remains CLOSED.
- Real actuator authority remains CLOSED until Site Integration & Commissioning.
- Keep trading/A1 CLEAN repositories completely separate.
- Work on a branch/fork and submit a PR for material changes; do not silently overwrite accepted `main`.
- Every PR should state: problem, evidence, files changed, tests run, effect on canonical behavior, and any remaining limitation.
- One assistant may implement while the other reviews; or one may analyze a defect and leave a reproducible finding for the other.
- If assistants disagree, resolve against Drive authority + reproducible runtime/CI evidence, not preference.

## Suggested handoff format
When leaving work for the other assistant, comment here or on the relevant PR with:
- `FROM:` ChatGPT or Claude
- `STATUS:` FINDING / PROPOSAL / IMPLEMENTED / REVIEWED / BLOCKED
- `BASE:` exact commit SHA
- `SCOPE:` files / subsystem
- `EVIDENCE:` observed behavior, test, logs, screenshots or code references
- `CHANGE:` what was changed or proposed
- `VALIDATION:` tests/workflows and result
- `NEXT:` exact next action

## Current product direction
Owner operation should remain simple and integrated: sensor/manual-simulation input → pond condition → automatic system response → physical/modelled process effect → verification → recovery/escalation → owner recommendation. Manual ON/OFF equipment controls are secondary maintenance tools, not the normal owner workflow.

This board exists so ChatGPT and Claude can help each other without forcing the owner to manually reconstruct context between assistants.

sample.title: handoff: idle-timer auto-handoff before the cache lapses
sample.body:
Proposal from discussion, not yet implemented. Design as refined:

## Problem
When a session's prompt cache lapses, the next turn re-uploads the whole context at the write rate. Running `/handoff` while the cache is still warm costs one cheap read plus a few thousand output tokens. A Stop hook can't fire later than turn-end, so it can't wait out the idle period itself — it needs to spawn something that outlives it.

## Mechanism
- **Stop hook, every turn end.** First, kill whatever pid is recorded in this lane's pidfile (`.handoff/<lane>.timer.pid`, same lane resolution as `handoff/scripts/lane.sh`), if it's still alive — any real turn cancels a pending timer. Then check guards: was this turn itself a `/handoff` run, is the transcript above the size floor worth writing, are teammates in this lane still active. If all guards pass, spawn a detached process (`setsid` + disown or equivalent) that sleeps 58 minutes, and write its pid to the pidfile.
- **Environment precondition.** Before spawning anything, the hook must check for `TMUX`/`TMUX_PANE` or `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`. Neither present, skip entirely — there is no way to inject text into a bare terminal session from a detached background process (no tmux `send-keys`, no herdr `pane.send_text`, and OS-level UI automation is a different, fragile category not in scope here). This also selects which injection method the timer uses when it does fire.
- **What fires at minute 58.** The timer can't call the handoff write logic directly — summarizing working state has to happen in the model's own session, not a script. So it injects `/handoff` into the live pane (`tmux send-keys` or herdr's `pane.send_text`, per the precondition check above), which runs normally and writes the lane file.

## Explicit constraint: write-only, no auto-clear
The handoff write itself is the user's manual signal that it's safe to `/clear` and continue elsewhere. Nothing in this feature should ever trigger `/clear` automatically — the timer writes the lane file and stops there. (A `PreCompact` hook that writes a handoff before auto-compaction was also discussed as a related, separate idea — worth its own issue if pursued, not part of this one. Note that `PreCompact` can block compaction via exit code 2 / `permissionDecision: "deny"`, but cannot itself substitute a `/clear` in its place — that would need the same keystroke-injection mechanism as this timer.)

## Guards to get right
- Skip spawning if the last turn was the handoff run itself (avoid immediately re-arming right after a fresh write).
- Skip if the transcript is under a size floor (not worth writing).
- Skip if teammates in this lane are still working.
- The pidfile is per-lane, matching the seat-keying scheme landed in #8, so multiple sessions in the same repo don't clobber each other's timer state either.

sample.title: portability guard: fabrika guard portability-guard check, its CI job and the review-skill wiring
sample.body:
**Stories:** 2
**TDD:** yes
**Containment:** exempt (a CI gate and a review check; no runtime surface to flag)

### What to build
A new fail-closed guard, `fabrika guard portability-guard check`, plus its CI job and its review-skill wiring. Scope: every file under `claude-plugins/fabrika/**` and `packages/fabrika-cli/src/**`. Red on any line carrying a repo-bound reference: `#NNNN` (an issue or PR number), `ADR NNNN` in either spelling (`ADR 0092`, `ADR [0092](...)`), a `.decisions/` link, a `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/(issues|pull)/` URL, and any name on the repo-name list `.fabrika.jsonc` declares (phoenix declares `phoenix`, `kamp-us`, `Tuval`, `sözlük`, `apps/web`; the shipped default is an empty list, so an adopter names its own). A markdown heading (`# `), a hex colour (`#fff`, `#1a1a1a`) and a `#NNNN` inside a string or template literal in a `*.test.ts` file or under a `__fixtures__`/`fixtures` directory are not hits.

Shape, copied from the two nearest guards:
- Matchers pure in `packages/fabrika-cli/src/guard/portability.ts`; scope walk, fail-closed floors and verdict in `guard/portability-verb.ts`, on the `no-gh.ts`/`no-gh-verb.ts` split. Zero scope in either root, or a group directory that contributed no file, is a red (ADR 0092). No `gh` in its source (`fabrika guard no-gh check` stays green). Self-exempt by file suffix for the guard's own source and tests, never a directory.
- Allowlist on the `apps/web/src/i18n/i18n-guard.config.json` shape, at a repo-root path the verb pins: two buckets with a mandatory `why` per entry. `exempt` is per file and permanent (test data, `claude-plugins/fabrika/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`'s `homepage`/`repository`, and the behaviour literals #7478 classes as config work: `guard/i18n-literal-verb.ts`, `guard/fanout.ts`, `config/keys/governed-roots.ts`, `config/keys/doc-leak-exempt.ts`). `unmigrated` is the floor: one row per sweep unit named in epic #8281's plan, ceiling equal to that unit's count at landing, each row naming the child that clears it. A ceiling is a count, so a new reference inside a listed unit still reds; a ceiling above the count reds too (shrink-only).
- The repo-name list is a `portability` key group in `.fabrika.jsonc` per `.patterns/fabrika-config-key-groups.md`: key module, one `register` line, schema fragment, `fabrika config schema --write`. A malformed value refuses fail-closed.
- CI: `.github/workflows/portability-guard.yml` on the `no-gh-guard.yml` shape, whole-tree, on `pull_request` and `push: main`.
- Review: the review skill's doc and skill classes run `fabrika guard portability-guard check` on any diff under the two roots and treat a red as a FAIL finding; the doc rubric and skill rubric each gain the rule, beside the existing dead-link and leak rules.

The guard lands with the floor equal to today's counts and reds nothing on `main`; the sweeps shrink it.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `fabrika guard portability-guard check` exists, is listed by `fabrika guard --help`, and is green on `main` with the floor config populated at the landing counts and every row naming its sweep child
- [ ] The verb reds on a fixture tree carrying each pattern (`#NNNN`, `ADR NNNN`, `ADR [NNNN](...)`, `.decisions/`, a `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/` URL, a declared repo name) and stays green on a markdown heading, a hex colour, and a `#NNNN` inside a string literal in a `*.test.ts` file or a fixtures directory
- [ ] The verb reds on zero scope in either root and on a ceiling above the observed count; a unit test pins each refusal
- [ ] A golden test pins the self-exempt suffix list, and `fabrika guard no-gh check` is green with the new guard in the tree
- [ ] `.fabrika.jsonc` gains a `portability` key group with a schema fragment; `fabrika config schema --write` leaves `.fabrika.schema.json` unchanged after the commit; `fabrika status settings` prints the declared name list
- [ ] `.github/workflows/portability-guard.yml` runs the verb on `pull_request` and `push: main` and is green on the branch
- [ ] `claude-plugins/fabrika/skills/review/SKILL.md` and its doc and skill rubrics run the guard on any diff under `claude-plugins/fabrika/**` or `packages/fabrika-cli/src/**`; `fabrika guard skill-lint check` is green
- [ ] `packages/fabrika-cli/README.md` or the guard's docblock states what the guard forbids, the allowlist's two buckets, and that the floor only shrinks

sample.title: Fence agent git side effects below the supervisor (force-with-lease CAS + lease-bound push credential)
sample.body:
## Problem

The genuinely hard failure in nano-workforce#768 is **split-brain**: if the supervisor (the fencing authority) dies, it cannot kill a preempted worker, so an **old worker and a new worker can both commit/push**, colliding. This cannot be solved by a supervisor-mediated fence — the fence must live **below** the supervisor so it holds even when the supervisor is gone.

## Proposed mechanisms (defense in depth)

1. **Git-level compare-and-swap (partly built).** Push with expected-parent / force-with-lease semantics so a **stale** worker's push is rejected because the branch advanced. jwulf/c8ctl-plugin-nano#231 / #233 already landed *"never commit-on-base then non-ff-lose the work"*; the symmetric extension is to make git itself the CAS for the committed side effect — the losing worker's push fails cleanly instead of colliding.
2. **Lease-bound push credential.** Hand the harness a short-TTL `GIT_ASKPASS` token tied to the activation lease; when the lease expires, push rights expire automatically, so a preempted worker loses the ability to push **without** needing the supervisor to intervene. This is the "supervisor brokers git on the agent's behalf" microVM design: the broker refuses a push from a job whose lease it no longer holds.

## Acceptance

- Two workers holding the same jobKey across a lease handoff cannot both land a push: the stale one is rejected (git CAS) or de-credentialed (lease-bound token).
- The fence holds with the supervisor process dead (no supervisor-mediated step in the critical path).

## Relationship

- Closes the collision window that Epics A/B cannot (they assume a live supervisor).
- The universal, host-independent complement is engine-side idempotency/fencing on settlement — tracked separately in Magikcraft/nano-bpm.

Refs nanobpm/nano-workforce#768

sample.body:
## Finding

**Location:** cmd/launcher/internal/waves/blocker_test.go:181

Also present in:
- cmd/launcher/testhelpers_test.go:148 (captureStdout)
- cmd/launcher/internal/settle/blocked_relay_test.go:19 (captureStderr)

A single shared internal test helper (e.g., a small `internal/testcapture` package, or a concurrent-drain variant) would fix the buffer-deadlock limit once and give every caller the same restore semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extract a shared internal test utility package (e.g., `internal/testcapture`) containing consolidated stdout/stderr capture helpers
- [ ] Consolidate the three copies into one shared helper covering both stdout and stderr

Found by review during #3075 (branch agent/issue-3075)

sanduhr-mcp says "widget not polling" when the running widget predates the snapshot writer
sample.body:
## What happens

`get_usage` returns `status: stale, reason: widget_not_polling`, with the remedy "start (or restart) the widget". It keeps doing that while the widget is open and polling normally.

Restarting doesn't help. The widget is fetching fine; it just never writes `snapshot.json`.

## Why

The running widget is the Microsoft Store build **3.3.0.0**, which has no snapshot writer. The statusline bridge and `sanduhr-mcp` ship in **3.4.0**. On this machine:

- `%APPDATA%\Sanduhr\snapshot.json` was last written **2026-07-26 22:56**, by a local dev build during the statusline and MCP work (commits `108f024`, `0ab4819`). That build has since been uninstalled.
- `%APPDATA%\Sanduhr\bin\sanduhr-mcp.cmd` is still registered with Claude Code from that dev build.
- The Store widget (3.3.0.0) polls every 5 minutes: `fetch-debug.log` shows `usage: status=200 tiers=6`. It appends each reading to `history.<account>.json` as usual, but it never touches `snapshot.json`.
- `settings.json` still has `statusline_enabled = true` from the dev build, so the setting looks right even though nothing honours it.

The result is a correct-looking MCP config reading a 48-day-old file, with a remedy that can't fix it.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Say what's actually wrong.** If the history file is recent but `snapshot.json` is old, or the snapshot's `app_version` predates the writer, return a distinct reason, e.g. `widget_too_old` / `snapshot_writer_missing`, with the remedy "update Sanduhr to 3.4.0 or later". Keep `widget_not_polling` for a widget that really isn't running.
2. **Document the version floor.** `sanduhr-mcp` needs widget ≥ 3.4.0. Put that in the MCP install flow and the 3.4.0 release notes.
3. **Optional fallback:** when the snapshot is stale but the history file is fresh, `get_usage` could serve the latest history point as `status: degraded` rather than nothing. The data is sitting right there.

## Workaround until 3.4.0 is installed

Read the latest point for each tier from `%APPDATA%\Sanduhr\history.<account>.json`. It's current to within 5 minutes.

Found while scoping token costs in another project.

sample.title: Should pgstore refuse a save over a row that moved since it was read?
sample.body:
Split out of #164, which measures and documents the loss but deliberately does not
change any behaviour.

## The situation

Two servers holding one document over one store at the same time lose the earlier
save. Measured in `TestTwoServersOverOneStoreLoseTheEarlierSave`: one writes
`AAAA`, the other `BBBB`, the store ends holding `BBBB` alone, and there is no
error anywhere. Every piece behaved as documented — `Store.Save` replaces, a server
holds its replica in memory — so nothing is wrong with the code. What is wrong is
that an operator can reach this configuration and never find out.

#164 states the constraint where an operator reads it and names the two supported
alternatives (`Server.Follow`, or a gitstore with a remote). This issue is about
whether one store should also **refuse**.

## The specific proposal

`pgstore.Save` is a blind upsert:

```sql
INSERT INTO t (document, snapshot) VALUES ($1, $2)
ON CONFLICT (document) DO UPDATE SET snapshot = EXCLUDED.snapshot, updated_at = now()
```

The table already carries `updated_at`. A `Store` could remember, per document,
the `updated_at` it last read or wrote, and make the update conditional on it:
0 rows affected means somebody else wrote, and the save returns an error instead
of carrying their work away.

## What is good about it

It matches this package's stated philosophy, which is explicit in `MultiStore`:

> Refusing keeps the operator's options open; answering closes them silently.

The same reasoning already governs a torn write (`Load` refuses zero bytes rather
than calling it a new document) and an impossible merge (`ErrUnmergeable`). A
silent permanent loss is exactly the thing this codebase refuses elsewhere.

It is also contained: no interface change, no new column, nothing outside pgstore,
and the real-PostgreSQL lane can measure it.

## What is not obvious

- **It makes `pgstore.Store` stateful** in a way it is not today. Two `Store`
  values in one process over one table — a server and a migration tool, say —
  would then fight, each holding its own idea of the last revision.
- **It makes one store safer while DirStore stays unsafe**, and the `Store`
  contract does not express the difference. An operator could reasonably read a
  guard in one store as a guarantee of the interface.
- **A rolling restart changes shape.** The departing server's final flush, if it
  lands after the arriving one has already saved, would be refused rather than
  clobbering — better, but it turns a case that works today into one that reports
  an error, and the operator has to know that error is benign.
- It guards an **unsupported configuration**. There is a reasonable position that
  documenting it is the whole of the answer, and that spending statefulness on a
  shape nobody should deploy buys the wrong thing.

## What I would need to decide it

Whether "two servers over one PostgreSQL" is a shape worth defending against, or
one that documentation settles. That is a call about the deployments this project
means to serve, so it is yours rather than mine.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

sample.title: Subagent children ignore ANTHROPIC_CLI_VERSION, making current-generation models undispatchable
sample.body:
## Symptom

`anthropic/claude-fable-5-1` — the `authorDefault` and lead entry of every review pool — works from the CLI and fails instantly when dispatched as a subagent child:

```
400 invalid_request_error
Claude Code 2.1.75 does not support this model; version 2.1.251 or newer is required
```

## Cause

The parent shell exports `ANTHROPIC_CLI_VERSION=2.1.259`. Subagent children do not load the anthropic-auth extension, so they fall back to the built-in default of 2.1.75 and the version gate rejects the model.

The model is fine. The dispatch path is not.

## Why this matters beyond one model

A panel roster is only useful if its entries can be **dispatched**. Three properties are independent, and this repo has now been bitten by all three:

| Property | How it fails silently |
|---|---|
| Present in `pi --list-models` | a stale provider prefix names no provider at all |
| Invocable by this caller | `402 Insufficient Balance`; IAM denies the inference profile |
| Dispatchable as a child | the child runtime lacks the parent's extensions |

A dispatch-path probe of the full roster found `deepseek-v4-pro`/`-flash` returning `402` while ranked above three working models, and the undated `claude-haiku-4-5` alias failing a launch identity check while leading `task_validate`. Both were listed and both looked healthy.

## No fallback route for this one

`fable-5-1` has no usable provider-route twin, so dispatch recovery has nothing to reach for:

- there is no `eu.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1` inference profile
- `anthropic.`, `global.` and `us.` variants exist but this account's role is denied `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on them

Verified by dispatch probe, 2026-09-04.

## Fix candidates

1. Load the anthropic-auth extension in subagent children, or propagate `ANTHROPIC_CLI_VERSION` into the child environment. This is the actual fix.
2. Failing that, raise the built-in fallback version.

## Related

`resolve-panel --pong` probes the **CLI** path, so it would have passed this model. Whatever proactive health check lands under #141 should probe the dispatch path instead, or it will certify models that cannot review.
