sample.body:
## Description

`docs/security-checklist.md` (Build & Deploy section, line 39) states:

> No secrets needed for this site - if a future feature introduces an API key (e.g. a contact form provider), add it via Netlify environment variables, never commit it

This is no longer accurate. `lib/github.ts` already reads a secret from the environment in two places:

- `lib/github.ts:27` — `const token = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN;` (used as a Bearer token for the REST repos call)
- `lib/github.ts:45` — same env var, required (function returns `null` if absent) for the GitHub GraphQL contribution-calendar query

This is consumed by `components/GitHubActivity.tsx`, a Server Component (no `"use client"`), so the token itself isn't shipped to the browser — that part is safe. The problem is purely that the checklist text was never updated when this feature was added.

## Why it matters

The checklist is the project's own onboarding/reference doc for what secret-handling looks like on this repo (CLAUDE.md points contributors to it before "adding dependencies, external links, or any server-side feature"). Telling contributors "no secrets needed" when a secret is already wired in is actively misleading:
- A future contributor modifying `lib/github.ts` or `GitHubActivity.tsx` has no documented guidance that `GITHUB_TOKEN` exists, how it should be scoped/rotated, or that it must stay server-side.
- It undercuts the checklist's usefulness as a pre-flight check — the one existing secret in the codebase isn't mentioned at all.

## Suggested fix

Update `docs/security-checklist.md`'s Build & Deploy section to document the existing secret, e.g.:

```
- [ ] `GITHUB_TOKEN` (used by `lib/github.ts` for GitHub REST/GraphQL calls) is set via
  Netlify environment variables, never committed, and only read in Server Components
  (never exposed to the client bundle)
```

No code change needed — this is a documentation-only fix to keep the checklist accurate.

sample.title: Claude Code: the assistant text in the same message as a search never reaches the trace, because the host writes that entry after PreToolUse runs
sample.body:
Seen in the 0.2.10 release check on macOS (RC commit ee84237, Claude Code, row R1), router-confirmed: the request carried session, turn and call ids and no `history`. Reproduced in a second Claude Code session by capturing the bridge the lineage hook attached to a tool call: the `history` text was the assistant text of the **previous** assistant message, not the text written immediately before the call in the same message.

**What happened.** Claude Code runs the PreToolUse hook before it appends the assistant entry that contains the tool call to the transcript. The hook reads the transcript tail to find the assistant text of the current turn, so the text in the same message as the search is never on disk when it looks. Replaying the hook against the R1 transcript truncated just before that entry yields no history; including the entry yields 182 characters. When the model narrates in an earlier message of the same turn, that text travels (tool-result entries are correctly not treated as user turns); when its only narration is in the message that makes the search, which is the common shape, the envelope is identity-only.

**Likely cause.** Host write order, not the floor logic #65 fixed: `currentAssistantText` (`hook.go`) can only see what the host has written, and the current message is written after the hook runs.

**Why it matters.** The trace product's text for Claude Code is one message stale or absent, on the host with the most users. #65's changelog claim needs the honest wording.

**Expected.** One of: the search sends the text with the next request of the same turn as a late attachment keyed by the previous request id (protocol change on the router side); a PostToolUse hook forwards the text after the fact; or the README states the limit for Claude Code. A design decision for 0.2.11, not a hook patch.

Severity: minor, trace text only; identity lineage is correct.

**lean-ctx version:** (run `lean-ctx --version`)
3.10.0

**OS:** (macOS / Linux / Windows)
Linux/Windows

**AI tool:** (Cursor / Claude Code / Copilot / Crush / other)
Claude Code

"wrap claude" bypasses Pro/Max auth guard and writes "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL" unconditionally

## Summary

"lean-ctx wrap claude" configures Claude Code to use the local lean-ctx proxy by writing:

"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:4444"

to "~/.claude/settings.json".

Unlike the normal proxy setup path, "wrap claude" does not apply the existing Claude Pro/Max subscription guard before writing this setting.

For users authenticated through a Claude Pro/Max subscription without an "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", this redirects Claude Code OAuth traffic through a custom base URL that lean-ctx's own proxy code and diagnostics say is incompatible with subscription authentication.

The result is that "wrap claude" can create a configuration that "lean-ctx doctor" immediately considers invalid and that can cause Claude Code authentication failures.

Environment

Observed against lean-ctx 3.10.0. The relevant code path also appears to exist on current "main".

Claude Code authentication mode:

- Claude Pro/Max subscription
- OAuth authentication
- no "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"

## Relevant implementation

The active "wrap" command is dispatched through "cli::wrap_cmd".

For Claude, that implementation directly configures:

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>

and writes the same endpoint into Claude Code's "settings.json".

This path does not appear to call the existing:

anthropic_api_key_available(...)

guard used by the normal proxy setup implementation.

By contrast, "proxy_setup::install_claude_env_inner()" explicitly detects this situation and avoids redirecting Claude when no Anthropic API key is available.

Its comments describe the reason:

- Pro/Max uses OAuth
- subscription authentication only works directly against "api.anthropic.com"
- redirecting it through a custom "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL" causes a login loop / 401

Reproduction

1. Authenticate Claude Code using a Claude Pro/Max subscription.
2. Ensure no "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" or equivalent API-key authentication is configured.
3. Run:

lean-ctx wrap claude

4. Inspect:

~/.claude/settings.json

5. Observe a local proxy endpoint under:

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:4444"
  }
}

6. Run:

lean-ctx doctor

Depending on proxy configuration state, "doctor" reports either the stale-proxy configuration or the Claude subscription/proxy authentication conflict.

Claude Code may subsequently fail actual API requests with 401/authentication errors.

Actual behavior

"wrap claude" writes the Claude proxy endpoint without checking whether Claude is using subscription OAuth.

This differs from "lean-ctx proxy enable" / setup behavior.

It is also possible for "wrap" to leave the configuration in a state where the local proxy process exists but "proxy_enabled" is not set, causing "doctor" to report:

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL → http://127.0.0.1:4444 but proxy is not configured

Expected behavior

"wrap claude" should use the same Claude authentication policy as the normal proxy configuration path.

For example:

1. If an Anthropic API key is available:
   
   - enable/configure the proxy consistently
   - write "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"

2. If no Anthropic API key is available:
   
   - do not write a local "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"
   - remove a stale lean-ctx-owned local redirect if appropriate
   - leave Claude Code talking directly to "api.anthropic.com"
   - print a short explanation that Pro/Max OAuth cannot be routed through the proxy

"wrap" should not maintain a separate implementation of Claude proxy configuration that bypasses the safeguards already implemented in "proxy_setup".

Suggested implementation

Instead of writing "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL" directly from "cli/wrap_cmd.rs", reuse the existing proxy setup function or extract the Claude endpoint decision into a shared helper.

The important invariant should be:

no Anthropic API key
+
Claude Pro/Max OAuth
=
never configure Claude Code with a local ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL

It would also be useful to add an integration/regression test covering:

wrap claude
+ no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
→ no local ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL

and:

wrap claude
+ ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
→ proxy configured consistently

Impact

This is particularly confusing because "wrap claude" is presented as a one-command setup path.

A user can successfully install the MCP integration but simultaneously change Claude Code's API transport in a way that breaks subscription authentication.

The failure may only become visible on the next Claude Code request/restart, making the cause difficult to associate with "lean-ctx wrap".

sample.title: Picklist Dependency Explorer: make it a pure structure visualizer and remove every Apex-run surface
sample.body:
## Problem Statement

The Picklist Dependency Explorer currently fuses two things: a picture of what depends on what, and a report of the last Apex test run. The run half — pass/fail badges, the "Last check" banner, failure triage prose, the click-through into `.cls` methods and `report.md` — makes the panel useless until a user has generated *and deployed and run* Apex, and it pulls in results parsing, failure attribution and two action allow-lists that exist for no other reason.

The dependency structure itself is the part people want, and it is fully available from `manifest.json` alone.

## User Story

As a Salesforce admin exploring an org's dependent picklists, I want the Explorer to show me the dependency structure and nothing else, so that I can read what a controlling value unlocks without an Apex test run, a deployed org, or a results file existing.

## Scope Decisions

- **Strip every run surface** from the panel — no banner, no badges, no status filter, no triage, no run-report or spec-method links. The Explorer never reads the results folder.
- **`manifest.json` stays the source.** `Generate Picklist Dependency Tests` still produces the model; it simply stops being surfaced in the panel.
- **Delete the results code from the Explorer service** rather than relocating it. `PicklistDependencyCheckService` already reports its own run outcome.
- **Both Apex commands stay untouched** in `package.json` and the Command Palette.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Panel renders structure only

- [ ] Opening the Explorer with no `treecipe/PicklistDependencyResults/` folder at all renders the full object → dependent field → combination tree with no error, no banner and no empty-state caveat about a missing run
- [ ] No pass/fail/not-checked badge appears anywhere — object heading, node heading, record-type scope heading, or table-of-contents entry
- [ ] The toolbar has **Find** and **Expand/Collapse all** only; the **Status** select is gone
- [ ] A combination row renders exactly three things: controlling value, `unlocks`, and the collapsible `must not unlock`
- [ ] `Reveal in Explorer` on a field still works; `Copy combination reference` and the deep-link paste-to-focus flow still work
- [ ] There is no "Open spec method" and no "Open run report" button on any row

### Results code is gone from the Explorer service

- [ ] `loadLatestResults`, `findLatestResultsFilePath`, `getResultsFileName`, `getResultsFolderTimestamp`, `parseFailureLines`, `extractFailureMessageForControllingValue`, `applyFailuresToNodes`, `buildUnattributedFailureMessage`, `buildFailureTriage`, `buildFailureTriageByKind`, `buildFailureDetailViewModel`, `resolveRunReportFilePath`, `findApexMethodDeclarationLineNumber`, `findRunReportEntryLineNumber`, `buildOpenTargetKey`, `collectOpenableSpecTargets` and `collectOpenableRunReportTargets` are removed
- [ ] `IPicklistDependencyResultsFile`, `IPicklistDependencyResultsLoad`, `IPicklistDependencyResultsMethodOutcome`, `IParsedPicklistDependencyFailure`, `IPicklistDependencyFailureTriage` and `IPicklistDependencyFailureDetailViewModel` are removed
- [ ] `status`, `failures`, `fieldLevelFailures`, `runSummary`, `runLoadMessage` and `failureTriageByKind` are gone from the view model interfaces
- [ ] `openPicklistDependencyExplorer` no longer joins `ConfigurationService.getPicklistDependencyResultsFolderPath()` and no longer registers `openSpecMethod` / `openRunReport` message handlers
- [ ] `grep -rn "loadLatestResults\|openRunReport\|openSpecMethod" src/` returns nothing outside `PicklistDependencyCheckService`

### Invariants that must be restated, not silently dropped

- [ ] `applyModelLimits` / `applyTotalCombinationBudget` no longer prefer failing rows over passing ones (there is no status to prefer by) — the ordering rule that replaces it is deterministic, documented, and asserted by a test
- [ ] The dropped-row truncation notice still names what was dropped and still points at the objects it came from; a dropped row stays **absent and counted**, never re-labelled
- [ ] `resolveOpenableManifestFilePath` is still applied to every manifest path the host opens; if `generatedClassFilePath` no longer reaches an openable action, it is removed from the context rather than left as an unguarded string
- [ ] No metadata value is interpolated into `buildWebviewShellHtml`; every node is still written via `createElement`/`textContent`
- [ ] `renderPanelGuarded`, the `rendered` ack, the `window` error listener and the `render` vs `runtime` failure distinction are unchanged
- [ ] The load-phase banner, `yieldToExtensionHost` phase reporting, and the `checkFreshness` button with its five freshness states (`notChecked` / `pendingCheck` / `checkFailed` / stale / fresh) are unchanged — freshness is about metadata, not about a run

### Build & test

- [ ] Tests added/updated in `PicklistDependencyExplorerService/tests/` and `ExtensionCommandService/tests/`; run-results tests are deleted rather than skipped
- [ ] `npm run compile` — zero TypeScript errors
- [ ] `npm run lint` — zero ESLint errors
- [ ] `npm run jest-test` — all pass, coverage does not regress
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` gets a `3.17.0` entry; `package.json` version bumped to match

## Affected Areas

| Area | File(s) | Change Type |
|---|---|---|
| Explorer view model + panel script | `src/treecipe/src/PicklistDependencyExplorerService/PicklistDependencyExplorerService.ts` | Modify (large removal) |
| Explorer tests | `src/treecipe/src/PicklistDependencyExplorerService/tests/` | Modify/Delete |
| Command wiring + message handlers | `src/treecipe/src/ExtensionCommandService/ExtensionCommandService.ts` | Modify |
| Command tests | `src/treecipe/src/ExtensionCommandService/tests/ExtensionCommandService.test.ts` | Modify |
| Architecture bullets that assert run behavior | `CLAUDE.md` | Modify |
| Explorer feature description | `README.md` | Modify |
| Version history | `CHANGELOG.md`, `package.json` | Modify |

## Out of Scope

- `treecipe

sample.title: A filed brief lands in the column its classification already decides
sample.body:
Every brief lands in one column and a person sorts them afterwards. On this deployment that sorting has a rule, the rule is almost entirely mechanical, and the sync branch already holds everything it needs to apply it -- so the work is being done by hand for no reason, and a hand that forgets is a brief in the wrong place.

WHAT THE BRANCH ALREADY HAS. The payload reaches it whole: it reads the category out of it to write a label and five board fields (templates/scripts/github.sh:512 onward), and it writes one searchable marker per path. Category and paths are the whole input the rule needs. It also already decides a column -- STATUS_OPTION at templates/scripts/github.sh:320 -- and already sets it only where it finds the field empty (templates/scripts/github.sh:617-626), so it puts an item into a column once and never moves it between columns.

THE RULE IS THREE LINES. Where any of a brief's paths is one this target reads as text an agent or a script author consumes, the brief lands in the column a person reviews. Otherwise, where its category is one this target reads as wrong-today or needs-reading, it lands in that same column. Otherwise it lands in the deferred column. Ordering matters and the override comes first, which is what makes a documentation drift in an agent-facing file reviewable while the same category elsewhere defers.

THIS IS ROUTING AND NOT A VERDICT, which is the distinction that makes it safe to decide at filing time. A judgement stamped on a brief goes stale and nothing revisits it; a column is current state, corrected by dragging, leaving no record to contradict. The branch decides only where a brief *starts*, and the existing empty-status rule guarantees it never revisits that decision.

It is also conservative in the right direction. Everything agent-facing and everything wrong-today lands where it is seen; only the categories whose cost of waiting is flat land deferred. The failure mode is a fuller review column, not a buried finding.

IT MUST NOT TRAVEL, AND THE SHAPE THAT GUARANTEES THAT IS FORCED ANYWAY. Which categories defer, which paths override, and what the two columns are called are this target's judgements and belong in the installed copy alone. A standing test holds .harness/scripts/github.sh to differing from templates/scripts/github.sh only in lines that are constant assignments at the top, with a control that plants a non-constant difference and requires it reported -- so the deciding lives in the template and the four inputs are constants, each a single assignment whose value is data. A template shipping an empty deferred column means route nothing: every brief lands in the column the target already names, which is exactly today's behaviour, so no target inherits this deployment's triage.

WHAT STAYS MANUAL is the one thing no field decides: telling a weak error message from a real silent failure inside one category. Those route to the review column rather than being guessed at, and they are a handful.

Tests may not write this target's values down. story-134 established that the board values a test asserts against are read out of the installed script rather than written into the suite, with a standing guard that scans for one written down and is shown to catch a planted one. The categories, the path prefixes and the two column names are such values, so the guard has to see them and the drive has to read them from the copy it drives -- including a copy declaring invented categories and columns, routed onto the columns that copy declares.

Severity 2: nothing is broken, and what this pays for is every filing from here on, which on a deployment filing roughly three briefs per story is a recurring cost rather than a one-time one. Confidence high -- the branch's inputs, its existing column decision and the empty-status rule were read rather than recalled, and the rule was derived from a hand triage of 108 briefs before it was proposed as a mechanism.

sample.title: 🐛 A hive that heartbeats without a git_hash is invisible to the upgrade path and to the operator
sample.body:
## The gap

The hub decides whether to instruct an upgrade by comparing the hive's reported `git_hash` against the branch target. When a spoke heartbeats but reports **no** `git_hash`, that comparison cannot run, so the hub issues no instruction - and the hive silently stops receiving upgrades while continuing to look online.

Nothing detects this. The row keeps a stale version from the last good report, the hive counts as online because beats are arriving, and no drift signal fires.

## Two hives were in this state tonight, for hours

**`llm-d/llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler`** (ns `hive-hosted-hosted-llm-d-llm-d-worklo-wva1`). Its pod was `1/1 Running` and the hub logged its heartbeat every 120s, but measured in its own logs:

```
104  proxy client request read timed out
34   hub heartbeat collect timed out
0    successful heartbeat collections
```

It was sending last-good cached stats marked stale, with no version. It ran digest `14c75aa0` while `:stable` was `ef5a603a`, and the hub sent it no upgrade instruction at all. The dashboard showed a stale "Upgrade failed" with nothing actually retrying behind it. A `rollout restart` recovered it.

**`katamari/ibm-aiops-orchestrator`** (ns `hive-hosted-hosted-available-vllmd-01`) sat at "No heartbeat for 8h29m" and "Upgrading 29m" simultaneously - contradictory states that were both stale, because the hub had no fresh version to update the row with. Root cause there was #6024, but the *invisibility* is this issue.

## Why it matters beyond those two

The condition is indistinguishable from health on every surface an operator looks at. A hive can sit arbitrarily far behind, never be told to upgrade, and never raise an alert, provided it keeps beating. Tonight the fleet went from 41 failed upgrades to 0, and these two were the residue precisely because they were not *failing* - they were mute.

## Suggested detector

A drift signal for "heartbeat received, version absent", fired after N consecutive beats with an empty `git_hash`. It belongs next to `DriftKindStatusFlipping` and `DriftKindDuplicateSpoke` in `src/pkg/hub/drift.go` - same family: the row cannot be trusted, and the reason is knowable.

Cheap to compute (the hub already has both the beat and the field), and it would have surfaced both hives within minutes rather than hours.

Worth pairing with a spoke-side improvement: the spoke knows its own version and knows its stats collection timed out. Sending the version even on the degraded path - it is a static string, not a collected stat - would close the hole from the other side.

## Related

- #6024 - katamari's config trap, the cause of its particular silence
- #6003 - the iptables defect that put the autoscaler into its degraded state
- #5994 - the fleet upgrade recovery these two survived as residue

sample.title: feat(orchestrator): V3 — persistent execution engine, retries and recovery
sample.body:
# V3 — Execution Engine, persistência, retries e recovery

## Objetivo

Transformar o Task Graph da V2 em um **execution engine persistente e resiliente**.

A V3 deve permitir que o orchestrator não apenas planeje tarefas, mas também mantenha o estado da execução, despache agentes, registre resultados, detecte falhas, faça retries controlados, retome workflows interrompidos e encaminhe problemas que não possam ser resolvidos automaticamente para intervenção humana.

O objetivo não é criar infraestrutura distribuída sofisticada. O objetivo é criar um executor confiável usando a infraestrutura mínima necessária.

## Dependência

Depende de **#161 — V2 Task Graph, DAG e Scheduler**, que por sua vez depende de **#160 — V1**.

## Arquitetura alvo

```text
Task Graph
    ↓
Persistent Scheduler
    ↓
Dispatcher
    ↓
Agent Run
    ↓
Evidence
    ↓
Verification
    ├── PASS → próxima task
    ├── FAIL → Failure Classifier
    │             ├── RETRY
    │             ├── FIX TASK
    │             └── HUMAN
    └── BLOCKED → HUMAN
```

## Escopo

### 1. Persistência do workflow

Introduzir armazenamento persistente para o estado do orchestrator.

O estado mínimo deve representar:

- workflow;
- issue de origem;
- tasks;
- dependências;
- estado de cada task;
- agent runs;
- evidências;
- verificações;
- tentativas;
- falhas;
- decisões de escalonamento;
- timestamps.

Como o projeto já utiliza PostgreSQL como source of truth, avaliar primeiro o uso do próprio PostgreSQL. Não introduzir Redis/Kafka/RabbitMQ/SQS apenas para fila ou estado.

### 2. Workflow Run

Criar identidade persistente para cada execução:

```text
workflowRunId
issueNumber
workflowVersion
status
startedAt
finishedAt
currentState
```

O workflow deve sobreviver ao encerramento do processo que o iniciou.

### 3. Task persistence

Persistir as transições de estado das tasks.

Exemplo:

```text
PENDING
  ↓
READY
  ↓
RUNNING
  ↓
PASS
```

ou:

```text
RUNNING
  ↓
FAIL
  ↓
RETRYING
  ↓
RUNNING
```

Toda transição importante deve ser auditável.

### 4. Agent Run

Cada execução de agente deve ter registro independente contendo:

- task;
- agent type/role;
- início/fim;
- status;
- tentativa;
- prompt/context reference;
- resultado;
- output/evidence reference;
- tokens de entrada/saída quando disponíveis;
- duração;
- erro, se houver.

Não armazenar indiscriminadamente grandes volumes de prompt/output se isso criar custo ou risco desnecessário. O modelo deve permitir referências a artefatos quando apropriado.

### 5. Dispatcher

Implementar dispatcher responsável por pegar tasks `READY` e criar/executar agent runs de acordo com o contrato da V2.

O dispatcher deve respeitar:

- dependências;
- parallelism policy;
- allowed paths;
- role;
- token budget;
- limites de retry;
- gates arquiteturais;
- estado atual do workflow.

### 6. Retry policy

Implementar política explícita de retry.

Cada falha deve ser classificada antes de repetir.

Exemplos:

```text
TRANSIENT_PROVIDER_ERROR → retry
TEST_FAILURE             → diagnosis/fix
TYPE_ERROR               → diagnosis/fix
LINT_FAILURE             → diagnosis/fix
MISSING_CONTEXT          → context expansion / retry
ARCHITECTURE_VIOLATION  → human
UNKNOWN                  → human
```

Não permitir retries infinitos.

Configurar limite por task/workflow e registrar a razão de cada retry.

### 7. Failure classifier

Criar componente determinístico sempre que possível para classificar falhas conhecidas.

A classificação deve considerar:

- comando que falhou;
- exit code;
- output relevante;
- tipo da task;
- evidência produzida;
- regras de segurança/arquitetura.

Falhas desconhecidas devem ser escaladas, não mascaradas.

### 8. Recovery

O workflow deve conseguir recuperar de interrupções do processo.

Exemplo:

```text
Agent RUNNING
    ↓
process crash
    ↓
workflow restart
    ↓
identify stale run
    ↓
reconcile state
    ↓
retry/requeue safely
```

Implementar mecanismo de lease/heartbeat ou equivalente para detectar execução abandonada.

### 9. Idempotência

Operações de scheduler/dispatcher devem ser projetadas para evitar execução duplicada acidental quando o processo reiniciar.

Exemplos importantes:

- não iniciar duas execuções da mesma task por race;
- não duplicar evidências finais;
- não criar retries além do limite;
- não perder uma task ao atualizar estado.

### 10. Verification como gate real

Uma task não deve ser considerada `PASS` apenas porque o agente terminou.

O estado `PASS` deve depender de verification definida no Task Graph.

Exemplo:

```text
Agent completed
     ↓
verification
     ↓
PASS / FAIL
```

### 11. Token budget

Implementar orçamento de tokens por workflow e task.

Exemplo:

```text
workflow budget = 120k

planning       = 10k
implementation= 45k
testing        = 20k
verification   = 15k
recovery       = 30k
```

Quando o orçamento for excedido ou estiver próximo do limite, o sistema deve impedir loops caros e aplicar política definida:

- reduzir contexto;
- limitar retry;
- mudar estratégia;
- escalar para humano.

A implementação não deve ficar acoplada a um único provider.

### 12. State machine

Formalizar a máquina de estados do workflow:

```text
READY
  ↓
PLANNING
  ↓
IMPLEMENTING
  ↓
TESTING
  ↓
REVIEWING
  ↓
VERIFYING
  ├── PASS → DONE
  ├── FAIL → IMPLEMENTING
  └── BLOCKED → HUMAN
```

As transições inválidas devem ser rejeitadas.

### 13. Observabilidade operacional

Fornecer consultas/saídas para descobrir:

- workflows em execução;
- tasks bloqueadas;
- tasks stale;
- retries;
- falhas por categoria;
- custo/token usage;
- tempo por etapa;
- taxa de sucesso;
- intervenções humanas.

## Fora de escopo

- GitHub webhook/event-driven lifecycle completo;
- merge automático de PR;
- sistema de agentes distribuídos;
- Kubernetes;
- Redis/Kafka/RabbitMQ/SQS;
- microservices;
- AWS/Terraform sem ADR;
- autonomia irrestrita.

Esses pontos pertencem à V4 ou exigem decisão arquitetural separada.

## Critérios de aceite

- [ ] Workflow e tasks possu

sample.title: docs: reconcile v0-spec, the design skill, and tech-stack with the read view
sample.body:
> Epic: #157
> Depends on: #159, #162

## Goal

Correct the four project documents that the read view makes false. Each currently asserts something
the epic reverses, and a reviewer reading them would flag the shipped code as a violation.

## Context

- **Why this is its own slice:** the four files are edited by no other child, so a dedicated slice
  keeps three parallel siblings out of `doc/`. It runs last because it must describe what actually
  landed — including whether #159's deferred inner-language code highlighting stayed deferred.
- **Design spec:** `.agents/specs/2026-09-10-read-view.md` § *Documents Amended Outside the
  Glossary*. The glossary itself (`.agents/ubiquitous-language.md`) was **already updated** by the
  `/grill` session — do not re-edit it, only check it matches what shipped.
- **Precedent:** issue #147 did exactly this for the unified-sidebar epic.

## Affected Files

| Action | File Path | Purpose |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| MODIFY | `doc/v0-spec.md` | §5.1 and §5.6 — the preview is built; typeface and wikilink rules changed |
| MODIFY | `.agents/skills/acidanthera-design/SKILL.md` | Typeface rule, ember list, stale chrome-strip line |
| MODIFY | `doc/tech-stack.md` | Two promoted dependencies |
| MODIFY | `README.md` | Only if it describes the viewer as edit-only |

## Step-by-Step Implementation

**Step 1 — `doc/v0-spec.md`**

- **§5.1** currently ends *"Accepted cost: building preview/toolbar by hand."* That cost is now
  paid for the preview half. Rewrite to describe the **read view** as shipped: the two buffer
  views, the chrome-strip toggle, `Ctrl-w e`, and the walker over `@lezer/markdown` (cite ADR 0039).
  Say plainly that the toolbar half remains unbuilt.
- **§5.6** contains two sentences that are now wrong:
  - *"JetBrains Mono for content"* → sharpen to the rule the epic settled: **mono is for source,
    sans is for rendered prose**. Mono keeps metadata and code blocks.
  - *"inline `[[wikilinks]]` render via the `Wikilink` component (underline + hover, no color)"* →
    replace with the three link states and cite ADR 0040: resolving links are ember and navigable
    in **both** views; missing or ambiguous ones are muted and struck through.
- **§2 / §5.5** — add nothing. The read view is not a new deferral and introduces no new keyboard
  rule beyond one chord.

**Step 2 — `.agents/skills/acidanthera-design/SKILL.md`**

Three corrections:
- *"JetBrains Mono is for document content and metadata"* → the source/rendered-prose split from
  Step 1. Also note the ~680px prose measure and that headings stay capped at 500 in the read view.
- The **permitted-ember list** — add a resolving wikilink, citing ADR 0040, and state the boundary:
  a missing or ambiguous link gets no ember. Keep the existing entries.
- *"[the 40px chrome strip] carries no state and no controls (ADRs 0009, 0035)"* — **already stale
  before this epic**: ADR 0037 admitted view-scoped controls and the navigation-history pair
  shipped in #155. Correct it to the current rule and name both controls that now live there.
- Also correct the `src/components/ui/` inventory line if `Segmented`'s description mentions an
  accent active state, which #158 removed.

**Step 3 — `doc/tech-stack.md`**

- Add `@lezer/markdown` and `@lezer/common` to the frontend runtime-dependency table with the
  versions #159 pinned and a one-line role (`markdown parser + tree types behind the read view's
  walker`).
- Update the *"What each directory is built with"* row for `lib/editor/` to mention the walker.
- Update the snapshot date at the top of the file.

**Step 4 — `README.md`**

- Check whether it describes the viewer as an editor only, or lists features the read view changes.
  Update if so; if it needs no change, say so in the PR description rather than editing it.

**Step 5 — Verify the glossary matches what shipped**

- Read `.agents/ubiquitous-language.md`'s *buffer view*, *read view*, *markdown walker*, *note
  header block*, *wikilink resolution* and *view toggle* rows against the merged code.
- **Remove the two "settled ahead of implementation" markers** — one above the *Editor session*

sample.title: feat(fleet): export and verify bounded build source snapshots
sample.body:
A subordinate Fleet build must receive the exact eligible working source, including uncommitted and untracked changes. The existing dirty-worktree snapshot records recovery digests; it does not provide a complete transferable artifact with independent restore verification. This is the bounded Hephaestus snapshot dependency of HomericIntelligence/Agamemnon#508.

Implement a deterministic regular-file source export and checked restore. Bind the canonical manifest to the base commit, policy digest, file paths/modes/content hashes and positive member/byte counts. Match the Agamemnon commitment fields `reference`, `manifestDigest`, `baseCommit`, `members`, `bytes`, and `policyDigest`; treat submitted metadata as untrusted until actual bytes pass verification.

Include tracked working content, deletions and eligible untracked files. Exclude Git administration, declared private runtime roots and credential paths. The first profile rejects symbolic links, submodules, hard links, unsafe paths and special files. Use bounded reads, source-race checks and new private destinations without overwriting caller data. Reuse existing safe Git capture where applicable; preserve current recovery snapshot semantics.

Acceptance uses real temporary Git repositories and artifacts: exact dirty-source round trip and modes, deterministic output, exclusions, positive controls paired with unsafe/corrupt input rejection, count/byte/deadline bounds and source mutation detection. Obtain independent RED before implementation and focused GREEN plus static checks afterward.

This issue does not add a scheduler, executor, model call, network fetch, build authority, or changes to the existing contained-runtime candidate. Fixed-recipe/run-grant execution, transport, cleanup, output/receipt collection, stale-source comparison, MCP/BuildTestJob wiring and full CI remain separate gates.

The opportunity detail layout section of `content/docs/sales/opportunities.mdx` carries:

- The five buttons that do exist on this screen are the header's: `generate_quote`, `clone_opportunity`, `log_call`, `log_meeting`, `schedule_meeting`. None of them adds a line item.

So the bullet promises a control that is on no surface of the app. The sibling claim on the same list — the *Quote* related list's **Generate Quote** button — was corrected by #1709, because the button is real and merely in the wrong place; this one has nowhere to be moved to.

Deleting the clause is the conservative half, and it is not the whole job: **Line items — what's actually being sold** further up the same page tells a reader "Each opportunity can have line items", so the page owes them the real route to adding one, or an honest statement that there is not one on this screen today. sample.title: Shell completion framework for Rune terminals with composable providers
sample.body:
Add IRIS/Fig-style smart completions for shells running in Rune's terminal (vte) primary buffer, as a new package with a well-defined provider interface so multiple completion sources compose from user config.

The vte already owns the two hard parts: extracting the current prompt line and cursor, and writing programmatically back into the pty. What is missing is the spec sources and the suggestion UI.

## Proposed API

```go
type Match struct {
    Insert      string  // written to the pty on accept
    Display     string  // menu label; defaults to Insert
    Description string  // right-column doc (man text, AI rationale)
    Source      string  // provider id: "man", "ai", ...
    Kind        Kind    // flag | subcommand | argument | ai | history
    Score       float64 // provider-relative rank hint
}

type Request struct {
    Line   string            // prompt line text
    Cursor int               // shell cursor offset within Line
    Token  string            // token under cursor (derived)
    Dir    workspaceapi.URI  // terminal cwd
}

type Completer interface {
    Complete(ctx context.Context, req Request) iterator.Iterator[Match]
}
```

`Multi(completers ...Completer) Completer` fans providers in concurrently so a fast provider (cached man pages) streams into the menu while a slow one (AI) trickles in. Sequential aggregation is not sufficient: AI latency must not gate man results.

## Providers

- **man**: runs documentation, never the target binary. Resolves and reads the man page through the workspace executor, so completions describe the executor host's binaries and stay correct over SSH. Parses `OPTIONS`/`SYNOPSIS` entries into matches, with an LRU cache keyed by command. A `--help` fallback is opt-in and guarded: PATH-resolved commands only, never relative paths, stdin from `/dev/null`, timeout, output cap.
- **ai**: one completion request with line, cursor and cwd context, parsing newline-delimited suggestions, aborting on context cancellation when the menu is dismissed.

## Prompt detection

Prompt location should be abstracted behind a locator interface with the current heuristic as the default implementation and a first-ok-wins fallback chain. That lets an OSC 133 prompt-mark implementation be prepended later so both the vi overlay and completions upgrade with no call-site changes. This issue does not depend on that work; the relationship is plug-in, not prerequisite.

## Where to look

- `internal/term/vte/utils.go` - prompt-line extraction.
- `internal/term/vte/remote.go` - the pty write path used to insert an accepted completion.
- `internal/term/vte/handler.go` - vi-mode event routing and draw swap, the model for routing keys to an active menu.
- `internal/term/vte/component.go` - alt-buffer check; completions are primary-buffer only.
- `internal/term/vte/config.go` - the `CommandExpander` field is the precedent for injecting an IDE-layer callback into the vte.
- `internal/handler/search/list.go` - the suggestion list UI.
- `internal/ide/ideshell/handler.go` - the pattern for feeding a streaming iterator into a `search.List` off the event loop.
- `internal/ide/idelsp/lspcmd/complete.go` - cursor-anchored floating window placement.
- `internal/ide/config.go` - where a `terminal.completer` config section would be parsed and validated.

## Config sketch

Under `terminal.completer`: `enabled` (default false), `key` (default `<c-space>`), `providers` (ordered, default `["man"]`, `"ai"` opt-in), `man.help_fallback` (default false), `ai.model`, `max_results`. Invalid provider names and an enabled `ai` provider without a resolvable model should be reported as config errors rather than guarded at runtime.

sample.title: fix(experiment): reconcile deferred launch handoffs and inconclusive gates
sample.body:
## Problem

Deferred experiment issues still prescribe launch steps that the current authoring surface rejects, while the multi-production comparison procedure omits the canonical `INCONCLUSIVE` gate outcome. Following these handoffs can stop before authorship or assign judgment to the coordinator rather than an independent reviewer.

This is a post-#2406 readiness finding at master `d9307ed0ab5998d939c64984d12c89c08fcc5ac1`, not a request to launch a benchmark or reopen the completed implementation issues.

## Evidence

Static reproduction: read the operative bodies of #1825 and #1954 beside these current owners. No local product command, agent experiment, or render was executed.

| Handoff | Current contradiction |
| --- | --- |
| #1825 and the four #1954 creation commands omit `--language` | `readExperimentalArguments` in `build/experimental.ts` refuses creation without an explicit supported language before packing |
| #1825 says the generator prints `codex mcp add` and resumes `--last` | `runExperimental` prints ordinary project entry; `.agents/skills/experiment/SKILL.md` uses the exact session UUID and no AutoMovie tool server |
| #1954 names four shipped skills and `{ environments, models }` | The scaffold has five routed skills; `source-authoring/compilation.md` describes `{ environments, models, contexts }` and branch-specific ownership |
| #1954 assigns final cross-work judgment to the coordinator | `comparison.md` assigns it to an independent cross-work reviewer and explicitly excludes coordinator judgment |
| #1954 requires a blank production's argument-free preview to reach GPU | `readAutoMoviePreviewArguments` requires a real shot; captures require authored, current compiled targets. Library work remains shot-free |
| `comparison.md` role, gate paragraph, and known-failure row allow only PASS/FAIL | `records.md#calibrate-judgment-before-production-review` requires PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE, calibrated independent judgment, and escalation |

These are AutoMovie-owned instructions and API-use contradictions. External libraries, especially `@ttsc/evidence`, are trusted and outside verification scope. The initial suspicion that `packages/engine/src/subject.ts` was missing was disproved; preserve that existing subject API.

## Consequence surface and approach

Reconcile a proposed launch or resume with current canonical owners before freezing its next run. Preserve prior run identity, observations, limitations, and historical comments. A changed harness needs a successor rather than silently refreshing an old frozen run. Keep each issue's subject, model, driver, input links, and launch-authorization boundary.

Let `records.md` own this reconciliation and missing-record refusal; make the comparison caller handle INCONCLUSIVE without treating uncertainty as either PASS or a writer repair verdict. Update the operative #1825/#1954 bodies, replacing stale instructions with canonical routes rather than maintaining another copied command/observation contract.

## Scope

| Layer | Obligation |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/requirements` | No new product promise. Consume existing agent-authoring language/project ownership and review subject-inspection requirements; no edit expected |
| `docs/specifications` | No new system behavior. Consume existing authoring language/source authority and subject-inspection specifications; no edit expected |
| `packages/*` | Existing CLI/template/production logic is the evidence, not a change target; no public export or citation change |
| Sandbox engine surface | No new bridge, API, or tool server; retain ordinary project scripts and current library owners |
| `packages/template/scaffold/.agents/skills` | Consume the existing five routers and compilation/review contracts; do not duplicate or edit them without a separately proved defect |
| Tests | Manual handoff matrix and negative twins; no source-shape test or generated fixture. Executable logic is unchanged |
| Repository experiment instructions | `records.md` owns launch-record reconciliation and calibration; `comparison.md` consumes every verdict |
| GitHub issue bodies | Correct #1825/#1954 current handoffs while preserving historical observations, all four building inputs, fixed models, and no-launch status |
| CI and evidence configuration | Unchanged; rely on normal exact-head remote CI, no new validator |

## Acceptance and verification

- New sandbox instructions select a supported language; refresh preserves the existing language and frozen-generation boundaries.
- No operative instruction requires an AutoMovie MCP server or a recency-selected session; existing historical MCP observations remain history.
- Five shipped skill routes, library source ownership, and authored-target capture prerequisites are discoverable through canonical owners.
- PASS advances the submitted gate, FAIL returns the complete repair batch, INCONCLUSIVE leaves it unpassed and follows recorded escalation. Missing calibration never becomes ready through a coordinator verdict.
- A fresh launch fills the current campaign record before execution; an old incomplete run remains incomplete/inconclusive, never retroactively calibrated. Unknown actual fields are not copied from planned values.
- #1954 is still not launched; #1825 retains its historical executions. Input benchmark issues are not falsely closed. `wrtnlabs/interia#79` is not edited under this repository task.
- Perform two consecutive clean instruction-diff reviews with detailed PR COMMENT records; inspect rendered GitHub bodies and links; run `git diff --check`. This Markdown-only change follows the pull-request skill's formatter exception. Local tests/builds/install/benchmark/render are forbidden by the user; all build/test execution is remote CI only.

## Coordination

Discovered in two fresh whole-scope rounds after #2406; this issue has no unresolved implementation dependency. #2363 owns the readiness campaign. #1954 and #1825 own future experiment execution, not this

sample.title: [upstream][pi-mcp-adapter 2.29.0] Pin the MCP adapter runtime and eliminate dual mutable resolution
sample.body:
## Status / recommendation

**COMPAT-FIX.** Establish one Core-owned, reproducible `pi-mcp-adapter` version authority before treating current adapter behavior as a stable XTRM runtime contract.

This is not a generic dependency-bump request. Current Core has **two independently mutable resolution paths** for a runtime-critical MCP adapter:

1. `cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts` manages `npm:pi-mcp-adapter` as a required Pi package and defines “expected” as the current npm registry version at `xt update`/doctor time.
2. `.xtrm/config/pi.mcp.json` launches `npx -y pi-mcp-adapter ...` for `deepwiki` and `github-grep`, with no version qualifier, so server startup can resolve a different/latest adapter independently of the installed Pi-managed copy and independently of any Core commit.

The newly observed `2.28.0`/`2.29.0` releases make that source-identity defect material because the adapter now changes MCP recovery, OAuth credential concurrency, initialization, tool-catalog and host behavior across releases.

## Upstream release identity

### `v2.29.0`

- Upstream: `nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter`
- Package: `pi-mcp-adapter`
- Published: **2026-08-26T19:57:42Z**
- Primary evidence: https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter/releases/tag/v2.29.0
- Relevant delta:
  - opt-in Parallel Search setup preset;
  - non-TUI status rendering now tolerates hosts whose theme is a plain value rather than styling methods.

The specific `2.29.0` feature set does not itself require XTRM adoption. Its publication exposes that live Core runtime identity can advance without a Core source change.

### Recovery evidence: `v2.28.0`

- Published: **2026-08-26T05:29:54Z**
- Primary evidence: https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter/releases/tag/v2.28.0
- Compare: https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter/compare/v2.27.0...v2.28.0
- This release was recovered because `pi-mcp-adapter` was absent from the release-watch dependency map although current Core executes it.

Material `2.28.0` runtime changes include:

- transient MCP 503 recovery/backoff and preservation of valid cached catalogs;
- retry after failed first initialization instead of a permanently stuck session;
- removal of failed/backing-off servers from advertised direct/gateway tools;
- OAuth invalidation protection so a stale process cannot delete credentials replaced by another Pi process;
- versioned cross-extension runtime MCP registration;
- optional strict advertised-schema validation for direct tools;
- progress forwarding for proxy calls;
- corrected stdio startup diagnostics and package-install/public-helper behavior.

The compare contains the implementation commits, including `a3072f6` (`Harden Pi MCP transient recovery (#411)`). These are lifecycle/security/availability changes, not release-note-only presentation changes.

## Current XTRM baseline

Observed on `xtrm-dev/core@main` commit `4b1a5933aff84c69bfc8a5443090897cd2593cf1`.

### Managed-package path

`cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts`:

- `MANAGED_PACKAGES` contains `{ id: 'npm:pi-mcp-adapter', ..., required: true }`;
- `getExpectedPiPackageVersion()` executes `npm view <package> version` against npmjs;
- `assureXtManagedPiPackages()` classifies any installed version unequal to current registry latest as outdated and invokes `pi install npm:pi-mcp-adapter`;
- `xt update --apply` runs this global package assurance once after repository reconciliation.

Therefore the source baseline has **no pinned adapter version or accepted range**. Its desired version is time-dependent npm `latest`.

`.xtrm/config/pi/install-schema.json` also lists `npm:pi-mcp-adapter`. `cli/test/pi-packages-parity.test.ts` explicitly permits it to be absent from `package.json` and settings because it is treated as a runtime-managed exception.

### Direct MCP-server launch path

`.xtrm/config/pi.mcp.json` is the canonical Pi MCP server source. It launches:

```text
deepwiki
  npx -y pi-mcp-adapter https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp

github-grep
  npx -y pi-mcp-adapter https://mcp.grep.app
```

`docs/mcp-servers.md` documents those entries as canonical and synchronized into project `.pi/mcp.json`.

Those commands do not reference the Pi-managed package copy and contain no immutable version. A clean start can therefore select a newer adapter than the one last assured by Core.

### Related implementation boundaries

- `scripts/patch-external-pi-tools.mjs` patches Serena/GitNexus behavior only. It does not establish adapter version identity.
- Core's managed package flow owns installation/update policy.
- The adapter owns MCP transport/lifecycle mechanics. It must not become XTRM workflow or authorization authority.

## Impact analysis

### What can change without a Core commit

Today, npm publication can change:

- remote MCP startup/retry behavior;
- direct/gateway tool advertisement;
- authentication/credential-refresh behavior;
- progress and metadata semantics;
- runtime extension registration;
- schema-validation behavior;
- non-TUI host behavior.

A later `xt update --apply` can also advance the Pi-managed package independently of an already-materialized `.pi/mcp.json` launch path.

### Reliability consequence

Two adapter versions can be relevant to one operator environment. Failure/recovery evidence can then be impossible to reproduce from the Core Git SHA alone. A reconnect, restart or clean install can silently change behavior.

### Security consequence

`2.28.0` fixes an OAuth concurrency race in which stale refresh/invalidation state could remove credentials written by another Pi process. XTRM must not accidentally regress such fixes through an uncontrolled second resolution path or rollback to an unrecorded version.

### Performance/operations consequence

Unversioned `npx` can add network/cache work at MCP process start. A single installed version authority should avoid duplicate fetch/resolution where practical and make offline/restart behavior deterministic.

### What remains unchanged

- Core remains owner of Pi runtime

sample.title: Read stdin in a child so the bridge ticks while an agent is idle
sample.body:
Implements the decision recorded on #131.

`App\Support\Bridge::run()` reads stdin directly and paces its periodic work on `stream_select()`'s timeout. On Windows that timeout never fires on a pipe, so the heartbeat, the renewal, and the feed follow only happen when the harness sends a frame -- and a harness sends nothing to an idle server for minutes at a time. Move the blocking read into a child process, and let the bridge select on a socket instead, where the timeout does fire.

## What to build

1. **A reader child.** Started by the bridge with `proc_open`, inheriting the bridge's own STDIN as descriptor 0. It does a blocking `fgets()` and writes each line, unmodified, to a socket.
2. **A loopback listener in the bridge.** Bound to `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port, accepting exactly one connection, refusing any peer that cannot name a per-process token.
3. **One select loop, over the socket.** `periodic()` keeps running at the end of every pass, exactly as it does now; what changes is that a pass now happens on a timeout as well as on data.

This runs on **every platform**, not only Windows. A second implementation of the read loop that only runs on one platform can diverge from the other silently, and the read loop is load-bearing.

## Three things the prototype already paid for

- **The token travels in the child's environment, never in argv.** Other processes on this machine can read a command line -- measured, 476 of 628 were readable -- and the repository already keeps credentials off argv for this reason.
- **The bridge must close its own copy of the child's socket end after spawning.** Otherwise EOF never arrives and the bridge cannot tell that the harness has gone.
- **The child's stderr must go somewhere readable.** A prototype that discarded it reported a silent, tickless success, and the cause was only visible once stderr went to a file. A child that cannot start looks exactly like a child with nothing to say.

Passing the socket to the child as a descriptor instead of using a loopback port **does not work on Windows** -- the child's write fails with `errno=9 Bad file descriptor`. It is recorded on #131 so that nobody spends an afternoon rediscovering it.

## What must not regress

- **Fragmented reads.** `Bridge::run()` buffers and splits on newlines because `stream_select` reports a stream readable when any bytes have arrived: a 200,065-byte `tools/call` once arrived as 24 fragments and every one was forwarded as its own malformed request. Whatever reads the socket keeps that property.
- **stdout carries only protocol.** #122 measured this byte-exactly, and the diagnostic path goes to stderr.
- **Shutdown.** The documented SIGTERM path still ends the session, and the suppressed `stream_select` warning that protects the protocol stream from a rendered exception still applies to the new loop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With stdin quiet, a tick fires and `periodic()` runs, asserted on both the ubuntu and the windows CI cells rather than on one.
- [ ] Whether the **pre-fix** loop ticked on POSIX is recorded, which answers what #131 left unmeasured: run the same assertion against the old loop on the ubuntu cell and say what it did.
- [ ] A heartbeat is sent while an agent is idle for longer than `HEARTBEAT_SECONDS`, and the session is not swept stale.
- [ ] A message split across several reads is forwarded as one message, with a test covering a payload larger than the socket buffer.
- [ ] When the harness closes stdin, the child exits, the bridge sees EOF, and the session is ended exactly once.
- [ ] The token does not appear in the child's command line, asserted by reading the child's own command line rather than by inspecting the code.
- [ ] A peer that connects to the listener without the token is refused, and the bridge keeps working.
- [ ] The listener binds `127.0.0.1` and not a routable address.
- [ ] No child outlives the bridge, including when the bridge is terminated rather than closed.
- [ ] stdout carries only protocol, as #122 measured.

## Notes

#124 records that the bridge processes nothing when stdin is a regular file rather than a pipe. This change moves the read into a child doing a blocking `fgets()`, which behaves differently on a regular file than the current non-blocking `stream_select` path does, so #124 should be re-tested against this rather than assumed to be unaffected -- in either direction.

## References

- [`app/Support/Bridge.php`](https://github.com/robot-council/cli/blob/main/app/Support/Bridge.php) -- `run()`, `periodic()`, and the fragmentation comment that explains the buffering.
- [`app/Support/FleetFollower.php`](https://github.com/robot-council/cli/blob/main/app/Support/FleetFollower.php) -- what stops being polled while a bridge cannot tick.
- #131 -- the measurements, the decision, and the rejected alternatives.

sample.title: PRD: sidecar-based agent context tool (working name: actx)
sample.body:
## Problem Statement

Company policy forbids agent context files (CLAUDE.md, .claude/, etc.) from landing in the code repo's restricted branches (develop/master), yet I want them versioned, shared with teammates, and present in every work-tree. My current solution (agit — a bare overlay repo driven through a zsh wrapper with GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE juggling) has three chronic failures: the wrapper itself is buggy; parallel feature development across git worktrees breaks (per-worktree index confusion, stale deploys, half-provisioned worktrees); and context files are invisible to the agent's search/@-mention because they are gitignored.

## Solution

A single-file POSIX shell tool (working name `actx`) that materializes a project's agent context from a **sidecar** — a normal git repo cloned anywhere outside the project — into the **code repo**'s work-trees via whole-directory symlinks, hides those paths from git via `info/exclude`, and makes them agent-visible via `additionalDirectories`. The sidecar is operated with plain git (no wrapping); the tool does only overlay mechanics. A clone is bound to its sidecar once (**attach**, recorded in a **pointer file** in the git common dir), after which every worktree — current and future, via a post-checkout hook — is **linked** automatically and uniformly.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want to attach a code-repo clone to a sidecar by path, so that the clone knows where its context lives without any global configuration.
2. As a developer, I want the attach to write the pointer file into the git common dir, so that all worktrees of the clone share the binding automatically.
3. As a developer, I want to run link in a work-tree and get symlinks for every top-level entry of the sidecar (excluding `.git`), so that the sidecar's contents are the sole declaration of what is materialized.
4. As a developer, I want link to register the linked paths in the code repo's `info/exclude` inside a fenced marker block, so that git never sees the context files and re-runs stay idempotent.
5. As a developer, I want link to merge the sidecar's absolute path into `additionalDirectories` in `.claude/settings.local.json`, so that the agent can read, search, and @-mention context files despite the exclude.
6. As a developer, I want attach to install a post-checkout hook (chaining any existing hook), so that a fresh `git worktree add` self-provisions with no command to remember.
7. As a developer, I want the hook to be fast and silent when the worktree is already linked, so that everyday git operations are not slowed or noisy.
8. As a developer, I want to edit a skill file in any worktree and have the change visible in all other worktrees instantly, so that context stays uniform across parallel features by construction.
9. As a developer, I want to commit/pull/push sidecar changes with plain git in the sidecar checkout, so that no wrapper can corrupt or hide version-control state.
10. As a developer, I want `path` to print the sidecar directory, so that I can `cd $(actx path)` or script against it.
11. As a developer, I want `status` to report dangling symlinks, unlinked worktrees, exclude-block drift, a missing/moved sidecar, and whether the sidecar checkout is dirty or behind its remote, so that I can spot a broken overlay at a glance.
12. As a developer, I want `unlink` to remove the symlinks, the exclude block, and the settings.local.json entry, so that I can cleanly detach a work-tree or the whole clone.
13. As a developer, I want all commands to be idempotent, so that re-running them repairs rather than duplicates state.
14. As a developer, I want clear errors and non-zero exit codes when I run a command outside a git work-tree, in an unattached clone, or against a missing sidecar, so that failures are diagnosable instead of silent.
15. As a developer, I want link to refuse to overwrite a real (non-symlink) file at a target path and tell me about the collision, so that existing local files are never destroyed.
16. As a developer working in a dev-container, I want the sidecar bind-mounted at the same absolute path inside the container, so that symlinks resolve and the tool works identically in and out of the container (no host-only restriction like agit).
17. As a teammate, I want onboarding to be: clone the sidecar, run attach + link, so that I get the full agent context in minutes without learning git plumbing.
18. As a teammate on a single project, I want that project's sidecar to be a separate repo, so that being granted access to it does not expose context of other projects.
19. As a release engineer, I want the context files untracked and excluded (worst case a forced add stages a symlink, not content), so that they cannot reach develop/master by accident.
20. As a developer, I want machine-local files (e.g. `settings.local.json`) to live untracked in the sidecar checkout under its own `.gitignore`, so that they are shared across my worktrees but never pushed.
21. As a developer, I want the tool to work when invoked from any subdirectory of a work-tree, so that I don't have to cd to the repo root.
22. As a future maintainer, I want the tool to be a single POSIX shell file with black-box tests, so that it is installable anywhere (host and containers) and safely modifiable.

## Implementation Decisions

Respect ADRs 0001–0007; glossary terms per CONTEXT.md (Sidecar, Code repo, Attach, Pointer file, Link).

- Single POSIX sh executable on PATH; no zsh-function installation; depends only on git + coreutils.
- Command surface: `attach <sidecar-path>`, `link [<worktree>]`, `unlink [<worktree>]`, `status`, `path`. No git passthrough, no wrapping of git subcommands (ADR-0007).
- Pointer file: a plain one-line file holding the sidecar's absolute path, stored in the code repo's git common dir; resolved via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` so worktrees inherit it (ADR-0004). No registry; no enumeration across projects.
- Link set: every top-level ent

`type:e2e`

druga próba → BLOCK

previousFailureId istnieje

memory w E1 → active
mutacja pliku

Dodatkowo wymagane są `tsc --noEmit` i zakończenie wszystkich trzech scenariuszy demo bez nieudanej asercji.

sample.title: state.db WAL split-brain inside a SINGLE process: apply_wal_with_fallback runs the set-pragma when the journal-mode probe fails (unlinks sibling connections -wal/-shm)
sample.body:
## Summary

`state.db` repeatedly corrupted with `btreeInitPage() returns error code 11`, and I was able to catch the machine in the pre-corruption state and pin it to a specific code path.

The novel part versus the existing WAL-split-brain reports: **this happened inside a single process, with no second writer anywhere on the box.** `apply_wal_with_fallback()` has an asymmetric guard — when the on-disk journal-mode probe fails, the configured-DELETE path refuses to act, but the configured-WAL path falls through and executes the `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` *set*, which unlinks the `-wal`/`-shm` pair that sibling connections **in the same process** still hold open.

Related, but distinct: #101064 (same orphaned-WAL symptom, attributed to gateway+dashboard multi-process, no code path identified), #102589 (POSIX-lock drop via cron lifecycle guard), #103339 (doctor/repair as second writer), #100896 (repeated corruption, `journal_mode=delete` containment).

## Environment

- hermes-agent `main` @ `21b2095d0`
- Python 3.11.15, SQLite **3.53.1** (`sqlite_source_id` 2026-05-05) — i.e. *not* WAL-reset-bug vulnerable; `is_sqlite_wal_reset_vulnerable()` returns `False`
- Ubuntu, ext4 on LVM, local disk, 22% full — not NFS/SMB/virtiofs
- `database.journal_mode: wal` (only key set under `database:`)
- Effective pragmas: `journal_mode=wal`, `synchronous=2` (FULL), `mmap_size=0`, `wal_autocheckpoint=1000`, `page_size=4096`
- Single gateway under a systemd **user** unit; no dashboard, no TUI, no second profile

## Observed evidence

Four minutes after a clean start of a freshly rebuilt, `integrity_check`-clean database:

```
process (only holder, verified with lsof — no other process had the db or sidecars open):
  fd 10 -> ~/.hermes/state.db-wal (deleted)   inode 6946859   4152 bytes of live journal data
  fd 11 -> ~/.hermes/state.db-shm (deleted)   inode 6946863
  fd 16,22,30 -> ~/.hermes/state.db-wal (deleted)  inode 6946859
  fd 9,15,19,21,23,24,27 -> ~/.hermes/state.db    inode 6946854

on disk at the same moment:
  ~/.hermes/state.db       inode 6946854
  ~/.hermes/state.db-wal   inode 6946861   0 bytes, mtime frozen
  ~/.hermes/state.db-shm   DOES NOT EXIST
```

So the live connections were journaling into an unlinked WAL/SHM pair while a different, empty WAL sat under the canonical name. Any connection opened after that point attaches to the on-disk pair. Two connection sets on two `-shm` files cannot see each other's locks — SQLite's whole locking and page-version protocol lives in the shared-memory index — so both sides believe they hold the write lock and both checkpoint into the same main database. That is the `btreeInitPage error 11` signature.

Nothing was logged when the sidecars were unlinked.

## Mechanism

`_on_disk_journal_mode()` (`hermes_state.py:1141`) returns `None` for **any** non-EIO `OperationalError` — `database is locked` included:

```python
except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
    last_exc = exc
    if "disk i/o error" not in str(exc).lower():
        return None          # <-- "database is locked" lands here
```

Connections to `state.db` are opened with `timeout=1.0` (`SessionDB._connect_and_init`, with the comment that application-level retry with jitter handles contention instead of SQLite's busy handler). Under load, a 1-second busy timeout is easy to lose, so the probe returns `None` fairly often on a busy gateway.

In `apply_wal_with_fallback()` the two configured modes then diverge:

**configured `delete` + unknown mode → refuses** (`hermes_state.py:1463-1476`):
```python
if configured == "delete":
    if current_mode is None:
        # ... Ownership is not provably exclusive, so flipping journal modes
        # here could destroy committed-but-uncheckpointed WAL transactions ...
        raise sqlite3.OperationalError(
            "could not verify journal mode before applying configured "
            "journal_mode=delete (database is locked — possible "
            "concurrent openers); refusing to downgrade a database "
            "this process does not exclusively own"
        )
```

**configured `wal` + unknown mode → no guard** (`hermes_state.py:1509`):
```python
row = conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL").fetchone()
```

`current_mode == "wal"` returns early on the safe path (read-only probe, no set-pragma). But `current_mode is None` skips that early return and reaches the set-pragma, which re-initialises WAL and unlinks the sidecars other connections still hold.

The hazard is already understood in the file — `apply_wal_with_fallback`'s own docstring says:

> Read-only probe — no flock, no checkpoint, no WAL/SHM unlink. **Skipping the set-pragma prevents WAL-init from unlinking files other connections hold open.**

The guard just doesn't cover the probe-failure case. And because the reasoning for the DELETE refusal ("ownership is not provably exclusive") applies equally to WAL, the asymmetry looks unintended rather than deliberate.

Note this makes the failure **load-dependent**, which matches what we saw: corruption appeared only during long, busy multi-turn sessions, never while idle.

To be explicit about what is observed vs. inferred: the orphaned-WAL/SHM state above is directly observed, in a single process, and `apply_wal_with_fallback` is the only place in `hermes_state.py` that issues the `journal_mode=WAL` set for `state.db` (lines 1509 and the retry at 1551). The probe returning `None` at that moment is inferred — the unlink is silent, so there is no log line proving it. A `logger.warning` on the `current_mode is None` branch would make this directly observable.

## Impact

Silent, recurring, data-losing corruption on a stock single-gateway install with default settings on a fully supported filesystem. In our case it recurred three times in one day, each time within hours of a repair — because repairing opens fresh connections and re-splits the brain. One table (`gateway_routing`) lost 3 of 33 rows; the rest was recoverable by dump-and-rebuild
