sample.title: [E13][cloud-sync] S3 — push roast: idempotent connector session (upsert + telemetry)
sample.body:
Part of #955 (E13 cloud sync). Depends on S1 + S2. Cloud deps: #430, #417, #431.

## S3 — push roast: idempotent connector session (upsert + telemetry)

Wire the one-session upload that shares a completed roast to the cloud, using
the already-present SQLite scaffolding (`sync_jobs`, `cloud_sync_status`,
`cloud_roast_id`, `public_slug`).

### Session (first sync), grounded in the live procs

1. **PUT** the roast's telemetry JSONL to `@roast_artifacts/<run_id>/` with
   **`AUTO_COMPRESS=FALSE`** and the **exact lowercase basename** the proc
   expects. Default `AUTO_COMPRESS=TRUE` appends `.gz` and the telemetry
   **silently fails to load** (matches neither `PATTERN` nor
   `METADATA$FILENAME`; masked by `-20007`) —
   `R__proc_upsert_roast.sql:112`, `R__proc_load_roast_telemetry.sql` residual.
2. `CALL upsert_roast(run_id, payload)` (payload from S2) → returns
   `{cloud_roast_id, public_slug}` (`R__proc_upsert_roast.sql:129-131`).
3. `CALL load_roast_telemetry(run_id, cloud_roast_id)` — server-side run/roast
   binding, `-20014` on mismatch (`R__proc_load_roast_telemetry.sql:80-92`).

plan.md §5 lists telemetry first, which is **not executable on a first sync**
(the roast id doesn't exist yet). Follow the resolved **cloud #430** contract
(run/roast binding + replay ordering), not the stale plan ordering.

### run_id grammar bridge (must-fix, or upsert fails `-20008`)

`upsert_roast` requires a **hyphenated canonical lowercase UUID**
`^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`
(`R__proc_upsert_roast.sql:171-173`, `-20008 "Run id must be a lowercase UUID"`).
The agent's `roast_runs.id` is `uuid.uuid4().hex` — **32 hex, no hyphens**
(`api.py:1991`, `store.py:87`). Insert hyphens to form the canonical UUID and
use that **same** string for the stage path, `upsert_roast`, and
`load_roast_telemetry` (`load`'s grammar `^[0-9a-zA-Z_-]{1,64}$` is broader and
would mask a mismatch — pin the hyphenated form everywhere).

### Idempotency / retry / fail-safe (scaffolding already exists)

- `run_id` = the roast's idempotency key; replays return the same
  `{cloud_roast_id, public_slug}`. Set `cloud_sync_status='synced'` and store
  `cloud_roast_id` / `public_slug` **only** after a result carrying
  `cloud_roast_id`.
- Drive retries through `sync_jobs` (`idempotency_key UNIQUE`, `attempts`,
  status `pending/in_flight/done/failed`, `store.py:196-205`) with exponential
  backoff; any connector error leaves the run `pending_sync`.
- A failed sync **never** changes the local roast outcome (roast_runs is
  immutable post-completion except the cloud/operator fields,
  `store.py:223-254`).

### Telemetry JSONL shape (verify, do not assume)

The MCP already writes `roast.jsonl` (paths in
`roast_runs.export_manifest_json` via `LogManifest`, `models.py:1257-1267`;
parsed by `replay.py:311-347`). **Verify its per-line record schema matches what
`load_roast_telemetry`'s INSERT-SELECT filters/reads** (record-kind filter,
field names) against the live gate; if it diverges, serialize a conforming JSONL
from `telemetry_snapshots` (`store.py:127-144`). An empty/malformed stage file
is indistinguishable from a telemetry-free roast (`-20007`).

### Security requirements

- Writes stay proc-mediated (no direct DML). Consent: honour
  `contributed_to_learning` (it gates the telemetry INSERT server-side).
- No secrets in logs; no roast metadata echoed on guard failures.
- Only Celsius, IP-free payloads (guaranteed by S2) ever leave the agent.

### Acceptance criteria

- End-to-end on `ROASTPILOT_DEV`: a completed roast pushes, the roast renders on
  its `/r/<public_slug>` page, telemetry rows land, and a **replay returns the
  identical `{cloud_roast_id, public_slug}`** (live-gated).
- run_id bridge verified against `-20008` (a raw `uuid4().hex` is rejected; the
  hyphenated form is accepted).
- Retry/backoff, `pending_sync` on failure, and "failed sync never changes local
  outcome" unit-tested (hardware-free).
- `ruff` / `pyright` / `pytest` green.

### Reviewers

`safety-reviewer` (credential-reachable write path) + standard floor.

sample.title: Restore in-app views so nav stops leaving the map app; restore COALITION_COLORS
sample.body:
## Problem

Tapping a nav item leaves the app. The site reads as a map plus a separate
document section, not as one product.

Measured: a tap on Politicians, Dewan, Bills, Sentiment or Projection is a full
document load — **118 KB of `app.js` and 51 KB of `styles.css` re-downloaded and
re-parsed**, map data re-fetched, and the map's zoom and seat selection
discarded. Returning to the map does it all again.

## Root cause

Commit `6c33e18` (#148) removed the in-app views, on the reasoning that #143 had
just repointed the nav at real static pages, leaving the in-app pairs
unreachable. It deleted:

- **five containers** from `frontend/public/index.html`:
  `#politicians-view`, `#dewan-view`, `#projection-view`, `#bills-view`,
  `#sentiment-view`
- **ten functions plus their listeners** from `frontend/public/app.js` (236
  lines): `openPoliticians`/`closePoliticians`, `openDewanPage`/`closeDewanPage`,
  `openBillsPage`/`closeBillsPage`, `openSentimentPage`/`closeSentimentPage`,
  `openProjectionPage`/`closeProjectionPage`

That reasoning was half right. Static pages *are* the correct entry point for
search and direct links. But the architecture was built to do **both** —
server-render for entry, hydrate for in-app navigation.
`politikku_bills.py:292` still states the contract in its own docstring:
*"the `#bills-view` contract `app.js` hydrates onto."* #148 deleted the
hydration half and kept only the static half.

## What survives

Almost all of the machinery is still in place. Only the switch that connected it
was removed.

| Piece | State |
| --- | --- |
| `renderPoliticiansDirectory`, `renderDewanPage`, `renderDewanRows`, `renderBillsPage`, `renderSentimentPage`, `renderProjectionPage` | **all present** in `app.js` |
| `POL_VIEW`, `DEWAN_VIEW`, `BILLS_VIEW`, `SENTIMENT_VIEW`, `PROJECTION_VIEW` constants | present, but resolve to `null` — their containers were deleted |
| body-class CSS: `.politicians-open` (16 rules), `.dewan-open` (12), `.bills-open` (12), `.sentiment-open` (12), `.projection-open` (10) | **all present** in `styles.css` |
| View ids emitted by the Python renderers | **still emitted** — `bills-view`, `dewan-view`, `pol-grid` |

**`git apply --reverse --check` on `6c33e18` passes cleanly against current
`main`**, for both files. The deleted code can be restored without conflict.

## Decision

**Restore the in-app views, and keep the static pages.** Navigation becomes
progressive enhancement:

- Nav items stay real anchors — `<a href="/politicians">` — so search engines,
  direct links, middle-click, and no-JS visitors all still get the
  server-rendered page. Wave 3's SEO work is unaffected.
- When `app.js` is loaded, it intercepts the click, calls `preventDefault()`,
  and opens the in-app view instead. The map stays mounted behind it.

This is the architecture the code was already written for. It is a restoration,
not a new design.

## Track A — restore hydration

**Files (exclusive):** `frontend/public/app.js`, `frontend/public/index.html`

1. **Restore what `6c33e18` deleted.** `git show 6c33e18` is the exact diff and
   it reverse-applies cleanly. Restore the five `<section>` containers in
   `index.html` and the ten functions plus their event listeners in `app.js`.
   Do **not** blind-revert the whole commit — read what comes back and confirm
   each restored call site still matches surrounding code that has changed since.
2. **Intercept nav clicks.** The five sidebar and topbar anchors currently
   perform a full navigation. When `app.js` is running, a plain left-click
   (no modifier key, no middle-click) calls `preventDefault()` and opens the
   matching in-app view. Modifier-clicks, middle-clicks and context-menu opens
   must keep working as real links — do not swallow them.
3. **Restore hash routing.** The deleted `open*` functions each pushed a hash
   (`history.pushState(null, "", "#politicians")`). Only one `#dewan` reference
   survives in `app.js` today. After the restore, confirm all five deep links
   work on a cold load and that Back closes the view rather than leaving the
   page.
4. **Do not delete the static pages or change any nav `href`.** They are the
   entry point and the no-JS fallback.

## Track B — restore `COALITION_COLORS`

**Files (exclusive):** `src/lpa/politikku_dewan.py`,
`src/lpa/politikku_politicians.py`

Issue #149 told a worker to retire `COALITION_COLORS`. **That instruction was
wrong.** It came from `design_handoff_politikku`'s "No party colours anywhere"
rule — a rule belonging to the navy/paper system ADR 0015 retires. The system
actually adopted says the opposite:

- `docs/design/mypolitik-new-views-spec.md:51` — *"`COALITION_COLORS` already
  defined in `frontend/public/lib.js:10-21` (`partyColor()`) — reuse verbatim,
  do not redefine."*
- ADR 0012 lists `COALITION_COLORS` under "components to reuse (do not invent
  new ones)". ADR 0015 did not supersede it on this point.

Effect today: PN, PH and BN render as three identical grey pills on `/dewan/`.
The table cannot be scanned by Coalition.

1. Restore coalition colour on the pills in both pages. **Reuse `partyColor()`
   from `frontend/public/lib.js` — do not redefine a colour map in Python.** If
   the value must cross into Python, read it from one source rather than
   duplicating the table.
2. Keep the contrast floor from #149: any text on a coloured pill clears 4.5:1.
   Coalition colours were chosen for a light background; verify each on the dark
   surfaces and darken the pill or lighten the text where a pair fails.
3. **Do not touch `monogram_color()`** in `politikku_politicians.py:227`. Those
   tile colours hash the person's *name*, not their party — they only look
   party-coded by coincidence of the badge sitting next to them.

## Out of scope

- **Component unification.** `.bento-tile` (6 rules in `styles.css`, 13 uses in
  `app.js`, **0** in any Python renderer) and `.sharebar` (30 rules, 0 uses) are
  named by `mypolitik-new-views-spec.md` as components to reu

sample.title: hub: paginated template/harness-config lists drop one row at each page boundary
sample.body:
## Problem
Paginated template and harness-config lists drop one row at every page boundary for callers on the per-item authorization path (non-admin users and agents). Walking all pages returns N-1 rows per boundary: for example, 121 of 123 at the default limit, and 11 fewer at limit=10.

## Cause
In `pkg/hub/authorized_list.go`, the per-item scan loop (around lines 288-291) handles a filled page by setting `NextCursor` to the cursor of the *next* allowed item, which is not returned. Store cursors are exclusive, so the next page starts after that item and the item never appears.

## Fix
- Keep `NextCursor` as the cursor of the last *included* item. Drop the overwrite in the page-filled branch.
- Add a multi-page regression test. It should walk the full list at several limits (for example 1, 10, 25 and the default) and assert that the union of the returned pages equals the expected set, with no duplicates.
- Check the group lists that share `authorizedList`.

Introduced with ptone/scion#1916. Skills listing uses a different mechanism and is not affected.

sample.title: prisma: drop @unthrown/prisma and move to Prisma 8 — with unthrown and RLS rebuilt on its middleware
sample.body:
Drop `@unthrown/prisma` and move the persistence starter to Prisma 8, and answer two questions while doing it: whether unthrown's `Result` surface can be rebuilt on Prisma 8's own middleware, and whether row-level security survives the move. The Prisma 8 work is meant to be **donated to `btravstack/unthrown`** once Prisma 8 is stable, so it has to be written as a package that does not need this repository.

## Why now, and why not yet

Prisma 8 is not a version bump. Measured on npm, 2026-09-17:

| Package | Tag | Version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prisma` (CLI) | `latest` | `8.0.0-rc.15` |
| `prisma` (CLI) | `prev` | `7.10.0` |
| `@prisma/client` | `latest` | `7.10.0` |
| `@prisma/orm-postgres` | `latest` | `8.0.0-rc.11` |
| `@prisma/orm-framework` | `latest` | `8.0.0-rc.11` |

**`@prisma/client` has published no 8.0.0 line at all** — not even an RC; the only 8.x versions on it are `8.1.0-dev.*`. The v8 runtime is a different package family: `@prisma/orm-postgres` ("the one package a Postgres application installs") over `@prisma/orm-framework` ("Prisma 8 target-agnostic runtime: contract, components, authoring surface"), whose own dependencies are `arktype` and `@standard-schema/spec`. `@prisma/adapter-pg` and `@prisma/client` both disappear; `@prisma/orm-postgres` peers on nothing but `typescript >=5.9`.

So this issue cannot be executed today. It is filed now because the decision it contains — whether `@btravstack/prisma` survives in its current shape — blocks how much more gets built on the v7 surface, and because two things already point at it:

- **`@unthrown/prisma@0.4.0` peers `@prisma/client: ^7`.** It is unusable on v8 by construction, whatever else is decided.
- **The catalog's `mysql2` advisory override exists only because we are on v7** (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`): v7's CLI bundles a driver per datasource, and the note already records that "there is nothing upstream to take without moving to an RC". `prisma@8.0.0-rc.15`'s dependency list carries no `mysql2` — worth confirming the override becomes deletable.

Two numbers in that catalog comment are stale and should be re-measured when this is picked up: it says `latest` is `8.0.0-rc.12` (now `rc.15`) and reads as though `@prisma/client` had an 8.x, which it does not.

## What actually breaks

The blast radius is small, which is the good news — the blocker is upstream availability, not this repository's footprint.

**`packages/prisma`** — every mechanism it owns is a v7 client-extension mechanism:

- `instrument.ts` wraps `$extends({ query: { $allModels: { $allOperations } } })`. There is no `$extends` in the v8 API as documented.
- `tracing.ts` + the `@prisma/instrumentation` loader contributed to `Instrumentations` traces at the **engine** level. Prisma 8 is a TypeScript runtime with no engine, so this needs re-answering rather than porting.
- `rls.ts`'s `tenantScoped` is a `Prisma.defineExtension` whose recursion guard is "issue every `set_config` through the pre-extension client", plus a hand-copied `ITXClientDenyList` held honest by `rls.test-d.ts` gate 6. All three pieces are v7-shaped.
- The three Prisma peers (`@prisma/client`, `@prisma/adapter-pg`, `@prisma/instrumentation`) collapse to one.
- `prismaDatabase(name)({ client })`'s whole premise — the application hands us a constructed generated client, because only it can name its schema — needs re-checking against `postgres<Contract>({ contractJson, url, middleware })`.

**`examples/order-infrastructure`** — about thirteen `try*` / `$tryTransaction` call sites plus `tryPaginate(...).withCursor(...)`, all in one workspace, plus the `PrismaPg` adapter and the generated-client path.

**Error identity changes shape.** v7 P-codes (`P2002` → `UniqueConstraintViolation`) are what `qualifyPrismaError` keys on; the v8 docs show codes like `RUNTIME.DECODE_FAILED`. The mapping is not portable, and `examples/order-application`'s `DuplicateOrder` / `MalformedCursor` translations sit directly on top of it.

**Pagination.** `@unthrown/prisma`'s `tryPaginate` owns the cursor arithmetic today and is what keeps `@btravstack/contract`'s `Page<T>` / `PageRequest` free of any persistence type (root `CLAUDE.md`, *Persistence*). Whatever replaces it has to keep that line.

**Node floor.** `prisma@8.0.0-rc.15` declares `engines.node >= 22.18.0`. Published packages here promise `>=22`; raising a published floor is a breaking change, so decide deliberately rather than inheriting it.

## Investigation 1 — can unthrown ride Prisma 8's middleware?

Prisma 8 ships a first-class middleware API (docs: [how middleware works](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/middleware/how-middleware-works), [authoring custom middleware](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/middleware/authoring-custom-middleware)). A middleware is a plain object — `{ name, familyId? }` plus hooks — registered in an array at client construction:

```ts
export const db = postgres<Contract>({
  contractJson,
  url: process.env['DATABASE_URL']!,
  middleware: [queryLogger()],
});
```

The hooks, per the docs: `beforeCompile(draft, ctx)` (the typed AST, before SQL compilation — return a new draft to rewrite), `beforeQuery(plan, ctx, params?)`, `interceptQuery(plan, ctx)` (return `{ rows }` and the driver never runs), `onRow(row, plan, ctx)`, `afterQuery(plan, result, ctx)` with `result.rowCount` / `latencyMs` / `completed` / `source`, and the write-path twins `beforeExecute` / `interceptExecute` / `afterExecute`. Throwing from a hook stops the ones after it. Every query — "the ORM client, a query builder, a raw fragment, or an API that an extension added" — reaches the database as a **plan**, and middleware sees that structured object.

**The hypothesis to falsify: middleware is the wrong layer for unthrown, and the right layer for half of it.** A hook is a runtime interceptor. It cannot change the *static* type of `db.order.create(...)`, and `@unthrown/prisma`'s entire value is that `tryCreate` returns `AsyncResult<Order, UniqueConstraintViolation | Fo

sample.title: Postgres-tier tests with --parallel fail unreliably on two machines: diagnose (clone/locks/idmapper/memory) and make the worker heuristic cgroup-aware
sample.body:
## Problem

Postgres-tier tests run with `--parallel` fail unreliably on two different machines. On Dan's 16 GB laptop (4 GiB devcontainer cap, #3649) heavy runs OOM-kill the container and take the Claude session with them. TehomCD reports the same shape on a stronger machine: Postgres tests in parallel "always go down in flames", and several diagnosis attempts have not found the cause. That second data point matters: it says this is not only a memory-cap problem.

What is known today, from the code rather than from the failures:

- `arx test --parallel` derives its worker count from `/proc/meminfo` (VM-wide), not from the cgroup limit (`docs/devcontainer-setup.md` "Memory-aware test parallelism"; `src/cli/arx.py`). Inside a capped container that overestimates available memory by design, and the doc calls the resulting OOM "the intended failure mode".
- The parity tier reuses a pre-built test database with `--keepdb` (`tools/build_schema.py`, ADR-0083). Django's parallel runner clones the test database once per worker (`CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE`); with a partitioned table, materialized views and composite FKs in the template, and `max_locks_per_transaction` already needing a bump for the chain's cumulative FK count (`.github/workflows/nightly-migration-replay.yml:30`), the clone step is a plausible place for lock or connection exhaustion that would look like random failures.
- The idmapper (SharedMemoryModel) is process-global; a parallel run forks workers after Django setup, so any identity-map state populated before the fork is shared by inheritance. Rolled-back mutations are known to survive in the cache (memory: idmapper rollback staleness).
- The local `db` container is limited to 1 GiB on Dan's machine and has `fsync` off; TehomCD's setup is different, which argues against a purely Postgres-tuning cause.

None of this is a diagnosis. The failure signatures from TehomCD's runs have not been captured in one place.

## Ask

A diagnosis first, then a fix. Steps that would settle it:

1. Collect the actual failure output from both machines (first error type, `Ran N tests`, worker count, Postgres log lines at the same timestamps) into this issue.
2. Reproduce with a fixed worker count (`--parallel 2`) to separate memory pressure from a correctness problem.
3. Check the template clone path: connection count and `max_locks_per_transaction` on the local `db` versus the CI container's bumped setting; whether every worker's clone carries the partition, matviews and composite FKs.
4. Make the worker-count heuristic read the cgroup's `memory.max` and `memory.current` when they exist (cheap, and removes the machine-specific half regardless of the rest).

Not critical for launch. Filed so it stops being tribal.

Related: #3649 (container limits), #3656 (the migrate-side cost on the same machines), ADR-0083, ADR-0008 (SharedMemoryModel).

sample.title: the adversary is told to run a command it has no tool for
sample.body:
## What we want

Panel's mechanical refusal is run by something that can run it, and the adversary's instructions ask
only for what the adversary can do.

## The contradiction, in one file

`plugins/panel/agents/adversary.md`:

| Line | |
|---|---|
| 5 | `tools: Read, Glob, Grep` |
| 25 | *"`bin/verdicts.sh prior <dir> <round> <review>` names the record you must read. It exits 1 when nothing records the round being claimed — say so and stop."* |

**It has no tool that runs a shell script.** `plugins/panel/agents/newcomer.md` is the same shape,
`tools: Read, Glob, Grep`.

## Why it matters more than a stale line

`plugins/panel/README.md:83` states the plugin's mechanical promise:

> Mechanical — `bin/verdicts.sh` refuses a round claiming a prior verdict

**The refusal is mechanical only if someone runs it.** The agent told to run it cannot, so in
practice the check is run by whoever is holding the verdict — which is the coordinator the same
paragraph warns about.

## Observed, not inferred

Four adversary reviews ran here on 4 September. **At least one opened by saying so unprompted:**

> No prior verdict exists for this charter. I could not run `bin/verdicts.sh prior`: my toolset is
> `Read`/`Glob`/`Grep`, no shell. **Nothing below reports a command's outcome.**

It judged by reading files instead, which worked — and which is exactly the *summary* the
instruction forbids relying on.

## Not in scope

- **Whether the chain works.** It does not, and that is #461. **This issue stands even after #461
  lands** — a working command an agent cannot run is still unrun.
- What a verdict says, or who may write one.
- Giving the adversary write access. It must not gain one.

## Done when

- [ ] the adversary either has a tool that runs the check, or its instructions stop telling it to
- [ ] if the harness runs the check instead, the agent file says that plainly and says who
- [ ] `README.md`'s *mechanical* claim names what actually runs it
- [ ] the newcomer's file is checked for the same shape — it has the same three tools
- [ ] a reviewer who cannot run a command says so in its verdict, rather than judging silently

## What this does not fix

**Giving the adversary a shell is not obviously right.** It judges work it did not write, and a
read-only judge is a real safeguard, not an oversight. **The other route — the harness runs the
check and hands the answer in — may be the better one**, and this issue does not choose.

Refs #461, #332

sample.title: UC-CHPED: execute the serial comparison.csv regeneration run and publish verify counts
sample.body:
## Scope

Split out of #103, which is being landed in two halves. The **code half** —
`benchmarks/uc-chped/uc_chped.cpp` gains a `--out` CSV writer, an explicit
`--feas-tol` flag, and the stale ramp-constraint language in
`benchmarks/instances/uc-chped/comparison.csv` and `benchmarks/uc-chped/FIDELITY.md`
is corrected — is fast-verifiable and lands under #103.

**This issue is the measurement run**, which is wall-clock-limited and cannot be
verified by a unit or smoke test.

## What to run

One serial pass, on a quiet box (`uptime` load average below 1 — CLAUDE.md's
*Measuring and testing engine changes* forbids running these concurrently),
from a clean tree at a known commit, against a Release build with `CBLS_SANITIZE`
empty in `build/CMakeCache.txt`.

The runner's documented per-period budgets are `{1:10, 3:30, 6:60, 12:120,
24:300, 48:600, 168:600}` seconds over the ucp13/ucp40/ucp100/ucp200 roster,
which is roughly **75 minutes of solve time** plus model build and greedy/FJ
initialisation. Run with `--verify` on and the tolerance stated explicitly:

```bash
uptime   # must be quiet before starting
cmake -B build && cmake --build build -j$(nproc) --target cbls_uc_chped
./build/cbls_uc_chped --verify --feas-tol 1e-6 \
    --commit "$(git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD)" \
    --out benchmarks/instances/uc-chped/comparison.csv
```

Exact flag names follow whatever #103 lands; check the runner's `--help`/source
first rather than trusting this snippet.

## Acceptance criteria

- `benchmarks/instances/uc-chped/comparison.csv` is regenerated in a **single
  serial pass** at the documented budget and seed, covering ucp13, ucp40, ucp100
  and ucp200, with `commit_sha` and the feasibility tolerance recorded per row.
- `--verify` pass/fail counts are published for **ucp40, ucp100 and ucp200**, not
  just ucp13. `--verify` had only ever been run on ucp13; the others were skipped
  for time. (This was #40.)
- Any material change from the pre-removal numbers is explained in the benchmark
  README as tolerance or engine drift rather than presented as an algorithmic
  gain. A looser feasibility tolerance can only admit *more* solutions, so expect
  equal-or-better feasibility counts; an objective that improves must be
  cross-checked against the verifier, because part of the gain may be the extra
  constraint slack.
- The published table must not silently drop the 10 cited `Pedroso MIP (1hr)`
  reference rows.

## Baseline to compare against

The pre-removal CBLS rows were measured at engine commit `fc600ea`, seed 42,
under the old `1e-9` tolerance, and were removed from the table because the file
recorded no tolerance and they could not be interpreted. Recover them with:

```bash
git show c159402:benchmarks/instances/uc-chped/comparison.csv
```

They read: ucp13 1p 12172.0 (4.03%), 3p 42192.8 (8.60%), 6p 98104.1 (7.33%),
12p/24p INFEASIBLE; ucp40 1p 62801.8 (12.86%), 3p 185257.1 (3.85%), 6p/12p/24p
INFEASIBLE; ucp100/ucp200 carry only SA-era rows.

Several search-trajectory changes have landed since `fc600ea` in addition to the
tolerance move, so the delta is not attributable to any single cause without
saying so. Establish the current engine commit and name it in the README text.

## Why it can't be verified fast

Objective quality at a fixed wall-clock budget depends on how many iterations the
process gets. A shortened run produces numbers that are not comparable either to
each other or to the published tables, so there is no smoke-sized version of this
criterion. The verify counts and the delta explanation are outputs of the run and
cannot be written before it.

Part of #25 and #87. Split out of #103.

sample.title: Impact: Qualify the Installed Product, Physics Claims and Desktop/Web Experience
sample.body:
Parent Epic: #9546

## Scope

Own the final acceptance matrix across existing #9484 (web distribution), #9349 (canonical consumer migration), Tools #4251 (physics approximations), and I1–I3. This does not duplicate those implementation tickets.

## Acceptance Work

1. Freeze a model-capability matrix: instantaneous versus finite-duration, tangential spin support, off-center gear effect, inertia tensor use, velocity-dependent COR, shaft/grip assumptions and numerical limits. A model lacking spin support must say unavailable/normal-only, not imply a predicted zero-spin result.
2. Use shared golden cases for centered/off-center, left/right, loft/path/attack, no-hit, low-speed, high-speed and supported boundaries. Check SI/imperial conversion, spin signs, exact vector frames, loss/passivity, momentum including external impulses, instantaneous limits and convergence.
3. Establish physical-reference datasets and predeclared model-specific error/uncertainty criteria before marketing predictive accuracy. Synthetic fixtures and agreement with another implementation are code verification.
4. Demonstrate a clean supported installation serves real JS/assets at `/impact-explorer-app/`, not merely HTTP 200 or the fallback page; provider artifact revision must match the pinned source. Test restart, reload, base paths, missing artifacts and offline behavior that the product claims.
5. Perform real rendered PyQt and web inspection: defaults, responsive layout, keyboard/focus, labels/units, contrast, meaningful errors, progress/cancel, stale-result handling, charts/3-D synchronization, reporting and session recovery. Use representative screen sizes and a reproducible screenshot/video manifest.
6. Confirm every exposed control changes the intended contract or has an explicit disabled reason. Compare identical saved scenarios across runtimes numerically; update feature parity using evidence rather than the mere existence of an iframe.

## Closure

- [ ] Dependency tickets have implementation and exact-pin evidence.
- [ ] Review packet includes install logs, golden comparisons, supported Python matrix, rendered artifacts, reference-validation results and bounded claims.
- [ ] Main's protected release gates and post-merge smoke checks pass.
- [ ] No claim of polished or predictive delivery based only on the 16 library tests from this audit.


## Agent Execution Contract

Audit baseline: UpstreamDrift `1f69a51fce997932f04a6ad1dd95bf4d065ba971`; pinned Tools `3d93bb2c89813e17551814d3be7e895f791e29af` (2026-09-04 Pacific). Re-fetch and record both exact revisions before implementation; this is an audit snapshot, not a floating-main guarantee.

Read `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, relevant ADRs, public `__init__.py` façades, `SPEC.md`, and `AGENT_HANDOFF.md`. Check the fleet issue lease before starting; use an isolated worktree and preserve occupied work. Search shared infrastructure before adding a module. Apply TDD (show the failure), DbC for units/frames/time/provenance/resource bounds, DRY, and LoD. Tools owns shared impact/flight and mocap runtime; upstream provider changes there, then consume an immutable reviewed pin here. Never edit `vendor/ud-tools` to implement a fix.

A completion comment must contain: implementation PRs and merged SHAs; exact provider pin; test command/environment/results including skips; numerical/physical evidence where applicable; rendered desktop/web evidence for changed UI; remaining limitations; SPEC/manual/feature-parity/handoff updates. Follow current protected CI and fleet scheduling rules; no bypasses or issue closure on planning, mocks, or skipped hardware tests. Publish only sanitized capture fixtures; no uploading personal video without authorization.

sample.title: Everything arrives as a claim: a branch per source, per-field trust, drift as a pull request
sample.body:
Part of #133. This is the idea I would actually aim at — the strongest consequence of putting versions under the model, and the one that changes what `main` *means*.

## 1. "Import" is the wrong word for the general case

The same trust question applies to every door data comes through:

- a **spreadsheet** somebody maintains on a share;
- a **meeting or workshop**, read for claims about the estate (§5.38 already does this);
- a **pasted block** from a mail;
- a **connected system** answering through MCP (§5.37);
- anything in the **source catalogue** — the register of enterprise systems Nexus can connect to, which is precisely a list of things that will one day propose changes;
- an **agent's inference** — "these two look like the same system";
- **a person drawing on a canvas**, which is data construction with a mouse.

None of these is more or less trustworthy by virtue of its door. Each produces **claims**, and a claim is not the model until somebody with standing says it is. Every rule below applies to all of them.

## 2. Two rules decide where new data goes

The governance model in two lines:

1. **Anything new lands on a branch.** An object that did not exist before never appears in `main` because a nightly job ran. It waits on a branch until somebody works on it — which is exactly what a campaign (#134) is for.
2. **A known object's new values flow straight through.** Where the object is already reconciled and the source is the recognised owner of that field, the update goes to `main` without ceremony: recorded, attributed, reversible, and **breaking the quality seal on that field** if somebody had validated it (#134).

The second rule matters as much as the first. Putting routine updates through review is how a review queue becomes a thing people rubber-stamp at 4pm on a Friday, and once that habit forms the first rule is worthless too. **Ceremony for what is new or contested; silence for what is routine.**

What it needs:

- A **per-source, per-field ownership and trust order** — ServiceNow owns `lifecycle`, the CMDB owns `hosting`, a person's edit beats both. The staging pipeline already models this as a file trust order; this would make it durable and per-field.
- A definition of **reconciled** — an object that has been through a campaign at least once, or that carries a source key from that system.

## 3. A branch per source system

Each connected system gets a **long-lived branch** that re-syncs on a schedule: LeanIX, ServiceNow, the CMDB, the spreadsheet somebody maintains.

`main` stops being *what the last import wrote* and becomes **the reconciled model — what we chose to believe after seeing what each source claims.**

When two sources disagree about an owner, that is a **merge conflict with both claims visible**, instead of last-write-wins in the small hours. Which is the single biggest difference between this and every import pipeline in the category, today's included.

## 4. Drift as a pull request

Run the source branches nightly. If reality has moved, the branch diverges and **the system opens a pull request by itself**: *reality proposes 34 changes to the model this week.*

That is a far better artefact than a health score. It is specific, reviewable, and it either gets merged or it gets an argument — and either outcome is progress, where a score that has been amber for six months is not.

## Why 3 and 4 move together

Separately they are a sync job and a notification. Together they change the semantics of the whole repository: an import stops being an *event that overwrites* and becomes a **standing claim from a source, reconciled deliberately**.

## Open questions

- **Who may auto-update what?** The per-source, per-field trust matrix of rule 2 is the honest model and a horrible screen if it is not defaulted well. Probably: a sensible default per connected source, overridable per field, and visible on the fact sheet as *this value comes from ServiceNow*.
- What happens when a source branch's claim contradicts a **validated** value? The seal breaks and the object returns to a queue — but a source that breaks a hundred seals a night is itself the finding.
- Does a source branch ever get squashed? A nightly branch with a year of history is a lot of commits for one question.
- Does a source deletion mean *retired* or *no longer visible to me*? Absence is not evidence, and an import that treats it as such is how estates lose objects.

sample.title: 2026-09-05 | [Manus] | z-drive-gog full skill mode correction
sample.body:
## Summary

Corrected the z-drive-gog design after user feedback. The skill is now one full Google Drive skill with temporary Test Mode and approved Work Mode, rather than a permanently read-only skill.

## Activities

- Reframed the design in plain English around the user’s actual goal: agents must eventually read, save, upload, create, organize, and safely share Drive files.
- Defined Test Mode as a short read-only validation period for three or four real retrieval tasks.
- Defined Work Mode for the same skill, enabling uploads, folder creation, template copying, renaming, moving, archiving, and controlled sharing.
- Retained safeguards for client-folder boundaries, stable IDs, duplicate/overwrite handling, untrusted file content, large-file controls, private receipts, and no permanent deletion.

## Correction

The prior design overcorrected toward safety and treated the testing lock as if it were the permanent product. That was inconsistent with the user’s stated need for an agent that can actually operate Google Drive.

## New Direction

Use GOG’s built-in read-only profile only during testing. After successful live read tests, switch the same skill to a controlled work profile that permits normal Drive operations while blocking permanent deletion and requiring approval for sharing, trashing, moving files outside the client boundary, and overwriting existing content.

## Status

Design complete. The next execution step is to build and test the single skill on one agent, one approved account, and one test-client folder, then move that agent into Work Mode after successful validation.

sample.title: Re-creating an agent leaves stale persona/runtime events; mentions route to dead agent
sample.body:
## Summary
Deleting/re-creating a managed agent with the same name leaves the old kind:30175 (persona) and kind:30177 (runtime binding) events live on the relay. The mention autocomplete then resolves the OLD agent pubkey (first match), so tasks are created with a p-tag pointing at a nonexistent agent: the running agent never sees them and the UI eventually reports "never picked this up — it may be offline."

## Repro
1. Create agent "X" (pubkey A) — mention works
2. Delete agent record locally / recreate "X" (pubkey B, new persona_id)
3. @-mention "X": p-tag resolves to pubkey A; running agent B ignores the message

## Observed (canary DB)
- kind:30177 events for both ea641811… (old) and 10722b79… (new) at 18:05 and 19:03 UTC
- mention kind:9 tag p=ea641811… while the live agent was 10722b79…
- Only after deleting the stale 30175/30177 events did the mention resolve to the live agent and the round-trip succeed

## Expected
Agent deletion/replacement should replace (or tombstone) prior persona/binding events, and mention resolution should prefer the newest binding.

Motivation: a fresh agent mapping Sandcastle from scratch cost ~60k tokens and 2¼ minutes; this doc converts that to one file read.

sample.title: [Detail Bug] Controller: Lost release-write race can expire queue positions still within the admission grace window
sample.body:
# Detail Bug Report

https://app.detail.dev/org_a825fb44-0706-44ee-b06f-93cbf0f0caf1/bugs/bug_828c75d5-6983-4487-8dba-41457b7d973a

Introduced in [#57](https://github.com/smoketurner/virtual-waiting-room/pull/57) by @jplock on Sep 10, 2026

# Summary
- **Context**: `run_pass` in `crates/controller/src/lib.rs` advances `serving_counter` with a guarded `write_release`, then expires positions the cursor left behind using `expiry_cutoff(decision.next_serving_counter, …)`.
- **Bug**: When `write_release` loses a race against a concurrent invoke, `dynamo::write_release` swallows the `ConditionalCheckFailedException` and returns `Ok(())`, so `run_pass` cannot tell the release did not land and proceeds to `expire_due` with a cutoff derived from a `next_serving_counter` that was **never persisted**.
- **Actual vs. expected**: The cutoff can be higher than the actually-persisted `serving_counter` justifies, marking `expired` positions whose owners were offered a place fewer than `ADMISSION_GRACE_SECS` (120 s) ago.
- **Impact**: `mark_expired` is a one-way status flip from `issued` to `expired` (`dynamo.rs:221-255`, condition `#s = :issued`), and `generate_token` returns `Denied::Spent` (HTTP 410, `lib.rs:106-109`, `main.rs:179`) for any `Expired` position — a **permanent** denial; no code path in the system reinstates an expired position. So even a small over-expiry permanently denies visitors whose positions were still in the grace window.

# Code with Bug
`crates/controller/src/lib.rs` — `run_pass`:
```rust
let decision = compute_release(state.inputs, state.prev_no_show);
store
    .write_release(event_id, &decision, state.inputs.serving_counter)
    .await?;  // <-- BUG 🔴 Ok(()) on BOTH success and race-loss; caller can't detect lost write

let expired = expire_due(
    store,
    event_id,
    expiry_cutoff(decision.next_serving_counter, state.inputs.target_rate),
    //       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ non-persisted value
)
.await?;
```

`crates/controller/src/dynamo.rs` — `write_release`:
```rust
match result {
    Ok(_) => Ok(()),
    Err(SdkError::ServiceError(se))
        if matches!(
            se.err(),
            UpdateItemError::ConditionalCheckFailedException(_)
        ) =>
    {
        // Another invoke advanced first; this pass's release is stale.
        tracing::info!(event_id, "release write lost the race; skipping");
        Ok(())  // <-- BUG 🔴 masks race-loss; run_pass continues as if release persisted
    }
    Err(e) => Err(StoreError(format!("update_item release: {e}"))),
}
```

# Explanation
- Two scheduled executions can overlap, causing two `run_pass` invocations to read the same persisted `serving_counter` and race on the guarded DynamoDB update.
- When the losing writer hits `ConditionalCheckFailedException`, `write_release` returns `Ok(())`, so `run_pass` proceeds to `expire_due` using `decision.next_serving_counter` computed *before* the write attempt.
- Because `decision.next_serving_counter` was never persisted (and `run_pass` does not re-read the persisted cursor), `expiry_cutoff(decision.next_serving_counter, target_rate)` can be ahead of the true cursor-derived cutoff, and `expire_due` can mark positions as `expired` even though they are still within the 120s grace window.
- `Expired` is irreversible in this system (status flip is one-way; `generate_token` returns HTTP 410 for `Expired`), so any over-expiry permanently denies affected visitors.

# Recommended Fix
Signal the race-loss to `run_pass` so it can skip `expire_due`. The minimal change:

In `write_release`'s return type, return `Ok(ReleaseRace::Lost)` (or equivalent) instead of `Ok(())` on `ConditionalCheckFailedException`:

```rust
// dynamo.rs
tracing::info!(event_id, "release write lost the race; skipping");
Ok(ReleaseRace::Lost)
```

In `run_pass`, skip `expire_due` on `Lost`:

```rust
if !store.write_release(...).await?.is_lost() {
    let expired = expire_due(
        store,
        event_id,
        expiry_cutoff(decision.next_serving_counter, state.inputs.target_rate),
    )
    .await?;
}
```

The next pass (which reads the persisted cursor with a consistent read) will compute the correct cutoff and expire the correct positions.

# History
This bug was introduced in commit 6a2a5ad. The change switched position expiry from time-based (`expires_at < :now`, using wall-clock time) to cursor/positional-based (`queue_position < :cutoff`, where `cutoff = expiry_cutoff(decision.next_serving_counter, target_rate)`). The `write_release` race-loss masking (returning `Ok(())` on `ConditionalCheckFailedException`) already existed from the initial commit `20ade0a`, but it was harmless because `expire_due` used the wall clock, not the cursor. By making expiry depend on `decision.next_serving_counter` — a value computed before the write and never re-read after — the new positional expiry path inherited the masking without accounting for it, allowing `expire_due` to run against a non-persisted cutoff when the release lost the race.

sample.title: perf(cockpit): Waiting-Pulse rendert die ganze Fensterszene mit 31 FPS
sample.body:
## Priorität

P2

## Problem und Nutzerauswirkung

`WaitingPulseElement::paint` ruft bei jedem Paint `ctx.repaint_after(32 ms)`, solange `reduce_motion` aus ist. Der Repaint-Timer in warpui_core setzt `redraw_requested` und läuft `Presenter::build_scene`: vollständiges `layout` + `after_layout` + `paint` **aller** Views des Fensters, nicht nur des 14-px-Glyphs. Solange irgendein Agent wartet (der Normalzustand im Cockpit), läuft die App dauerhaft mit ~31 vollen Frames pro Sekunde, auch im Hintergrund und in unfokussierten Fenstern: hohe CPU-Last und Akkuverbrauch auf Laptops.

## Beleg

- `app/src/cockpit/panel.rs:58`, `113`–`130`, `167`–`172`, `935`–`945`, `1112`–`1124`
- `crates/warpui_core/src/core/app.rs:3283`–`3290`; `crates/warpui_core/src/presenter.rs:333`–`367`

## Ursache

Element-Animation ohne Kadenz-Begrenzung und ohne Fokus-Bedingung.

## Lösungsvorgabe

`WAITING_PULSE_REPAINT` auf mindestens 100 ms anheben. `WindowId` des Panels speichern, Fokuswechsel beobachten und ein Animationsflag aus Reduced-Motion plus `WindowFocusDimming::is_window_focused` ableiten; bei deaktivierter Animation den statischen Waiting-Glyph rendern; Element-Level-Repaint-Scheduling beibehalten (kein Model-Timer mit `notify()`, der zusätzlich View-State invalidieren würde).

## Abnahmekriterien

- Animierte Waiting-Glyphs planen höchstens 10 FPS; Reduced Motion plant keinen Repaint.
- Inaktive/unfokussierte Fenster planen keinen Waiting-Pulse-Repaint; Animation läuft nach Fokusrückkehr ohne Inventaränderung weiter.
- Mehrere Glyphs in einem Fenster erzeugen weiterhin nur einen zusammengefassten Timer.

## Zwingende Rot-Tests

`panel_tests.rs::waiting_pulse_repaint_interval_is_battery_bounded`: `assert!(WAITING_PULSE_REPAINT >= Duration::from_millis(100))`. Heute 32 ms.

## Abgrenzung

#120 (Pane-/Tab-Glow, stale) ist eine Feature-Idee; dieses Issue betrifft den bestehenden Puls.

Quelle: Codebase-Audit 2026-09-05, Batch 3 (Befund-IDs: H0022), Gegenprüfung Codex gpt-5.6-sol.

sample.title: [Bug][Dashboard] Codex disable dialog and state are misleading
sample.body:
### Client or integration

OpenCodex dashboard

### Area

Dashboard

### Summary

Disabling Codex from the Integrations overview opens the Grok Build consequence dialog, and after confirmation the Codex card can retain its pre-toggle state until a full page reload. The status API also supplies the OpenCodex config path instead of Codex's effective `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`, so the dialog cannot accurately identify the file it will change. Expected: Codex-specific consequences name the actual file, and the card refreshes its desired and observed state immediately after the toggle.

### Reproduction

sample.title: tom_select_no_event_boundary_review の package/docs inventory guard を検討する
sample.body:
## 背景

`doc/tom_select_no_event_boundary_review.html` は、stale / aborted Tom Select request の no-event boundary を request-failure state と並べて確認する map-only companion artifact です。`doc/visual_references.md` と Product Profile では、request-start / finish events、retry UI、production CSS、request lifecycle behavior を Rails Fields Kit responsibility にしない静的 review lane として案内されています。

一方で、確認した範囲では、この artifact が packaged maintained docs から落ちないこと、また no-event boundary が current public event surface と混同されないことを扱う dedicated open Issue は見当たりませんでした。

## 確認した事実

- `doc/visual_references.md` は `tom_select_no_event_boundary_review.html` を stale / aborted request no-event boundary の map-only companion lane として案内している
- Product Profile の Visual reference family にも同 artifact が listed されている
- `doc/events.md` は success / failure events と host-app-owned feedback boundary を source of truth として扱う
- duplicate search では `tom_select_no_event_boundary_review` / `no event boundary review` の package inventory guard 専用 open Issue は見当たらなかった

## この Issue でやること

`doc/tom_select_no_event_boundary_review.html` を package/docs inventory guard に含める価値があるか判断する。

採用する場合は、次の narrow quality/docs slice に閉じる:

- artifact が packaged maintained docs から落ちた時に気づける representative signal を追加するか判断する
- `doc/events.md` の current event surface と、no-event companion artifact の役割差を代表 wording で守る
- guard は file path、stale / aborted no-event boundary、request-failure comparison、map-only companion lane の代表 signal に留める
- request-start / finish events、retry UI、loading UI、production CSS、runtime request lifecycle behavior には広げない

採用しない場合は、manual docs review と existing visual map / events docs で十分な理由を Planner comment に残す。

## 受け入れ条件

- [ ] `doc/tom_select_no_event_boundary_review.html` を package/docs inventory guard に含めるか、含めない理由が明確である
- [ ] 追加する場合、artifact が packaged docs から落ちた時に気づける
- [ ] stale / aborted no-event boundary と current success / failure event surface の責務差が保たれている
- [ ] brittle な全文一致や visual reference redesign になっていない
- [ ] runtime JavaScript behavior、event payload、request lifecycle、production CSS には触れていない

## 非目標

- Tom Select request lifecycle implementation の変更
- request-start / finish event の追加
- built-in loading / retry UI の追加
- visual reference artifact の redesign
- screenshot approval CI の導入
- `doc/events.md` の全面 rewrite

## 想定変更範囲

- `spec/package_contents_spec.rb` または近接 docs inventory guard
- 必要なら Product Profile / `doc/visual_references.md` / `doc/events.md` の link signal 最小確認のみ

## 次の担当

Planner / quality-docs 行き。Workflow Manager では `agent:planned` は付けません。

sample.title: swt: each worktree it creates names its parent, and swt list shows the children of a branch
sample.body:
## Problem

In this issue, the **parent** is the worktree where `swt create` runs. A **child** is a worktree that `swt create` makes.

A child keeps no record of its parent. In a parent worktree `issue-42` on the branch `issue-42`, `swt create fix-parser` makes these names:

```text
directory  <directory that holds issue-42>/fix-parser-<token>.swt
branch     swt/fix-parser-<token>
```

Neither name contains `issue-42`. Thus nothing can find the children of a branch:

- An orchestrator starts three subagents, then loses its context. It cannot find their worktrees again.
- A person who is about to merge or delete the parent cannot see that unmerged work is in a child.
- `swt` has no command that shows what it made. The person must read `git worktree list` and guess from the names.

**Expected:**

1. The names of a child show which parent it came from.
2. `swt list`, run in a worktree, shows the children of the branch that the worktree has checked out.
3. A hook or a skill can find the same children with plain git, without `swt`.

## Root Cause Analysis

The naming step of `swt create` builds both names from two inputs only: the name that the caller gives, and a uniqueness token (process id and clock, in base 36). It does not read the branch or the name of the parent worktree.

The directory goes beside the parent. That position does not identify the parent, because many parents share one directory. All worktrees under `tools-worktrees/` put their children into that one directory. The main checkout puts its children into `~/code`, next to every other repository.

Nothing needed the relation until now. `swt merge` reads the branch from the HEAD of the child, and merges into the worktree where it runs. Thus no code recorded the parent.

No other tool in this repository, and no skill in the dotfiles, parses the `swt/` branch prefix or the `.swt` suffix. Only the `swt` tests pin the current format.

## Design

### The key is the branch of the parent

The branch of the parent is the thing that `swt merge` merges into. It is also the thing a tool knows when it asks "does this branch have children?".

| Name | Today | Proposed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Branch | `swt/<name>-<token>` | `swt/<parent-branch>/<name>-<token>` |
| Directory | `<name>-<token>.swt` | `<parent-worktree-name>--<name>-<token>.swt` |

- **The branch keeps the parent branch verbatim.** Git accepts a valid branch name in the middle of a ref, slashes included. `git check-ref-format` accepts `refs/heads/swt/feat/foo/fix-parser-abc`. The part `<name>-<token>` never contains `/`, so the parent is exactly the text between `swt/` and the last `/`. This key loses nothing, so a hash gives no benefit and costs readability.
- **The directory keeps the name of the parent worktree** (the last component of its path), and stays beside the parent. `ls` then shows each child next to its parent. A child of the main checkout becomes `tools--fix-parser-<token>.swt`, not a bare `fix-parser-<token>.swt` in `~/code`. The directory name is for people. `swt list` does not parse it.
- **One token, minted once, keys both names**, as #284 requires.
- **A parent on a detached HEAD has no branch.** `swt create` refuses it before it creates anything, and says why. `swt merge` into a detached parent works today only when the parent did not advance. It reads the parent branch as the literal `HEAD`. When the parent advanced, the rebase step runs `git rebase HEAD` in the child. That command does nothing, so the second fast-forward fails too.

### `swt list`

- Run in any worktree, `swt list` shows the children of the branch that is checked out there.
- Its source is `git worktree list --porcelain -z`, the registry of git. It does not scan directories. The NUL-separated form keeps a path with a newline in one entry.
- A child is shown only when its parent is **equal** to the current branch. A prefix is not sufficient: the children of `feat/foo` are not children of `feat`.
- Each child is one line on stdout: the path, a tab, and the branch. The path comes first, so the output can go directly to `swt merge`.
- When git marks a child `prunable` (its directory is gone), the line gets a third field, `prunable`. The user can then prune it.
- When there are no children, stdout is empty, a note goes to stderr, and the exit status is 0. `[ -n "$(swt list)" ]` is then a complete check.
- On a detached HEAD, `swt list` has no branch to ask about. It exits 1 with a message on stderr.

### A check with plain git

A hook or a skill can find the child branches without `swt`:

```sh
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' "refs/heads/swt/$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD)/*"
```

Git 2.55 gives these results. In `for-each-ref`, `*` does not cross `/`, so the pattern for `feat` shows only the children of `feat`. Two similar commands are wrong:

- `git branch --list 'swt/feat/*'`: here `*` crosses `/`, so the result also contains the children of `feat/foo`.
- `git for-each-ref refs/heads/swt/feat` (no `*`): a literal prefix, with the same error.

This command shows child **branches**. `swt list` shows child **worktrees**.

## TDD Fix Plan

Each cycle runs the real binary against a fixture repository, as the current end-to-end tests of `swt create` do. Every spawn of git sheds the inherited `GIT_*` environment through `gitscratch`.

1. **RED:** Write a test for a parent on branch `issue-42` and a parent on branch `feat/foo`. In each, `swt create fix-parser` prints one path. The directory is `<parent-worktree-name>--fix-parser-<token>.swt`, beside the parent. Its branch is `swt/<parent-branch>/fix-parser-<token>`, with the same token.
   **GREEN:** Give the naming step two more inputs: the parent branch and the parent worktree name. `swt create` reads the parent branch before it creates anything.
   *Existing expectations:* the tests that pin `swt/<name>-<token>` and `<name>-<token>.swt` change to the new format in this red commit, on purpose. The properties that they pin do not ch

sample.title: Update our repository coding standards
sample.body:
Clear, documented coding standards keep the codebase consistent and make it easier for new contributors (and Copilot) to produce correct changes. Our current guidance on comments and documentation is thin, which leads to inconsistent commenting — some files are over-commented with restated code, others lack any explanation of intent. We want a single, well-understood convention that says what to document, where, and how, with emphasis on comments and documentation.

## What we want

- **Comment intent, not mechanics.** Comments should explain *why* a piece of code exists or the reasoning behind a non-obvious decision, not restate *what* the code already says. Remove comments that merely paraphrase the line below them.
- **Document the data layer.** Every exported function in `db/` and `src/lib/` must have a TSDoc/JSDoc comment describing its purpose, parameters, and return value. Helpers should keep their injectable `db` argument documented so the testing pattern stays clear.
- **Document component contracts.** Each reusable `.astro` component should document its `Props` interface so the component API is self-explanatory.
- **Keep comments current.** Treat outdated comments as bugs — update or delete them in the same change that touches the related code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.github/instructions` files document a clear comment philosophy: comment *why* (intent/decisions), not *what*, and avoid restating code
- [ ] TSDoc/JSDoc expectations are documented for exported functions in `db/` and `src/lib/`, including describing parameters and return values
- [ ] Documentation expectations for `.astro` component `Props` interfaces are documented
- [ ] TypeScript formatting rules are documented and, where possible, enforced through ESLint
- [ ] The README links to or summarizes the updated coding standards
- [ ] Linting passes with any newly added rules (run through the `quality-checks` skill / `npm run lint`)

sample.title: Roadmap: harden the existing execution model before expanding scope
sample.body:
# Roadmap: harden the existing execution model before expanding scope

## 背景

sshx 当前已经具备较完整的 Agent 远程执行能力，包括：

- 单主机 / 多主机远程执行
- 稳定的 JSON / JSONL 执行契约
- dry-run
- 结构化 audit
- host / credential 管理
- SFTP / transfer
- guarded `apply`
- guarded `sql`
- host inspection / plugin
- stdio MCP
- human-only interactive login
- source address binding
- release signing / SBOM / provenance

当前阶段不应继续横向增加大量新功能。

接下来的重点应该是：

> 提高执行确定性、安全性、可验证性、稳定性和长期维护能力。

目标是让 sshx 从“功能完整的 Agent SSH CLI”进一步收敛为：

> **A predictable, auditable and safe remote execution primitive for agents.**

---

## 核心原则

新增能力应优先满足以下条件之一：

1. 减少 Agent 判断次数
2. 减少执行结果的不确定性
3. 提高执行前后的可验证性
4. 提高错误分类和恢复能力
5. 提高审计证据质量
6. 提高跨平台一致性
7. 降低长期维护成本

避免仅仅因为某个远端工具存在，就增加新的 sshx verb。

---

# P0 — Execution Plan Integrity

目前 `--dry-run` 可以展示执行计划，但计划与实际执行之间还缺少明确的完整性绑定。

目标：

```text
resolve
  ↓
plan
  ↓
review / agent decision
  ↓
execute exactly that plan
  ↓
audit
```

增加稳定的 execution plan fingerprint。

例如：

```json
{
  "schema": "sshx.plan.v1",
  "target": "db-01",
  "action": "apply",
  "risk": "mutation",
  "plan_hash": "sha256:..."
}
```

执行时允许：

```bash
sshx apply ... --expect-plan=sha256:...
```

如果执行环境或影响执行语义的输入发生变化，应拒绝执行。

### Tasks

- [ ] 定义 `sshx.plan.v1`
- [ ] 明确哪些字段参与 plan hash
- [ ] 排除时间戳、随机 ID 等非确定字段
- [ ] `--dry-run --json` 输出 `plan_hash`
- [ ] 支持 `--expect-plan=<hash>`
- [ ] plan mismatch 返回稳定 `error_kind`
- [ ] audit 记录 `plan_hash`
- [ ] MCP 暴露相同语义
- [ ] 增加 deterministic serialization 测试
- [ ] 增加 TOCTOU / changed-input 测试

### Acceptance

相同输入产生相同 plan hash。

任何会改变实际执行目标、权限或副作用的关键输入发生变化后，旧 plan hash 不得继续执行。

---

# P0 — Unified Risk Model

目前不同执行路径已经存在安全限制，但风险语义还可以进一步统一。

建议引入统一风险等级：

```text
read
mutation
privileged
destructive
```

风险不是单纯根据命令字符串判断，而应该来自：

```text
action
+ target
+ privilege
+ operation type
+ known side effects
```

例如：

| Operation | Risk |
|---|---|
| `uname -a` | read |
| download file | read |
| upload new file | mutation |
| `apply` | mutation |
| sudo read | privileged |
| sudo mutation | privileged |
| destructive SQL | destructive |
| disk / filesystem destructive command | destructive |

### Tasks

- [ ] 定义统一 risk enum
- [ ] `run` 使用统一风险分类
- [ ] `apply` 使用统一风险分类
- [ ] `sql` 使用统一风险分类
- [ ] `sftp` / transfer 使用统一风险分类
- [ ] dry-run 输出 risk
- [ ] JSON result 输出 risk
- [ ] audit 输出 risk
- [ ] MCP 保持一致
- [ ] `--force` / bypass 与 risk 模型统一
- [ ] 补充风险分类测试矩阵

### Acceptance

Agent 不需要根据不同 verb 单独推断风险。

所有产生副作用的执行入口使用相同风险语义。

---

# P0 — Preconditions & Postconditions

对于 mutation，sshx 应尽可能提供执行前后的事实，而不是只报告命令成功。

例如 `apply`：

```text
before_sha256
expected_sha256
after_sha256
backup_path
changed
```

对于其他操作也可以提供适当的 precondition / postcondition。

目标：

> Execution success != desired effect confirmed.

### Tasks

- [ ] 抽象通用 precondition result
- [ ] 抽象通用 postcondition result
- [ ] `apply` 完善 before / after fingerprint
- [ ] SQL mutation 返回明确 affected-state evidence
- [ ] SFTP mutation 返回目标文件 metadata
- [ ] execution result 中增加 `changed`
- [ ] 区分 `executed` 与 `verified`
- [ ] audit 保留 verification metadata
- [ ] verification failure 使用独立 `error_kind`

---

# P1 — Execution Fingerprint

除了 plan hash，实际执行结果也应产生 fingerprint。

例如：

```json
{
  "plan_hash": "sha256:...",
  "execution_id": "...",
  "execution_fingerprint": "sha256:...",
  "started_at": "...",
  "finished_at": "...",
  "verified": true
}
```

用于关联：

```text
plan
execution
result
audit
```

### Tasks

- [ ] 定义 execution identity
- [ ] CLI / MCP / audit 使用同一个 execution ID
- [ ] multi-host execution 为 parent / target 分配稳定关联 ID
- [ ] audit query 可按 execution ID 查询
- [ ] export 保留关联关系

---

# P1 — Cancellation & Deadline Semantics

多主机 fan-out 已经存在，下一步重点应放在失败和取消语义。

### Tasks

- [ ] 明确 per-host timeout
- [ ] 明确 global timeout
- [ ] context cancellation 全链路传播
- [ ] SSH connect 可取消
- [ ] command execution 可取消
- [ ] SFTP 操作可取消
- [ ] multi-host fan-out cancellation
- [ ] MCP cancellation 映射
- [ ] cancellation 返回稳定 `error_kind`
- [ ] audit 区分 timeout / cancelled / failed

---

# P1 — Fan-out Failure Policy

增加少量、明确的 fan-out 控制能力：

```bash
--fail-fast
--max-failures=N
```

不要演化成 workflow engine。

### Tasks

- [ ] `--fail-fast`
- [ ] `--max-failures`
- [ ] stopped / skipped target 进入结构化结果
- [ ] 保证 JSONL completion semantics
- [ ] audit 记录停止原因
- [ ] MCP progress 与最终结果一致

---

# P1 — Error Taxonomy Review

系统能力已经增长较多，需要重新审视 `error_kind`。

目标：

Agent 可以根据 error kind 明确决定：

```text
retry
fix config
request credential
request approval
abort
inspect target
```

### Tasks

- [ ] 审计当前所有 error paths
- [ ] 清理依赖字符串匹配的错误
- [ ] 避免相同错误出现多个分类
- [ ] 明确 retryable / non-retryable
- [ ] 考虑增加 `retryable` 字段
- [ ] 为主要 error kind 建 contract tests
- [ ] 文档提供 Agent decision table

---

# P1 — Audit Evidence Quality

当前 audit 已支持 query / export。

下一阶段重点不是增加日志数量，而是提升证据质量。

建议保证能够回答：

```text
Who/what initiated it?
Which host?
Which resolved address?
Which credential role?
Which plan?
Which risk?
Was a bypass used?
What was executed?
Was state changed?
Was the result verified?
What failed?
```

**Where:** src/agentic_hil/comports.py:1577-1591 (payload_bytes hex branch), 1586-1590

**Fixture:** In-process fake serial handle recording write() calls; the contract is the tool description ('text or hex stimulus'), and a container variant over a socat pty confirms the bytes on the line.

**Where:** src/agentic_hil/can.py:1101-1111

sample.title: scrapex/cli.py auto-merges clean and raises NameError: BEHIND moved to dbupgrade.py
sample.body:
**Git reports `scrapex/cli.py` as a clean auto-merge. The result raises `NameError` on every `scrapex init-db` without `--db`.** No conflict, no test failure on either side, nothing for a reviewer to see.

## The measurement

`BEHIND` was a module-level constant in `scrapex/cli.py` at the branch's base. `main` **moved it** to `scrapex/dbupgrade.py` and left a comment where it used to be. The branch, meanwhile, added a **new use** of it in `_back_up_before_init_db_advances_a_schema`.

The merge takes `main`'s deletion and the branch's new use, and neither side is wrong on its own tree:

```bash
git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/claude/drive-without-a-server
# -> 163d65b4f97b00965ad3b5f143211c741e5de699
git cat-file blob 163d65b4:scrapex/cli.py > /tmp/merged_cli.py
```

Measured on that exact blob:

```
definitions of BEHIND in merged cli.py : NONE
imports from dbupgrade                 : upgrade_what_is_only_behind   (BEHIND is NOT imported)
use at line 109                        : if state.get("ok") or state.get("status") != BEHIND:
```

On `main` today:

```
scrapex/dbupgrade.py:36   BEHIND = "Needs upgrade"
scrapex/cli.py            no definition — only a comment saying it moved
```

## Why it matters beyond one import

This is the exact failure class `tools/merge_tree_check.py` was built for: **two changes that touch no common line and break each other anyway.** The branch's CI (had it ever run) would have been green; `main`'s CI is green; the merge is red. Only a suite run against the *merge tree* can see it.

It is also the second instance in this repository — the first was #314 + #309 on 2026-09-03, a moved line number rather than a moved symbol. **A moved symbol is the worse version**, because a stale line number can still land on plausible code while a missing name is a hard runtime failure that no static check in this repo looks for.

## The fix

One line, in whichever branch rescues this code:

```python
from .dbupgrade import BEHIND, upgrade_what_is_only_behind
```

## The check that would have caught it

```bash
py -3 -m tools.merge_tree_check claude/drive-without-a-server -- -m docs
```

Run it **last, before the merge** — not while preparing the branch. Its own docstring says why: the result is only meaningful against the head that is actually about to merge.

sample.title: Task: Task-held environment leases and nested Agent-run lifecycle
sample.body:
Part of #24
Blocked by: #30, #31

## Goal contribution

Implements the outer Task begin→end lifecycle and the nested Agent run begin→end lifecycle proven by #31, so unfinished environment state remains exclusively assigned to its Task across multiple Agent runs, idle periods, failures, and human validation.

## Outcome

Production Tasks can explicitly begin on one environment, retain one durable Task-owned Environment lease until explicit end, and run multiple sequential Agents under that lease. Agent-run settlement never releases a Task lease. Restart, timeout, and interruption fail safe without making unfinished environments reassignable.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A Task has explicit begin and end operations. Creating a `todo` Task does not reserve an environment; beginning it resolves one environment, acquires one Task-owned lease, and durably records the selected environment and lease before Agent work starts.
- [ ] `EnvironmentLease` identifies a tagged Task or one-round Run holder. SQLite persistence and migration preserve existing lease records without silently changing their ownership.
- [ ] A Task's selected environment is stable from begin through end. Later advances never rematch or migrate the Task to another environment.
- [ ] A Task-linked Agent run verifies and reuses the Task's active lease. The run records the shared lease id and environment, but settling, stopping, failing, or interrupting that run never releases the Task lease.
- [ ] Only one Agent run may be active inside one Task at a time. A second concurrent advance is rejected without changing the Task lease or environment state.
- [ ] `in-progress`, `blocked`, idle-between-runs, and awaiting-human-validation Tasks retain their leases and continue blocking other Tasks and one-round mutating Runs from the environment.
- [ ] Lease timeout, Sprout restart, Worker loss, or an interrupted Agent run cannot make the environment automatically reassignable. Recovery can resume only the owning Task or explicitly preserve/discard and end it.
- [ ] Task end refuses while an Agent run is active and follows a recoverable ending sequence. The lease is released only after required Task cleanup reports success.
- [ ] Direct status patching cannot bypass Task end, cleanup, or lease release. Failed/blocked Agent runs do not make the Task terminal automatically.
- [ ] One-round Message-triggered Runs remain separate and may use a Run-owned lease released at their terminal state.
- [ ] HTTP routes expose Task begin, advance, end, and recovery with precise 404/409 failure classes.
- [ ] Real SQLite restart tests cover begin and end crash windows, idle Task retention, interrupted nested Runs, resume-by-owning-Task, competing-Task refusal, and idempotent retries.
- [ ] `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run web:build`, and `git diff --check` pass.

## Constraints

- Implement the interface and ordering accepted by #31 rather than inventing a second lifecycle.
- A Task owns the lease; an Agent and Agent run do not.
- Environment safety and recoverability take priority over utilization. No automatic expiry-to-free transition is allowed for unfinished Task work.
- Preserve the primary SQLite store (ADR-0002), engine neutrality, and Environment-worker ownership (ADR-0003).
- Follow repository privacy rules and sanitized commit metadata.

## Non-goals

- Task context filesystem preparation or cleanup implementation beyond the interface needed to order lease release; #33 owns the Worker implementation.
- Web UI changes.
- Live Pi/Codex collaboration.
- Cross-environment Task movement.
- Environment queueing or optimization.

## Location
- `supabase/config.toml:L65-L70` — `[db.seed]` with `sql_paths = ["./seed.sql"]`; `supabase/seed.sql` does not exist (verified: `ls supabase/seed.sql` → not found; `supabase/` holds only `config.toml`, `migrations/`, `tests/`)
- `AGENTS.md` — "Schema (`supabase/migrations/`)" paragraph lists `20260903014208`, `20260903014211`, `20260904010000`, `20260904020000`, `20260905090000` and omits `20260903080000_sync_push_concurrency.sql` (advisory-lock serialization, Issues #13/#14) and `20260903170000_tags_string_array_check.sql` (Issue #40); its `sync_push` summary describes only the original `20260903014211` body
- Repo root — `CLAUDE.md`, `agent.md`, `claud.md` alongside `AGENTS.md`

## Details
AGENTS.md is the operating guide this project expects agents and new contributors to follow; its "Migration Flow" tells them to run `db reset --local`, which now stops after migrations because the configured seed file is missing (`supabase db reset` applies seeds by default when `[db.seed]` is enabled). The stale schema section means an agent reasoning about the security surface from AGENTS.md misses the concurrency serialization and the tags constraint entirely — the exact two migrations that changed `sync_push`'s behavior after the version the doc describes. The mirror files duplicate the guide without a reconciliation story; the staleness in (2) shows that risk is already realized.

## Suggested fix
1. Either delete the `[db.seed]` block from `config.toml` (the pgTAP setup lives in `tests/000-setup.sql`, so no seed is needed) or add a minimal `supabase/seed.sql` (even a no-op comment) — whichever matches intent.
2. Update the AGENTS.md schema list to all seven migrations with one line each (the migration headers already carry the summaries), and note that `sync_push` has been `create or replace`d by later migrations.
3. Reduce the agent-guides to one canonical file (`AGENTS.md`) and make the others one-line pointers (`@AGENTS.md`), or delete them.

## Severity rationale
P3 — no runtime or security impact, but all three actively mislead the contributors and agents the docs exist for, and the seed misconfiguration breaks a command the docs themselves instruct people to run.

_Found during comprehensive review at commit `4c35cab39ca04be6c8adef9e657bcf2337bb2505`._

sample.body:
### Summary

Re-sync `ui/` with the [`@nebari` shadcn registry](https://nebari-dev.github.io/nebari-design/) as part of nebari-dev/nebari-design#143: re-install every registry-owned component with `npx shadcn add --overwrite`, move the `src/ui` folder to the standard `src/components/ui` alias, move orphaned/app-owned files out of the registry folder, and install the `@nebari/claude-skill` item.

### Motivation

- `components.json` aliases `ui` to `@/ui`, so registry files land in `src/ui/` with rewritten imports and can never be byte-identical to the registry; #143 calls this alias drift out explicitly.
- 15 of the 22 installed registry components have drifted from the registry (`toast` most of all, then `table`, `code-block`, `select`).
- `src/ui/avatar.tsx` maps to no registry item (`avatar` was reverted upstream) and is unowned.
- `src/lib/utils.ts` carries an app-owned `copyText()` helper appended to the registry file, so `@nebari/utils` cannot be re-synced without moving it.
- `.claude/skills/nebari-ui/` is not installed, so coding agents in this repo have no design-system guidance.
- The header defines its own `--header-background`/`--header-border` tokens even though `@nebari/theme` now ships `--header`/`--header-foreground`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `components.json` uses `"ui": "@/components/ui"` and all `@/ui/*` imports are rewritten to `@/components/ui/*`
- [ ] Every registry-owned file under `src/components/ui/` is byte-identical to `registry/nebari/ui/<name>.tsx` in `nebari-design` (no formatter in this package)
- [ ] `avatar.tsx` lives outside `components/ui/` as an app-owned component and `copyText()` lives in its own `src/lib` module; `utils.ts` matches `@nebari/utils`
- [ ] `src/hooks/use-theme-preference.ts` and `theme-provider.tsx` match `@nebari/use-theme-preference`
- [ ] `ui/.claude/skills/nebari-ui/SKILL.md` is installed via `npx shadcn add @nebari/claude-skill`
- [ ] Header uses `bg-header text-header-foreground border-border`; only `--header-action-hover`, `--notification-badge`, `--sign-out-foreground` remain app-defined
- [ ] No hard-coded hex/`rgb()` colors in `.tsx` outside `components/ui/`
- [ ] `@base-ui/react` satisfies the registry's `^1.6.0`
- [ ] `npm run build` and `npm test` pass in `ui/`
- [ ] Header matches the canonical recipe in the `nebari-ui` skill, or the remaining gap is filed as a follow-up issue

### Out of Scope

- Adding new components to the `nebari-design` registry — this only propagates items that already exist there.
- Visual/UX redesign of the app; this is a parity sweep against the registry, not a redesign.
- Automating the sync (a `shadcn diff`-style CI check) — follow-up once the manual baseline is established (tracked in nebari-dev/nebari-design#143).
