sample.title: Epic 9: Review-Quality Simplification
sample.body:
**Goal**: Reduce this engine's brittleness (25.7k lines, 43% of non-merge commits are fix/bug/regression subjects) without losing function, while making the actual deliverable review-verdict trustworthiness rather than a line-count target. Line reduction (an estimated 2,300-2,600 lines, ~10%, across Phases A-D) is a byproduct of this work, not its justification.

Full evaluation, verified against current `main`: `sonic:~/repos/claude/ai-pr-review-simplification-review-2026-09-11.md` (original document) plus this epic's own session notes (three findings the original document did not contain, and twelve settled scoping decisions). Priorities, in order: review quality, token efficiency, maintainability.

## Rationale

The brittleness is measurable, not a vibe: 1,038 non-merge commits, 444 (43%) with fix/bug/regression subjects; a 45-branch review-reuse state machine; 67 distinct issue numbers cited in source comments. Two bugs found and fixed by E9.S1 (system_prefix dropped on 3/5 LLM providers, a suppression-config spelling mismatch) had zero test coverage and were live on `main` for months. A third defect (agent prompts imported from a plugin with an incompatible tool-access model) already shipped literal `<tool_call>` XML to a production PR comment once (#446) and reintroduced a self-contradictory empty-state instruction once (#372).

Review nondeterminism (#799) is the sharpest finding this epic surfaced that the original document missed entirely: this repo's own `tests/canary/consistency_eval.py` records ten byte-identical PRs producing five distinct verdicts, and temperature is not an available lever on the default models. That is why a measurement harness (E9.S2) sits ahead of every judgment-level prompt change in this epic's sequencing, rather than after it.

## Stories

- [x] #795 — system_prefix dropped on 3/5 LLM providers (F2) — fixed
- [x] #796 — suppressions.json verify-type mismatch (F3) — fixed
- [x] #797 — Prompts imported from claude-comprehensive-review carry unusable instructions + empty-state contradiction (F4/F5a) — fixed, see ADR 0004
- [ ] #798 — Severity derived from confidence, contradicting governance + outcome.py (F5b) — deliberately deferred to E9.S3, first measured arm
- [ ] #799 — Review verdicts are nondeterministic across identical input — ongoing, measured not "fixed"
- [ ] #800 — E9.S2: Build measurement harness and capture baseline variance
- [ ] #801 — E9.S3: Phase A remainder (shared context block / #177, retire profile routing, cache layout, docs-missing-check removal)
- [ ] #802 — E9.S4: Phase B dispatch/orchestration cleanup (mechanical)
- [ ] #803 — E9.S5: Phase C VCS/slash dedup (behavior-preserving; PUT-reuse removal is a separate decision gate)
- [ ] #804 — E9.S6: Phase D analyzer table-driving, config pruning, deprecation warnings, v3.0.0 removal target
- [ ] #805 — E9.S7: Phase E repository hygiene

## Acceptance criteria

- Every quality-affecting change ships as a measured arm against the E9.S2 harness (precision non-decreasing, no baseline High/Critical true positive lost); the harness's runs-per-PR figure is derived from observed baseline variance, not asserted.
- No breaking changes: every input/env var accepted today stays accepted, as a documented no-op where the feature it controlled is removed, with a deprecation warning and a named removal release (v3.0.0) rather than permanent silent residue.
- Judge pass and tree-sitter context enrichment are decided on data (on/off arms in the harness), not carried forward by default.
- Prompt parity with `claude-comprehensive-review` is not a goal; language-profile parity (the one surface that's actually shared, and byte-identical today) stays audited by the narrowed `parity-audit` tooling.

## Out of scope

- The GitHub review-body PUT-reuse removal decision (deferred inside E9.S5, gated on E9.S3's measurement results).
- Any change to the LLM judge pass's or tree-sitter enrichment's *default* until the harness produces a decision.

## Context

- Source document: `sonic:~/repos/claude/ai-pr-review-simplification-review-2026-09-11.md`, written against `4538ba7`, re-verified this session against `38496e0` (v2.10.0) — every size metric and both claimed bugs confirmed unchanged.
- Size: XL (spans multiple releases; E9.S1 alone is one PR).
- This epic intentionally does not follow the 'one epic, one branch, one PR' pattern of Epics 1-8 — the work is too large and too sequentially gated (each phase's start depends on the prior phase's measured result) for a single branch.

sample.title: [P0][Source Snapshot] Replace polling with webhook-driven main/develop refresh
sample.body:
## Objective

Make canonical Google Drive source snapshots for protected integration branches update from GitHub events instead of scheduled reconciliation.

When any `StreamScapeTV/*` repository advances `main` or `develop`, the corresponding canonical Google Drive snapshot must be refreshed through the existing Agent State -> Central CI path without waiting for cron polling.

## Owner decision

The automatic mechanism must be **trigger-based only**.

- Use the existing organization GitHub webhook path.
- Accept GitHub `push` events for `refs/heads/main` and `refs/heads/develop` only.
- Route those events through the existing Cloudflare -> Supabase -> Agent State -> CI broker -> Central CI architecture.
- Keep one authoritative source-snapshot mutation implementation in Central.
- **Remove the scheduled source-snapshot reconciliation/polling mechanism after the event-driven path is deployed and proven.**
- Do not retain cron polling as a second automatic implementation or fallback.
- Explicit/manual `source.snapshot` recovery may remain available because it uses the same Central mutation path; the prohibition here is on a second automatic polling implementation.

## Current problem

`ci-workflows/.github/workflows/source-snapshot.yml` currently has:

- a direct `push` fast path for `ci-workflows` itself; and
- a scheduled reconciliation pass intended to discover stale `main`/`develop` snapshots across the organization.

That does not provide prompt organization-wide freshness. GitHub `push` events are repository-scoped, so another repository such as `organization-rules` does not directly trigger the workflow in `ci-workflows`. The cron-based reconciliation can be delayed, leaving Google Drive stale long enough that an agent bootstrap must perform explicit recovery.

Observed example on 2026-09-06:

- `StreamScapeTV/organization-rules@main` advanced to `b618cc2339eeadbbba76d3b7de418ccc725b0f88` at `16:12:43 UTC`;
- the canonical Drive snapshot was stale during a later agent bootstrap;
- Drive was eventually repaired, but not by a prompt organization-wide merge/push trigger;
- this demonstrates that polling is not an acceptable freshness mechanism for canonical bootstrap state.

## Existing infrastructure to reuse

### GitHub -> Cloudflare

`StreamScapeTV/cloudflare-edge` already contains the deployed `github-agent-state-filter` Worker used as the public organization-webhook ingress.

It already:

- verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256`;
- bounds request size;
- filters noisy GitHub events before Supabase;
- forwards the original raw body plus GitHub delivery/event/signature headers unchanged so Supabase can independently verify the same HMAC.

Today it only admits selected issue lifecycle events. Extend the same ingress to admit the required protected-branch push events.

### Cloudflare -> Supabase

`StreamScapeTV/agent-state-supabase` already has the GitHub webhook receiver pattern that independently verifies the GitHub HMAC and validates organization/repository identity before mutating Agent State.

Add protected-branch push ingestion using the same trust boundary. Do not trust fields merely because Cloudflare forwarded them.

### Agent State -> Central CI

The existing Agent State CI request flow already emits `ci_runs` rows which are relayed by `ci-broker` into `StreamScapeTV/ci-workflows/.github/workflows/central-ci-dispatch.yml`.

`ci-broker` must remain transport-only. It must not learn GitHub push semantics, branch policy, source-snapshot workflow semantics, or Google Drive behavior.

If the current Agent State request API requires human Agent identity/origin semantics, add a bounded trusted system/webhook request path in Agent State rather than spoofing `Agent N`. The resulting CI request must still flow through the existing generic broker/dispatcher contract.

## Event classification

Use the GitHub **`push` webhook**, not `pull_request.closed`/`merged`.

The source-snapshot invariant is that an integration branch advanced, regardless of whether that occurred by merge commit, squash merge, rebase merge, direct push, or authorized automation.

Cloudflare/Supabase must accept only events satisfying all applicable checks:

1. `X-GitHub-Event == push`;
2. repository owner is exactly `StreamScapeTV`;
3. `payload.ref` is exactly one of:
   - `refs/heads/main`
   - `refs/heads/develop`
4. the push is not a branch deletion;
5. `payload.after` is a valid lowercase 40-character Git SHA;
6. repository identity is valid/registered under the existing Agent State authority.

All feature branches, issue branches, tags, deleted refs, and unrelated event families must be discarded before creating a CI request.

## Desired flow

```text
GitHub push to StreamScapeTV/<repo>@main|develop
        |
        v
existing organization webhook
        |
        v
Cloudflare github-agent-state-filter
  - verify GitHub HMAC
  - accept only main/develop push events
  - drop all other pushes
        |
        v
Supabase webhook receiver
  - independently verify original GitHub HMAC
  - validate repository/ref/SHA
  - deduplicate delivery
  - create bounded Agent State source.snapshot CI request
        |
        v
existing Agent State ci_runs webhook
        |
        v
ci-broker (transport only)
        |
        v
central-ci-dispatch.yml
        |
        v
existing authoritative source.snapshot implementation
        |
        v
Google Drive <repository>/<main|develop>/ updated in place
```

## Agent State request semantics

The generated request must represent exactly:

- repository: the GitHub webhook repository, e.g. `StreamScapeTV/organization-rules`;
- ref: `main` or `develop` derived from `payload.ref`;
- `is_tag: false`;
- workflow: existing `source.snapshot` semantic workflow;
- exact source identity: `payload.after` must be retained as event/request evidence and Central must still verify the live branch head before Drive mutation.

Do not expose arbitrary workflow, runner, ref, repository, or Drive input

sample.title: Epic: deliver the voice-only thesis study and validate the complete pilot workflow
sample.body:
## Outcome
Deliver a pilot-verified thesis experiment comparing **self-similar versus generic voice within participants**, with counterbalanced order, balanced search difficulty, trustworthy trial/motion/audio data, and a standardized participant procedure.

Source: user-supplied meeting summary received **2026-09-15**. Its exact meeting date is not supplied. This epic records planning scope, not completed implementation or institutional approval. It updates the thesis delivery sequence from #6; retain that roadmap as historical context.

## Decisions and boundaries
- **Meeting decision:** voice type is the thesis manipulation; the agent remains always gaze-contingent. Every participant experiences both voice blocks, with approximately equal order allocation.
- **Open decision:** pilot collaborative “we/let’s” and stronger external/third-person scripts, then freeze one perspective **for both voices**. Current `VoicePromptText.cs` changes wording only for the self-similar condition; that confound must be resolved before claiming a voice-only comparison.
- **Implemented baseline, subject to headset QA:** eight surrounding planes, 56 objects, two practice trials, 14 measured trials in two voice blocks, search-onset gating, block NASA-TLX, stable object manifests and audio events. Eight starter clips followed by background loading are implemented locally; do not revert to full-library startup blocking based on old issue text.
- **Open decision:** measured-trial count and repetitions per geometric difficulty. The current seven trials per voice are not an established balanced schedule. Meeting examples of 120° are illustrations, not a new required zone on the eight-plane layout.
- **Protocol proposal:** roughly 15–20 participants (often discussed as 18–20), not a completed power calculation or guaranteed adequate sample.
- **Protocol proposal:** immediate block workload ratings, headset break, individual voice ratings/manipulation checks, and final qualitative interview. Qualtrics preferred; fallback if access delays the study.
- Full perspective factorial design and physiological eye-movement claims are future/exploratory work, not thesis launch gates. Save raw data now; validate sampling and detectors before claiming fixations/saccades or cognitive load.

## Work order and linked tasks
The order below distinguishes early drafts/rehearsals from final study gates. Start survey access and protocol drafting in parallel with engineering. Dependencies in the linked issues govern readiness.

| Stage | Work | Issues |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — unblock and define | Freeze a provisional thesis contract/reference convention; fix/validate eye calibration; start survey access and instrument/protocol drafts | #7, #14, #26, #27 |
| 2 — trustworthy trial execution | Build a provisionally balanced schedule; log geometry and first contact; timestamp/count actual speech; capture raw motion; stop obsolete guidance | #10, #20, #21, #22, #23 |
| 3 — lock the participant experience | Rehearse collaborative/external scripts and choose one shared style; improve cloning sample; verify progressive voice readiness; wire breaks/surveys and standard procedure | #24, #25, #12, #13, #26, #27 |
| 4 — validate the dataset | Reconstruct a development session and produce descriptive trial-level quality reports | #28, #15 |
| 5 — pilot and freeze | End-to-end pilot/rehearsal; feed observed difficulty, duration and quality into final trial/sample/analysis choices and reconciled materials | #17, #10, #16, #7, #18 |

#16 rationale/measure work and #18 data-flow/material review begin early; their final decisions follow pilot evidence. Participant-use review in #18 is a prerequisite to the applicable human research pilot, not an afterthought. Full recruitment follows the relevant readiness and institutional gates.

### New implementation and preparation issues
- [ ] #20 — target geometry, first contact and final selection
- [ ] #21 — actual playback and before/after-contact guidance counts
- [ ] #22 — frame-level HMD/gaze/playback context
- [ ] #23 — obsolete guidance cancellation
- [ ] #24 — script alternatives and a shared thesis perspective
- [ ] #25 — natural enrollment sample separated from comprehension
- [ ] #26 — workload, voice ratings/manipulation checks and interview
- [ ] #27 — standardized procedure, headset break and survey handoffs
- [ ] #28 — reconstructable fixture and dataset validation

### Existing work reused under this epic

sample.title: Make review recovery and adjudication preserve round state
sample.body:
## Description

### review-pr, adjudication

A round-3 review posted after round 4 had been adjudicated; nothing says how to handle it

Proposed change: "A review that lands out of order is adjudicated against current HEAD, not the commit range it was given: mark each finding live, already fixed and by which commit, or no longer applicable, and say which commits the reviewer did not see."

### review-pr, section 6

The paginated comment listing is stated as advice for reviewers; the adjudicating writer hits the 400-line truncation harder (751 lines on #504)
Nothing covers a pull request kept a draft for a reason outside the review (another PR holding the files it needs)
Seen again.
section 3 gives one diff-capture command, `git diff origin/main...HEAD`, and section 6 says to size a later round "by the diff of what changed since the previous round rather than by the size of the whole PR". It never says to capture that diff, and there is no command for it, so a session either sends round two's reviewers the whole pull request (which is what the only command in the skill produces, and which makes them re-review work already adjudicated) or invents a range. I sent two patches — the fix diff for the lenses judging the fixes and the whole diff for a lens whose subject is the change as a whole — and had to decide that split myself, including that the fix diff wants a path filter so an unrelated merge from `main` does not arrive as part of it.

Proposed change: "Read the PR's comments with `gh api repos/ImpowerGames/impower/issues/P/comments --paginate`, never `gh pr view P --comments`, whether adjudicating or preparing a reviewer's prompt; the later rounds are the ones that fall off the cut."
"When something outside the review keeps the pull request a draft, say so in the same Notes bullet, name what has to happen first, and list the remaining work in the order a follow-up session should do it."
add to section 6, after the sentence about sizing the tier: "Capture that diff as well as, or instead of, the whole one: `git diff <the commit the previous round reviewed>..HEAD -- <the paths this change owns> > \"$SCRATCH/review-<round>-fixes.patch\"`. A lens judging the fixes gets the fix diff; a lens whose subject is the change as a whole (prose consistency, blast radius) gets `origin/main...HEAD`. The path filter matters once `main` has been merged in mid-review, or the merge's own commits arrive as part of the fixes."

### review-pr, section 3 (reviewer prompt)

A heredoc carrying a backslash is refused by the harness; reviewers writing comment bodies hit it
during the #512 handoff, the PR had a round-2 state comment but no round-2 review comments. The recovery rule says a round did not run after the parent's exit unless its comments already landed, so I relaunched the missing prose lens. The original prose, undirected, and check-honesty reviews then posted successfully. The original reviewers had survived the handoff; the replacement prose review duplicated paid work. Both reports are preserved and adjudicated on #512 (comments 5620584590 and 5620687157).
Seen again.

Proposed change: Applied in #503 (write the comment body with the editor tool, never a heredoc); confirm it survived
Earlier item: applied in PR #503; new feedback requires triage.
use a launch record instead of treating a missing comment as proof that a reviewer stopped. “Each review launch records its task id or process id, start time, and output path in the round state; recovery checks that launch's status and replaces it only after confirming it stopped without posting.” Checking the start time prevents a reused process id from being mistaken for the reviewer. The runner-specific launch/status mechanism fits the review invocation work in #496; no new Gotchas entry is proposed.

### review-pr, section 4 (Adjudicate, on the PR)

the section says "Post one adjudication comment (again via `--body-file`) naming each finding and what happened to it", and the sentence before it says to adjudicate every comment a reviewer posted. On a round with four reviewers and twelve findings, one comment naming all of them is a wall a reader has to map back onto four separate reviews by hand, and a reviewer's own comment shows no sign of having been answered. My orchestrator asked for one adjudication comment per review instead, which read far better on the pull request: each comment names the review it answers by id, and every finding in that review is disposed of in it. Nothing in the skill says which shape to use, so a session following the text alone produces the harder-to-read one.

Proposed change: replace "Post one adjudication comment (again via `--body-file`; `CLAUDE.md` has the `@-` footgun) naming each finding and what happened to it" with "Post one adjudication comment per review (again via `--body-file`; `CLAUDE.md` has the `@-` footgun), each naming the reviewer comment's id in its heading and disposing of every finding in that review; a round with a single reviewer takes a single comment. Answering each review beside itself is what lets a reader follow a finding to its disposal without holding four reviews in their head."

## Motivation

These items were observed while following the repository skills and collected in #510.

## Scope

Address the items above. Prefer a checked mechanism for preventable mistakes; confirm prose proposals against current code and instructions before applying them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each item above is fixed or explicitly adjudicated.
- [ ] Any mechanism has a failing-then-passing check and the standalone checks pass.
- [ ] Skill text describes current behavior and the pull request lists applied feedback.

## Additional context

Filed by the hand-invoked triage-skill-feedback run for #510.

Related to #496, which handles runner portability and model invocation. This follow-up covers review workflow behavior and is not a prerequisite for #494 or #496. The heredoc instruction cited in the section

sample.title: Windows sandbox provisioning fails on stale CUA dependency-cache paths over 260 characters
sample.body:
## Summary

After updating Codex Desktop for Windows, every sandboxed command and computer-use call failed before process launch with:

`helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`

The failure was traced to the Windows sandbox helper validating stale CUA dependency-cache directories whose paths exceed the legacy Win32 path limit. Moving only those unused stale caches out of the runtime tree immediately restored sandbox setup, shell execution, and computer use.

## Environment

- Codex Desktop: 26.911.7940.0
- Codex CLI: 0.155.0-alpha.2.6
- OS: Windows 11 Professional, 10.0.26200, x64
- Sandbox backend: elevated Windows sandbox
- First recorded failure: 2026-09-17T11:33:27Z

## Observed behavior

- All sandboxed commands failed before launching a process.
- Computer-use calls also failed.
- `codex doctor` reported: `elevated Windows sandbox provisioning recorded a structured failure` with `helper_unknown_error`.
- App restart, full reboot, Windows app Repair, and app reinstall did not resolve it.

## Root-cause evidence

The sandbox log reported runtime read/execute validation failure on a stale generated path under:

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\f24ab376120677c2\bin\node_modules\@oai\sky\dist\js-dependency-cache\shared-v1\applied-bk-agent-openai-js\pnpm-store\v11\links\@rollup\plugin-typescript\12.1.2\a522fe9000e9cb07598cb89328c5f87afda445b7562f1579b3d4e1f77197a142`

Evidence collected locally:

- Failing path length: 293 characters.
- Longest affected cache directory: 312 characters.
- The directory existed.
- The sandbox group already had Read & Execute permission.
- Direct `CreateFileW` with the normal path failed with Win32 error 3.
- The same path with a `\\?\` extended-length prefix succeeded.
- The signed helper executable's embedded manifest did not declare `longPathAware`.
- Two stale runtime caches were affected; the active runtime itself was not.

## Reversible workaround that restored operation

I moved only the unused stale `js-dependency-cache` directories outside `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node` into a backup directory. No ACL, Defender, sandbox-policy, or registry changes were made.

Immediately afterward:

- sandbox setup refresh completed with `errors=[]`;
- normal commands launched again;
- computer use worked again;
- `setup_error.json` was absent;
- the sandbox checks in `codex doctor` passed.

The backup remains available for engineering reproduction if requested.

## Expected behavior

The Windows helper should either:

1. use extended-length Windows paths when validating runtime trees; or
2. avoid recursively validating generated dependency caches in stale, inactive runtimes.

A single stale cache path should not abort sandbox provisioning for every command and computer-use call.

## Additional notes

A repository search found multiple reports of the generic `helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`, but no issue matching the exact `js-dependency-cache` / `CreateFileW` long-path evidence. Sanitized logs and a reproducible diagnostic script can be provided if maintainers need them.

sample.title: Simplify comparator PEX: klt pex workaround for #1395/#1396 is now obsolete
sample.body:
## What to Simplify

`layout/comparator/pex/run_pex.py` (458 lines) and
`layout/comparator/pex/normalize_extracted_units.py` (122 lines) — a
hand-rolled re-implementation of `klt pex`'s three logical steps (extract,
re-simulate each leg, diff) plus a unit-normalization post-process step —
work around two upstream `klayout-tools` bugs that are **now fixed in the
exact version this repo already pins**.

The repo's own `layout/comparator/pex/README.md` ("Why not just `klt pex`")
already documents the exit condition:

> Once both upstream issues are fixed, this workaround can be deleted and
> `run_pex.py` replaced with a single `klt pex layout.gds pex_request.json
> --deck sky130 --pdk sky130A --pdk-root $PDK_ROOT` call — `pex_request.json`
> is deliberately kept in the exact shape that call already expects.

## Why It's Bloat (Evidence)

Both blocking bugs are closed upstream, fixed, and already shipped in the
version this repo pins:

1. **[2AMLogic/klayout-tools#1395](https://github.com/2AMLogic/klayout-tools/issues/1395)**
   (models.lib mis-resolution on the extracted-side leg) — fixed by merged
   PR [#1403](https://github.com/2AMLogic/klayout-tools/pull/1403).
2. **[2AMLogic/klayout-tools#1396](https://github.com/2AMLogic/klayout-tools/issues/1396)**
   (sky130 X-card unit-suffix incompatible with `.option scale=1.0u`) —
   fixed by merged PR [#1404](https://github.com/2AMLogic/klayout-tools/pull/1404),
   which added a per-PDK-family `GEOMETRY_STYLE_BARE_UM` so sky130 extraction
   emits bare-micron geometry automatically, no post-processing needed.

`layout/requirements.txt` already pins `klayout-tools==0.4.0`. Verified via
GitHub's compare API that both fix merge commits (`bf42833`, `43bb36a`) are
ancestors of the `v0.4.0` tag (`git compare bf42833...v0.4.0` and
`43bb36a...v0.4.0` both report `status: ahead`, i.e. `v0.4.0` contains them
plus more). Confirmed directly in `v0.4.0`'s source
(`src/klayout_tools/pex.py:_prepare_extracted_request`,
`src/klayout_tools/pdk_models.py:_format_um`/`_GEOMETRY_STYLE_BY_FAMILY`)
that both fixes are present as described.

In other words: this repo has been running the fixed `klt` version since
issue #102's pin bump (0.3.0 -> 0.4.0), while still carrying ~580 lines of
workaround code the fix made unnecessary.

## Impact Analysis

**Files affected**:
- `layout/comparator/pex/run_pex.py` (458 lines) — replace bespoke
  extract/normalize/sim/diff orchestration with a single `klt pex` call
- `layout/comparator/pex/normalize_extracted_units.py` (122 lines) — delete
  entirely, the fix makes this a no-op
- `layout/comparator/pex/README.md` — update "Why not just `klt pex`"
  section (or remove it) now that the answer is "no longer applicable"

**LOC removed**: ~580 lines of workaround code, likely replaced by a much
shorter `klt pex` invocation wrapper (or none, if `run_pex.py`'s only
remaining job is writing the evidence record).

**Risk Level**: Low-to-Medium. The change touches a verification flow whose
job is producing gating evidence (issue #112's PEX record), so re-running
and diffing the new record against the existing evidence
(`layout/comparator/reports/<latest>/record.md`) before/after is required —
not just a green test suite.

## Proposed Approach

1. On a branch, replace `run_pex.py`'s multi-step orchestration with the
   single `klt pex layout.gds pex_request.json --deck sky130 --pdk sky130A
   --pdk-root $PDK_ROOT` call the README already prescribes, keeping
   `pex_request.json` as-is (already shaped for this call per the README).
2. Delete `normalize_extracted_units.py` — confirm `klt extract`'s sky130
   output is already bare-micron (no `U`/`P` suffixes) so no normalization
   pass is needed.
3. Re-run and record a new evidence record; diff its AC2/AC3 numbers
   (parasitic capacitances, pick-off deltas) against the current record
   under `layout/comparator/reports/` to confirm the single-call path
   reproduces the same result the two-bug workaround produced.
4. Update `layout/comparator/pex/README.md` to drop the now-resolved
   "Why not just `klt pex`" workaround rationale (or mark it historical),
   and keep the file list current if fewer files remain.

Created per autonomous Hermit systematic-check pass (stale-workaround
check: repo's own docs name the exact upstream issues and exit condition
for a workaround, then verify with GitHub API whether that condition holds
now).

sample.title: [Feature]: Honor `tools.toolSearch` for bundle-MCP CLI backends — the loopback MCP config hardcodes `alwaysLoad: true`
sample.body:
## Summary

The generated loopback MCP config for CLI backends unconditionally sets `alwaysLoad: true`, so every OpenClaw tool schema is eagerly expanded into the harness prompt on every turn and `tools.toolSearch` is silently a no-op on `claude-cli` runs. Derive that flag from resolved config instead of hardcoding it.

## Problem to solve

On CLI-backend runtimes OpenClaw does not build the model request; it exposes gateway tools to the child agent through the loopback MCP bridge (`bundleMcp`). The generated server entry is built in one place and always carries `alwaysLoad: true`:

```js
function createMcpServerConfig(port, headers) {
  return {
    mcpServers: {
      openclaw: {
        type: "http",
        url: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/mcp`,
        alwaysLoad: true,
        headers,
      },
    },
  };
}
```

Both `createMcpLoopbackServerConfig()` and `createMcpAttachGrantServerConfig()` funnel through it, and there is no config input, plugin hook, or per-backend override.

Per the bundled Claude Agent SDK types, that flag means:

> When true, all tools from this server are always included in the prompt and never deferred behind tool search. Equivalent to setting `defer_loading: false` on the API. Default: tools are deferred when tool search is enabled. As a side effect this also blocks startup until the server is connected (capped at the standard 5s connect timeout) even though MCP startup is otherwise non-blocking by default.

So OpenClaw explicitly opts out of a deferral mechanism the harness already implements. This is observable: in the same Claude Code turn, other MCP servers are correctly deferred and their schemas are pulled on demand via `ToolSearch`, while all ~40 `mcp__openclaw__*` schemas are expanded up front.

`docs/tools/tool-search.md` documents `tools.toolSearch` as the answer to exactly this problem, but it is implemented only in the OpenClaw embedded runner. Operators whose primary model resolves to `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"` therefore have no knob at all — neither the OpenClaw-side one (does not apply to harness runs) nor the harness-side one (overridden by `alwaysLoad`).

### Measurements

Installed `openclaw@2026.9.1`, Claude Code `2.1.261`, `claude-cli` runtime, `tools.profile: "full"`, Telegram-only single agent:

| Prompt component                                                             | Approx. tokens |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `mcp__openclaw__*` schemas (~40 tools)                                       | 13,000–14,000  |
| of which `message`                                                           | ~2,500         |
| of which `browser`                                                           | ~1,600         |
| of which `skill_workshop`                                                    | ~1,300         |
| Total static prefix (all schemas + system prompt + skills + workspace files) | ~36,000        |

The OpenClaw catalog is the single largest component of the static prefix, and the harness is already capable of deferring it.

## Proposed solution

Set `alwaysLoad` from resolved config rather than hardcoding it:

- When `tools.toolSearch` is enabled, omit `alwaysLoad` (or set it to `false`) in the generated MCP server entry, letting the harness defer OpenClaw tool schemas behind its own tool search.
- When `tools.toolSearch` is disabled, keep `alwaysLoad: true` so current behavior is unchanged by default.
- Optionally expose an explicit override for operators who want to decouple the two (`tools.toolSearch.cliBackendAlwaysLoad`, or a `bundleMcp` field on the backend registration).

The value of routing it through the existing key is portability: one operator-facing setting then means the same thing on the embedded runner (`code` / `tools` / `directory` modes) and on harness runtimes (native MCP deferral), so a config does not have to change when the selected model changes runtime.

Restricted runs that already pin an exact allowlist — for example the Claude node MCP listener that publishes only `mcp__openclaw__skill_workshop` — can keep eager loading; the flag matters for full catalogs.

## Alternatives considered

- **Patch the installed `dist` locally.** Works, but is lost on every upgrade and is not a solution for other operators.
- **Trim the catalog with `tools.deny`.** Removes capability. The point of tool search is to keep every tool reachable while paying for only the ones used.
- **Drop `agentRuntime.id` and run the same model over the provider API**, so the embedded runner applies `tools.toolSearch`. This changes billing from subscription to per-token, gives up the harness, and makes the config runtime-specific — the opposite of the goal.
- **Register a custom CLI backend plugin.** `api.registerCliBackend(...)` exposes `bundleMcp` / `bundleMcpMode`, but the MCP server entry itself is generated in core, so a plugin cannot shape this field.

## Impact

- **Affected:** every operator on `claude-cli` — the documented default path for Claude Code and subscription users — and any future `bundleMcp` backend whose harness supports deferred MCP tools.
- **Severity:** performance and cost. Nothing is functionally broken; the run is just larger than it needs to be.
- **Frequency:** always. Every turn of every session, plus every scheduled heartbeat and cron turn.
- **Consequence:** ~13–14k tokens per request that the harness is already able to defer. With the default 30-minute heartbeat that alone is ~48 extra turns/day carrying the full catalog on turns whose entire output is `NO_REPLY`. On a subscription route this surfaces directly as quota burn rather than a line item.

## Evidence / examples

- Generated config: `createMcpServerConfig()` in the MCP HTTP loopback runtime module (`dist/mcp-http.loopback-runtime-*.js` in the published package), used by `createMcpLoopbackServerConfig()` and `createMcpAttachGrantServerConfig()`.
- A second hardcoded occurrence for t

`area/q5`, `type/theorem-proof`, `priority/medium`, `blocked/lean-expert`, `blocked/codex-review`

sample.title: Q-EXTERNAL-CHECK-FRAMEWORK-01 + Boot State Machine thin formalization (Z1 candidates + prototypes)
sample.body:
## What & why

Z1 package delivering two related thin formalizations and working prototypes:

1. **Boot Process State Machine** (companion to PR #330 / `BOOT_PROCESS_MAP.md`)
2. **External Check Framework v0.1** (Witness / Jester / Witch / Oracle) — second-order AI-safety assurance layer that observes the safety-information system without becoming it.

Both are **advisory / observational only**. They do not amend `SESSION_RITUALS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GOVERNANCE.md`, or `CURRENT.md`. Sources still win.

smag_p: 0.75

## Zone

- [x] **Z1** — AI-executable, no ratification needed for the prototypes themselves
- [ ] **Z2** — needs operator ratification (candidate blocks + any claim of normative status)
- [ ] **Z3** — involves credentials / billing / deploy (operator-run)

## Candidates ready for REGISTERED.md

### Q-BOOT-STATE-MACHINE-01
Thin formalization of `BOOT_PROCESS_MAP.md` into an advisory state machine (enum + transitions + failure states). Mirrors existing SESSION_RITUALS §A/§B, §F.9, IC-029/IC-030, PATH_C. No new enforcement, no new halt conditions, no ACAT-in-guard.

### Q-EXTERNAL-CHECK-FRAMEWORK-01
Four distinct control planes:

| Layer | Primary question | Failure attacked |
|-------|------------------|------------------|
| **Witness** | What actually happened, and what evidence exists? | fabrication / evidence loss |
| **Jester** | Does the evidence really support the conclusion? | institutional self-confirmation |
| **Witch** | What hidden dependencies or common-mode failures exist? | false independence |
| **Oracle** | Given what we know, what should we expect next? | unjustified certainty |

Core rules (executable invariants):
- `UNKNOWN ≠ SAFE`
- `AUTHORITY ≠ EVIDENCE`
- `NO_GATE ≠ PASS`
- `AGGREGATED ≠ INDEPENDENT`
- `evidence ≠ conclusion`
- No single trust score — returns a structural vector only
- HumanAIOS sits **beside** safety institutions; never manufactures clearance

## Prototypes (session artifacts)

Working code was developed and tested in-session under:

```
artifacts/
├── boot_sm_proto/
│   └── boot_state_machine.py          # minimal advisory state machine + constrained agent
└── external_check_framework/
    ├── src/
    │   ├── witness.py

Define the minimum Store-owned transport/API projection needed to carry an existing ORS-admitted write reservation across the authenticated Kernel→Store boundary. This closes #67's missing trusted-input seam for #988. It is a projection of canonical reservation evidence, not a new reservation issuer, lease service, signature system or scheduler.

Current examined StoreRequest::Apply and KernelStoreGateway::apply carry context, PreparedTransition and expected heads but no WriterReservationToken binding. A self-consistent caller-created scope list must not acquire scheduling authority merely because it passes structural validation. ORS remains the uncommitted reservation owner; Store heads/receipts remain committed truth.

## Dependencies and ordering

Read accepted current Store request/identity/receipt/failure contracts, ORS reservation_model and I5.7. Reuse their exact lower-level identities; Store API must not import the ORS implementation or duplicate its mutable state/lifecycle. Required identity/epoch/failure corrections at these boundaries must be accepted first under their actual owners, not presumed from an old issue number.

This contract may be implemented independently of #986–989. Its lib.rs export/client-method edits are serialized after #773 and #950 where their current source overlaps; no task depends on final #67 completion. - new `crates/storage/eliot-store-api/tests/data/write_admission.json`.

No wire enum/capability activation yet, existing apply signature break, adapter/Kernel/ORS implementation, Cargo/lock/dependency, workflow/docs or shared registry changes. Freeze exact public fields/signatures and compatibility before coding. An optional method declaration cannot advertise runtime support; the later process owner enables it only with an actual backend.

## Required reading

Follow root/storage AGENTS.md, WORKFLOW.md and ACTIVE. Route these four paths together through `python scripts/docs_read.py read` with repeated --path and the standard bundle/read-receipt outputs. Read every required routed item and directly read `docs/architecture/I05-07-ordering-and-parallelism.md`, `I05-04-canonical-transition.md`, `I05-16-common-durable-fields.md`, `I05-27-canonical-operation-identity-and-effect-identity.md`, `I07-20-agent-facing-error-contract.md`, `I15-02-principal-and-session-binding.md`, `I05-22-schema-and-migration-rules.md`.

Routing does not provide shard contents.

## Required contract

Expose a closed versioned Store-write admission projection and reserved-write request using existing canonical identity types. Preserve expected RevisionHeads and all immutable semantic input exactly; no locally normalized command or new semantic admission.

Document an explicit field-to-ORS/Store owner mapping and canonical encoding. The token digest binds the actual canonical token bytes under its owner, not a second ad hoc serializer or a claimed opaque receipt. The Store projection is intentionally not a serializable validated-authority wrapper: successful decode means shape only. The receiving boundary must authenticate the Kernel generation and validate the current owner evidence before creating its private executable admission value. Do not add a worker-controlled valid/verified/eligible Boolean, infer issuer trust from a string, or accept a payload-supplied principal over transport identity.

Intrinsic validation checks nonempty complete scope set, unique canonical order, bounded members, exact operation/transition/fence/head matching, state-specific required evidence and closed version/shape. It cannot query ORS, validate current time by an ambient clock, assert canonical eligibility or allocate sequence/epoch. Expiry needs the existing owner/time contract; wall timestamps alone are not authority.

The additive client operation accepts this closed request and returns existing WriteReceipt/typed StoreError semantics. sample.title: arch-discover: consider making package staleness a first-class warning (field report)
sample.body:
## Context

We evaluated **ase** in an agent-assisted workflow for a small Astro marketing site and ended up adopting several of its concepts into our project rituals (task-grill-style briefings, merge-readiness evidence, the funnel pattern, persisted decision logs). Thank you — the conceptual clarity is genuinely useful even without installing the toolkit.

This issue is a small field report + suggestion for `ase-arch-discover`.

## Field case

An earlier human+agent library selection in our project picked **Splide v4** as a carousel library, based on docs quality, feature fit and bundle size. What everyone missed: its last release was **November 2022** (~3.5 years unmaintained at decision time). The mistake only surfaced months later when an adversarial re-review explicitly checked registry health signals — which then also revealed that the best candidate was "no library at all" (a static, 0-dependency layout beat every carousel for the actual content volume).

## Suggestion

Since `ase_component_info` already retrieves version, dates and download metadata, `arch-discover` seems well positioned to prevent exactly this failure class:

1. **Hard staleness flag:** if the last release is older than a threshold (e.g. 12–18 months), surface it as a prominent warning/gotcha on the candidate row (and optionally penalize its rank) — rather than relying on the reader to notice a date column. Stale-but-popular packages are precisely the ones that pass "gut feeling" checks.
2. **"No dependency" as an implicit candidate:** for small-scope functionality, consider always listing a "hand-rolled / no library" row in the result table, so the funnel explicitly weighs it against the packages.

If parts of this already exist in current versions, feel free to close — we scraped the docs a while ago and may be behind.

---
*Transparency: drafted by a Claude agent (Fable) as part of an agentic evaluation workflow, posted on behalf of and reviewed by Mathias Böni (@Milofax).*

sample.title: epic(mac): reach 30 tok/s raw single-stream and 300 tok/s unified agent throughput on Apple Silicon M3 Pro
sample.body:
## Umbrella Goal

Break through the single-stream 15.22 tok/s ceiling to reach 30 tok/s raw, and scale agent concurrency to 300 tok/s unified throughput across X=24 agents on Apple Silicon M3 Pro (36GB). Keep all execution fak-native all the way on Metal, with zero fallback to external runtimes.

## Parent Context

- Builds directly upon #9430 (`epic(perf): ship the next ten fak-native Qwen Mac improvements`), which established the resident hybrid state and command-buffer amortization roadmap.
- Expands and scales #12235 (`epic(mac): end-to-end Apple Silicon Metal Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative decoding for Qwen 3.8 / 3.6`), elevating the target past the 14.5–18 tok/s single-stream MTP floor toward 30 tok/s raw and 300 tok/s unified multi-agent throughput.
- Inherits the verified on-device benchmarking baseline and physical envelope on `node-macos-a` established in #2723 (`bench(macbench): head-to-head fak vs llama.cpp vs MLX on real Mac hardware`).

## For / Problem / Today / Better because / Witness

- **For:** Autonomous multi-agent workloads and local developer workflows running Qwen3.8 natively on MacBook-class Apple Silicon (M3 Pro 18-core GPU, 36GB unified memory, 150 GB/s bandwidth).
- **Problem:** Single-stream decode on 27B Q4 is bandwidth-capped at ~7.6–8.2 tok/s autoregressive, and initial MTP drafts cap near 15.22 tok/s. Concurrently, scaling multi-agent serving to X=24 parallel agents exhausts unified memory under standard full-attention KV allocations and stalls on fragmented memory transfers.
- **Today:** Single-stream decode achieves ~7.6 tok/s autoregressively and ~15.22 tok/s with basic depth-2 MTP drafting. Serving 24 concurrent agent sessions at standard attention allocations requires >48 GB KV state, exceeding physical 36GB DRAM and forcing serialized execution or out-of-core eviction.
- **Better because:**
  1. Ultra-compact 2-bit UD-Q2_K_XL compression reduces resident model weights to 8.5 GB, raising the physical memory-bandwidth ceiling to >17.6 tok/s autoregressive and enabling Wide-M tree verification (M=16..24) to reach ≥30 tok/s raw single-stream.
  2. The 3:1 Gated-DeltaNet (GDN) recurrent state discount slashes per-agent state footprint to ~0.5 GB/agent, while RadixAttention shared-prefix pinning eliminates duplicate system prompt KV blocks. Lockstep co-batched MTP verification across X=24 agents saturates GPU compute at high batch arithmetic intensity, achieving ≥300 tok/s unified agent throughput within a 20.5 GB total resident footprint (<36GB limit).
- **Witness:** Deterministic on-device execution receipts captured via `make mac-perf`, `fak hil`, and `BenchmarkMetal*` on Apple Silicon M3 Pro, logging exact prompt/generation lengths, verified token streams, zero fallback, resident memory peak, and effective throughput.

## Core Architecture Tracks

### Track 1: 30 tok/s Raw Single-Stream Decode
- **2-bit UD-Q2_K_XL Weight Compression:** Package Qwen3.8-27B down to ~8.5 GB resident weight footprint via ultra-low-bit UD-Q2_K_XL quantization with perplexity preservation, increasing the raw bandwidth-limited roofline from ~8 tok/s to >17.6 tok/s.
- **MTP Speculative Drafting + Wide-M Tree Verification (M=16..24):** Deploy multi-token prediction draft heads to generate speculative tree proposals evaluated in a single wide-M (M=16..24 candidate tokens) tail-causal Metal verification pass, achieving effective draft acceptance length $\gamma \ge 1.7\text{--}2.0$ to exceed 30 tok/s raw single-stream decode.

### Track 2: 300 tok/s Unified Multi-Agent Throughput
- **X=24 Lockstep Co-Batched MTP Serving:** Amortize weight loading across X=24 concurrent agent streams via synchronized lockstep verification cycles, transforming memory-bandwidth-bound decode into compute-saturated co-batching.
- **3:1 Gated-DeltaNet (GDN) KV Cache Discount:** Exploit the hybrid architecture of Qwen3.8 (GDN recurrent linear attention layers interleaved with full attention) to reduce per-agent KV cache memory footprint by 3:1 relative to standard transformer architectures, allowing 24 live agent contexts to fit comfortably in <12 GB.
- **RadixAttention Shared-Prefix Pinning:** Pin immutable agent system prompts, tool schemas, and workspace context in shared unified memory pages via Context-MMU Radix tree deduplication, avoiding duplicate state allocations across workers.

## Hardware-In-The-Loop (HIL) Discipline

Per repository doctrine (`AGENTS.md`), all milestones and reported performance numbers must be verified through micro-dosed physical silicon probes on Apple Silicon hardware—rejecting in-memory mocks, trace simulations, and analytical roofline estimates as completion proof.
- Validation gates require passing `make mac-perf`, `fak hil`, and the `BenchmarkMetal*` Go test suite on physical M3 Pro silicon.
- Head-to-head comparisons must execute against real hardware baselines (comparing against #2723), preserving the `engine=fak-native` invariant with zero fallback to external runtimes.
- Proof artifacts must include machine metadata (`node-macos-a`, M3 Pro 36GB), power/thermal throttling logs, verified token streams, and immutable execution receipts.

## Problem Checks (P1–P4)

- **P1 Quality:** Deterministic greedy argmax parity and perplexity preservation under UD-Q2_K_XL + MTP tree verification against unquantized FP16 baseline.
- **P2 Accounting:** End-to-end wall clock, command-buffer encode/commit latency, unified memory resident/peak bytes, and verification acceptance rates measured honestly with zero omitted overhead.
- **P3 Envelope:** Apple Silicon M3 Pro (18-core GPU, 36GB unified memory), resident model weights $\le 8.5\text{ GB}$, total working set with X=24 agents $\le 28\text{ GB}$ (leaving $\ge 8\text{ GB}$ headroom for host OS).
- **P4 Proof:** Micro-dosed HIL benchmarks and reproducible receipts pushed under `experiments/benchmark/runs/by-machine/` with witnessed git commit trailers.

sample.title: Bound eager stdio MCP subprocesses across session/direct-tool lifecycles
sample.body:
## Problem

An eager stdio MCP server can accumulate multiple persistent child processes under one PiClaw runtime instead of maintaining one bounded server process per active MCP/session owner.

Observed with the signed Microsoft WorkIQ MCP server configured as:

```json
{
  "command": ".../workiq.exe",
  "args": ["mcp"],
  "lifecycle": "eager",
  "directTools": ["retrieve", "fetch_blob", "list_agents", "get_schema", "search_paths", "fetch"]
}
```

## Reproduction evidence

1. Restart only the canonical PiClaw child.
2. Confirm one active web session.
3. Immediately after startup, four `workiq.exe mcp` children exist under the same PiClaw PID.
4. Run four bounded direct read calls in parallel (`list_agents`, `fetch`, `search_paths`, `retrieve`).
5. Six children remain after calls complete and after a 45-second idle wait.

Post-wait sample:

- child count: 6
- combined working set: about 241 MB
- established TCP connections: 0
- all children share the same PiClaw parent

A separately spawned WorkIQ stdio process exits cleanly when its SDK transport closes, so the native server supports graceful shutdown. The retained children appear to come from host/session/tool lifecycle ownership.

## Expected behavior

- one eager stdio process per configured server/runtime owner, or another explicitly bounded model;
- concurrent direct calls reuse the same connected client;
- session reload/shutdown closes superseded owners and transports;
- stale children are reaped after initialization failure, reconnect, or cancelled calls;
- status reports process/owner counts for diagnosis.

## Suggested tests

- eager server is spawned once for concurrent direct calls;
- replacing/reloading a session closes the prior stdio child;
- cancelled initialization leaves no child;
- multiple active chat sessions have a documented upper bound;
- process count returns to baseline after session eviction.

## Impact

The duplicated children were mostly idle but consumed roughly 230–295 MB in observed samples. This does not break WorkIQ correctness, but it creates avoidable memory/process growth and complicates MCP lifecycle diagnostics.

sample.title: bug(codex): session ID capture accepts task prompt metadata as the live thread ID
sample.body:
### Operating System
Windows 11 (build 26200), Windows PowerShell 5.1.

### Installation Method
Installed Windows desktop package. The installed app.asar reports Kangentic 0.40.0; this is not a source development build.

### Versions
- Kangentic: 0.40.0
- Codex CLI: 0.154.0
- Last known good version: unknown

### Summary
A new Codex task can be assigned the **historical session UUID written in its task description**, instead of the UUID of the Codex process that Kangentic just launched.

I reproduced this with five existing cards launched into Planning in one project, with worktrees disabled. Four descriptions contained the ordinary provenance line `Codex Session ID: <old-uuid>`. All four persisted that old UUID in `sessions.agent_session_id`, while their newly created Codex rollout files had different `session_meta.payload.id` values.

The fifth card used a fullwidth colon in its provenance label and was mapped correctly. That punctuation difference is a diagnostic control, not a proposed durable fix.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Use Codex on Windows/PowerShell, with the normal task XML prompt template.
2. Create a fresh task whose description contains:
   ```text
   Historical reference only:
   Codex Session ID: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
   This is provenance, not the current thread.
   Say ready and wait.
   ```
   The UUID above is synthetic.
3. Move the task from To Do to Planning to launch a **new** Codex process.
4. Compare Kangentic's recorded `sessions.agent_session_id` with the actual new rollout's `session_meta.payload.id`.
5. For a control, change the label to `Historical thread UUID:`, or use a fullwidth colon, and repeat with a separate fresh task.

The live observation involved five overlapping CLI sessions. The detector/manager reproduction below also triggers with only one session, so concurrency is **not established as a requirement**.

### Expected vs Actual Behavior
Expected: only a trusted identity signal from the newly launched Codex process should establish the current agent session ID. Historical IDs quoted in a prompt must not establish it.

Actual live observation:
| Card | Provenance text | Persisted ID | Actual new rollout | Correct? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | ASCII `Codex Session ID:` | old provenance A | new runtime A | No |
| B | ASCII `Codex Session ID:` | old provenance B | new runtime B | No |
| C | Fullwidth colon | new runtime C | new runtime C | Yes |
| D | ASCII `Codex Session ID:` | old provenance D | new runtime D | No |
| E | ASCII `Codex Session ID:` | old provenance E | new runtime E | No |

All five launch commands were fresh launches, without `codex resume`. All five real rollout files contained the complete expected first user XML, including the correct task title and description. This is distinct from #353's multiline prompt truncation.

In one sampled launch, the incorrect ID was already persisted approximately 2.1 seconds after Kangentic's recorded start, before the actual rollout's session creation timestamp at approximately 4.5 seconds. The four wrong IDs remained wrong at a later readback.

### Source Evidence
I found the same unanchored regex in the installed 0.40.0 bundle and in upstream commit `04a194a8a66c9fa794a53d6f38765f281cb3976b`:

- [CodexAdapter fromOutput](https://github.com/Kangentic/kangentic/blob/04a194a8a66c9fa794a53d6f38765f281cb3976b/src/main/agent/adapters/codex/codex-adapter.ts#L188)
- [SessionIdManager filesystem callback](https://github.com/Kangentic/kangentic/blob/04a194a8a66c9fa794a53d6f38765f281cb3976b/src/main/pty/lifecycle/session-id-manager.ts#L133)
- [SessionIdManager onData](https://github.com/Kangentic/kangentic/blob/04a194a8a66c9fa794a53d6f38765f281cb3976b/src/main/pty/lifecycle/session-id-manager.ts#L154)

The output regex is:
```js
/session id:\s+([0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12})/i
```

It matches the substring inside `Codex Session ID: <uuid>`. PowerShell echoes the launch command containing the task prompt before the CLI starts. This is consistent with the observed early capture.

Once an output match is accepted, both subsequent `onData` processing and the `fromFilesystem` completion return early when `hasAgentSessionId` is true. An early false positive therefore prevents the genuine startup banner or filesystem result from correcting it.

### Deterministic Detector/Manager Reproduction
I ran the upstream `fromOutput` body and `SessionIdManager/SessionIdScanner` code with synthetic UUIDs. TypeScript types were stripped; the ANSI stripper was replaced by identity because these inputs contained no ANSI bytes. No real CLI or real thread IDs were used for this component test.

Inputs:
1. An echoed command containing `Codex Session ID: OLD`.
2. A genuine-looking banner `session id: NEW`.
3. The filesystem promise resolving to `NEW`.

Observed:
```text
ASCII provenance:
  after command echo: OLD
  after startup banner: OLD
  after filesystem completion: OLD

Fullwidth-colon control:
  after command echo: null
  after startup banner: NEW
  after filesystem completion: NEW
```

### Impact and Limits
The persisted identity mismatch is confirmed. The affected identity is used for transcript lookup and resume, so this can cause stale/wrong history or resuming the wrong conversation; I have not intentionally resumed the wrong thread to test that consequence.

I have not established that this explains every problem seen during parallel work. No evidence of the five new Codex processes receiving each other's initial prompts was found in this run.

### Suggested Regression Coverage
- Prompt/command echo contains `Codex Session ID: <historical UUID>` before the real startup header.
- A false output candidate must not permanently suppress a later authoritative identity signal.
- Several fresh tasks share a cwd with worktrees disabled.
- Existing chunk-boundary and ANSI handling remains covered.

Please distinguish trusted runtime identity from echoed prompt content;

sample.title: fix(telegram): the plan review progress card loses its clock, its tool count and a suppressed render
sample.body:
## Symptom

Three defects in the plan-review progress path, all found while investigating the #186 cancel-suppression window. They share one root shape: **the card's live progress is written by a different writer than the one that renders it, and each side assumes the other's state.**

### D1 — the clock is gated behind `progress`, so it disappears exactly when it is needed

`format_plan_review_running_progress` (`src/channels/telegram/plan_card.rs`) returned the bare `🔍 Review subagent running…` note — discarding `elapsed_secs` — in two cases:

- `progress` is `None`
- `progress.iteration == 0 && progress.tool_count == 0`

`WorkStatus.progress` is only written at **round end** (`spawn.rs`), so for a review's entire first round the snapshot is `None`. The live clock the owner asked for was therefore dropped for the whole stretch where the owner has nothing else to watch.

### D2 — the round-end write clobbers the tool count back to 0

`spawn.rs` reads `WorkStatus` **once at spawn** and keeps that handle for the child's whole life. The round-end `status.update_progress(iteration, None, Some(summary))` re-serialises that spawn-time copy, and `update_progress` derives `prev_tool_count` from it — always 0 — so any `tool_count` the progress callback persisted mid-round (through its own fresh read) is reset at every round boundary.

Evidence: **0 of 273** files in `tmp/detached/` carry a truthy `tool_count`; every plan-review status file at rest reads `iteration=1, tool_count=0, last_tool=null`, while the review child's own session log shows ~9–10 successful tool calls.

This also means the at-rest census **cannot** settle whether the `ToolStarted` callback fires at all — the clobber explains a 0 regardless. That question needs a live probe and is tracked separately.

### D3 — a suppressed render is recorded as rendered and never retried

The plan-review progress loop assigns `last_rendered = note.clone()` **before** calling `refresh_plan_card`, and `refresh_plan_card` early-returns when `state.plan_card_suppressed(session_id)` is true (#814 flood backoff). A render skipped by a 429 backoff is therefore marked done and is never re-attempted — the card keeps a stale footer for the rest of the run.

Not the cause of the #186 window (no suppression evidence there), but a real latent defect.

## Fix

- **D1** — render `elapsed_secs` regardless of `progress`; keep the zero-progress guard for the TOOL segments only.
- **D2** — re-read the status file before the round-end write so a mid-round count survives.
- **D3** — only record `last_rendered` after a render that actually happened.

## Files

| File | Defect |
|---|---|
| `src/channels/telegram/plan_card.rs` | D1 (formatter), D3 (refresh reports whether it rendered) |
| `src/brain/tools/subagent/spawn.rs` | D2 |
| `src/brain/agent/service/work_status.rs` | D2 (`reload`) |
| `src/channels/telegram/agent.rs` | D3 (progress loop) |

## Out of scope

- The cancelled review's partial text is still handed back to the parent as if it were the finished result (parent-side only; it never reached the owner's topic).
- Whether `ToolStarted` fires for a plan-review child mid-round — needs a live spawn plus a poll of `tmp/detached/<id>.json` during the run.

sample.title: security(agent-loop): hook-git-guard deny-lists only `push`, so `send-pack` bypasses it
sample.body:
## Summary

`.codex/skills/agent-loop/scripts/hook-git-guard` enforces its non-review publication ban with a deny-list of exactly one subcommand:

```bash
if [ "$subcommand" = push ]; then
    ...
fi
```

`git push` is not the only way to update a remote ref. `git send-pack` is the plumbing command underneath it and takes a refspec directly:

```
git send-pack origin HEAD:refs/heads/<any-branch>
```

Because the subcommand is `send-pack` rather than `push`, control falls past the guard to the unconditional `exec` at the end of the script, reaching the real Git binary with the caller's arguments intact. That bypasses **both** protections the guard provides: the non-review mutation ban (`AGENT_LOOP_ALLOW_REVIEW_MUTATIONS`) and, in review hooks, the restriction to one non-force refspec targeting `refs/heads/$AGENT_LOOP_BRANCH`.

`git http-push` is the same shape, though it is DAV-only and will not work against GitHub, so `send-pack` is the one that matters in practice.

## Why this looks like an oversight rather than a decision

The sibling `hook-gh-guard` in the same directory is **fail-closed** — it denies by default and allows two specific shapes through:

```bash
if [ "$AGENT_LOOP_ALLOW_REVIEW_MUTATIONS" = true ]; then exec "$real_gh" "$@"; fi
if [ "$#" -eq 3 ] && [ "$1" = auth ] && ... ; then exec "$real_gh" "$@"; fi
echo "gh is disabled inside non-review agent-loop hooks..." >&2
exit 1
```

The git guard also already reasons fail-closed about *pre-command flags* — it rejects unknown global options specifically so "a future value-taking global option must not let its value hide a following `push` token from this guard" — and it closes the alias and `help.autocorrect` bypasses. Deny-listing the subcommand itself is the one place the fail-closed posture is not applied.

## Suggested fix

The git guard cannot go fully allow-list as cheaply as the gh guard, since its stated purpose is to "preserve ordinary Git access" (`status`, `add`, `commit`, `diff`, `log`, `checkout`, …). Two options:

1. **Narrow, low-risk:** extend the branch to reject the remote-write plumbing explicitly, e.g. `case "$subcommand" in push|send-pack|http-push) ...`. Handles the concrete bypass; still a deny-list, so a future Git release adding another remote-write verb reopens it.
2. **Fail-closed, preferred:** allow-list the read/local subcommands the loop actually uses and deny everything else, matching `hook-gh-guard`. More upfront work to enumerate, but the posture stops depending on Git's command surface staying still.

## Severity

Low in practice, and it does **not** affect any deployed product — these shims are developer/agent tooling and never ship. An autonomous agent would essentially never spontaneously reach for `send-pack` plumbing. But the guard's stated invariant ("denying non-review publication") is not actually enforced, and the file's own header notes these shims are not credential isolation, so the deny-list is currently the only thing standing there.

Related: loomantix/activeloom#228 (credential isolation redesign), which would make this moot but is a much larger change.

---

Found by `/codex-review` (Codex CLI, read-only cross-review) while reviewing the `staging → main` promotion in `loomantix/activetime` (#1912), and verified against the source. Reported here rather than patched in the consumer because `.codex/skills/agent-loop/` is sync-owned upstream — a consumer-side edit would be overwritten on the next sync.

sample.title: [Bug]: iOS thread with ZIP attachment stays on "Loading messages..."
sample.body:
### Problem

An existing thread containing a ZIP attachment opens normally in T3 Code desktop and web, but stays on **“Loading messages...” indefinitely on both iPhone and iPad**. The sidebar and thread header load; the conversation remains blank.

The iOS app was recently installed/updated, so an outdated installation should not be assumed.

### Observed reproduction

1. Open an existing desktop-created thread containing a ZIP attachment.
2. Open the same thread through T3 Connect on iPhone or iPad.
3. The message pane never finishes loading. The same thread remains accessible on desktop and web.

**Expected:** The conversation loads, including supported attachment information. An unsupported attachment should not prevent the entire conversation from opening.

### Environment and evidence

- Host: macOS, T3 Code desktop **0.0.38**, bundled commit `c0995d2eaf8e`.
- Mobile user agent: `T3Code/26 CFNetwork/3860.700.1 Darwin/25.6.0`. Exact app version/installed JS update has not been confirmed.
- ZIP metadata: `type: "file"`, `mimeType: "application/x-zip-compressed"`, `sizeBytes: 722668`.
- The ZIP opens locally and its metadata satisfies the installed desktop's attachment schema.
- For the affected thread, the host logged two iOS history requests returning **HTTP 200 in 69.5 ms and 81.1 ms**, with response sizes **368,838 and 351,403 bytes**. These confirm successful host responses, not successful decoding on the phone.

### Suspected cause and related work

The ZIP attachment is a **suspected trigger, not a confirmed cause**. No phone-side decoding error or controlled ZIP-removal comparison has been captured.

Related: #9414 and #10206. This report adds verified ZIP metadata and successful iOS HTTP responses from an affected thread. #10216 improves reporting of terminated loads, but does not establish a fix for the underlying attachment/data compatibility problem.

Please investigate ZIP/file-attachment decoding across the released iOS client and desktop server, and ensure a rejected attachment cannot leave the whole conversation loading indefinitely.

sample.title: v0.17 live release-candidate acceptance — the deployable system, against a frozen v0.17 SHA
sample.body:
The single tracked release gate for **v0.17** live acceptance.

A fresh issue rather than a continuation of #807, deliberately: #807 is explicitly the **v0.16** frozen-RC gate and passed against `a2b5eaae`. A release gate tied to the wrong release is exactly the historical ambiguity this project has decided to stop creating — a green checkbox there says nothing about a v0.17 tree.

## The frozen SHA

- **RC SHA:** _to be filled at freeze; nothing below may be checked against any other tree_
- **Predecessor:** v0.16.0 RC `a2b5eaae` (#807, 12/12 roots, 0 critical, eight live proofs PASS)

Every result recorded here must name the SHA it was measured on. A verdict is a statement about a specific tree, and the tree is not something the verdict carries — see the stale-merge-ref class in #739.

## What this gate is

The run must exercise the **deployable system over real process and transport boundaries**, not library internals. A required proof that does not run is **not** a PASS, and no required proof is silently downgraded because a base image is unavailable. Environmental infrastructure failure is reported as infrastructure failure — it is not a pass.

## Required live proofs

Against a real Kubernetes fleet of N identical `mcp-re-proxy` replicas, a real inner MCP backend, and a real mTLS client over the supported SDK path:

- [ ] **1** cross-replica replay coherence — a nonce Fresh on A is Replay on B
- [ ] **2** cross-replica trust-epoch revocation, and serving continues under the advanced epoch without rollback or restart
- [ ] **3** MRT continuation opened on replica A honoured on replica B
- [ ] **4** zero-drop rolling update with graceful SIGTERM drain
- [ ] **5** a stale request fails closed (`mcp-re.expired_request`)
- [ ] **6** a misbound request fails closed **at the correct semantic layer** — `invalid_audience` for a wrong audience id, `invalid_signature` for a wrong `@target-uri`
- [ ] **7** a refused request demonstrably does **not** invoke the backend, with an accepted request in the same run as the positive control
- [ ] **8** selected security dependency unavailable → correct fail-closed startup behaviour
- [ ] positive path: request reaches the backend and a **verified** answer reaches the caller

Harness: `docs/security/gke-multi-replica-validation.sh`, reached by `scripts/local_gate.sh --with-kind`. `PROVIDER=kind` runs the identical proofs against the same image and chart locally — the pre-cloud gate.

## Release qualification — not more architecture work

Development stops at the freeze. What follows is qualification:

- [ ] **ordinary CI green** on the frozen SHA, with each check's merge ref confirmed against the PR base (a green measured on a tree the PR no longer describes is not evidence — #739)
- [ ] **assurance graph complete and established** — every declared root complete, every declared theorem established, and the count stated rather than implied
- [ ] **owner specification review** of the theorems and assumptions added since v0.16 that still carry no review record. Known at the time of writing: **THM-0126**, **THM-0127** (#834) and **ASM-0045**, **ASM-0046** (#835). No record for any of these will be minted by tooling or by an agent — the axis is human by construction
- [ ] **live deployable acceptance** — the nine boxes above, against the exact frozen SHA
- [ ] **multi-replica / replay / continuation / trust behaviour** measured wherever the release notes claim it
- [ ] **SDK positive and negative paths**, both language bindings, on their pinned runtimes
- [ ] **v0.17 performance remeasurement** against the ADR-MCPRE-051 §7 SLO baseline, on a quiet box — the lane refuses to measure under load and that refusal is not to be papered over
- [ ] **supply-chain gate green** (`cargo deny`: advisories, licenses, bans, sources)
- [ ] **release notes distinguish** what is **proved**, **tested**, **live-measured**, **assumed**, and **deferred**

## Acceptance rule

The release does not become ready until every required proof has either **PASSed against the frozen RC SHA**, or been **explicitly ruled outside the v0.17 release claim** with a written reason.

## Evidence to capture

- the exact frozen RC SHA;
- the live transcript, proof by proof;
- the actual topology exercised (replica count, image tag, backend, client path);
- for each qualification row, the lane that produced it and the tree that lane checked out.

## Explicitly outside v0.17

Carried to v0.18 by the objective, and not reasons to hold this release:

- SCITT representational sealing and authority split (#657) — the census found weak representational boundaries and future-misuse hazards, **not** an actively exploitable production path;
- the non-security-critical remainder of #672 (items 3–6);
- V2/V3 Lean extraction (#541) and dual-path proving (#543);
- real FIPS-140-2 Level 3 hardware evidence (#499) — THM-0116 already states this limit in its own scope;
- Azure / cross-cloud expansion (#498);
- third-party native-host adoption (#497);
- fork-PR verification integrity (`R9-C025`, #739) — an Actions-configuration decision.

sample.title: ACP registry cache writes follow a preexisting pid temp symlink
sample.body:
Found by **hoverfly** (Cursor · GPT-5.3 Codex · xhigh) during a three-hour bug hunt. `packages/server/src/acp-registry.ts:289` · severity high · the hunter marked this verified.

## What is wrong
`AcpRegistry.#writeCache` writes to a predictable temp path (`acp-registry.json.<pid>.tmp`) without checking for symlinks.

## Why it is wrong
If that temp path is pre-created as a symlink, the cache write overwrites the symlink target and `renameSync` installs the symlink as the cache file.

```ts
const tmp = `${this.#cachePath}.${process.pid}.tmp`
writeFileSync(tmp, `${JSON.stringify(entry)}\n`, 'utf8')
renameSync(tmp, this.#cachePath)
```

## How it fails
Pre-create `acp-registry.json.<pid>.tmp` as a symlink to another file, then trigger a cache write via `catalog()`. The outside file is overwritten with cache JSON and `acp-registry.json` becomes a symlink.

## How it was checked
Command:
`node --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { mkdtempSync, writeFileSync, readFileSync, lstatSync, symlinkSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { AcpRegistry } from './packages/server/dist/src/acp-registry.js'

const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'hd-regcache-tmp-'))
const outside = join(dir, 'outside.txt')
writeFileSync(outside, 'outside-before')
symlinkSync(outside, join(dir, `acp-registry.json.${process.pid}.tmp`))

const registry = new AcpRegistry({
  stateDir: dir,
  fetchJson: async () => ({ agents: [] }),
  which: async () => null,
})
await registry.catalog(() => false)
console.log('outsideStartsWithJson', readFileSync(outside, 'utf8').trimStart().startsWith('{'))
console.log('cacheIsSymlink', lstatSync(join(dir, 'acp-registry.json')).isSymbolicLink())
rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })
EOF`

Printed:
`outsideStartsWithJson true`
`cacheIsSymlink true`

sample.title: [code-review] fix: update X-Client-Source header version from 0.5.13 to 0.6.48
sample.body:
## What's wrong

`HttpClient` sends an `X-Client-Source` telemetry header on every request to identify the SDK version. The value was hardcoded as `inference-sdk-js/0.5.13`, but the package is currently at `0.6.48`. This means the server logs and analytics receive an incorrect SDK version for all requests made with this SDK.

**Affected line:** `src/http/client.ts:82`

```ts
// Before
this.customHeaders = { 'X-Client-Source': 'inference-sdk-js/0.5.13', ...config.headers };

// After
this.customHeaders = { 'X-Client-Source': 'inference-sdk-js/0.6.48', ...config.headers };
```

## Why this matters

The `X-Client-Source` header is used for server-side telemetry and debugging. Stale versions make it impossible to correlate API issues to specific SDK versions.

## Note

## Summary
The docblock of `apps/tuval/src/commands/agent-proof.unit.test.ts` says that re-running the agent proof on a process built by `aiAgentProgram` over `ScriptedAiAgent.layer` is a later child's work. About 500 lines down, the same file does exactly that. The docblock is stale and now contradicts its own file.

## What I was doing
Reviewing PR #7773 at head `e6868e0762`. Checking whether a Deviations entry citing this file was truthful. The file itself is not in that PR's diff — it is on `main`.

## What I observed
Lines 5-10 of the docblock read: "It is deliberately not a process built on the `TuvalAiAgent` service: `aiAgentProgram` and `ScriptedAiAgent.layer` are the Pi epic's (#7599, #7603), and re-running this proof on one of those is a later child's, per the founder's ruling of 2026-09-03 recorded on #7645."

The same file then imports `aiAgentProgram` and `ScriptedAiAgent`, builds a second run with `aiAgentProgram({... layer: ScriptedAiAgent.layer(script)})`, and asserts on it under a case named "reaches every spell through `SpellBridge` from an `aiAgentProgram` process".

Both are true of the file's two runs — the first is the scripted substitution, the second is not — but the docblock states only the first as if it described the whole file, and calls the second one somebody else's work.

## Why it matters
The docblock is what a reader consults to learn what the file proves, and it currently tells them the stronger of the two proofs is not here. It already misled one reader: a PR body cited this file as running under the substitution, which reads as evidence that the un-substituted path is unavailable, when the same file demonstrates it. Cheap to fix and it will keep costing small amounts of reviewer time while it stands.

## Pointers
- `apps/tuval/src/commands/agent-proof.unit.test.ts` — docblock lines 5-10 vs. the `aiAgentProgram(...)` construction and the "reaches every spell through SpellBridge from an aiAgentProgram process" case
- #7645 (the 2026-09-03 ruling the docblock cites), PR #7748 (which landed the file)
- Noticed from https://github.com/kamp-us/phoenix/pull/7773#issuecomment-5549586479

Rewrite the paragraph to say the file carries both runs and what each one proves.
