sample.title: Harden station issue actions and restart recovery
sample.body:
## Parent

#187 Add RTS-style agent station view for workflow visibility

## Outcome

Make station issue actions and history durable, authenticated, bounded, and correct across service and browser restarts.

## Scope

- Add dismiss, address, and resolve mutations with explicit actor/project/run/station checks and bounded action text.
- Preserve the issue's chronological attempted-resolution history and active-alert behavior without timeout or silent clearing.
- Prove restart-safe API/browser readback and one end-to-end run moving across stations before resolving an issue.

Not included: automatic retries, workflow-state mutation beyond issue actions, real-time transport, or simulation behavior.

## Implementation notes

- Owns the fixing and reliability category for #187 on the shared parent branch and PR.
- Reuse existing authenticated dashboard action handlers, persistence transactions, redaction, and lifecycle fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dismiss hides the active alert while preserving the issue record and history.
- [ ] Address records an attempted resolution; resolve closes the issue as fixed with the full history retained.
- [ ] Unauthorized, stale, mismatched, or oversized actions fail closed without changing issue state.
- [ ] Issue state and attempts reload correctly after service/browser restart and remain visible until an explicit action.
- [ ] An end-to-end browser scenario observes state-derived station movement and resolves a persisted issue.

## Verification

- Add unit/API tests for each action, authorization, stale identity, bounds, ordering, restart persistence, and safe error readback.
- Add browser/E2E coverage for persistent alerts, action feedback, reload, station movement, and resolution.
- Run the focused new suite plus existing dashboard lifecycle, projection, and session persistence regressions.

sample.title: Run the full validation and portable hotkey suite on macOS, Windows, and Linux
sample.body:
## Goal

Run BrunoTable's complete deterministic validation matrix on real GitHub-hosted Linux, Windows, and macOS runners, and prove that portable `Mod` shortcuts behave as `Control` on Windows/Linux and `Meta` (Command) on macOS.

This follows #75. It must use `@tanstack/react-hotkeys` as the public React integration and its re-exported `resolveModifier` utility for platform-aware test input. Do not duplicate modifier resolution in BrunoTable or scatter operating-system `if/else` branches through tests.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **USER-MERGE-ONLY:** An agent may implement, validate, review, push, and open/update the PR, but it must never merge it or enable auto-merge. **@bmvantunes will inspect and merge this PR personally.**

## Dependency

- Blocked by #75. Rebase on the merge commit that lands the TanStack React Hotkeys Adapter before implementation.
- Do not recreate or bypass the adapter introduced by #75.

## Required design

### Cross-platform GitHub Actions matrix

Create the repository CI workflow needed to run on:

- `ubuntu-latest`
- `windows-latest`
- `macos-latest`

Every runner must exercise the repository's complete deterministic validation surface:

- formatting/lint/type checking;
- Node logic tests;
- Playwright-backed Vitest Browser Mode source tests;
- package builds;
- emitted-package type and runtime/browser consumer tests;
- export/tarball/output guards and other deterministic package checks already required by the repository.

Do not silently skip a suite on one operating system. If a check is genuinely machine-dependent or unsuitable for hosted runners (for example, a timing benchmark), document the reason in the workflow/PR and keep the functional regression coverage cross-platform. No platform exception is accepted merely because setup is inconvenient.

Use Vite+ commands and the repository's pinned package/runtime setup. Cache only data that is safe to share for the exact platform and lockfile.

### Portable shortcut tests

- Keep shortcut definitions portable through the `Mod` abstraction supplied by TanStack Hotkeys.
- Use `resolveModifier` from `@tanstack/react-hotkeys` (it re-exports the Hotkeys core API) in shared Vitest Browser Mode helpers to resolve the modifier for the current test platform.
- The same test body must run on Linux, Windows, and macOS. Do not add repeated `process.platform === ...`, user-agent checks, or per-OS copies of shortcut tests.
- Prove at minimum that:
  - Copy resolves to and responds to `Control+C` on Windows/Linux.
  - Copy resolves to and responds to `Meta+C` (Command+C) on macOS.
  - The non-native counterpart does not accidentally activate the command on each platform.
- Apply the same portable helper to every BrunoTable-owned `Mod` shortcut covered by the suite, not only Copy.
- Preserve native-input, portal, IME/composition, AltGr/Option, repeat, scope, Strict Mode, remount, and cleanup behavior established by #75.

### Browser-test rules

- DOM/interaction coverage runs only in real Playwright-backed Vitest Browser Mode.
- Do not install or use JSDOM, happy-dom, React Testing Library, `getByTestId`, or synthetic platform branches.
- Prefer accessible role/name locators.
- Keep React Compiler enabled and verify emitted-package behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A GitHub Actions OS matrix runs on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS.
- [ ] All deterministic repository checks pass on all three runners.
- [ ] Browser Mode launches successfully on all three hosted operating systems.
- [ ] One shared platform-aware helper uses TanStack's `resolveModifier`; BrunoTable contains no second modifier interpreter.
- [ ] Shared tests prove Ctrl shortcuts on Windows/Linux and Command shortcuts on macOS, including rejection of the wrong modifier.
- [ ] Existing hotkey lifecycle, ownership, accessibility, and performance guarantees remain green.
- [ ] No JSDOM, happy-dom, React Testing Library, test IDs, Babel fallback, or manual hotkey parser is introduced.
- [ ] Workflow cancellation/concurrency prevents stale commits from consuming the full three-OS matrix unnecessarily.
- [ ] Required checks expose clear per-OS names so a failure identifies the affected runner and suite.
- [ ] Documentation records how contributors run the equivalent local validation and how `Mod` is resolved in tests.
- [ ] The repository's complete local three-axis convergence gate is clean at the final head.
- [ ] GitHub Codex and CodeRabbit review the exact final head, subject only to the repository's documented rate-limit exception.
- [ ] The PR remains open for @bmvantunes to merge manually; no agent merges it.

## Primary references

- TanStack Hotkeys `resolveModifier`: https://tanstack.com/hotkeys/latest/docs/reference/functions/resolveModifier
- TanStack React Hotkeys package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tanstack/react-hotkeys
- Vitest Browser Mode: https://vitest.dev/guide/browser/
- GitHub-hosted runners: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-github-hosted-runners/about-github-hosted-runners

## Review focus

Reviewers must explicitly inspect:

1. whether the test helper delegates platform resolution to TanStack rather than reimplementing it;
2. whether the macOS job generates real `metaKey` evidence and Windows/Linux generate real `ctrlKey` evidence;
3. whether the wrong modifier is rejected;
4. whether every deterministic suite truly runs on all three operating systems;
5. whether the PR is still unmerged and auto-merge remains disabled.

sample.title: Nothing detects two concurrent Meta reservations of the same Alembic number before merge
sample.body:
Found by doing it wrong. Filed as a harness-process gap, separate from #2019/#2032 and #1701, both of which behaved correctly.

## What happened

On 2026-09-16 two migrations independently claimed revision **061**, both chained off `060_processed_events_epoch`:

- `061_credential_owner_enumeration` (#2019, merged as #2032)
- `061_workflow_and_subject` (#1701)

A forked Alembic history. Caught only when PR #2027 went `CONFLICTING` — which also silently prevented CI from running at all, since GitHub computes `pull_request` runs against a merge commit that cannot exist while a PR conflicts. So the first symptom was not "your migration collides", it was "no checks appear", which took a false webhook-anomaly diagnosis and a wasted re-trigger commit to see through.

## Why it happened, and why the current rule does not prevent it

CLAUDE.md and the slice configs are emphatic and correct: *migration numbers are assigned by Meta, never read from head.* Both slices followed that rule. The rule still does not prevent the collision, because a Meta reservation is derived from `main` plus **open PRs** — and a sibling session's work is invisible until its PR opens.

Two sessions reserving from the same `main` reserve the same number, and nothing detects it until one of them conflicts. Neither agent did anything wrong; the mechanism has no cross-session coordination.

This is not hypothetical any more and will recur whenever two sessions work this repo concurrently, which is now normal.

## Shape of a fix

Options, roughly in order of cost:

- **Detect at CI time.** A cheap gate that fails when the branch introduces a migration whose `down_revision` is already claimed by another revision on `main`, or when `alembic heads` resolves to more than one head. A forked chain is mechanically detectable and today nothing looks for it.
- **Detect at reservation time.** `meta_prepare_executor.py` could read sibling worktrees (`git worktree list`, `.worktrees/issue-*`) and warn when another tree holds an unmerged migration.
- **Make numbers non-colliding.** A monotonic reservation ledger committed to `main`, or dropping sequential prefixes for the hash-style revision ids Alembic natively supports.

The first is the one that actually closes the failure mode, because it does not depend on any agent remembering to look.

## Acceptance criteria

1. GIVEN a branch adding a migration whose `down_revision` is already claimed by a different revision on `main`
   WHEN CI runs
   THEN it fails, naming both revisions
   Observable at: `.github/workflows/pr.yml`
   Verified by: a test in `tests/unit/`

2. GIVEN a branch whose migrations resolve to more than one Alembic head after merging `main`
   WHEN CI runs
   THEN it fails, naming the heads
   Observable at: the migration-check job
   Verified by: a test in `tests/unit/`

3. GIVEN a branch with a single clean chain
   WHEN CI runs
   THEN the check passes and adds no measurable time to the job
   Verified by: a test in `tests/unit/`

## Note

`agent-runtime/artifacts/release-evidence-plan-issue-1701.json` still records "061 is RESERVED BY META... no other in-flight branch adds a migration". That was true when written and is stale now. It is deliberately left unedited as a historical planning record — rewriting a Meta-authored planning artifact after the fact would destroy the evidence of how the collision happened.

Refs #1701, #2019, #2032

sample.title: feat: wire the analysis cache into the BBA parallel analyzer
sample.body:
## Problem

`agents/black-box-analyzer/scripts/parallel_analyzer.py` advertises incremental caching that it does not perform.

- `AnalysisCache` is imported, but only to service `--clear-cache`
- `use_cache` is accepted as a parameter, documented in the docstring, and passed in from the CLI as `not args.no_cache` — then never read
- `--no-cache` therefore changes nothing

Three e2e tests already specify the intended behaviour and are marked skipped with the reason "Cache integration not yet implemented in parallel_analyzer":

- `tests/e2e/test_end_to_end.py::test_incremental_cache`
- `tests/e2e/test_end_to_end.py::test_cache_invalidation_on_file_change`
- `tests/e2e/test_end_to_end.py::test_clear_cache_flag`

## Functional intent

Re-analysing an unchanged project should reuse the previous result rather than re-running the whole pipeline. Editing a file must invalidate that file's cached entry, so a stale result is never served. `--no-cache` must force a full analysis and `--clear-cache` must discard everything.

## Scope

- Read the cache before dispatching a file for analysis; write the result after
- Honour `use_cache` so `--no-cache` is meaningful
- Invalidate on file content change, consistent with the content-hash keying CCA and SSA already use
- Un-skip the three tests

## Notes

Two of the three tests assert on elapsed run time. If that proves flaky, prefer asserting on cache hit counts over wall-clock duration.

Blocks #16: that PR reports the three skips, and this issue is intended to merge first so the repository reaches zero failures and zero skips.

sample.title: Canvas can skip sessions when paging from the sidebar cache
sample.body:
## Problem

Canvas can omit sessions until a later refresh even after background pagination finishes. The large-page speedup is on main, but the first `sessions.listPage` call can still return the sidebar's mutable display cache and derive a server continuation cursor from its last row.

That cache is not necessarily a contiguous prefix of the server's ordering: live updates can insert older watched rows, and loaded pages can overlap.

## Reproduction

On main `3c42e8298`:

1. Canonical newest-first order is `A, B, C, D`.
2. The sidebar cache contains `A, D` and reports more rows.
3. An extension requests a two-row first page. The host returns `A, D` with cursor `D`.
4. Continuing after `D` returns nothing. `B, C` are never loaded.

Expected: cached rows may paint immediately, but authoritative pagination starts from the beginning of the server list and returns every session exactly once.

## Proposed fix

Separate the optional cached preview from canonical session pages. Canvas should merge preview and fetched rows by ID while loading, then use the completed authoritative list to remove stale preview-only rows. Preserve the 1,000-row background batches.

sample.title: A QA companion: scenarios in markdown, runs and ratings in a local web UI, results in the repo
sample.body:
## Why

`e2e/LIVE-TEST.md` is 303 lines and 61 table rows: a script one person follows by hand against a real model and a real install, pasting eighteen numbered prompts, opening JSON files in an editor, and writing ✓ or ✗ into a single Result column with no date, no run and no history. Thirteen rows have ever been filled in; the money tables the file calls "the test's real output" are empty. It hard-codes `lamplit-0.1.0` in two places. The problem is not the content, which is good, but the medium: a text file is the wrong place to run a test and the wrong place to keep its results.

The automated suites already prove what a machine can prove (128 e2e tests against a fake model, 233 unit tests). What is left is the part only a person can judge — does the app feel right, does it look right, does the real model tell a decent story in every mode — and that judgement wants a place to play freely, note things as they are noticed, rate what was read, and keep the record. Nothing existing fits: UnitTCMS is GPL, Docker, login-only and database-backed with no export; Kiwi TCMS heavier still; Testspace is paid SaaS with results on their side; the markdown-to-GitHub generators are command-line only. A Playwright-driven live run was proposed and rejected: it forces an order and a terminal, and its scenarios would duplicate the automated ones instead of covering what they cannot. So this is a small tool of our own, a dev-ops artefact never shipped to users.

## What to do

**A QA companion: `npm run qa`**, a `qa/` workspace in the repo.

**Scenarios are markdown files** in `qa/scenarios/`, one per area, with a little front matter (`id`, `title`, `area`, `time`, `needs` such as a real model or a phone) and a list of steps. Each step says what to do and what to look for; a step may carry a `rating:` line naming what is rated (prose, look and feel, responsiveness, summary quality) on 1–5 with a note. The rubrics from the current file move in verbatim as rating steps. A free-form **exploratory charter** template has only a mission, a time box and a notes area, for playing around. An agent writes and extends scenarios like any other file; the format is documented at the top of `qa/README.md` in twenty lines.

Starting set: first run and connection (the look of onboarding); a narrator story end to end (today's journey, with the chaptered-versus-long-chat cost comparison as an optional block computed from the token counts the app already shows when `showTokenCounts` is on); a cast story in both role-play modes with switching and a cast event; world and lore proposals on chapter close; the reading experience across palettes, themes and fonts; author directions and voice; preferences and customisation; upgrade notice and What's new; the phone (once #20 exists); the blank charter. `e2e/LIVE-TEST.md` retires; `tools/smoke.mjs` stays as the way to get a fresh packaged install running, and the first scenario tells you to use it.

**The UI is a local web page** in Lamplit's own visual language (the colour tokens copied from `styles.scss`), free of any forced order:

- Home: the scenarios with their last verdict, and past runs.
- Run: pick a scenario, the tool stamps the run with version, build and commit read from the running app's `/api/health` (URL asked once, remembered), plus model and provider typed in. The step list on the left, the current step on the right with verdict (pass / fail / skip), rating where the step asks for one, a notes box, and paste-a-screenshot. Jump anywhere, leave a run half done, come back to it.
- Report: a button on any step that opens a prefilled GitHub new-issue page (title, the step, your note, the build number, the `bug` label) — issues stay the one channel.
- History: scenarios against runs, verdicts and rating trends, folder size per run.

**Stack: Preact + htm, no bundler.** Components, hooks and a virtual DOM in ~4 KB, JSX-shaped tagged templates without a build step; ES modules served straight from `node_modules` by the QA server, so it works offline and needs no config. State in one `@preact/signals` store; all mutations through one API module. `marked` (already in the workspace) renders the scenario markdown. One file per component, one stylesheet. Server: a small Express app like Lamplit's, with routes for scenarios, runs, images and the snapshot; `node --test` for the markdown parser and the run store.

**Persistence: plain files in the repo, written by the server** with the same temp-file-and-rename pattern as `server/src/store.js`. Every verdict, rating or note is posted to the server the moment it is entered. One folder per run:

```
qa/runs/2026-09-12-narrator-story/
  run.json      who, when, build/version/commit, model, provider,
                per-step verdict + rating + note + timestamps, overall notes
  scenario.md   the scenario file as it was on that day
  images/       pasted screenshots, PNG, downscaled to the viewport at 1x
  snapshot/     settings.json (key removed), stories/*.json, chapters/*.json
                copied from the app's data folder when the run is ended
```

The scenario copy keeps old runs readable after scenarios change. The snapshot is the evidence: the prose the model wrote sits next to the rating it got, and the eight "open the JSON in an editor" steps disappear. The API key is stripped before the copy is written. History is computed from the `run.json` files on startup; there is no index to go stale. The tool shows which runs are not yet committed but never runs git: a run is committed like a screenshot. Browser storage and GitHub as the store were both rejected: the data belongs in the repo.

**Docs**: `docs/development.md` gets a short "The QA companion" section; `qa/README.md` holds the scenario format and the folder layout.

## Depends on

- Nothing hard. Best after #17 so the narrator scenario describes the composer that will ship; the phone scenario waits for #20.

## Acceptance

- `npm run qa` opens the page; with the app runni

sample.title: water doctor does not detect outdated libva/libpipewire versions on Ubuntu 22.04
sample.body:
## Summary

`water doctor` on Ubuntu 22.04 reports Linux system packages as OK, but `cargo build` of the workspace still fails because the installed `libva` and `libpipewire`/`libspa` packages are too old for the `cros-libva` and `libspa-sys` crates that WaterUI's media stack depends on.

The current `LinuxSystemToolchain::check` only verifies that the package is installed via `dpkg-query -W`, not that the version satisfies the header/API requirements of the transitive Rust dependencies.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
- WaterUI branch: `dev`
- Rust: 1.98.1
- Installed packages:
  - `libva-dev` 2.14.0 (provides VA-API headers)
  - `libpipewire-0.3-dev` 0.3.48
  - `libspa-0.2-dev` 0.3.48

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a fresh Ubuntu 22.04 machine, install the dependencies listed in `AGENTS.md` / `setup-linux-deps`:
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get install libgtk-4-dev libasound2-dev libva-dev \
       libfontconfig1-dev libgbm-dev libegl-dev libxcb1-dev \
       libglib2.0-dev libpango1.0-dev libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
       libpipewire-0.3-dev libudev-dev
   ```
2. Run `water doctor` (or just the Linux system packages check).
3. Run `cargo check -p waterui-cli` or any example that pulls in the default `media` feature.

## Observed behavior

`water doctor` reports `Linux system packages` and `GTK4` as OK. Then the build fails in two places:

### 1. `cros-libva` expects `libva` ≥ 2.19 / VA-API 1.19+

```text
error[E0061]: this function takes 15 arguments but 18 arguments were supplied
   --> cros-libva-0.0.12/src/buffer/av1.rs:606:13

error[E0560]: struct `_VAEncPictureParameterBufferAV1` has no field named `refresh_frame_flags`
   --> cros-libva-0.0.12/src/buffer/av1.rs:1086:13
```

`cros-libva`'s `build.rs` does emit `cfg(libva_1_19_or_higher)`, but the `Default::default()` argument after the `#[cfg(libva_1_19_or_higher)] mono_chrome` argument is not conditionally compiled, so the code path does not work with the old headers. More importantly, the bindgen-generated `new_bitfield_1` expects the newer structure fields that Ubuntu 22.04's `libva` 2.14 does not provide.

### 2. `libspa` expects newer PipeWire/libspa headers

After upgrading `libva` to 2.22.0 manually, the next blocker is `libspa-sys 0.10.1` against the Ubuntu 22.04 `libpipewire-0.3` / `libspa-0.2` 0.3.48 headers:

```text
error[E0425]: cannot find function `spa_meta_region_is_valid` in crate `spa_sys`

error[E0425]: cannot find function `spa_meta_first` in crate `spa_sys`

error[E0560]: struct `spa_video_info_raw` has no field named `flags`

error[E0609]: no field `flags` on type `spa_video_info_raw`

error[E0308]: mismatched types
   --> libspa-0.10.1/src/param/video/raw.rs:266:27
    |
266 |         self.0.modifier = modifier;
    |         ---------------   ^^^^^^^^ expected `i64`, found `u64`
```

## Expected behavior

`water doctor` should detect that the installed `libva` and `libpipewire`/`libspa` versions are too old and report the problem, ideally with an actionable message like:

```text
libva: installed 2.14.0, need ≥ 2.19.0
libpipewire: installed 0.3.48, need ≥ 0.3.x
```

It currently only checks presence, not version, so the failure surfaces much later during `cargo build`.

## Suggested fix

In `cli/src/toolchain/linux.rs`, extend `LinuxSystemToolchain::check` to query the minimum required versions for packages that have version-sensitive Rust bindings, e.g.:

- `pkg-config --modversion libva` and require ≥ 2.19.0
- `pkg-config --modversion libpipewire-0.3` and require a version that satisfies `libspa-sys 0.10.1` (which expects the newer `spa_video_info_raw` and meta APIs)

This can reuse the existing `ToolchainError` machinery:
- If the package is missing or too old, report `Missing` (manual) with the installed vs. required versions.
- If the package manager can provide a newer version, mark it `Fixable`; otherwise mark it `Unfixable` and explain that the distro is too old.

## Workaround used

To get WaterUI running at all, I disabled the `media`/`assets` feature chain and used the `dew` CPU backend (`waterui-dew` with `embedded-simulator` and `system-fonts`). That avoids `cros-libva` and `libspa` entirely, but it is not a general solution for users who want the GPU backend or media examples.

sample.title: chore: P3 backlog from the 2026-09-12 repository review
sample.body:
### Objective

Backlog of lower-severity findings from the 2026-09-12 repository review. None are included in the v1.5.0 validation-correctness milestone; they are recorded here so they are not lost.

### Scope of Changes

1. **Stale token figures.** The repository's own `scripts/measure-tokens.sh` measures `templates/agent-directive-template.md` at 100 lines / 7,680 characters, reporting `~1920 tokens` and `~90% reduction`. The documentation claims three different numbers:

   | Location | Claimed tokens | Claimed reduction |
   | :--- | :--- | :--- |
   | `README.md:23`, `README.md:297` | ~1,944 | ~89.5% |
   | `docs/BENCHMARKS.md:16,22,24,40` | ~1,944 | ~89.5% |
   | `docs/BENCHMARKS.md:94` | ~1,934 | ~89.5% |
   | `measure-tokens.sh` (measured) | ~1,920 | ~90% |

   Refresh the figures from the tool and add a footnote stating the measurement method, so the claim stays verifiable.

2. **Property harnesses are not in CI.** `grep -c properties .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns `0`. `run-execution-control-properties.sh` (5 properties x 100 iterations) and `run-release-record-properties.sh` (12 properties x 100 iterations) both pass locally and are the strongest safety net in the repository, but they run manually only. Both complete in under a minute combined, so the cost of adding them is low.

3. **`local x="$(cmd)"` masks exit status (SC2155 x22).** 21 of the 22 occurrences are in `scripts/validate-execution-control.sh`. This matters more than usual in a validator whose purpose is detecting failure.

4. **Inconsistent executable bits.** `init.sh`, `validate-execution-control.sh`, `run-behavioral-contract-tests.sh`, and `run-execution-control-fixtures.sh` are mode `755`; the other eleven `.sh` files are `644`. Harmless because everything is documented as `bash script.sh`, but arbitrary. Consider normalizing to `644` with `init.sh` the sole exception, since the README instructs `./.promptkit/init.sh`.

5. **Unquoted expansion in `init.sh:139`.** `"${SCRIPT_DIR#$PROJECT_ROOT/}"` leaves `$PROJECT_ROOT` unquoted inside the prefix strip, so glob metacharacters in a directory name would misbehave. Low probability; quoted separately it is a one-character-class fix.

### Context

ShellCheck 0.11.0 over all fifteen `.sh` files reports **0 errors, 36 warnings, 30 notes**, so none of the above is currently broken.

### Verification Plan

- `bash scripts/measure-tokens.sh`
- `bash scripts/tests/run-execution-control-properties.sh`
- `bash scripts/tests/run-release-record-properties.sh`
- `shellcheck init.sh scripts/*.sh scripts/tests/*.sh`

sample.title: An ended Claude session keeps its pane id, so its run can still address a reused pane
sample.body:
Found by the security reviewer while reviewing #119 (issue #98). Pre-existing on `main`; #119 deliberately did not change it, because fixing it changes how an ended session's card composes and that is a design decision of its own.

## What is wrong

`hook/hook.go` `apply()` sets `State = StateEnded` on `SessionEnd` but never clears `tmux_session/window/pane`, and nothing deletes the state file — `hub` drops a session only on an fsnotify Remove. So:

- `paneGone` (`runs/hooksource.go`) never fires: the pane is still listed, it is just running something else now.
- `paneForeign` never fires either: same tmux server, and the state postdates its start.
- The hooks layer therefore keeps publishing a run keyed on that physical pane id indefinitely, `runs/tmuxsource.go` publishes a layer for the same key, and `deriveCaps` (`runs/registry.go`) grants `Terminal`/`Kill`/`Reply` from layer presence alone.

## Why it matters

Opening that ended session's card from history (or a stale tab, or `/api/runs/:id`) can send keystrokes into whatever now occupies the pane — an unrelated shell, another tool, another agent. Same class as #98, reached by pane reuse after `SessionEnd` rather than by a resume.

## Options

Treat `hook.StateEnded` like a distrusted pane in `runs/hooksource.go`'s `build()` (strip the coordinates before the key is derived), or clear them in `apply()` on `SessionEnd`, or have `deriveCaps` refuse to grant caps through a hooks layer whose own state is `StateDone`. The first is smallest; the tradeoff is that an ended session's card stops inheriting the window's branch/codename chips.

Parent: #98. PR that surfaced it: #119.

sample.title: An Analytics surface — and the one decision that splits it into two different Issues
sample.body:
# An Analytics surface — the owner's ask, and the one decision that splits it into two different Issues

**Owner ask, 2026-09-11, verbatim:**

> «as metricas do nosso GA poderiam virar uma sessao do site Analytics. assim demonstro minha competencia e consigo ler as metricas de uma forma mais agradavel para meu proprio entendimento. Agrego meu tom critico sobre como eu gosto de acompanhar analytics de plataformas digitais. Agrega a defesa do meu perfil profissional.»

`product` · `reader-facing`. **Intake run 2026-09-11 against `-io` `origin/main` = `3f7c7d6`**, both leads dispatched in isolation. **`ready` is NOT applied** — one decision is the owner's and the description cannot close without it.

<!-- owner-take: supplied -->
> «Agrego meu tom critico sobre como eu gosto de acompanhar analytics de plataformas digitais.»

---

## THE DECISION THIS ISSUE IS WAITING ON

**Does this page carry GA4's FIGURES, or what the repository knows about its OWN MEASUREMENT?**

Both leads reached this independently and neither will decide it. They are **different Issues with different preconditions**, and describing them as one is `/definition-of-ready`'s flagship failure arriving at filing time:

- **the numbers page** — GA4 counts. Needs a credential decision, a generator, a staleness answer, and a new record.
- **the schema page** — what is emitted, what each measurement can and cannot establish, what is deliberately not concluded. **Buildable today, no credential, no network.**

Everything below is downstream of that one answer.

---

## The ask is THREE artifacts under one name, and the split is clean

| his reason | what actually serves it | on this site? |
|---|---|---|
| **read the metrics pleasantly, for himself** | **`-skills#401`** — the funnel rite, `ready`, `sp:8`, already queued | **no.** A published page is a *worse* tool than the console he already has: the console is live, the page is a transcription with a staleness clock |
| **demonstrate competence** | a published argument, his numbers as the worked example | **yes** |
| **his critical tone + the professional case** | the same artifact | **yes** |

**Purpose 2 gets an explicit no.** A page that serves him must update often; a page that serves a reader must age well. Those are opposite requirements on one file, and every design satisfying both lands on a dashboard stale for him *and* rotting for the reader. It is not dropped — it is pointed at the Issue that already owns it.

---

## The measured argument that decides the shape: this site already ran this experiment and it is failing right now

`/architecture` publishes a hand-typed count of the decision library. **It is false in both editions, today:**

```
ls docs/adr/[0-9]*.md | wc -l                                                   # -> 51
node -e "console.log(require('./apps/fed/src/content/generated/adrs.json').length)"  # -> 51
grep -rnoE "[0-9]+ decis(ões|ions)" apps/fed/src/content/architecture.{pt,en}.md
# -> architecture.en.md:299: 49 decisions
#    architecture.pt.md:301: São 49 decisões
```

**False since 2026-09-04 — seven days — and it went false inside the very slice that shipped the analytics events this proposal wants to publish.**

**The page predicted its own failure.** Its prose says the `49` is typed by hand and that cutting the rendered table removed the binding that kept it honest. It predicted, shipped anyway, and the failure arrived in ten days.

**That is the empirical answer to *what would publishing these numbers argue*.** Not a hypothesis — a measured instance, on the same page, on the surface whose whole thesis is that the inventory is *derived*. A `/analytics` page of hand-transcribed GA4 figures is that defect with a faster clock and a bigger surface: GA4 moves daily, the ADR library moves weekly.

**This finding is tracked separately and is not this Issue's to fix** — see the closing note.

### And the owner has already published the criterion that excludes a GA4 figure

`apps/fed/src/content/architecture.pt.md:279` declines to publish a measured token figure and states why:

> *«O número não é publicado porque a fonte é uma transcrição de sessão privada, que gate nenhum alcança.»*

**GA4 is exactly that class** — a private console, no credential, no gate reaches it. So a page of GA4 figures does not merely risk staleness; **it contradicts a criterion already live on the site.** Any numbers version must say out loud that its source is a console no gate reaches, and that the figure is transcribed on a stated date.

---

## The two leads' positions — recorded as a disagreement, deliberately not resolved

### `product-lead` — BUILD, rescoped and sequenced

**Verified rather than inherited: the five zeros are a behaviour fact, not a wiring fact.** Every one of the eight events has an emitter *and* a mounted caller:

```
for f in trackArticleEndReached trackArticleProgress trackShareComplete trackContactClick \
         trackShareOpen trackContactReach trackOutboundClick trackNavClick; do
  grep -rl "$f" apps/fed/src --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' \
    | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -v 'lib/analytics.ts'; done
# -> useArticleProgress · ShareLinks · ShareModal · useContactClicks
#    ShareButton · useContactReach · useOutboundClicks · AppShell
```

**That matters: the zeros are honestly zero and are publishable as zeros.** Dead wiring would have made them a false floor.

**Priced both ways, and this is the positioning call:**

- **Most honest thing on the site, if the numbers are evidence.** `/architecture` already publishes a small unflattering measured figure — R$ 34,31/month — with the arithmetic shown and an admission of waste found late. In that register a small number is an **asset**: the number is small and the method is rigorous, and the method is what is being sold.
- **A liability if the numbers are the headline**, and the asymmetry is not subtle: the cost figure is about a **system he controls**; the analytics figure is about an **audience he

sample.title: Upgrade pydantic-ai to 2.x
sample.body:
## Summary

Reboot pins `pydantic-ai-slim==1.87.0` (`reboot/requirements.in`), which pins `pydantic-graph==1.87.0`. pydantic-ai 2.0 is stable and upstream has moved on (latest is 2.43.0). We should upgrade, both to keep up and to pick up fixes we're currently working around.

## Why now

pydantic-graph 1.87.0 lets a cancelled agent run surface as `anyio.ClosedResourceError` instead of `asyncio.CancelledError`: a tracked task sends its result into a stream the cancelled run has already closed, and only `BrokenResourceError` is ignored there. A workflow that catches everything except cancellation then keeps running, which made `//tests/reboot/examples/agent-wiki:test` hang at shutdown. #179 works around it in `_agent_run`. The fix upstream first ships in pydantic-graph **2.2.0** (no 1.x release has it); once we're on it, the workaround in #179 can be removed.

## Picking a target

| pydantic-ai / pydantic-graph | `ClosedResourceError` fix | HTTP client | Anthropic SDK (`anthropic` extra) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.87.0 (current) – 1.99.0, 2.0.0 – 2.1.0 | no | `httpx` | 0.x |
| 2.2.0 – 2.30.x | yes | `httpx` | 0.x |
| 2.35.0 – 2.43.0 | yes | `httpx2` | `>= 1.3` |

- **2.2.0 – 2.30.x** keeps `reboot[anthropic]` on `anthropic==0.125.0` (per `requirements.in` / `requirements-anthropic.in`, Anthropic SDK 1.x rejects the `httpx` client pydantic-ai hands it before the `httpx2` switch).
- **2.35+** also means moving the `anthropic` extra to SDK 1.x and `httpx2`.

A reasonable path is to land 2.30.x first, then take the `httpx2` / Anthropic SDK 1.x step separately.

## What it takes

1. **Port Reboot's wrapper** (`reboot/agents/pydantic_ai/`, ~2,300 lines) — most of the work.
   - Of the 50 names it imports from pydantic-ai, against both 2.2.0 and 2.43.0: `pydantic_ai.tools.AgentBuiltinTool` no longer exists and `pydantic_ai.mcp.MCPServer` no longer resolves; `CompletedStreamedResponse` moved from `pydantic_ai.models.wrapper` to `pydantic_ai.models` (deprecated in 2.43). `pydantic_ai.toolsets.fastmcp` wasn't checked with the `fastmcp` extra installed.
   - `_agent.py` mirrors the full signatures of `run` / `iter` / `run_stream` / `run_stream_events`, and wraps toolsets (`_toolset.py`) and models (`_model.py`). V2 is a harness-first redesign around [capabilities](https://ai.pydantic.dev/capabilities/) (see the [upgrade guide](https://ai.pydantic.dev/changelog/)), so signatures, toolset wrapping and model wrapping all need checking against 2.x, not just imports.
2. **Pins and lock:** `pydantic-ai-slim` (and possibly `anthropic`) in `reboot/requirements.in` and `reboot/requirements-anthropic.in`; regenerate `reboot/requirements_lock.txt`.
3. **Remove the #179 workaround** in `reboot/agents/pydantic_ai/_run.py` (`_raised_while_cancelling` and the `ClosedResourceError` conversion) and its `CancellationTestCase` tests, or keep the tests asserting a cancelled run raises `CancelledError`.
4. **Docs and examples:** the Python skill references (`reboot/plugin/skills/python/references/agent-pydantic-ai.md`, `agent-tools.md`, `testing-external-context.md`), and examples that use agents (e.g. `reboot/examples/agent-wiki`, whose `uv.lock` resolves `pydantic-ai-slim`).
5. **Dashboard:** the static analysis in `reboot/dashboard/backend/code_watcher.py` recognizes `Agent`'s entry points and tool registration by name (`RUN_NAMES`, `TOOL_REGISTRATION_NAMES`, constructor and run arguments); check those still match 2.x, and its test fixture of the agents module in `tests/reboot/dashboard/code_watcher_tests.py`.

## Testing

- `//tests/reboot/agents/pydantic_ai/...`
- `//tests/reboot/examples/agent-wiki:test` and other agent examples
- `//tests/reboot/dashboard:code_watcher_tests_py`

sample.title: M07 planning hardening — timeline authority and reference integrity
Pitch aim tell does not follow the rubber walk or in-flight break
sample.body:
Sitting-found child (Jack, standalone, 2026-09-12). Filed per AGENTS.md: do not silently patch; build the rail under the parent epic. Spec: [docs/gameplay-spec.md](https://github.com/jackguillet/grand-sluggers/blob/main/docs/gameplay-spec.md). Parent: #563 (P1 pitch and swing contract); related #533, #534.

## Observed

When pitching, the **aim tell does not move** with the pitcher walking the rubber, and it does not follow the ball's break while the pitch is in the air.

## Cause (from the code map)

Spec §4.2 ⚠️: the human crossing moves 1.35× the rubber offset (`AtBatDirector.cs:224` sets both `AimX` and `RubberX`; `PitchFlight.Point` adds `rubberX*0.35` again) while the CPU's moves 0.35× (`Match.cs:667`); break is steered in flight by mutating `_pitch` (`AtBatDirector.cs:311-314`) after the tell was drawn. The tell is drawn from a stale command.

## Observable when fixed

- One function gives the crossing for a `PitchCommand` at any `u`; the aim tell, the ball, the umpire, and the CPU batter all read it. Walking the rubber moves the tell the same world distance as the body, once. Break moves the tell during flight, capped at half a zone.
- The white frame never lies (spec §4.4); `PitchJudgmentGate` extended to the tell.

## Files

`src/GrandSluggers.Sim/PitchFlight.cs`, `AtBatControl.cs`, `unity/.../AtBatDirector.cs`, `StrikeZone.cs`, `HudView.cs`.

## Tests

- Spec S-04 (steered pitch judged from the final crossing), S-16 / S-17 (rubber walk reaches the body the same for both seats), and a gate that the drawn tell equals `PitchFlight.Point(u)` every frame.

sample.title: Pairing: a code can enrol two devices, and a lastSeenAt stamp can undo a revoke
sample.body:
## Summary
Two races in `bridge/pairing.ts` let the single-use pairing code enrol two devices, and let a background `lastSeenAt` stamp resurrect a device that `collie devices revoke` just removed. Both are TOCTOU gaps around `paired-devices.json`, which is written by the bridge process and by the CLI process.

## Context
Raised by CodeRabbit on youngsecurity/collie#17 (threads on `bridge/pairing.ts:454` and `:492`, both rated Critical). Verified against `dev-joe` at `0e9e278`:

1. **`claim()` validates the pending code outside the critical section.** `checkClaim` runs on a fresh `readPending()`, then `generateToken`, then `this.serialize(...)` enrols the device, then `deletePending()` runs after the serialized block. Two concurrent `POST /api/pair` requests with the same code and different labels both pass `checkClaim` before either deletes the pending record, both enrol, and both receive a bearer token. The doc comment on `claim` promises "a code is single-use even within its TTL".
2. **`resolve()`'s stamp re-reads inside the queue but the write is still not exclusive across processes.** The serialized block re-reads the registry (the comment explains why) and then calls `writeRegistry(fresh)`. `bin/collie devices revoke <label>` runs in another process and rewrites the same file. A revoke that lands between that re-read and that write is overwritten, and the revoked device's token hash is back in the registry. The window is small but the outcome is a credential store undoing a revocation, which the header of `bridge/pairing.ts` names as the one thing it may not do.

Pairing is exactly on when the registry is non-empty, and it is one of the two device gates that guard writes (CLAUDE.md → Security posture), so both gaps sit on the write-authorisation path.

## Decisions
- Keep the two gates independent (CLAUDE.md); the fix stays inside `bridge/pairing.ts` and the CLI's registry writer, not the HTTP layer.
- No new dependency for locking. A lock file beside the registry (`O_EXCL` create, pid + timestamp, stale after a bound) or an atomic compare-and-swap on the registry's own mtime/etag is enough; pick whichever `bridge/pairing.ts`'s `io` seam expresses most simply.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `claim()`, move `readPending` + `checkClaim` + `deletePending` into the same `serialize` block as the enrolment, so validate, enrol and consume happen once per code. A duplicate-label refusal must still leave the pending record alive (existing behaviour).
2. Add a cross-process exclusive section around every registry read-modify-write: the stamp in `resolve()`, the enrolment in `claim()`, and the CLI's `devices revoke` (`cli/pairing.ts`, which writes the same file). A lock file in the state dir at 0600 is the least new machinery; document its staleness rule where `bridge/pairing.ts` documents the registry.
3. Tests in `bridge/pairing.test.ts`: two concurrent `claim` calls with one code and two labels enrol exactly one device and return one token; a revoke interleaved between the stamp's re-read and write does not come back. The CLI side is covered by `scripts/collie-cli.test.sh`'s pairing section if a shell-level interleave can be staged; otherwise a `bun test` over the shared writer.

## Files Summary
| File | Action | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bridge/pairing.ts` | modify | consume the pending code inside the critical section; cross-process lock around registry writes |
| `cli/pairing.ts` | modify | `devices revoke` takes the same lock |
| `bridge/pairing.test.ts` | modify | concurrency cases |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two concurrent `claim` calls with the same code enrol at most one device and return at most one token
- [ ] A `devices revoke` that lands during a `lastSeenAt` stamp is never overwritten by that stamp
- [ ] Both gates (`COLLIE_DEVICE_HEADER`, pairing) remain independent and compose by AND
- [ ] `bun run test` and `bash scripts/collie-cli.test.sh` green; CHANGELOG Unreleased line added

## Out of Scope
- Any change to the pairing wire format or to `/api/pair`'s responses.

## Risks & Mitigations
- A stuck lock file would deny every write until it goes stale: bound staleness the way `update.lock` is bounded (`STALE_AFTER_MS` in `bridge/update-run.ts`) and reuse that shape.

## Related Issues
- Related: #17

## Bug Description

Frozen-pin **product cache-key** bug: honcho cache-busting memo and raw-config cache miss same-tick same-size rewrites. Present on pin `8068c09432d3e7a23d30aa5f4f7d5a17783f8668` (tree `234d7940ae82786dd94ea47899a1109c827fe373`) and candidate `3a1cad03ef0e9a77a7649ff5e9b409c285b8356a` (tree `7a4e383bafffacc46383023c543c4b5bfd54fa53`) with **identical blobs** for the failing tests and cache implementations.

This is **not** EventBridge `#298`. Do **not** waive with faketime, sleeps, skips, or a new VM. Official hosted GREEN on pin 8068 is a different inode clock, not a local official-runner flag.

Owner routing: originally misfiled on a private catch-all tracker (`s#30`). Canonical owner is this Hermes fork issue. Original history is retained; this issue is the product tracker.

Related, not duplicate:
- Fork `#298` — EventBridge WAL/same-tick `state.db` mtime gate (different surface).
- Upstream `NousResearch/hermes-agent#100988` — snapshot-threshold **test isolation** (evict `_RAW_CONFIG_CACHE` in the test). That does not cover the honcho `pinPeerName` node and does not change the product cache keys.

## Nodes

1. `tests/honcho_plugin/test_pin_peer_name.py::TestPinTransition::test_cache_busting_signature_reflects_pin_peer_name`
   - Signal class: `assert True != True`
   - Mechanism: `GatewayRunner._extract_honcho_cache_busting_config` (`gateway/run_agent_cache.py`) memos `_HONCHO_CACHE_BUSTING_MEMO` on `(path, st_mtime_ns)` only. Adjacent same-size `honcho.json` rewrite (`pinPeerName` True→False) can share `st_mtime_ns` on coarse clocks, so the second read returns the cached True.

2. `tests/tools/test_browser_snapshot_threshold.py::test_cleanup_reloads_updated_profile_config`
   - Signal class: `assert 12000 == 15001`
   - Mechanism: `cleanup_all_browsers` clears `tools.browser_tool` caches, then `get_browser_snapshot_threshold` re-reads via `hermes_cli.config._read_raw_config_impl` keyed `(st_mtime_ns, st_size)`. Both YAML bodies size 37; same-tick mtime → stale 12000.

## Matched official-node evidence (isolated files, not full suite)

Same runner/env: workers=20, TZ=UTC, LANG=C.UTF-8, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, CPython 3.11.14, pytest 9.1.1. Inner: `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the two files above.

Official runner files (`tests.yml` / `ci.yaml` / `scripts/run_tests.sh`) have no faketime/high-res-tmp/TMPDIR knob that would make this GREEN without a product/test cache-key change.

Same-size same-tick content rewrites must bust honcho memo and `_RAW_CONFIG_CACHE` (content/generation, or size+mtime+inode/generation — product writer, not this routing pass).

Coarse `(path, mtime_ns)` / `(mtime_ns, size)` keys reuse the previous value.

sample.title: Add warm-start and resume-to-ink latency budgets and gates
sample.body:
<!-- sn-key: SN-GPRF-009 -->
**Key:** `SN-GPRF-009` · **Priority:** P2 · **Type:** test · **Size:** M · **SDLC:** verification
**Platforms:** all · **Areas:** perf, qa
**Parent:** #472 (`SN-PERF-001`)
**Depends on:** `SN-PERF-008` (`SN-PERF-008`), `SN-PERF-018` (`SN-PERF-018`)
**Security controls:** `MASVS-AUTH-2`

> New here? Read `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/README.md` first — they explain the architecture, the security rules, and how issues are structured.

## Context
Budget B6 measures cold start — process launch to first interactive frame (docs/platform/performance-budgets.md B6). But a student does not cold-start the app twenty times a lecture; they lock the tablet, unlock it, and expect to write. The path that dominates real use is warm start and resume: returning from background, reconnecting a scene after iPadOS window reconnection, coming back from an Android process death, restoring a web tab from bfcache, or relaunching an installed PWA. None of those have a budget or a test today, which means the most frequent "is it laggy?" moment in the product is ungoverned. Cold start is explicitly measured (`SN-PERF-008`); this issue adds its everyday sibling.

## Scope
**In:** proposing and ratifying three additional budget entries in the registry (`SN-PERF-018`) — warm start to interactive, resume-to-ink from background with the process alive, and restore-after-process-death (which MAY use the cold budget); trace markers and harness scenarios for each per surface; the gate wiring at the same cadence as B6; a first-stroke-after-resume assertion so the wet-ink path is proven live, not just the UI.
**Out:** the cold-start measurement (`SN-PERF-008`), state-restoration correctness on iPad (`SN-IPAD-028`) and Android (`SN-PHN-017`), which this measures but does not implement, and the deferred-init work (`SN-GPRF-011`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Three budgets exist in the registry with targets, statistics (median plus p95), gate devices and cadence; the proposed defaults are warm start <= 600 ms, resume-to-ink <= 300 ms, restore-after-kill within the cold-start budget, and any change to them is an explicit registry edit.
- [ ] Resume is measured to *first ink accepted*, not first frame: the scenario resumes the app and immediately replays a stroke, and the timestamp captured is the first presented wet-ink frame.
- [ ] Each surface has a working scenario: iOS/iPadOS scene reconnect, Android `onStart` with the process alive and again after `am kill`, web tab restore including bfcache, and installed-PWA relaunch.
- [ ] A regression fails the perf check on the Tier 1 slots at the same cadence as B6.
- [ ] Results separate the three cases; a restore-after-kill run is never reported as a warm start.

## Technical notes
Reuse the first-usable-frame marker from `SN-PERF-008` and add a resume marker on the lifecycle transition (`AppLifecycleState.resumed` in Flutter, with the native side stamping the OS-level callback so the Dart hop is inside the measurement, not before it). Android process death is driven with `adb shell am kill`; web bfcache with a scripted navigation plus `pageshow.persisted`. Beware the trap that makes warm start look free: the app may render a stale frame instantly and only accept input hundreds of milliseconds later, which is why the acceptance criterion is first ink, not first pixel.

## Security & privacy
Resume crosses a security boundary: a locked note or a biometric-gated notebook must re-authenticate on resume, and the harness must not disable that to make the number look good. The scenario therefore runs in both states and asserts that a gated notebook shows its lock on resume (#5 area; MASVS-AUTH-2). No content appears in traces.

## UX notes
The felt experience is picking up the tablet mid-lecture and writing immediately. If a surface cannot hit resume-to-ink, the fallback is to make the editor accept and buffer strokes while the rest of the app finishes waking, never to show a spinner over the page.

## Test plan
Integration per surface in `tools/perf_harness/scenarios/resume_*`, run on the Tier 1 slots. Unit: the marker resolver mapping lifecycle transitions to the right scenario type. Manual: a lab pass on iPad and a low-end Android confirming the numbers with a stopwatch-class sanity check, recorded under `tools/device_lab/results`.

## Dependencies
`SN-PERF-008`, `SN-PERF-018`

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

sample.title: [Ronin Handoff][Performance][P2] establish bounded performance regression guards
sample.body:
Ronin currently has no executable performance benchmark harness or regression gate for implemented foundation paths, even though the canonical backlog explicitly requires bounded deterministic guards for notebook DAG analysis, ledger replay and evidence persistence. Source-faithful bounded measurements show predictable scaling today, but there is no checked-in methodology or historical baseline to detect future regressions. Open PR #28 proposes catalog lookup optimization on a stale base but contains no reproducible performance evidence, reinforcing the need to measure before optimizing.

- [ ] Benchmark evidence is produced on pull requests that touch the measured paths, or at an explicitly documented cadence, without weakening existing correctness/security gates.
- [ ] No optimization such as stale PR #28 is accepted solely from asymptotic intuition; realistic cardinality evidence must demonstrate material value and semantic behavior must remain unchanged.

- `docs/automation/BACKLOG.md` on `a0af31717fb4252010caf54cc5790c992879746e` explicitly requires bounded deterministic performance guards for notebook DAG analysis, ledger replay and evidence persistence.

sample.title: Move to .NET 10 before net9.0 goes EOL on 2026-11-10 (needs an off-Kudu build)
sample.body:
## Deadline

Production now runs **net9.0** (deployed 2026-09-05, commit `6934f1a`), which reaches **end of support on 2026-11-10** — about two months out. `.NET 10` is the current LTS, supported to November 2028.

## Why net10.0 is blocked today

PR #2 targeted `net10.0` and the deploy failed:

```
error NETSDK1045: The current .NET SDK does not support targeting .NET 10.0.
C:\Program Files (x86)\dotnet\sdk\9.0.317
```

Deployment is External Git, so **Kudu builds the project server-side**, and its build image only has:

```
1.1.14  2.1.526  2.2.109  3.1.426  5.0.408  6.0.428  7.0.410  8.0.424  9.0.317
```

No .NET 10 SDK, in either the x86 or x64 install. The Kudu extension on that image is `2026.08.1.2` — an August 2026 build, so this is current, not stale. Ten months after .NET 10 GA the SDK still isn't there, so waiting for the platform is not a plan.

Note `dotnet|10` *is* available as an App Service **runtime** stack (`az webapp list-runtimes --os windows`). Only the build image is the constraint.

## Plan

### 1. Move the Slack token out of the filesystem

`TokenReader.GetToken` reads `File.ReadAllLines(".planningpokerconfig")` (`ITokenReader.cs:18`) — a gitignored file hand-placed in `D:\home\site\wwwroot` in 2020. Move it to an app setting:

```bash
az webapp config appsettings set -n planning--poker -g NewResourceGroup --settings \
  "PlanningPoker__SlackTokens=<team>:<xoxb-token>"
```

`ResolveToken` is already a pure function over `IReadOnlyList<string>`, so only the source of those strings changes and `TokenReaderTests.cs` is untouched.

**This is a prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.** Any deploy tooling that enables `WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE` mounts `wwwroot` read-only from the deployment zip. The config file isn't in the zip, so it would vanish, 500 every Slack call, and the Kudu VFS restore would fail with 409 against a read-only mount — turning a ten-second fix into a multi-step outage. `azure/webapps-deploy` can enable that setting depending on version and inputs.

Verified 2026-09-05: the file *does* survive a normal Kudu git deploy (KuduSync only prunes files it previously deployed). The hazard is specific to run-from-package.

### 2. Build off Kudu

GitHub Actions with `actions/setup-dotnet` pinned to `10.x`, `dotnet publish`, deploy the built output. SCM basic auth is enabled on the app, so the publish-profile route works without setting up OIDC.

Side benefits: reproducible builds independent of the platform image or any laptop (there is currently no local SDK and no CI), and the test project finally runs on PRs.

Then delete the External Git integration so the two mechanisms don't fight.

### 3. Target net10.0

One line in `PlanningPoker.csproj`, once the build no longer depends on Kudu's SDKs.

## Also worth setting

`PlanningPoker:PollSecret` (`Controllers/PlanningPokerController.cs:79`) is configured nowhere — not in `appsettings.json`, not in Azure. Until it's set, `/crmhelper/poll` returns 401 on every request, so the confirmation-poll feature in #1 is not usable once merged. Value must match what the STCRM caller signs with.

## Deploy notes for reference

Merging to `master` deploys nothing by itself — External Git is manual-integration:

```bash
az webapp deployment source sync -n planning--poker -g NewResourceGroup
```

`netFrameworkVersion` is still `v4.0` and does **not** need changing; ANCM resolves the runtime from the published `runtimeconfig.json`.

sample.title: fix(config): make /seam config model failure-atomic and honest
sample.body:
## Context

PR #188 made `/seam config agent` failure-atomic and honest. The sibling `/seam config model` path still has the earlier failure mode:

- the picker renders its success panel before `applyModelChange()` runs;
- the session row is persisted before the thread overlay;
- an overlay write failure is only logged, after which the command continues and reports success;
- the picker-delay path can operate from a stale session snapshot.

That can leave session config, thread overlay, and live runtime disagreeing while the user is told the model changed.

## Required behavior

- Re-read the live session after picker latency and preserve unrelated concurrent updates.
- Commit session config and the thread model overlay as one failure-atomic operation.
- Treat returned errors, thrown writes, and hot-reload failures as failures and restore the prior effective state.
- Render picker success only after persistence and effective-state verification complete.
- Keep live `setModel()` failure semantics truthful: either a verified next-turn model is durable or the command fails.

## Acceptance criteria

- Explicit-ID and real picker paths share the same commit-then-render transaction.
- Overlay `{ok:false}`, thrown write, reload failure, and effective-state mismatch never produce a success message.
- Rollback restores the prior session/overlay identity without restoring an ACP session under a different effective model.
- A concurrent unrelated session update during picker latency survives both success and rollback.
- Tests exercise real persistence, real picker ordering, and mutation controls for each failure edge.

## Origin

Production-reliability follow-up identified during the independent review of PR #188 at `d5bdd19`.

sample.title: [feat] Add plan-driven dynamic fan-out with deterministic join and durable resume
sample.body:
## Problem / motivation

Goobers v0.4.0 supports static fan-out/fan-in through `spec.parallels[].branches[]`, but every branch and referenced `goober` name must be known when the workflow is authored. A run cannot take an immutable array selected by an earlier planning stage and map each assignment into native Goobers branches without static slots, rediscovery, an external orchestrator, or sequential execution.

Representative generic scenarios include immutable runtime-selected review rosters, test shards, migration batches, and research lenses.

## Proposed solution

Add a native plan-driven map/dynamic fan-out primitive in the next evolvable DSL interpreter that extends static fan-out/fan-in. Required semantics:

- immutable pinned item set sourced from run input;
- stable per-item identity and digest;
- exact-roster validation that rejects missing, extra, duplicate, or changed items;
- native per-item workspaces, retries, timeouts, cancellation, journal entries, and artifacts;
- deterministic join ordered by identity, independent of completion order;
- durable resume without rediscovery;
- bounded concurrency using the existing scheduler;
- initial scratch and repo-readonly workspace support only;
- downstream results through normal Goobers data flow.

A V1 should reuse the current parallel runner and branch journal model, adding a frozen runtime expansion step rather than a second scheduler. Register the feature in the DSL feature registry/support matrix and keep it preview until the contract is proven.

### Conformance cases

1. A pinned three-item plan expands into exactly three mapped branches with stable identities and digests.
2. Completion order does not change deterministic join order.
3. Missing, extra, duplicate, and digest-mismatched items fail closed.
4. `maxConcurrent` is enforced.
5. Retry and timeout remain scoped to one item.
6. Fail-fast records unstarted items as cancelled.
7. Resume reconstructs the roster and cursors from durable state without rediscovery.
8. Artifacts and context pointers retain item identity.
9. Scratch and repo-readonly are accepted; writable concurrent repo workspaces are rejected.
10. Empty input behavior is explicit and deterministic.

## Alternatives considered

- **Static slots:** arbitrary maximums and placeholder branches.
- **Runtime rediscovery:** nondeterministic resume if the roster changes.
- **Custom dispatcher:** loses native Goobers execution and observability semantics.
- **Sequential generic worker:** loses bounded concurrency and per-item recovery.

## Additional context

Related upstream work: Agent-Clubhouse/Goobers#155 provides static parallel foundations; Agent-Clubhouse/Goobers#2891 tracks writable concurrent repo branches and remains out of scope; Agent-Clubhouse/Goobers#5123 tracks complementary exact-SHA repo-readonly workspaces.

Suggested split if needed: V1 for DSL/schema/compiler/graph plus local-runner expansion, deterministic join, journal/resume, and conformance; follow-up for remaining distributed-engine/tier-3 integration and broader workspace modes.

sample.title: [可靠性] Adapter Stop 只校验数字 PID，残留 PID 被复用时可能终止无关进程
sample.body:
核验版本：上游 main `a090b807d57ce6d0bea108b22f3249c0002c1228`（2026-09-07）

## 核验结论

adapter PID 文件只存数字，Stop 仅用 kill(pid, 0) 判断 PID 存在，未验证进程身份，随后向该 PID 发送 SIGTERM，等待后仍存在则 SIGKILL。

## 代码证据

- https://github.com/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/blob/a090b807d57ce6d0bea108b22f3249c0002c1228/src/common/llm/adapter_manager.cpp#L61：ReadPid 从 adapter runtime 的 .pid 文件读取整数
- https://github.com/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/blob/a090b807d57ce6d0bea108b22f3249c0002c1228/src/common/llm/adapter_manager.cpp#L68：ProcessExists 只检查存在性/EPERM
- https://github.com/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/blob/a090b807d57ce6d0bea108b22f3249c0002c1228/src/common/llm/adapter_manager.cpp#L104：WritePidFile 只写 PID，不保存启动时间或其他实例身份
- https://github.com/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/blob/a090b807d57ce6d0bea108b22f3249c0002c1228/src/common/llm/adapter_manager.cpp#L147：Stop 直接按该 PID 发 SIGTERM/SIGKILL，GetPid/IsRunning 也只检查存在性
- https://github.com/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/blob/a090b807d57ce6d0bea108b22f3249c0002c1228/src/daemon/main.cpp#L371：daemon 的 adapter 停止路径实际调用此 Stop

## 场景与影响

adapter 非正常结束后 PID 文件残留，同一次系统运行期间该 PID 被复用为另一同用户进程，用户请求停止原 adapter，代码便可能终止新进程，造成工作中断或未保存数据丢失。

这是残留状态与 PID 复用的生命周期正确性问题，不依赖恶意用户篡改 PID 文件，也不主张跨用户提权。/run/user 下文件通常会在注销/重启时清理，但不能消除同一次会话中的复用风险。

本轮是源码核验，没有向用户进程发送信号，也未强制触发内核 PID 复用。可在隔离测试中用可牺牲的自建子进程模拟失配 PID；预期 Stop 拒绝发送信号且只清理失效状态。

## 建议

保存并核对进程启动时间和期望身份；注意“先验证再 kill”仍有竞争窗口，优先用 pidfd/可靠 supervisor 持有进程实例，验证后通过稳定句柄发送信号。身份失配时只清理 stale PID 状态。增加 PID 失配、自然退出及等待期间退出的回归检查。

来源：https://github.com/Accel-White/fcitx5-vinput/issues/6

sample.title: Studs rebuild: keep/port/drop sweep of every crate
sample.body:
Founding table for the "studs rebuild": every crate in the deka workspace (`main` @ `9d0b372f`, `v0.48.1`), read directly, classified against the five essential functions:

1. execute compiled JS on V8 via deno_core (isolate pool)
2. serve HTTP (axum/routing/websocket)
3. resolve the closed module universe (io/math/…, ds_modules, deka.json security manifest, wasm extensions)
4. build — drive dsc, emit dist/, artifact-only serving
5. the CLI (init/serve/run/build/self)

Storefront serving is on the Cloudflare edge now (per-shop Workers, 2026-08-02 pivot) — fleet-era multi-tenant serving machinery is suspect. Neo4j/Redis are replaced by Zega — transports for them are suspect. PHP-era anything is residue by definition. The framework (JSX/islands/bundler) is explicitly **paused** as of 2026-09-10 — "get the base coherent and stable... then framework on his terms from fundamentals" — which bears directly on several verdicts below.

**Corroboration used:** the astra structural review (staff#10, `gpt-6-astra` against deka `d9a8bb9`/dsc `91d3d9a`), and the shared-code drift inventory (deka#772: 100 of 137 non-fixture shared paths between deka and dsc have drifted). Findings from staff#10 are cited by number (F1–F13) where they agree or disagree with a verdict below. Note: CLAUDE.md's citation of deka#213 as the "elephants" issue is itself stale — #213 now resolves to an unrelated version-bump PR; deka#391 (framework.rs split) and deka#772 are the live corroborating issues instead.

Line counts are `.rs` under each crate's `src/`, via `wc -l`. "php-signal" is `rg -c 'php|Php|PHP' <crate>/src` summed — a crude residue proxy, not a verdict on its own (`deka_host` is high because its host-operation module is literally named `modules/php`, which is itself finding #7's point). "Depended on by" is grep over in-workspace `Cargo.toml`s only — it does not see dsc's copies.

## The table

| Crate | Lines | Actual function | Verdict | Evidence / what leaves |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `core` | 908 | CLI command/arg registry (`Context`, `Registry`, handler dispatch) that both `cli` and `wasm_cli` build on | **PORT** | Function 5 substrate. One of 7 crates duplicated deka↔dsc (deka#772: 5/6 files drifted). Depended on by `cli, compile, introspect, runtime, wasm_cli`. What leaves: nothing removed, but needs single ownership per staff#10's general duplication remedy. |
| `bundler` | 3,907 | swc-based JS bundler + treeshaker + CSS bundler; wired exclusively into `runtime::islands.rs` (client-side island hydration bundles) | **DECIDE** | Not one of the 5 studs functions — it is framework client-bundling machinery, called from nowhere except the paused islands feature. Duplicated deka↔dsc (deka#772: 5 drifted, 18 vs 9 files); F1: the two `parallel_bundler.rs` are byte-identical while the surrounding bundler differs. Depended on by `cli, runtime` (both transitively, only for islands). Question: does framework-adjacent bundling enter the rebuild while the framework itself is paused? |
| `cli` | 16,337 | The `deka` command dispatcher: init/serve/run/build/self/install/publish/task/auth/etc. | **PORT** | Function 5, essential and largest crate. F5: duplicates `pm`'s rehash/lock-mutation logic in `cli/src/cli/install.rs` — two implementations of the same lockfile rewrite. F8: `build_dsc.rs` detects compiler capability by string-matching "unknown argument"/"usage: dsc" instead of a structured protocol. F12: command handlers are `fn(&Context)` with no result type, so failure handling is ad hoc per command. What leaves in a port: the duplicated pm-mutation path in `install.rs`, the prose-matching compiler-capability probe. |
| `compile` | 1,024 | `deka compile`: single-executable packaging (`Embedder`, binary embed, `vfs`) | **PORT** | Function 4 adjacent (final artifact packaging). F11: does its own source-entry discovery instead of consuming the build's artifact manifest; `Embedder`'s configurable include patterns are never consulted by its traversal (embeds everything). What leaves: the independent source-discovery path — must consume the built artifact tree instead. |
| `deka_host` | 13,278 | Host operation registry consumed from JS: filesystem, Postgres, network, crypto, concurrency bridges (`modules/php/*`, 7,168 lines), plus module/import validation (`validation/`, 3,247 lines), plus `neo4j.rs` (516) and `redis_mod.rs` (638) | **PORT** | Functions 1 + 3. F7 confirms the live host operations under `modules/php` are real and load-bearing — "a blanket deletion of `modules/php` would be wrong" — but `has_configured_cluster()` in `neo4j.rs` always returns `false` (shard subsystem archived) and both `neo4j.rs`/`redis_mod.rs` carry override branches guarded by that dead constant. F2: the capability inventory in `runtime_core::security` is tested against itself, not against this crate's actual registered operations — coverage claims are unverified. What leaves: `neo4j.rs`, `redis_mod.rs` (Zega replaces both; thesis explicitly flags these transports), the dead-constant branches. What must survive the rename off "php": db/net/fs/crypto/concurrency host ops. Highest php-signal in the workspace (219) by construction — the module is literally named `php`. Depended on by `cli, platform_server, pm, pool, runtime`. |
| `engine` | 1,329 | Request dispatch + response envelope between `pool` and `http` (`RuntimeEngine`, `execute_request`) | **KEEP** | Functions 1+2 glue, clean, no residue signal (php-signal 4, incidental). Depended on by `http, runtime, transport`. |
| `http` (`deka_http`) | 3,793 | axum HTTP server: router, websocket, rate_limit, analytics, `utility_css`, `Neo4jConfig` | **PORT** | Function 2, essential. Carries `Neo4jConfig` (Zega replaces Neo4j — thesis-suspect transport). `utility_css` is an actively-designed-but-unshipped feature (RFD 58 + 5 amendments in staff#11, filed the day before this sweep) — not residue, but not core-5 either. What leaves: `Neo4jConfig` and its default `"neo4j"` credentials. `utility_css`

sample.title: DH SPEC: Demo hardening (upload → agent → Gate 2 → Gate 3/export)
sample.body:
## Problem Statement

The HELIX demo path (upload → agent steps → Gate 2 traceability → Gate 3 review & export) works end to end on `feat/steven-workspace` @ `d4e5015a`, but it does not feel proactive or clean in front of a scientist:

- After the human freeze (Gate 1), nothing happens. The operator has to click a progress stage and then "Run agent steps to the next stop".
- While the agent sequence runs, the selected stage does not follow the server's `current_stage_id`, so the ProgressBar moves while the stage view sits on an old stage.
- The legacy `StudyJourney` panel still mounts under every stage view, duplicating agent controls (double-command risk) and cluttering the page.
- The scientist-facing per-section drafts (`ReportAssembly` + `ChatDock`, `content_drafts`) live in a second scroll stack instead of the Gate 3 body.
- Gate 2 and the export receipt need copy and density polish; demo-frozen runs are not visibly marked and can still be exported.

## Solution

Refine-only demo hardening of the four shipped stages. After a human freeze the workbench selects the server's current stage and auto-starts the governed agent sequence once; the stage view follows the server while the run is in flight and stops at every human boundary. The legacy duplicate panels leave the default path (components kept). The HITL draft body folds into Gate 3 in phases. Gate 2 and export copy are tightened. Demo-frozen runs carry a small "Not qualified" status label and export fails closed for them.

No functionality is deleted, Steven's deliberate removals stay out, freeze stays human-only (409 `human_freeze_required`), and nothing auto-freezes, auto-passes a gate or auto-exports.

## User Stories

1. As a study director, I want the agent to start working as soon as I freeze the package, so that the demo feels proactive after my one human decision.
2. As a study director, I want freeze to remain my explicit, consented action, so that no agent can pin a run on my behalf.
3. As a study director, I want the stage view to follow the stage the server is working on, so that I can watch each step complete.
4. As a study director, I want the ProgressBar and stage view to agree during a run, so that I am never looking at a stale stage while the agent moves on.
5. As a study director, I want to stop the agent sequence at any time, so that I stay in control of the run.
6. As a study director, I want the agent to stop on any error and tell me which step failed, so that later steps never run on a bad state.
7. As a study director, I want the agent to stop at blockers and human decisions (retry, stop for review, ineligible promotion), so that judgment calls stay with me.
8. As a study director, I want the agent to stop at Gate 2 traceability and never disposition claims, so that the scientific gate stays human.
9. As a study director, I want the agent never to sign Gate 3 or export, so that release stays a human act.
10. As a study director, I want manual stage selection when nothing is running, so that I can inspect completed stages at my own pace.
11. As a study director, I want my manual pick respected after the sequence stops, so that follow-current never yanks me away mid-inspection.
12. As a study director, I want parse/resolve/provenance shown only as the server reports them, so that the demo never shows fake progress.
13. As a study director, I want the idempotent Data Validation replay to read as "confirming the freeze receipt", so that it does not look like a failure or a re-run.
14. As a study director, I want one set of agent controls per stage, so that I cannot fire the same command twice from two panels.
15. As a demo presenter, I want the legacy StudyJourney hidden from the default path, so that the page shows one primary surface per stage.
16. As a maintainer, I want StudyJourney kept in the codebase, so that no behaviour is lost before a slice migrates it.
17. As a study director, I want the per-section grounded drafts and chat inside Gate 3, so that report assembly and sign-off happen in one place.
18. As a study director, I want Final Study Approval, export and downloads unchanged when drafts fold into Gate 3, so that release governance is preserved.
19. As a study director, I want empty or `needs_review` sections shown honestly, so that no numbers are invented.
20. As a study director, I want Gate 2 traceability dense and calm with the first blocker open, so that I can disposition quickly.
21. As a study director, I want "Inspect provenance" from the report to land on the right claim, so that navigation into evidence is exact.
22. As a maintainer, I want no blocker-count chrome reintroduced at Gate 2, so that Steven's removals stay out.
23. As a study director, I want the export receipt to say plainly what was exported and list the slice-11 approved hashes, so that I can verify the package.
24. As a study director, I want the Gate 3 disclaimer to say "FDA-like layout for demonstration only" once, so that nobody mistakes the output for a submission.
25. As a maintainer, I want the `qualification.py` docstring to state that the `run_requested` event carries package ids (not the label), so that the code documentation is accurate.
26. As a study director, I want a demo-frozen run to show a small "Not qualified" status label, so that I know its packages skipped qualification.
27. As a demo presenter, I want no demo-flag banners or chrome, so that the UI stays clean.
28. As a QA reviewer, I want export to fail closed (409) for demo-frozen runs, so that unqualified output can never leave the system.
29. As a QA reviewer, I want strict runs and flag-off behaviour unchanged, so that the guard has no side effects.
30. As a maintainer, I want each slice proven by local gates (pytest vs base, ruff, tsc, build, verify-live) with new seams tested, so that nothing regresses.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Gate numbering (code wins):** Gate 1 = Upload/freeze, Gate 2 = Traceability, Gate 3 = Review & export.
