sample.title: review: doctor asks a referenced table's permissions on every catalog column, not on the columns the foreign key names
sample.body:
Raised by Codex on PR #193 (P2, reviewed commit `e12c24b`):
https://github.com/pongbiphang/pbps/pull/193#discussion_r3956193285
Answered there and filed here.

**The finding.** A foreign key into `shared.parent(code)` needs `REFERENCES` on
`code` and the preflight probe reads only `constraint.references_columns`
(`preflight::rows_after` projects exactly those). `doctor` asks the referenced
table with `Columns::Catalog`, which requires the permission on **every** column
the catalog shows — so an account granted `SELECT` and `REFERENCES` on `code`
alone is reported as missing both, because of the unrelated `label`.

**Why it was not fixed on #193.** It is an over-demand and not one of the three
the review loop fixes ((a) a valid plan refused, (b) a wrong recording, (c) a
concurrent case SPEC §7.6 promises to catch), and — the part that decides it —
it is not a regression from that PR. Before it, the object-scope question
answered 0 for that account and `doctor` reported the same gap; the column
fallback only ever turns a 0 into a 1, so no account is worse off than it was.
What #193 did was remove the over-demand for an account granted every column,
and leave it for one granted a subset.

**The fix, and why it is not a line.** `doctor` is not handed the referenced
*columns* today: `referenced_tables` (pbps-cli) collects `fk.references_table`
and discards `fk.references_columns`. Fixing this means carrying the union of
referenced columns per target through to `permissions`, and giving `Columns` a
third case — a declared list that is *not* the object's whole column set and
must not be read as one. That is a change to what the readiness check is given
rather than to how it asks, the same shape as #194.

**Tests.** Live, mirroring #193's: an account granted `SELECT` and `REFERENCES`
on exactly the columns a declared foreign key names, on a target outside the
managed schemas, reports ready and both the emitted `REFERENCES` and the
preflight probe run; one of those columns short reports a gap. And a negative
case: a column of the target that no foreign key names is not asked about.

sample.title: Install paths are compared as strings, so one install spelled two ways reads as two installs
sample.body:
`clodex patch` and `clodex patch --restore` compare install paths with plain string equality —
`manifest.binaryPath === binaryPath`, and the install path inside a provenance record. One install
spelled two ways therefore reads as two installs.

**This is not Windows-only.** APFS is case-insensitive and the `fs.realpathSync` clodex uses
preserves caller-supplied case (only `.native` corrects it), so a hand-typed
`TWEAKCC_CC_INSTALLATION_PATH` reaches it on macOS. Reproduced.

## What it costs today

Both consequences are safe directions, which is why #204 shipped without fixing this:

- **A false refusal.** With a provenance record written under spelling A, a restore under spelling B
  reads the record as another install's and refuses instead of falling back. The message names the
  recorded spelling, so following its own advice recovers.
- **A manifest that outlives its install's restore.** `--restore` clears the manifest only when
  `manifest.binaryPath === binaryPath`, so a manifest written under the other spelling survives a
  successful restore. Stale rather than harmful — `evaluatePatchState` sees the hash mismatch and
  re-patches — but it says the install is patched when it is not.

## The fix, and why it is not a one-liner

One path-equivalence helper — exact string match first, then compare `realpathSync.native()` results
(or `stat` device+inode) while both paths exist — used consistently for record keys, selection,
manifest matching, and manifest cleanup.

`realpathSync.native` would fix the root cause, but it changes the spelling clodex resolves to, which
**invalidates the `binaryPath` in every existing manifest**. That needs a migration: on read, accept a
manifest whose `binaryPath` differs only by case/link resolution and rewrite it. Without the
migration, every user's first run after upgrading looks like "the manifest records a different
install" and refuses.

Raised during the #204 review; the behaviour is documented under "Pristine backups are
content-addressed" in `.claude/docs/patcher.md`.

sample.title: Wayland: NULL wl_pointer dereference in setCursorImage when seat drops pointer capability while an animated cursor is shown
sample.body:
## Environment
- GLFW 3.4.0 (also present on current master, 92dcf4c)
- Ubuntu 26.04, GNOME/Mutter Wayland session, libwayland-client 1.24.0
- Statically linked into a closed-source application; crash reproduced from an Apport core dump

## Summary
When the compositor removes `WL_SEAT_CAPABILITY_POINTER` from the seat (Mutter does this whenever the last pointer-capable device is removed, e.g. unplugging the only USB mouse or a Bluetooth mouse going to sleep), `seatHandleCapabilities` destroys `_glfw.wl.pointer` and sets it to NULL but leaves the rest of the pointer state untouched. If an animated cursor was active at that moment, the cursor timerfd is still armed, and on the next tick `handleEvents` calls `incrementCursorImage` -> `setCursorImage` -> `wl_pointer_set_cursor(NULL, ...)`, which segfaults inside `wl_proxy_marshal`.

## Backtrace
0  wl_proxy_marshal () from libwayland-client.so.0     (proxy == NULL, opcode == WL_POINTER_SET_CURSOR)
1  setCursorImage (src/wl_window.c, wl_pointer_set_cursor call)
2  incrementCursorImage
3  handleEvents  (cursorTimerfd POLLIN branch)
4  _glfwPollEventsWayland
5  application main loop
Registers at the fault: `rdi=0` (proxy), `rsi=0` (opcode), `rdx=<pointer enter serial>`, `r8/r9=<hotspot>`.

## Analysis (3.4 line numbers, master equivalents in parentheses)
- `seatHandleCapabilities` (wl_window.c:1880, master:2072): on capability loss it does `wl_pointer_destroy(_glfw.wl.pointer); _glfw.wl.pointer = NULL;` and nothing else. `_glfw.wl.pointerFocus` (master: `_glfw.wl.pointerSurface`), `window->wl.hovered` and `_glfw.wl.cursorTimerfd` all keep their previous state. The compositor does not send `wl_pointer.leave` before the capability change, so nothing else clears them.
- `handleEvents` (wl_window.c:1288, master:1472): when the cursor timerfd fires it calls `incrementCursorImage(_glfw.wl.pointerFocus)` (master: `incrementCursorImage()` which reads `_glfw.wl.pointerSurface`). The stale focus passes the checks.
- `setCursorImage` (wl_window.c:1078, master:1248) re-arms the timer and calls `wl_pointer_set_cursor(_glfw.wl.pointer, ...)` with `_glfw.wl.pointer == NULL`.

The timer is only armed for cursors whose `wl_cursor_image.delay` is non-zero, so a static arrow never triggers this; an animated theme cursor (e.g. "wait"/"progress") is required.

## Steps to reproduce
1. GNOME Wayland session with exactly one pointer device (e.g. one USB mouse, no touchpad).
2. Run any GLFW 3.4 program and make it show an animated cursor (a `glfwCreateCursor` cursor with multiple images, or a theme where the chosen standard cursor is animated) while the mouse hovers the window.
3. Unplug the mouse.
4. The program expected to crash in `wl_proxy_marshal` within one cursor frame delay.

## Workaround for my application
Running with these env changes fixed this issue:
```
env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11 my-app
```

## Suggested fix
In `seatHandleCapabilities`, when destroying/releasing the pointer, also:
- disarm the cursor timer (`timerfd_settime` with a zeroed `itimerspec`),
- clear `_glfw.wl.pointerFocus` / `_glfw.wl.pointerSurface`,
- if the focused window had `wl.hovered` set, clear it and emit `_glfwInputCursorEnter(window, GLFW_FALSE)` so the application sees a cursor leave, mirroring `pointerHandleLeave`.

Additionally, `setCursorImage` (and the other `wl_pointer_set_cursor` call sites) could early-return when `_glfw.wl.pointer == NULL` as a defensive check.

sample.title: [Bug: High] PR #489 fix is incomplete — pg_store._PG_CONNECT_KWARGS + _connect still pass options='-c statement_timeout=60000' kwarg, regression test enforces it
sample.body:
## Summary

PR #489 fixed the `fe_sendauth: no password supplied` regression for `src/web/server.py::execute_query` only. The shared helper `src/data/pg_store.py::connect_with_timeouts` and the `PostgresDataStore._connect` method STILL pass `options="-c statement_timeout=60000"` as a psycopg connect kwarg — the exact broken path PR #489's PR body identifies as libpq's DSN-password-dropping behavior under scram-sha-256. The bug is dormant for `alphard-bot` today (bot stays on the alphard-net bridge, no `network_mode: host`), but the helper is exported and used by every other Postgres-touching code path (`src/coordinator.py`, `src/data/quality/audit.py`, `src/main.py:_universe_metrics_loop`, plus the three cron scripts in `scripts/`). Any future endpoint or backfill loop that calls `connect_with_timeouts` from alphard-web re-introduces the same `fe_sendauth` failure that closed #428.

## Severity
High

## Type
bug + security-adjacent (the same libpq/options-kwarg behaviour that broke #428)

## Location
- `src/data/pg_store.py:52-55` — `_PG_CONNECT_KWARGS` literal
- `src/data/pg_store.py:58-74` — `connect_with_timeouts` (the helper itself)
- `src/data/pg_store.py:117-139` — `PostgresDataStore._connect` (the bot's data store path)
- Callers of `connect_with_timeouts`:
  - `src/coordinator.py:584-586`
  - `src/data/quality/audit.py:160-162`
  - `src/main.py:746-750`

The call sites themselves are not at fault; the bug is the literal `options` kwarg in the helper they all share.

## Root cause

PR #489's PR body states:

> libpq's behaviour with `connect(dsn, options="-c statement_timeout=...")` dropped the password under alphard-web's `network_mode: host` + scram-sha-256 setup.

The fix only patched the local `execute_query` function (which does its own `psycopg.connect(dsn, connect_timeout=10)` and `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` inline). It did NOT remove the same kwarg from the shared helper that 4+ call sites depend on. The same regression returns the moment a future commit makes any of those sites the alphard-web path — or vice versa, if alphard-bot ever gets `network_mode: host` for a debugging session.

Worse: `tests/test_psycopg_timeout_coverage.py::TestConnectWithTimeouts::test_passes_statement_timeout_option` (line 87-91) **positively asserts** `options == "-c statement_timeout=60000"` is present in the kwargs. So the test suite ENFORCES the regression to keep coming back. The test was added in PR #46 / issue #232 as a regression guard for the OPPOSITE direction (no timeout guards), but its current form pins the broken kwarg in stone.

## Proof / Code Snippet

`src/data/pg_store.py:52-55`:
```python
_PG_CONNECT_KWARGS: dict[str, Any] = {
    "connect_timeout": 10,
    "options": "-c statement_timeout=60000",
}
```

`src/data/pg_store.py:138`:
```python
self._conn = self._psycopg.connect(
    self._dsn,
    autocommit=True,
    connect_timeout=10,
    options="-c statement_timeout=60000",
)
```

`tests/test_psycopg_timeout_coverage.py:87-91` (positive assertion that locks the broken kwarg in):
```python
def test_passes_statement_timeout_option(self, recording_connect: _RecordingConnect) -> None:
    from src.data.pg_store import connect_with_timeouts
    connect_with_timeouts("host=h dbname=d")
    assert recording_connect.calls[0]["options"] == "-c statement_timeout=60000"
```

Same libpq/options-kwarg issue that PR #489 closed for `execute_query` is still active everywhere else.

## Impact

1. `src/data/quality/audit.py` runs the audit log write for every alphard-bot pipeline run. Today it works because alphard-bot is on alphard-net bridge. If alphard-bot ever needs `network_mode: host` (Portainer sandbox debugging, see #411 pattern), the same `fe_sendauth` regression hits every audit write — silent data loss because the catch-block at `coordinator.py:597-599` swallows the exception (`logger.warning("AUDIT persist failed...")`).
2. `src/main.py::_universe_metrics_loop` is called every minute from the alphard-bot heartbeat (`ALPHARD_METRICS_PORT=8765`). It runs `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ticker_universe` and `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ticker_universe WHERE backfill_complete = TRUE` — losing those metrics means `alphard-web`'s universe panel stops reporting. Today it works; tomorrow it may not.
3. The cron scripts (`scripts/backfill_full_universe.py`, `scripts/backfill_delisted_via_tinkoff.py`, `scripts/mark_terminally_failed.py`) all use the helper. If a future cron container is migrated to alphard-web's pattern for unified observability, every cron run would silently fail auth.
4. The fix in PR #489 is incomplete and creates "magic" — a developer reading the new `execute_query` function sees `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` and assumes that's how the project enforces the timeout. The helper still uses the old broken kwarg, and the test actively forbids changing that. A new endpoint added to `dispatch()` that calls `connect_with_timeouts` would silently inherit the bug.
5. The PR body claim that alphard-web has `network_mode: host` is factually wrong — alphard-web has NEVER had `network_mode: host` in the current `docker-compose.yaml`. The original PR #425/cef229a fix removed `options=` from a different cause (likely a runtime psycopg/libpq interaction with the specific DSN format or scram-sha-256 mode used at the time), and the new fix perpetuates the same myth instead of getting the root cause right.

## Suggested Fix

Mirror the SET LOCAL pattern from PR #489 into `connect_with_timeouts`:

1. In `src/data/pg_store.py:52-55`, remove `options` from `_PG_CONNECT_KWARGS`:
   ```python
   _PG_CONNECT_KWARGS: dict[str, Any] = {
       "connect_timeout": 10,
   }
   ```
2. In `src/data/pg_store.py:117-139`, replace the inline `options=` kwarg in `PostgresDataStore._connect` with a `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 60000` issued as the first query on the cursor (autocommit=True means each `execute()` runs in its own implicit txn, but `SET LOCAL` requires an explicit txn — so wrap the call sites in a `with

sample.title: AppImage crashes with EGL_BAD_PARAMETER on pure X11 sessions with no Wayland compositor (reproduces on AMD Strix and AMD Vega/renoir iGPUs)
sample.body:
## Summary

The Linux AppImage aborts on startup with no window shown, on any X11 session where no Wayland compositor is running (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset). This is distinct from #129, which is about the bundled `libwayland-client` conflicting with an *existing* Wayland compositor — here there is no Wayland session at all.

## Environment

Reproduced on two independent machines, both pure X11 (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` empty):

- AMD Ryzen AI (Strix Point) iGPU, Radeon 880M, Mesa 26.1.8, Fedora 44
- AMD Renoir iGPU, Radeon Graphics (renoir), Mesa, Fedora 44

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
echo "session=$XDG_SESSION_TYPE wayland=$WAYLAND_DISPLAY display=$DISPLAY"
# session=x11 wayland= display=:0

timeout 15 GitHub-Copilot-linux-x64.AppImage --no-sandbox > /tmp/copilot_out.log 2>&1
grep -i egl /tmp/copilot_out.log
```

## Actual result

```
Could not create default EGL display: EGL_BAD_PARAMETER. Aborting...
```

The process aborts (SIGABRT) with no window. The Rust `github_app` backend and CLI/websocket server processes keep running as orphans; only the WebKitGTK renderer crashes.

## Confirmed GPU/driver independent

The crash reproduces identically even with software rendering forced, ruling out a hardware/driver-specific EGL path:

```bash
LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 timeout 12 GitHub-Copilot-linux-x64.AppImage --no-sandbox 2>&1 | grep -i egl
# still: Could not create default EGL display: EGL_BAD_PARAMETER. Aborting...
```

None of the following env vars prevent the crash: `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE`, `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER`, `WEBKIT_DMABUF_RENDERER_DISABLE_GBM`, `WEBKIT_SKIA_ENABLE_CPU_RENDERING`, `WEBKIT_WEB_RENDER_DEVICE_FILE`, `GDK_BACKEND=x11`, `EGL_PLATFORM=x11`, `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=llvmpipe`.

## Confirmed fix: fake Wayland compositor

Running a throwaway headless Wayland compositor and pointing `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` at it avoids the crash entirely, on both machines:

```bash
weston --backend=headless-backend.so --socket=wl-fake &
WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wl-fake GDK_BACKEND=wayland GitHub-Copilot-linux-x64.AppImage
```

## Root cause (inferred)

The bundled WebKitGTK/Tauri renderer appears to require a Wayland display handle to succeed its default EGL platform display initialization, even when running under `GDK_BACKEND=x11`. On hosts with no Wayland compositor running at all (headless X11-only setups, some window managers/distros), this init unconditionally fails and the renderer process aborts, regardless of GPU vendor or software/hardware rendering.

## Related issues

- #129 — same error message, but scoped to bundled `libwayland-client` conflicting with a *running* Wayland compositor. Root cause here is different: no Wayland compositor exists at all.
- #3060 — documents hardcoded `GDK_BACKEND=x11` and bundled glib conflicts; relevant background on the Tauri/WebKitGTK Linux packaging fragility, but doesn't cover this no-compositor case.

## Suggested fix

Ideally the renderer should fall back gracefully (e.g. to a non-accelerated/X11-only EGL path) when no Wayland display is available, instead of hard-aborting. Short-term, documenting the `weston --backend=headless-backend.so` workaround in the README's Linux troubleshooting section would help other X11-only users hitting this.

sample.title: [auth] P2: Session management UX lacks trust signals and self-service controls
sample.body:
# P2: Session management UX lacks trust signals and self-service controls

## Context (2026-07-02 UX review, verified in code)
The `Session` contract carries only method/status/expiry (`auth/features/sessions/ui/contracts.ts`) — no created-at, device, IP, location, or last-active. The list shows User/Account/Method/Status (`session-list-page.tsx:23-32`) with no "current session" indicator, no revoke from the list (view→detail→revoke), no "sign out all others", and detail prints raw ISO `expires_at` (`session-detail-page.tsx:57`). The consumer surface `/account/sessions` reuses the admin table wholesale and hardcodes `limit=50&offset=0` while dropping limit/offset so pagination is `undefined` — sessions past 50 are unreachable (`account-sessions.tsx:13-15`). The Security page description promises "sessions" but does not link to them (`account-security-page.tsx:34-36`).

## What to do
1. Enrich the session read model with created-at + device/user-agent (and IP/approx-location if available).
2. Mark the current session; add list-level revoke and a "sign out everywhere / all other devices" action (this also needs a server-side bulk-revoke — coordinate with auth).
3. Fix the pagination drop so older sessions are reachable; render human-readable timestamps.
4. Link Security → Sessions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Users can see per-session device/created-at/last-active, identify the current session, revoke individual sessions from the list, and sign out everywhere.
- [ ] Sessions beyond the first page are reachable.
- [ ] Tests for current-session marking + bulk revoke.

## Constraints
- Sibling `YYYYMMDD-topic` worktree; run `pnpm run verify:static` + scoped tests before push. Rebase onto latest `main` right before pushing (localization fingerprint is a single-line conflict on concurrent PRs).
- Add a regression test that FAILS on current code and PASSES after the fix — pin the corrected behavior, not the broken one.

sample.title: Resume omp past sessions instead of launching fresh
sample.body:
## Goal
When someone reopens a past `omp` session from the console's session list, the engine
should relaunch `omp` pointed at that same session — the same way it already does for
`claude`, `codex`, and `opencode`. Right now it silently starts a brand-new `omp`
process with no resume flag, so the past conversation the user picked is unreachable
from the UI even though Locklane already detected, captured, and listed it correctly.

Root cause: `TerminalWebSocketHandler.resolveLaunchCommand(String cmd, String resume)`
(`engine/src/main/java/dev/locklane/engine/ws/TerminalWebSocketHandler.java:404-420`)
has a branch per known tool (`claude --resume`, `codex resume`, `opencode --session`)
but none for `omp`, so it falls through to a bare `{"omp"}`. The same omission exists
in the restart-reattach overload `resolveLaunchCommand(String sessionId, String cmd,
String resume)` (~line 344-350), and `isAgent`/`seededLaunchCommand` in the same file
also exclude `omp` (affects seeded first-prompt launches, the sibling feature).
`ConsoleSessionTitles` likewise has a branch per tool for auto-generated conversation
titles but none for `omp`, so past omp sessions show no title.

This gap was flagged as deferred follow-up in task #681's commit message when omp
support was first added ("full launch-time parity ... needs `TerminalWebSocketHandler`
... flagged as a follow-up") and was never picked up — #695 explicitly listed
`TerminalWebSocketHandler` changes as out of scope.

## Done when
- `resolveLaunchCommand(cmd, resume)` returns `{"omp", "--resume", <id>}` when
  `cmd.equals("omp")` and `resume` is a valid id, with a test alongside the existing
  claude/codex/opencode cases in `TerminalWebSocketHandlerLaunchCommandTest.java`.
- The restart-reattach overload also resumes an `omp` session after an engine restart,
  with a test in `TerminalWebSocketHandlerRestartResumeTest.java`.
- `isAgent` and `seededLaunchCommand` recognize `"omp"` alongside claude/codex/opencode,
  so a seeded first-prompt launch works for omp too.
- `ConsoleSessionTitles` gets an `omp` branch so past omp sessions get an
  auto-generated title instead of the untitled default.
- `./mvnw -B test` passes.
- Stale javadoc touched by this fix (the `TerminalWebSocketHandler` class-level doc
  still saying `cmd=<claude|codex|shell>`, and `ConsoleResumeSessionRecord`'s `tool`
  field doc still saying `"claude" or "codex"` only) is updated to mention opencode
  and omp.

## Scope
`engine/src/main/java/dev/locklane/engine/ws/TerminalWebSocketHandler.java`,
`engine/src/main/java/dev/locklane/engine/persistence/ConsoleSessionTitles.java`,
`engine/src/main/java/dev/locklane/engine/persistence/ConsoleResumeSessionRecord.java`,
and their tests under `engine/src/test/java/dev/locklane/engine/ws/` and
`engine/src/test/java/dev/locklane/engine/persistence/`.

## Non-goals
No changes to `ResumeIdScanner` or the resume-id capture/storage pipeline — already
correct and well-tested for omp. No changes to the client session-list UI — already
tool-agnostic since #695.

sample.title: Plan: show Hearth notifications on the Omarchy desktop
sample.body:
## Outcome

New Hearth inbox notifications appear as native desktop notifications on an Omarchy machine, including when Hearth runs on a remote server. A notification offers **Open in Hearth** to the corresponding task/run. The listener runs automatically during the user's graphical session and recovers from network loss and desktop restarts.

Hearth's inbox remains the durable record. Displaying, clicking or dismissing a desktop popup does not mark its inbox notification read.

## Starting point

- `docs/inbox.md` and `backend/hearth/observation/notifications.py` describe durable run notifications committed with their owning operational facts. External forwarding is not implemented there today.
- The operator snapshot exposes a bounded, unread-first notification window. Polling that window is not a reliable catch-up protocol: older arrivals can fall outside it.
- The inspected Omarchy installation has `notify-send` and a Quickshell notification server. Use the standard desktop notification interface; no modification to packaged Omarchy files is needed.

## Scope

One opt-in desktop listener, one configured Hearth instance per listener, the existing run success/failure/cancellation notification kinds, and an Open in Hearth action. Use a systemd **user** service tied to the graphical session and its D-Bus session bus. No root service or connection from the Hearth server into the desktop session.

The listener reads notification metadata over Hearth's authenticated HTTP interface and emits notifications locally through `org.freedesktop.Notifications`. `notify-send` is useful for the manual smoke check; choose a maintained D-Bus client for the listener so action callbacks and daemon restarts do not require one blocked subprocess per popup.

## Implementation plan

### 1. Define the feed and desktop delivery contract

- Read `docs/rebuild-plan.md` and record an ADR for notification consumption, authentication scope, cursor identity and desktop delivery uncertainty.
- Add a bounded authenticated incremental notification feed through the observation interface. Reuse the existing monotonic `notification.recorded` audit sequence where appropriate rather than sorting UUIDs or timestamps. Define pagination and a high-water cursor consistently with one SQLite snapshot.
- Bind cursors/checkpoints to the source store identity or generation so switching households or restoring an older store cannot silently skip new notifications. Define explicit reset handling.
- Prefer bounded polling for the first slice. If an existing event stream is used to wake the listener, the durable feed still owns recovery; missed stream messages must not lose inbox entries.
- Decide and document authentication explicitly: a dedicated read-only notification credential is preferred. If existing operator authentication is reused for the initial slice, disclose its broader authority rather than calling it read-only. Credentials stay in protected user configuration/credential storage, never argv, URLs, unit-file literals or logs.

### 2. Build the listener and local checkpoint

- Configure the Hearth base URL, credential reference, polling interval and bounded catch-up policy. Require HTTPS for remote connections and verify certificates; allow HTTP for explicit loopback development.
- On first setup, establish a high-water checkpoint and start with new arrivals, avoiding a flood of historical inbox entries. Offer an explicit bounded catch-up option.
- Persist the cursor and per-notification presentation state atomically in the user's state directory. Exclude concurrent listeners for the same profile. Ordinary polling, reconnects and service restarts must not repeat already acknowledged desktop submissions.
- Do not promise exactly-once visible popups: D-Bus submission and local checkpoint persistence are not one transaction. Record an uncertain submission when the desktop reply is lost or the process crashes in that window; do not automatically resubmit that item. The durable Hearth inbox remains available, and local diagnostics must expose the uncertainty.
- Bound network requests, backoff, queues and catch-up batches. Collapse a large backlog into a clearly counted summary linking to the inbox. Never advance over unprocessed entries silently.
- Treat missing desktop service, a restarted notification daemon, offline Hearth, rejected authentication and malformed responses as distinct recoverable/diagnostic states. Reconnect without notification storms. Authentication rejection stops repeated credential attempts until configuration changes or an explicit retry.

### 3. Native presentation and navigation

- Use app name **Hearth**, a suitable icon, normal desktop urgency and short summaries such as “Resident run failed” or “Resident run finished”. Use only allowlisted notification metadata; never include task instructions, report bodies, credentials or raw server errors on the lock screen.
- Add **Open in Hearth** using the recorded local resource link, resolved against the configured trusted base URL. Validate the destination, invoke the browser without shell interpolation, and never place authentication credentials in the link. The browser uses its normal Hearth login.
- Respect desktop do-not-disturb and notification history behavior. A successful D-Bus reply means the desktop accepted the notification, not that a person saw or read it.
- Do not mutate Hearth read/unread state for popup submission, dismissal or action invocation. Only existing explicit inbox actions do that.

### 4. Package and document setup

- Ship the listener entry point, a systemd user-unit template and an Omarchy setup/runbook with install, configure, enable, status, logs, smoke check and removal instructions.
- Tie service lifetime to the graphical session with the correct user environment and session bus. Verify behavior across logout/login and suspend/resume; do not enable user lingering merely to show notifications.
- Keep user customization under su

sample.title: Naming convergence, deferred pieces: repo-slug sweep (agent-supervisor only, not agent-tui), state-dir migration, stop-new-debt guard
sample.body:
Decision on `#naming` (director brief): **B — fix the wire format now (dispatched: #767), stop new naming debt from accumulating, let the rest age out.**

This tracks the deferred pieces, explicitly not urgent, not blocking anything:

## 1. Hardcoded repo-slug sweep (`agent-tui` 285, `agent-supervisor` 100 references)

**Do not sweep `agent-tui` references yet.** The migration's Step 7 deletes that repo; sweeping 285 references to it now may be work that gets thrown away for free once that lands. Re-scope this once Step 3 (issue transfer, currently blocked on the private/public disclosure question) and Step 7 are further along.

`agent-supervisor` references (100) are a different case — real, live drift (the pre-rename slug), same class already fixed piecemeal this session (#734, #742, #752, #755's own near-miss). Worth a real, scoped sweep, but as its own deliberate pass with the same "don't blanket sed, some are historical citations" discipline `#729`'s own sweep already established — not a blanket rename.

## 2. State directory migration

```
~/.local/state/agent-dotfiles-supervisor   1267 entries   <- the real ledger, live data
~/.local/state/estate-loop                  210 entries
~/.local/state/hill90-codex-supervisor        9 entries
~/.local/state/hill90-supervisor                          <- named in adapter.py's shim contract
```

Moving the ledger directory is a migration, not a rename — 1267 live entries, and everything that reads `SUPERVISOR_STATE`/`AGENT_SUPERVISOR_STATE_DIR` (which is most of `scripts/supervisor/`) needs to keep resolving correctly through it. Needs its own scoping pass before anyone touches it: what moves, what's a symlink-back compat shim, how it's verified before the old path is ever removed.

`hill90-codex-supervisor` and `hill90-supervisor` carry the tenant name directly — same "wrong on principle" class as the wire format (#767), just in state-directory form rather than protocol form. Lower urgency than the wire format (no accumulating write-once-read-forever cost the way GitHub markers have), but real.

## 3. tmux session

Already tracked: `#739` (converge the warm lane pool from `agent-supervisor` into `agent-estate`). This issue doesn't duplicate it — just noting it's part of the same naming-convergence story.

## 4. Stop-the-bleeding guard

No new `hill90-*` (tenant name) or `agent-supervisor` (dead repo slug) references should land in new code going forward. Worth a cheap, mechanized guard (grep-based CI check with an allowlist for historical citations and existing files pending the sweeps above) rather than relying on review discipline alone — same shape `cross_repo_references_test.go` already uses for stale issue references. Not filed as a separate issue; whoever picks this up should decide if it's worth its own PR or folds into whichever sweep happens first.

Ref: director brief on naming, #767, #739

sample.title: Framework and sandbox CLI upgrades have no in-flight guard; sibling pages can race the Update Center queue
sample.body:
## Symptom

Two of the four update kinds have **no server-side guard against a second concurrent upgrade of the same target**, and the web app has several surfaces that can trigger the same upgrade independently of the Update Center's single queue:

- Framework upgrade (`POST /agents/:id/framework-version/upgrade[-stream]`): `apps/api/src/modules/agents/framework-versions/framework-upgrade.service.ts` runs `execSprite` (npm install, or a 5–15 min rebuild) inline with no lock, no in-flight status, no 409. Two overlapping requests run two installs on the same sprite.
- Sandbox CLI upgrade (`POST /sandboxes/:id/cli/upgrade`): `apps/api/src/modules/sandboxes/sandboxes.service.ts` `upgradeCli()` runs `curl | sh` inline, no lock, no rate limit.
- For contrast, daemon CLI upgrades have the 5/60 s per-actor limiter plus the daemon's own `'daemon update already in progress'` refusal, and skills serialize on `pg_advisory_xact_lock` in `skill-materializer.service.ts`.

Client-side, the Update Center store (`apps/web/src/lib/updateRunStore.ts`) refuses a second batch while one runs, but the sibling surfaces dispatch on their own: `apps/web/src/components/RuntimeDetailPanel.tsx` `handleUpgradeFramework`, `apps/web/src/pages/AgentRuntimesList.tsx` `handleUpgradeHostCli` / `handleUpgradeSandboxCli`, `apps/web/src/pages/Skills/AgentSkillsPanel.tsx` `update()`. Now that the queue keeps running after leaving `/updates` (#180), the window in which a user can race their own queue from another page is the whole remaining batch rather than one step.

Also: none of these handlers pass an `AbortSignal`, so a closed tab still completes the server-side work — fine for completion, but it means a retry after a "failed" network response can double-run.

## Suggested fix

1. Server: a per-target in-flight guard for framework and sandbox CLI upgrades (409 while one is running; the sprite exec could also record a `pending` version so the list endpoints can show in-flight state — today `GET /agent-runtimes` and `GET /sandboxes` can only report the final version).
2. Client (cheap, independent): a `useIsTargetUpdating(targetKey)` selector on `updateRunStore` that the sibling surfaces use to disable their own upgrade buttons while the queue holds that target.

sample.title: [Provider Profiles] Make creation actions and collapsed advanced summaries reflect actual state
sample.body:
## Decision and design source

Focused follow-up to closed #1205. Keep the existing single create/edit form, advanced disclosure, and credential lifecycle. This issue fixes misleading presentation and setup recovery, not the underlying provider architecture.

Design PR: #4000.

Canonical requirements:

- `docs/UI/ProviderProfileCreation.md` sections 4.9, 5.2–5.4, 9–11, 13, 14.2, and 14.8.
- `docs/UI/SettingsPage.md` sections 7.1.1–7.1.2 and 8.

Related: #4001 owns runtime/provider selectors and Profile ID suggestions. There is no functional dependency on that issue; coordinate changes to the shared form rather than introducing duplicate state models.

## Reviewed baseline

Reviewed 2026-09-05 against `2dc036a767d4408e5d9e07ae2134071c380ab462`. `ProviderProfilesManager.tsx` has the same component blob `1ac3935e936a48c1f861d706d3929fd37bd96531` as the prior source review.

The form already has backend creation presets/capabilities, guided API-key and OAuth continuations, visible connection/readiness, draft baselines, advanced-field validation focus, and a reset preview. The remaining presentation problems include:

- The normal creation button uses `Create profile` even when successful creation continues into credential enrollment.
- The collapsed advanced summary chooses `Using recommended ... launch settings` from the existence of an authentication capability, rather than comparing the actual draft against its recommendation. Custom values can therefore receive reassuring but inaccurate copy.
- Normal-form copy exposes preset versions and omission/normalization mechanics that belong in advanced diagnostics.

The existing conformance tests include literal `Create profile` assertions. Update the appropriate cases based on their real behavior rather than replacing that string globally. Source inspection does not establish that every enrollment-recovery case is broken; reproduce those cases before changing behavior.

## Goal

The form tells users what the next action does and whether advanced configuration is recommended, custom, or needs attention. It never confuses a saved profile with successful connection, activation, or launch readiness, and it never encourages duplicate creation after confirmed save followed by incomplete setup.

## Implementation plan

### 1. Derive action presentation from the existing save/continuation contract

Add or extract a small presentation helper around the current form state and generated capability/preset types. Use the exact runtime/provider/authentication identity, manual-path permission, supported setup action, existing-profile state, and pending mutation state that the save and post-save continuation consume.

Required states:

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Supported create with an actual guided OAuth/API-key continuation | `Create and connect` |
| Supported create without a credential setup continuation | `Create profile` |
| Explicitly supported manual creation returning a disabled profile | `Save disabled profile` with next-step guidance |
| Existing profile edit | `Update provider profile` |
| Missing/invalid choices, permission, capability, or preset | Disabled creation action with the specific reason |
| Save in progress | Disabled progress action, such as `Creating profile...` or `Saving changes...` |

Do not infer a supported continuation from an authentication-method name alone. Use the existing setup capability and actual handler availability. An imported-volume flow already validated by its backend may differ from pending OAuth enrollment and must not be mislabeled.

Button label, request payload, and continuation must use the same submitted snapshot. Late metadata or a user changing selection during a request must not redirect the saved profile into another credential flow. Suppress repeated submission while the same save is pending.

### 2. Make post-save notices and setup recovery truthful

Treat the normalized server result as authority for identity, connection, enabled state, and launch readiness. A successful create establishes persistence only unless the result also establishes the other outcomes.

Trace and test confirmed create followed by pending, failed, canceled, or expired enrollment. Keep the saved identity visible and use its existing connect/retry action. Do not present the original draft as an unsaved profile that should be POSTed again. A retry of credential enrollment must target the already-saved profile. Preserve the existing default-intent readiness guard and do not activate a disabled profile through a presentation change.

Use the existing saved-profile/enrollment state and recovery mechanisms. Do not build a new persisted onboarding workflow. An ambiguous create response is not confirmed persistence; retain the current reconciliation/error behavior and do not invent a success notice or silently retry creation.

Replace ordinary developer-oriented success copy with outcome-oriented guidance, such as `Recommended settings loaded` and `Connect this account to finish setup`. Keep preset identity and technical diagnostic detail available in the existing advanced region. Preserve actionable errors and secret redaction.

### 3. Compute an honest advanced-policy summary

Reuse or extract one pure comparison/presentation helper over the existing normalized draft, saved baseline, matching backend preset/capability metadata, source information, and diagnostics. Align it with the payload builder and reset semantics. Do not introduce a second backend default table or security-policy resolver.

Return enough presentation state to distinguish:

- **Recommended:** matching validated metadata, understood values, no advanced deviations or warnings.
- **Custom:** a bounded count and labels for known differing top-level advanced controls.
- **Needs attention:** unknown, incompatible, invalid, or warned advanced state. A warning takes precedence over reassuring recommendation text.
- **Comparison unavailable/loading:** missing, stal

sample.title: Players and coaches get no emails for reminders, confirmation, disputes or payouts
sample.body:
## Problem
After a player pays, the platform goes almost silent. For coaching sessions the API sends exactly two emails, both through `apps/api/src/calendar/ics-calendar.provider.ts`:

- **On payment:** `BookingsService.sendInviteOnce` sends the same `.ics` invite email to both parties. The coach gets no "you have a new booking" message with the player, service or attached clips. The player gets no receipt with the amount held in escrow.
- **On pre-start cancellation:** `BookingsService.cancel` → `sendCancellationIfInvited` sends the same CANCEL email to both parties. It doesn't say who cancelled or that the player was refunded.

Everything else in the session lifecycle sends nothing:

- **No reminders.** 24h / 1h reminders exist only for admin verification calls (`apps/api/src/scheduling/reminders.service.ts`, stamps `reminder24hSentAt` / `reminder1hSentAt` on `VerificationBooking`). `Session` has no equivalent.
- **Session ended.** `SessionProgressionService` moves the session to `awaiting_confirmation` and, 48h later (`AUTO_CONFIRM_WINDOW_HOURS`), to `completed_paid`. The player is never told to confirm or report a problem, so the deadline passes unnoticed unless they open the dashboard.
- **Disputes.** `DisputesService.open` and `resolve` never call the mailer. Admins learn about a new dispute only by opening `/dashboard/disputes`. The coach learns about it, and about the outcome, only from the sessions list.
- **Money.** `SettlementService` releases or refunds escrow silently. The coach is not told they were paid; the player is not told they were refunded.
- **Reviews.** `ReviewsService.create` doesn't tell the coach about a new review, and nothing asks the player to leave one.
- **Clips.** `SessionVideosService.replace` lets the player change the clip set until the session starts. The coach isn't told, so they may prepare on the wrong clips.

The emails that do exist have quality problems too:

- **English only.** `apps/api/src/mailer/mailer.service.ts` builds hard-coded English plain text. `User.locale` (en/fr/de/ru/zh) is ignored.
- **UTC times.** The session invite body shows `2026-09-20, 14:00–15:00 UTC` (`whenLine` in `ics-calendar.provider.ts`) instead of the recipient's `User.timezone`. The verification emails already format in the user's timezone (`SchedulingNotificationsService.whenLine`), but still in English.
- **No retry.** `MailerService.send` catches and logs every SMTP error. Callers can't know a send failed. `RemindersService` stamps the reminder as sent even when SMTP was down, so a failed email is lost.

## Why it's needed
- **Missed sessions cost money and trust.** A booking made a week ahead with no reminder is an easy no-show. A no-show ends in a refund, a dispute, or a coach paid for nothing.
- **The confirmation window only works if players know about it.** The 48h auto-confirm releases money by default. A player who had a problem but never saw the prompt loses the chance to report it. That is unfair to players, and it will surface as chargebacks once a real payment provider is in place.
- **Disputes wait for someone to look.** Escrow is frozen while a dispute is open. Without an admin alert, resolution time depends on how often an admin opens the queue.
- **Coaches need to prepare.** A coach who isn't told about a new booking or changed clips can't review the footage before a video-analysis call.
- **Money movements need a written record.** Paying into escrow and getting paid out are exactly the moments users expect an email. Without it, they contact support.
- **5 locales are a product promise.** A German or Russian user who gets English emails with UTC times reads the platform as unfinished.

## What it brings
- **For players:** a reminder before each session, a clear "confirm or report a problem by {date, your time}" prompt, and a written record of charges and refunds, in their language.
- **For coaches:** a "new booking" email with what to prepare, reminders, notice when clips change, payout and review notifications, and immediate notice when a session is cancelled or disputed.
- **For the platform:**
  - fewer no-shows and fewer disputes caused by silence;
  - faster dispute resolution (admin alert);
  - more reviews, because the request comes at the right moment;
  - one localized email layer that later features reuse (messaging, rescheduling, earnings).

**Hypotheses to validate after release** (DB queries or the admin analytics view):
- share of `completed_paid` sessions confirmed by the player (`playerConfirmedAt` set) vs auto-confirmed goes up;
- share of paid online sessions where a party has no attendance row goes down;
- reviews per paid-out session go up;
- median time from dispute opened to resolved goes down;
- daily email volume stays well below the provider cap; bounce and complaint rates stay low.

## Scope

### Events, recipients, timing
All links point to the recipient's locale (`/{locale}/dashboard/sessions`, the room URL, the coach page). All times use the recipient's `User.timezone` with the zone shown, and amounts use their locale's currency format. Free text written by the other party (dispute reason, admin note) is **not** copied into emails. The email links to the session, where the text is already visible to the parties.

| # | Event | Trigger | Player | Coach | Admins | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Booking paid | `pending_payment → paid_escrow` | Booking confirmed + receipt (amount held in escrow) + `.ics` | New booking: player name, service, clip count, link + `.ics` | – | Immediately |
| 2 | Clips changed | `SessionVideosService.replace` on a paid session | – | Clips updated, link | – | One email after 15 min without further changes |
| 3 | Reminder | Clock | Reminder with room link or venue | Same; for video analysis, "review the clips" | – | T-24h and T-1h. Skip a window that had already started when the booking was paid (same rule as `RemindersService`). |
| 4 | Session ended | `→ awaiting_confirmation` | Co

sample.title: [docs] Reduce ATS-EXTRACTION.md to the extraction policy it alone owns
sample.body:
## Goal

`docs/ATS-EXTRACTION.md` is 12,528 words — 35% of everything in `docs/`, and
2.8× the next-largest file. Reduce it to the extraction, tagging, and font
policy it alone owns, by removing the sections whose rule has a home in another
canonical source, and pointing at that source instead.

This continues the reduction already applied to `TESTING.md` (#502 → PR #503)
and `ARCHITECTURE.md` (#504 → PR #507), and the three earlier passes over this
same file (#262, #450, #480). It is not a rewrite: surviving prose is left
alone so the diff stays reviewable.

## Motivation

The file's own scope banner says it is design and reference material, not
documentation of shipped behavior. Several sections have drifted past that
line and now restate rules that `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the PDF
manual, and `RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md` own. Two consequences:

- A restated rule has to be corrected in two places, and one of them will be
  missed — the failure mode #492/#500 exists to catch.
- One restatement now **conflicts** with its owner. "Compilation policy" §
  "Supported command" prescribes a hand-written `lualatex -file-line-error
  -halt-on-error …` invocation, which `AGENTS.md` § "Build and test" forbids
  in favour of the `Makefile` targets.

Where the words are, measured (`## ` sections, descending):

| words | section |
|---:|---|
| 4470 | Tagged PDF and accessibility under current LaTeX |
| 1627 | Layout rules: safe defaults and risky patterns |
| 1527 | Typography and font engineering under LuaLaTeX |
| 1269 | Semantic structure for each career-document type |
| 994 | Hyperlinks, icons, symbols, bullets, and punctuation |
| 458 | Minimal reference template and class skeleton |
| 417 | Executive standard |
| 358 | What "ATS-friendly" should mean in this package |
| 358 | Sources and how to use this guide |
| 265 | A design and reference guide for CareerDossierTeX |
| 258 | What to do and what not to do while writing the package |
| 139 | Compilation policy |
| 119 | Ongoing maintenance rule |
| 90 | Current external references |
| 74 | Documentation requirements |

Size alone is not the criterion, and the histogram is deliberately not the
cut list: the four largest sections are the measured extraction and tagging
findings this file exists to hold, and they stay.

## Included

Each candidate below is a section whose *rule* is stated elsewhere. Each is
verified against its claimed owner before it is cut (see "How this could be
wrong").

- **Header § "Current published scope (`v0.8.0`)"** (~180 w) — restates the
  full class-option surface, which the manual owns. Currently accurate, and
  re-verifying it is a cost paid every release.
- **"Sources and how to use this guide"** (358 w) — a bibliography of general
  LaTeX class-authoring references (`clsguide`, *The LaTeX Companion*,
  `lshort`, `fontspec`). Not extraction policy, and six of its URLs already
  appear again in "Current external references" (90 w) at the foot of the same
  file.
- **"Compilation policy" § "Supported command"** — the conflict above.
  § "Reproducibility" and § "Warnings as engineering signals" are extraction
  and font policy and stay.
- **"Documentation requirements"** (74 w) — names `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  ("Documentation requirements") as owner, then restates it in the next clause.
- **"What to do and what not to do while writing the package"** (258 w) — a
  32-bullet checklist. Spot-checked, it restates Executive-standard rules 5 and
  6 nearly verbatim, `AGENTS.md` rules 1 and 10, and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  "Coding conventions". Cite-and-restate within one file.
- **"Minimal reference template and class skeleton"** (458 w) — the user
  template is the manual's, the class outline is `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s, and the
  section already labels the latter "(illustrative)".
- **"Semantic structure for each career-document type"** (1269 w) — audit only
  the entries tagged **(planned — later phase)** (Industry CV, Reference list)
  against `AGENTS.md` rule 3. The shipped types stay.
- **"Ongoing maintenance rule"** (119 w) — its seven release-cycle steps
  overlap `RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md`, which the section itself names as owner in
  its closing paragraph.

Candidate pool before verification: roughly 2,700 words, ~22%.

## Excluded

- Any change to the four measurement-bearing sections: "Tagged PDF and
  accessibility", "Layout rules", "Typography and font engineering",
  "Hyperlinks, icons, symbols, bullets, and punctuation". These hold findings
  that exist nowhere else — the Poppler block-grouping mechanism, the
  `\CDossierRecordListEdgeAboveSkip` floor, the `/ActualText` limits.
- Rewriting or re-toning prose that survives. Cut and point; do not reword.
- Deduplicating *user-facing* documentation. #479–#483 settled that boundary
  and it is not reopened here.
- Any change to what the file claims — no ATS, WCAG, or PDF/UA claim is added,
  removed, or softened (`AGENTS.md` rule 10).

## Proposed public interface

```latex
% None. Documentation only; no command, option, key, or environment changes.
```

## Likely files

The section histogram that produced the table above:

```bash
awk '
/^## / { if (sec!="") printf "%-6d %s\n", w, sec; sec=$0; w=0; next }
{ if (sec!="") w += NF }
END { if (sec!="") printf "%-6d %s\n", w, sec }
' docs/ATS-EXTRACTION.md | sort -rn
```

Inbound references, which decide what a removed heading may break:

```bash
grep -rn "ATS-EXTRACTION" . --exclude-dir=.git
```

- `docs/ATS-EXTRACTION.md` — the cuts
- any file whose `ATS-EXTRACTION.md#anchor` link targets a removed heading
- `CHANGELOG.md` — only if a user-visible statement changes, which is not
  expected

## Acceptance criteria

```bash
# No rule survives in two places: for each cut, the claimed owner must state it.
grep -rn "halt-on-error" . --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=build
# Every cross-document anchor still resolves.
make lint
```

- [ ] Every section listed under "Included" is either cut with a pointer to its
      owner, or kept with

sample.title: ♻️ Migrate the core agent sources to capability profiles and retire metadata.claude.model (epic #1100 seam f)
sample.body:
Part of epic #1100 — seam (f). Seams (a) to (e) are on `main`: the capability-profile vocabulary (spec 0195), the spec 0143 delta, the core default mappings (spec 0197, `f8336dc`), the build's resolution of a profile against the mapping in force (spec 0198, `8773a06`) and the organization-level override channel with the `regenerable` sync policy (spec 0199, `723ad8f`). Every mechanism exists; no agent source uses it yet. This ticket migrates the core agent sources to `metadata.model:` profiles and removes the legacy `metadata.claude.model` key, so the compiled agents finally carry a CLI-agnostic model declaration.

## Intent

Every core agent source declares a capability profile (`metadata.model:`) equivalent to the informal tier its `metadata.claude.model` key encodes today — `haiku` → `intelligence: medium`, `sonnet` → `intelligence: high`, `opus` → `intelligence: xhigh` (spec 0195 R7's anchor table; spec 0195 → *Out of scope* records this correspondence as the property seam (f) relies on) — and the legacy key disappears from every source. The build then regenerates all compiled agent outputs from sources × mappings, and the committed outputs change for the first time: a guidance sentence in the compiled `description` on Claude Code (the guard being `withheld`, no `model:` field) and on Antigravity CLI, a native `model:` field on Gemini CLI, nothing on GitHub Copilot CLI (zero offerings). Documentation that still presents a Claude-specific model override is demoted or removed in favour of the profile.

## Facts to build on (tree at `723ad8f`)

- 22 core agent sources under `artifacts/core/agents/*/AGENT.md` carry `metadata.claude.model`: 10 `haiku` (copywriter, pr-logbook, doc-writer, seo-specialist, scenario-author, regression-sentinel, accessibility-tester, accessibility-auditor, web-conformity-checker, visual-regression-tester), 11 `sonnet` (tester, designer, security, ci-parity, developer, ci-debugger, spec-author, pr-reviewer, astro-developer, ci-configurator, frontend-developer), 1 `opus` (architect). The library agent `artifacts/library/agents/harness-curator/AGENT.md` carries no model key.
- `scripts/build-components.sh` does not read `metadata.claude.model` (no occurrence); the compiled Claude outputs carry no model field today. `artifacts/FORMAT.md` documents an optional top-level `claude:` override section with `model` and `effort` fields (lines 55–66, 105–118) — the "Claude override" the epic says to demote or remove — and, since seam (d), the `metadata.model:` block.
- What the resolver emits today for a `medium` profile (`bash scripts/build-components.sh --resolve <source> <target>`): Claude — guidance prose `Run this agent on the haiku model.` appended to the description, no `model:` (guard `withheld`), a declared `reasoning` dropped `unsupported-on-model` on `haiku`; Gemini — `model: gemini-3.5-flash` (`high` → `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`; `xhigh` → the ceiling, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`); Copilot — nothing; Antigravity — prose naming `gemini-3.8-flash-medium` (`high`/`xhigh` → `gemini-3.1-pro-low` by lowest rank). Whether the migration also declares `reasoning` (and for which agents) is a decision for the spec.
- Every modified source needs a `metadata.provenance.version` bump in the same diff (`AGENTS.md` → *Version Bump Convention*, enforced by `scripts/check-skill-versions.sh`); adding a profile is an additive metadata change (MINOR).
- Seam (g), the flat compiled layout `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, is not done; the epic prefers (g) before (f) so the migration lands in the flat layout. The maintainer chose to run (f) now; the migration therefore lands in the nested layout and seam (g) moves the files later. The spec records this ordering and its consequence (one more regeneration of the same outputs).

## Scope (to be qualified by the spec)

- **Profile per source** — the mapping from the legacy tier to `intelligence` (medium/high/xhigh), whether any source declares `reasoning`, `specialization` or a tuning knob, and on what evidence; `harness-curator`'s profile (or its explicit absence); the removal of `metadata.claude.model` from all 22 sources; version bumps.
- **Regenerated outputs** — all four compiled agent trees regenerated in the same change set (`AGENTS.md` → *Built components*); the expected shape per target stated and verified (Claude/Antigravity description prose, Gemini `model:`, Copilot unchanged); spec 0143 delta-01 R1–R4 honoured (a `model:` field only where a resolution directs it); the `regenerable` policy makes the drift acceptable for forks.
- **Documentation** — `artifacts/FORMAT.md`: demote or remove the `claude:` `model`/`effort` override in favour of `metadata.model:` (decide: remove if unused by any source and by the build, else demote); `docs/agent-team-protocol.md` / any doc naming the haiku/sonnet/opus tiering as the way to pick a model (audit and update to the profile vocabulary); `docs/cli-matrix.md` row if a CLI-specific fact changes; a migration note for adopters (how an organization's own agent sources migrate; the org override channel is where a fork changes what a tier resolves to).
- **Guards** — the profile validator (`check-agent-profiles.sh`) is green on the migrated sources; a CI guard (or a documented convention) that no source re-introduces `metadata.claude.model`; `component-drift` green on the regenerated tree; `check-skill-versions.sh` green.
- **e2e / probe C** — the migration puts guidance prose into every Claude and Antigravity compiled agent; probe C (#1113) tests whether that prose is honoured and whether it disturbs a Copilot reader. The spec states what the migration does if probe C refutes a cell (the mapping edit of spec 0199/0198 removes the surface; the sources do not change).

## Out of scope

- Seam (g) flat layout; probe C execution; the org override channel's content (a fork's mappings); any change to the normative text of specs 0195, 0197, 0198, 0199, 0143 delta-01; new agents; changes to skills or commands.

sample.title: Launch: verify the /help journey end-to-end, including support delivery and failure states
sample.body:
## Scope

Audit the actual **krabiclaw.com/help** journey and verify that visitors and customers can find an answer or reach the intended support destination without a dead end. Review both the visible interface and the runtime delivery path; a successful page load or success toast alone is not completion.

Cover questions and connection problems for Claude and the ChatGPT plugin/app, plus the business verticals actually supported at launch.

## Work

### Establish and exercise the intended journey

- Inventory all entry points to /help, the actions it exposes, and their intended destinations: documentation, search/FAQ/AI assistance if present, account/billing guidance, contact/support forms, and any human-support escalation.
- Record expected behavior for each branch. Do not assume that a support channel, AI answer flow, or notification exists merely because copy mentions it.
- Test logged-out visitors, new users, signed-in owners/members, expired sessions, and users with more than one organization where applicable. Verify redirects and return paths; do not silently choose the wrong organization or site. Link #905 when its multi-org routing behavior affects the journey.
- Verify platform help stays in the intended platform context and does not accidentally submit to a tenant's business inbox or expose another organization's content.
- Check mobile/desktop layouts, keyboard navigation, visible focus, accessible labels/errors, loading indicators, navigation/back behavior, and supported light/dark appearance.

### Answers, forms, and delivery

- Exercise representative questions, Claude/ChatGPT setup and authorization errors, no-result queries, broken/stale article links, and escalation from an unanswered question. If AI answers/search are exposed, verify grounding in published documentation, working source links, and explicit no-answer/error behavior rather than invented instructions.
- For every exposed submission flow, test required fields, malformed inputs, loading, successful submission, provider/network failure, retries, duplicate clicks, refresh/back behavior, and applicable abuse/rate-limit responses. Failures must remain visible and recoverable; do not show a false success.
- Trace an authorized test submission from browser request through persisted support record, intended inbox/recipient, notification/delivery result, user acknowledgement, and reply/follow-up where those steps are part of the implemented flow. Confirm submission identity and routing; redact sensitive evidence.
- Use approved test accounts and controlled recipients. Do not send repeated tests to real customers or treat staging log-only delivery as evidence that production delivery works.
- Verify privacy/terms links and data-use copy against #936. Do not advertise response times, channels, or deletion behavior that have not been approved and implemented.

## Related work and sequencing

The functional audit can start now. Re-test help content, article links, search/knowledge retrieval, and relevant guidance after #938's documentation refresh and #936's approved policy changes. Check #917 for knowledge-index rebuild failures and #928 for shared notification/inbox rendering defects when those paths are used; link existing work rather than duplicate it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every visible help branch has a recorded expected result and a tested outcome.
- [ ] Both logged-out and signed-in users can complete the intended journey on mobile and desktop.
- [ ] Claude and ChatGPT guidance reflects the released integrations and routes to working documentation.
- [ ] Controlled support submissions reach the correct persisted record and intended recipient/inbox; acknowledgement and follow-up are verified where promised.
- [ ] Empty, validation, authentication, permission, network/provider, retry, and duplicate-submission cases are checked without false-success states or cross-tenant leakage.
- [ ] Launch-blocking defects are fixed and retested; remaining findings have linked issues, owners, and explicit launch dispositions.
- [ ] A dated browser/runtime verification report identifies environment/release, test accounts by non-sensitive identifiers, reproduction steps, screenshots, redacted delivery evidence, and reviewer sign-off.

sample.title: Agent-to-control-plane depends_on serialises teardown, costing ~29% of every destroy
sample.body:
## Related Files:
- `k3s_cluster/cluster_ec2.tf`

## Description:
`aws_instance.agentplane_ec2_node` declares `depends_on = [aws_instance.controlplane_ec2_node]`.
That is correct for **create** — agents join a cluster that already exists — but
`depends_on` reverses on **destroy**, so the agent must reach `terminated` before
Terraform will even *issue* the control-plane terminate calls.

Measured on a teardown of the default 3 control-plane + 1 agent deployment
(2026-09-11, total runtime 7m32s):

| Phase | Duration | % of destroy |
|---|---|---|
| plan | 17s | 4% |
| LB attachments, listeners, target groups | 9s | 2% |
| **agent terminating (control planes blocked)** | **2m56s** | **39%** |
| control planes terminating | 2m12s | 29% |
| Karpenter reap | 24s | 5% |
| network teardown (SG, subnets, IGW, VPC) | 1m34s | 21% |

Waiting on EC2 termination is **5m08s — 68% of the whole destroy**, and 2m56s of
that is serialization rather than work. The log shows the handoff precisely:

```
agentplane_ec2_node[0]:   Destruction complete after 3m52s   <- earlier run
controlplane_ec2_node[1]: Destroying...      (immediately after)
controlplane_ec2_node[0]: Destroying...
controlplane_ec2_node[2]: Destroying...
```

If the two planes terminated in parallel the instance phase would drop from
~5m08s to ~2m56s, saving roughly **2m12s (29%) off every teardown**.

It is also the source of run-to-run variance: across two teardowns of the same
cluster, Terraform issued the control-plane terminates at +172s and +252s. That
80-second swing is agent termination time, and it was what made an earlier
timing-based version of the Karpenter reaper (#128) fail on one run and pass with
48 seconds to spare on another.

## Additional Notes:
The comment on the block is also stale — it reads "Wait for EC2 node to be set up
before we start setting up ELB", but the `depends_on` is on the agent and points
at the control planes, and says nothing about the ELB.

Worth checking whether the dependency is needed at all: k3s agents retry joining,
and the bootstrap already tolerates a server that is not yet up. If the retry is
sufficient, removing it parallelises **create** as well as destroy.

If it must stay for create ordering, note that Terraform has no way to express a
create-only dependency — the options are to remove it, or to accept the destroy
cost.

Not urgent: a predictable ~7m30s teardown is fine, and the extra minutes of
Karpenter node runtime cost cents. Filed so the measurement is not lost.

## Acceptance Criteria:
- The destroy-time cost of the agent/control-plane ordering is either removed or
  documented as a deliberate trade with its measured cost
- If the dependency is removed, a deploy still comes up healthy (agents join)
- The stale comment on the block is corrected

sample.title: finding(types): four objectui#8499 arms of `AnyComponentSchema` have no named export on `./zod` — the objectui#7917 defect recurred one day after its repair
sample.body:
Filed from the objectui#8784 implementation run (the pin that fails when an `AnyComponentSchema` arm has no named zod export), by the `os-dev` seat on branch `claude/issue-8784-arm-named-export-pin`, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`. Filed unassigned and ungraded — `domain:*`, type and priority are the triage seat's. Not ridden onto that PR: adding an exported symbol is a `Clause-2` act and objectui#8784's dispatch says stop and report first.

## The reading

Fresh census on `7f27bc54343e6193f11ec3f58927fb9afb1bc635`, derived (not hard-coded): flatten `AnyComponentSchema` recursively through unions and `z.lazy`, then match each leaf arm to a named export of `./zod` **by identity**.

**111 arms / 154 `type` literals / 106 named / 5 unnamed.**

Four of the five are unnamed by accident:

| arm | `type` literals | landed |
|---|---|---|
| `layout.zod.ts#SemanticElementSchema` | 7 (`aside`, `main`, `header`, `nav`, `footer`, `section`, `article`) | `507b61bf7` |
| `layout.zod.ts#HtmlElementSchema` | 37 (`h1` … `q`) | `507b61bf7` |
| `form.zod.ts#InputShorthandSchema` | 2 (`email`, `password`) | `507b61bf7` |
| `form.zod.ts#UiCalendarSchema` | 1 (`ui:calendar`) | `507b61bf7` |

The fifth, `complex.zod.ts#RetiredKanbanNodeSchema` (`kanban`), is DECLARED internal in as many words on the barrel itself — "it is deliberately NOT exported — nothing outside this package parses against a refusal arm" (objectui#8802, maintainer ruling 2026-09-09). That one is correct as it stands and is ledgered as such by the objectui#8784 pin.

## Why this is the objectui#7917 defect again, not a new one

`507b61bf7` is PR #8763, `fix(types): arm AnyComponentSchema for seven registered node-slot renderers (objectui#8499)`, merged 2026-09-09T07:53:59Z. Its own commit message states the move: "Four arms, 47 literals, 107 to 154". Its file list touches `packages/types/src/zod/form.zod.ts` and `packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts` and **does not touch `packages/types/src/zod/index.zod.ts`** — the same shape as objectui#7917's `ObjectTreeSchema`, which PR #1892 added to a module and never to the barrel.

`./zod` is this package's ONLY zod subpath (`packages/types/package.json` maps it to `dist/zod/index.zod.js`), and the barrel carries no star re-export — every name on it is written out by hand. So these four schemas are maintained, are applied by the union, and cannot be named by any consumer: declared-and-unreachable, which is exactly the state objectui#7917 measured and PR #8777 repaired for the two arms it found.

They are not marginal or half-declared. All four were registered as first-class mirror pairs in the same PR — `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` gained a `ZOD_MIRRORS` row and a TypeScript counterpart for each, and `EXPECTED_MIRROR_PAIRS` moved 158 to 162. The objectui#7917 repair used exactly that fact ("the parity census registers both as first-class mirrors with a TS counterpart rather than exempting them") as its evidence that the omission was accidental.

None of the four carries any of this directory's seven "Deliberately NOT exported" / "`@internal` … is not re-exported" markers.

## Timing — why objectui#8784 reads 107/107/0 and this reads 111/154/5

objectui#8784 was filed 2026-09-09T07:05:02Z. `507b61bf7` merged 48 minutes later. The card's census was correct when it was taken and went stale within the hour, which is itself the strongest available argument for the pin objectui#8784 asks for: the invariant broke again, in the same way, one day after a review repaired it, and nothing said a word.

## What is being asked

A ruling per arm: re-export it from `packages/types/src/zod/index.zod.ts`, or mark it deliberately internal with a reason the way `RetiredKanbanNodeSchema` is marked.

Recommendation: export all four. Each is a registered, live renderer with catalog fixtures (that is why objectui#8499 armed them); each has a TypeScript counterpart already; and the alternative reading — that a `type` an author is taught to write in `content/docs/utilities/runner.mdx` should be un-nameable — matches nothing else on this face.

Cost if exported: four new names on a published surface, hence `Clause-2`. Cost if not: an author validating a single `h1` node has no schema to validate it against, and objectui#8784's pin carries four ledger rows saying the answer is owed.

Until the ruling lands, the objectui#8784 pin ledgers all four against this card, so nothing here is silent and no NEW omission can hide behind them.

Refs: objectui#7917 (the same defect, two other arms) · PR #8777 (its repair) · objectui#8499 (the card that armed these four) · PR #8763 (`507b61bf7`, the commit that armed them without the barrel) · objectui#8784 (the pin) · objectui#8802 (the `RetiredKanbanNodeSchema` ruling)

Dedup: the 300 most recently updated issues and pull requests were listed over the repository-scoped REST issues endpoint and grepped locally for `HtmlElementSchema`, `SemanticElementSchema`, `UiCalendarSchema`, `InputShorthandSchema`, `barrel`, `named export`, `index.zod` and `8499` — a live reader, 25 substantive hits including objectui#8784 itself, none claiming this. Bounded honestly: the search endpoint is not reachable from this session, so this is a recency-window read, not a full-corpus one; the defect is 1.5 days old, so a card about it would fall inside that window. Nearest neighbour is objectui#8775, which is about whether the same seven sectioning tags belong in the curated layout vocabulary — a different question about the same arms.

Written by the ObjectStack `os-dev` agent seat with Claude Code; session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`.

Audited version: `0.1.0`, commit `5972b32d42d2428285e3e7ae1daa40120238b419`. Findings are against this revision, not a claim that later revisions remain affected. Local npm test passed; these are additional installation/behavior probes. No provider behavior or live CI status is inferred.

## Assessment

Medium. The destination's documentation/command contract is incomplete for an advanced user installing into an existing project.

Install level 3 into a fresh directory, selecting Obsidian as notes_tool to exercise the companion guidance.
