sample.title: E3.5 - Route identity: fail closed when the observed route differs from the requested one
sample.body:
Sub-issue of #33 · lane: `lane:n5` · topic: `features`

A dispatch that silently runs on a different model or effort than the one requested is
indistinguishable from a correct one until the bill or the output quality says otherwise. The
provider must fail closed.

netscript already does this. `launch-codex-slice.ts` compares the identity the app-server reports
back at `thread/start` (`result.model`, `result.modelProvider`, `result.reasoningEffort`,
`result.cwd`) against what was requested, and refuses the launch on any mismatch unless the
operator passes an explicit `--allow-route-mismatch` exception.

One detail is load-bearing and was learned the hard way upstream: **effort must be resolved at
`thread/start`, not as a turn-only override.** A turn-only override makes the launch evidence
report the stale default. See the comment in
`.llm/tools/agentic/codex/app-server-message.ts` → `threadStartRequest`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `DispatchResult` carries the observed route (provider, model, effort, cwd) as reported by
      the server, not the requested one echoed back
- [ ] Dispatch returns `refused` when observed ≠ requested on any of those fields, and the reason
      names which field differed and both values
- [ ] `model_reasoning_effort` is set in the `thread/start` params, and a test asserts the
      observed effort equals the requested one rather than the daemon default
- [ ] An explicit opt-out exists for the operator exception case, off by default, and its use is
      recorded in the run evidence
- [ ] A run whose route could not be observed at all is `unknown`, never `accepted`

## Why this one first

`isSafeToRetry` is true only for `refused`. A route mismatch that reports `accepted` is therefore
both wrong and unretryable — the worst cell in the matrix.

sample.title: Subagent launch fails across all profiles mid-session (4 distinct failure modes)
sample.body:
## What happened

During one driver session (started 2026-09-03 ~19:04, darwin), subagent launches worked all day: `rustcoder` (profile `zai-glm-flash`) completed 5+ tasks between 2026-09-03 22:00 and 2026-09-04 evening. Then within minutes, every launch route failed with four different errors:

1. `rustcoder` (profile `zai-glm-flash`):
   `No API key resolved for Anthropic-compatible endpoint "https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic". Configure an explicit credential (auth-key, auth-keyfile, or auth-key-name) for this profile; OAuth against api.anthropic.com is not used for third-party base URLs. Credential resolution failed; kind=credential-source-failed; provider=anthropic; profile=zai-glm-flash; attemptedMechanisms=[provider-auth-key, provider-auth-keyfile, constructor-api-key, global-auth-key, global-auth-key-name, global-auth-keyfile, env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY]`

2. `rustreviewer` (profile `opusthinking`):
   `No authentication available for Anthropic API calls. Run /auth claudecode login to authenticate (or /auth claudecode logout to clear any expired session). kind=credential-source-failed; provider=claudecode; profile=opusthinking; attemptedMechanisms=[provider-auth-key, provider-auth-keyfile, constructor-api-key, global-auth-key, global-auth-key-name, global-auth-keyfile, env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, oauth]`

3. `rustporter` (profile `dsflash-mi300x`):
   `Provider retries exhausted after 6 transport attempts: Connection error.`

4. `codeanalyzer` (profile `glm`):
   `LoadBalancer profile 'glm' references non-existent profile 'chutesglm52'`

The driver session itself kept working the whole time (it authenticated at startup).

## Evidence pointing at shared-config mutation by concurrent sessions

This machine routinely runs 8 sibling TS driver sessions (branch-1..8 worktrees) plus headless code-rs instances. Grepping for the phantom profile name from failure 4:

```
$ grep -rl chutesglm52 ~/Library/Preferences/llxprt-code/
.../code-rs-sessions/rs-issue-5t1/session.json
.../code-rs-sessions/rs-issue-5t1/session.alt.json
.../code-rs-sessions/rs-issue-7w2/session.json
```

`chutesglm52` exists only inside files written by headless rs instances. It does not exist as a defined profile anywhere the TS driver can resolve, yet the `glm` LoadBalancer profile references it, which suggests the rs sessions and the TS drivers read/write the same profile store and one side's writes can strand the other's references.

Separately, `list_subagents` shows the `rustcoder` agent's profile was switched to `zai-glm-flash` at 2026-09-03T22:25:22Z, which is exactly when this session's first rustcoder task launched, so sibling sessions are also editing agent definitions while others use them.

## Hypothesis

Concurrent sessions (TS drivers and headless rs instances) mutate shared profile/credential state with no coordination. Subagent launch resolves credentials and profile references from whatever the shared state contains at launch time, so a sibling's write (profile rename, key removal, OAuth invalidation) breaks subagent launching in live sessions. Credentials resolved at driver startup stay valid for the driver, which matches what I observed.

## Suggested directions

- Snapshot credentials/profiles per session at startup and resolve subagent launches against the snapshot, or
- Version/lock the shared profile store so a session cannot delete a profile another live session references, and
- A `--diagnose-subagents` style command that prints which config file each failing reference came from; finding `chutesglm52`'s origin required hand-grepping Preferences.

Happy to provide session logs or the runtimeIds from the errors if useful.

sample.title: docs(review): PraisonAI PR #4885 (parity reports: stale is a warning, not a failure) — no user-facing docs required, internal CI tooling only
sample.body:
## Source PR

- Repo: `MervinPraison/PraisonAI`
- PR: [#4885 — fix(parity): stop every branch conflicting on the same generated reports](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAI/pull/4885)
- Branch: `fix/parity-reports-stop-conflicting` → `main`
- Merged: 2026-09-06
- Head SHA: `57298abd835258b272b01a172f0984aa9218c79d`
- Author: @MervinPraison
- Change size: `+100 / -8`, 4 files

## Recommendation

**No user-facing documentation update is required for this PR.** This change is entirely internal CI/tooling plumbing for the parity checker used by PraisonAI maintainers. It does **not** touch any user-visible SDK API, agent feature, configuration option, import path, or workflow.

If another agent picks this up, please do **not** create a page under `docs/features/`, `docs/tools/`, `docs/guides/`, or `docs/concepts/` for this. Per `AGENTS.md`, documentation is user-focused and must not describe features absent from the user-visible surface of `praisonaiagents/` — the parity checker lives in `praisonai/_dev/parity/`, which is a developer-only tree that is mirrored (not published) into this repo.

This PR is the natural follow-on to #4774 (line-number masking) reviewed in issue #3782 — same shape, same rationale, same "no docs" conclusion.

## What actually changed in PR #4885

Two open pull requests could not merge, both on the same two files:

```
src/praisonai-ts/BEHAVIOUR_PARITY.md
src/praisonai-ts/behaviour-parity.json
```

That was structural, not bad luck: every branch that closed a parity option regenerated these files, so every branch conflicted with every other branch on generated content nobody edits by hand. Meanwhile `update-parity-tracker.yml` already regenerates all eight generated reports on every push to `main` and commits them — so main heals itself within a minute of a merge, and asking each PR to also carry the regeneration bought nothing but conflicts.

The fix downgrades a **stale** generated report from a failure to a note in both the behaviour and signature checks:

```
note: src/praisonai-ts/behaviour-parity.json is out of date --
      main regenerates it on push; run --write if you want it in this change
```

A **missing** report is still a failure (no baseline to compare against). Every substantive gap — a rise in unhonoured options, missing / required / default / TS-only-required signature gap — still fails. The ratchet reads the committed baseline, so a stale-but-lower committed total is a **stricter** floor, never a looser one.

### Files touched

| File | Kind | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| `src/praisonai/praisonai/_dev/parity/behaviour.py` | Internal tool code | +6/−1: stale reports become `print('note: ... is out of date -- main regenerates it on push; run --write if you want it in this change')` instead of appending to `failures`. |
| `src/praisonai/praisonai/_dev/parity/signatures/compare.py` | Internal tool code | +20/−5: extracts `classify_report_freshness(evaluation, path, rel, content)`. Missing → `evaluation.failures.append(...)`; stale → `evaluation.warnings.append(...)`. |
| `src/praisonai/tests/unit/_dev/test_behaviour_parity.py` | Tests | +22/−2: `test_closing_one_reports_the_improvement` flipped to exit 0 (staleness is a note now); adds `test_a_stale_report_alone_does_not_fail` and `test_a_stale_report_does_not_hide_a_rise` as controls. |
| `src/praisonai/tests/unit/_dev/test_signature_parity.py` | Tests | +52/0: new `TestReportFreshnessContract` — missing fails, stale warns, fresh silent, line-only shift still fresh, stale does not mask a live failure. |

Test count: 249 → 252 passing.

### Behaviour delta

- `--check` still fails on: a missing report, a rise in unhonoured options, a changed parameter, a changed waiver, a surface moving to a different file, a waiver whose gap is closed, an expired waiver, a run comparing nothing.
- `--check` no longer fails on: a stale committed generated report when nothing substantive has regressed.
- `update-parity-tracker.yml` (unchanged in this PR) continues to regenerate and commit these files on every push to `main`.

## Why no user docs are needed

Verified against the user-doc conventions in `AGENTS.md`:

1. **Not a user-facing feature.** The parity checker is a maintainer tool for keeping the Python and TypeScript SDKs in sync at the behaviour and signature levels. End users of PraisonAI (developers, non-developers, beginners) never invoke it.
2. **Not a new SDK export.** No new class, function, config, parameter, or import path is introduced or renamed in `praisonaiagents/`.
3. **Not agent-centric.** No change to how users write agents, tasks, workflows, tools, memory, knowledge, MCP, or any other user-facing surface.
4. **The user-facing parity page is unaffected.** `docs/features/typescript-parity-notices.mdx` describes *which TypeScript options are accepted but not yet acted on* — a count that this PR does not change. The Note in that page tracks substantive parity milestones (e.g. PR #4841 honouring `Agent` options, PR #4880 hardening the checker's evaluation contract). PR #4885 is neither: it is a CI ergonomics fix that changes when the checker fails, not what a user sees or which options are honoured.
5. **The ratchet's user-facing guarantee is unchanged.** The committed `BEHAVIOUR_PARITY.md` baseline still ratchets downward; a stale-but-lower committed total is strictly stricter. No user-visible parity claim needs revising.
6. **Auto-generated SDK reference is untouched.** `docs/sdk/reference/typescript/` and `docs/sdk/reference/rust/` are generated by the docs parity system; this PR does not change SDK surfaces, so the auto-generator has nothing new to emit.
7. **Not a concept, feature, tool, or guide.** Placement under `docs/concepts/` (human-only), `docs/features/`, `docs/tools/`, or `docs/guides/` would violate folder rules and drop non-user content into user-facing navigation.

## Mirrored files that auto-sync (no action needed)

The `PraisonAIDocs` repo mirrors `praisonai/_dev/` f

sample.body:
### Preset ID

intake-authoring-governance

### Preset Name

Intake Authoring Governance

### Version

0.3.0

### Description

Governs traceable intake CRUD and language-aware requirements collections with atomic migrations, rollback evidence, and safe series authoring.

### Author

Thorsten Hindermann

### Repository URL

https://github.com/hindermath/spec-kit-preset-intake-authoring-governance

https://github.com/hindermath/spec-kit-preset-intake-authoring-governance/archive/refs/tags/v0.3.0.zip

https://github.com/hindermath/spec-kit-preset-intake-authoring-governance/blob/v0.3.0/README.md

### License

MIT

### Required Spec Kit Version

>=0.8.3

### Required Extensions (optional)

None

### Templates Provided

- `intake-governance-config-template` - schema-2 language, naming, role, collection, and legacy-alias contract
- `intake-governance-migration-journal-template` - hash-bound atomic migration, rollback, and repair evidence
- `intake-authoring-policy-template` - repository policy for paths, profiles, language, update, URL, and split boundaries
- `intake-authoring-receipt-template` - schema-2 lifecycle receipt with stable intake identity
- `intake-authoring-series-template` - approved multi-intake coverage, order, DAG, and lineage manifest
- `intake-authoring-operation-template` - transactional proposal, approval, validation, and publication journal
- `intake-authoring-tombstone-template` - logical deletion and byte-identical archive evidence
- `intake-authoring-intake-template` - portable Spec Kit-ready intake core with safe prompt markers
- `intake-authoring-profile-template` - optional repository-specific structure and target-path contract
- `intake-authoring-runbook-template` - create, clarify, read, update, delete, validate, migration, and review-handoff workflow
- `intake-authoring-agent-guidance-addendum-template` - agent-neutral authoring and authority guidance
- `intake-authoring-field-validation-summary` - synthetic, composition, migration, and fleet evidence

### Commands Provided

- `speckit.intake-create` - creates one intake or one explicitly approved intake series
- `speckit.intake-read` - summarizes one intake or series read-only
- `speckit.intake-update` - updates one intake or performs an explicitly authorized atomic requirements migration
- `speckit.intake-delete` - logically deletes active intake artifacts through archive and tombstone evidence
- `speckit.intake-create-status` - checks source, target, receipt, language, role, series, prompt, and authority freshness without writes

### Number of Scripts (optional)

7

### Tags

intake, authoring, governance, requirements, migration

### Key Features

Hi @mnriem, thank you again for reviewing and merging the v0.2.0 catalog update in #3720 and PR #3721.

This compatible v0.3.0 update adds a shared language-aware requirements-collection contract without adding another preset or granting new authority.

- Adds `requirements/intake-governance-config.json` schema 2.0 with an explicit BCP-47 documentation language independent of programming language and operating-system locale.
- Adds German, English, and explicit naming profiles for the canonical requirements index, intake filename pattern, and order view.
- Adds four portable roles and six collection paths for the index, active intake inventory, order, baseline, archive, backlog, history, and series manifest.
- Replaces manually maintained inventory counts with deterministic derivation from the hash-bound active series and repository files.
- Adds a migration journal with before/after hashes, update authority, moved paths, updated references, validation evidence, rollback boundary, and `NeedsRepair` behavior.
- Preserves existing names and content unless explicit rename authority exists; ambiguous language, collisions, stale hashes, mixed naming, or partial failure blocks writes.
- Retains the existing five CRUD/status commands. No new command or implicit Specify, Autonomous, commit, push, PR, merge, provider, or admin authority is introduced.
- Remains optional at priority 64 and composes with Intake Review at 65, Intake Sequencing at 66, Autonomous Run at 70, and Parallel Autonomous at 80.
- Passed German, English, bilingual, explicit-override, schema-1 migration, no-rename, LF/CRLF/BOM, rollback, `NeedsRepair`, collision, stale-reference, and multiple-Eligible fixtures with Bash/PowerShell parity.
- Passed Spec Kit 0.12.11 add, list, info, resolve, disable/enable, remove/reinstall, and command uniqueness with all eleven stacked presets.
- Field validation covered seven migrations/adoptions: TuiVision, TinyCalc, TinyPl0, Home Baseline, InventarWorkerService, cc65, and absdd-image-sandbox. Requirements content and product code were preserved.
- The released versions were also distributed through 26 version-only PRs so all 32 registered Level-1/Level-2 repositories now use the same eleven-preset matrix.
- Six pilot PRs passed their technical checks. The 26 version-only PRs were locally validated and then independently classified at each exact head as GitHub provider-zero-step billing/spending rejection: every rejected job had zero executed steps and all PRs had zero actionable review threads.
- The v0.3.0 ZIP passed installation and integrity smoke tests. SHA-256: `902748540bdb3f6f1b30384107826206f52fb4e5952cba743d22bb9a0cfa526b`.

Maintainer feedback on the schema-2 role model, language/naming boundary, atomic migration journal, metadata, and suitability for the community catalog would be appreciated. The preset remains opt-in and does not claim organizational requirements certification.

### Testing Checklist

- [x] Preset installs successfully via `specify preset add`
- [x] Template resolution works correctly after installation
- [x] Documentation is complete and accurate
- [x] Tested on at least one real project

### Submission Requirements

- [x] Valid `preset.yml` manifest included
- [x] Linked README explains how to use

sample.title: [review-gate] Require independent ChatGPT and Claude approval before governed merges
sample.body:
## Linear anchors

- Primary: `DEN-3570`
- Bot hardening: `DEN-3793`

## Scope

Make dual-agent review a verifiable merge precondition across governed repositories without allowing either bot to approve its own changes or bypass human/repository policy.

## Acceptance gate

- Define normalized review receipts for ChatGPT and Claude with exact repository, pull request, head SHA, policy version, verdict, findings digest, reviewer identity, and timestamp.
- Require two independent approving receipts for the same immutable head; dismiss approvals on head drift.
- Reject self-review, shared credential identities, stale reviews, ambiguous bot accounts, missing inline-thread resolution, or non-terminal checks.
- Preserve repository-specific required reviews and branch protection; this gate may strengthen but never weaken them.
- Add test-org end-to-end fixtures for approve, request-changes, stale-head, identity collision, unavailable reviewer, and retry/idempotency cases.
- Emit bounded audit evidence without prompt bodies, secrets, or hidden reasoning.

## Safety boundary

No auto-merge or admin bypass is authorized by this issue. Any merge remains subject to the target repository’s own `AGENTS.md`, exact-head checks, and human review requirements.

sample.title: Daemon-first 후속: 정식 CLI·선택적 Web UI·Daemon 수명 관리 설계
sample.body:
## 배경과 요청 근거

**#23 「Daemon-first 보장을 위한 개발 규칙·코드 경계·Headless 검증 정비」의 후속 제안이다.**

#23이 UI 없는 업무 조작·공개 계약·Headless 검증을 정비한다면, 이 이슈는 그 기반을 사용자가 일관된 명령으로 실행·확인·종료하는 **정식 CLI 및 운영 계약**으로 연결한다. 사용자는 Paseo의 `paseo daemon start --web-ui`와 같은 명령 도입을 논의한 뒤, 관련 방향을 종합해 기존 daemon-first 이슈의 후속 이슈로 기록하도록 요청했다.

> **권고: `worknaru daemon start`를 독립 실행의 공식 진입점으로 만들고, `--web-ui`로 같은 Daemon에 연결되는 공식 Web UI를 선택적으로 제공한다. 명령 이름뿐 아니라 실행 대상·소유권·준비 완료·정상 종료·실패 처리의 의미를 함께 정한다.**

이번 승인은 **새 이슈 작성과 방향성 기록**이다. 구현 착수, 저장소 변경, 배포·설치, Accepted ADR 변경까지 승인된 것으로 해석하지 않는다. 아래의 명령·기본값·구현 순서는 검토할 제안이며, 현재 지원되는 명령 목록이 아니다. 승인 전 `idea`로 관리한다.

### 검토 기준과 현재 확인한 근거

- 확인일: **2026-09-09**.
- 코드 기준: `main`의 **`b7574204a00b4a5b906139d2ac90174fbecd45dd`**. 이번 기록은 코드·문서 열람에 근거하며 실행 시험을 새로 수행한 결과가 아니다.
- #23에는 `build:daemon` / `test:daemon`, 작은 공통 `rpc` 호출 도구 등의 구현 승인이 기록되어 있다. 아래 snapshot의 `package.json`에는 아직 해당 진입점이 없으므로, 착수 시 최신 결과를 확인해 재사용하고 중복 구현하지 않는다.

| 현재 근거 | 관찰과 후속 과제 |
| --- | --- |
| [`package.json`][w-package] | `npm start`는 `node dist/main.js`를 실행하며 `bin`은 없다. 개발 실행과 정식 CLI 진입점을 구분해야 한다. |
| [`src/main.ts`][w-main] | `startDaemon()`을 호출하는 foreground 실행기다. `--data-dir`, `--workspace`, `--port`, `--origin`, `--acp` 등을 받고 SIGINT/SIGTERM에 종료한다. 별도 CLI에서 호출하는 `status` / `stop` 운영 계약은 없다. |
| [`src/daemon.ts`][w-daemon] | 독립 `startDaemon()`과 WebSocket 업무 계약, 실행 식별자, 종료 경로가 있다. 일반 HTTP 요청에는 현재 404를 반환하며 번들 UI를 제공하지 않는다. |
| [`scripts/dev.mjs`][w-dev] | Daemon·Vite·브라우저와 개발 실행 종료를 조립한다. 재사용할 경험과 코드가 있으나, 이를 그대로 제품 CLI로 이름만 바꾸는 것은 아니다. |
| [`vite.config.ts`][w-vite] | Web 빌드 산출물은 `dist/web`다. 정식 실행은 이 산출물을 제공하는 경로와 개발용 Vite/HMR 경로를 구분해야 한다. |
| [`src/paths.ts`][w-paths] | 개발 데이터는 checkout 내부의 별도 디렉터리로 제한하며 사용자 홈에 자동 생성하지 않는다. `bin` 추가만으로 전역 설치·사용자 데이터 경로까지 해결되지는 않는다. |
| [ADR-0002][w-adr2] | 독립 Daemon과 앱 관리 Daemon의 소유권·종료 정책이 이미 Accepted다. CLI 도입으로 이 정책을 뒤집지 않는다. |

**평가:** 기존 Daemon 구조를 다시 만들 필요는 없지만, 단순한 명령 alias 추가만으로도 충분하지 않다. 인스턴스 발견·안전한 원격 종료가 아닌 로컬 종료 제어·정적 UI 제공·실패 복구를 갖추는 실제 운영 기능 개발이 필요하다.

## 1. 원하는 결과와 아키텍처 원칙

1. **업무 기능은 Daemon 계약이 원본이다.** 구현된 업무 조작은 Web UI 없이 요청·조회·제어할 수 있어야 한다. CLI와 Web UI는 같은 업무 계약을 소비하며 DB·ACP·파일 변경을 별도 경로로 우회하지 않는다. 모든 기능에 전용 human-friendly CLI subcommand를 만드는 것이 필수는 아니며, #23의 공통 RPC 도구를 재사용할 수 있다.
2. **Web UI는 선택적 클라이언트다.** UI 없이도 Daemon의 업무 capability는 유지되어야 한다. UI 제공 여부와 ACP 실행 활성화 여부는 독립적이다. UI를 켠다는 이유로 AI를 자동 활성화하거나 승인 대기를 자동 허용하지 않는다.
3. **정적 UI를 같은 HTTP 서버에서 제공해도 daemon-first에 위배되지 않는다.** 브라우저에서 실행되는 UI와 업무 엔진의 책임 분리가 핵심이며, 별도 UI 서버 프로세스를 의무화하지 않는다. 반대로 Daemon 기동에 React 렌더링·Vite 서버·Web 빌드가 필수가 되어서는 안 된다.
4. **운영 제어와 업무 제어를 구분한다.** 시작·종료·프로세스 관리는 수명을 소유하는 CLI/실행기/OS의 책임으로 둘 수 있다. 모든 운영 기능을 일반 WebSocket 업무 API에 억지로 넣지 않는다.
5. **독립 실행과 상시 백그라운드 실행은 다르다.** 브라우저가 없어도 동작하는 것과 터미널·로그오프·재부팅을 넘어 상주하는 것은 별도 요구다. 지원하지 않는 수명을 보장한다고 표현하지 않는다.

업무별 판정은 Daemon이 관리하는 해당 Module 서비스에 남긴다. CLI 도입을 이유로 모든 업무 규칙을 Platform Core에 집중시키지 않는다.

## 2. 권장 CLI 계약과 첫 범위

### MVP: 세 가지 운영 명령 + 선택적 Web UI

아래 명령은 대상 옵션을 생략한 형태다. 실제 첫 사용 예시는 다음 절과 같이 데이터 영역·Workspace를 명시한다.

| 제안 명령/옵션 | 권장 의미 |
| --- | --- |
| `worknaru daemon start` | **첫 구현의 기본은 foreground.** 독립 Daemon을 시작하고 준비 완료 후 주소와 식별 정보를 출력한다. 터미널에 붙은 실행과 백그라운드 실행을 혼동하지 않는다. |
| `worknaru daemon start --foreground` | 기본 동작을 명시하는 형태. 로그·시그널·종료 코드를 직접 확인할 수 있게 한다. |
| `worknaru daemon start --web-ui` | 업무 Daemon에 더해 **빌드된 Web UI 제공을 활성화**한다. 브라우저 자동 열기나 별도 Vite 서버 실행을 뜻하지 않는다. |
| `--open` / `--no-open` | UI 제공과 브라우저 실행을 분리한다. 첫 기본값은 자동 열기 없음이며 `--open`으로 요청한다. `--no-open`은 명시적 억제다. 양쪽 동시 지정이나 UI가 없는 `--open`은 명확히 거절한다. |
| `worknaru daemon status [--json]` | 지정한 인스턴스의 실제 응답·상태·주소·버전을 확인한다. 조회 때문에 Daemon을 시작하거나 데이터 영역을 생성하지 않는다. |
| `worknaru daemon stop` | 지정한 인스턴스의 정상 종료를 요청하고 완료를 확인한다. 실행·승인 대기가 있으면 기본적으로 거절하고 영향을 설명한다. |
| `daemon stop --cancel-active` | 활성 작업을 중단하고 종료하겠다는 명시적 의사 표시의 제안 이름이다. **승인을 허용하거나 OS 프로세스를 무조건 강제 종료한다는 뜻이 아니다.** 최종 이름은 구현 설계에서 확정한다. |
| `--help`, `--version` | 설치 환경과 명령 계약을 확인한다. 기동·인증·데이터 변경 없이 동작한다. |

### 후속 확장으로 남길 명령

`daemon start --background`, `daemon restart`, `daemon logs`, `web open`은 실제 필요에 따라 추가한다. `web start`는 독립 UI 서버가 필요한 사용 사례가 확인될 때만 검토한다. 동일 서버의 정적 UI 제공으로 충분하다면 만들지 않는다.

백그라운드 기능을 추가하더라도 기존 `daemon start`의 foreground 의미를 조용히 바꾸지 않는다. `--background`와 `--foreground`는 동시에 지정할 수 없게 하고, Windows에서 실행기 종료 후 생존·로그 출력·재조회·정상 종료·고아 프로세스 방지를 검증한 뒤 지원한다고 표시한다. OS Service, 로그온 자동 시작, `install/uninstall/enable`과 자동 업데이트는 MVP가 아니다.

### 대상·옵션·기본값

- 첫 구현은 **데이터 영역 하나당 Daemon 하나**를 기준으로 하며 기존 단일 소유권을 재사용한다. 사용자 전체·컴퓨터 전체 singleton으로 확대하지 않는다.
- `start`, `status`, `stop`은 같은 `--data-dir`을 같은 대상으로 해석해야 한다. 정규화된 경로와 인스턴스 식별자를 사용하고, 작업 디렉터리가 달라졌다고 우연히 다른 Daemon을 제어하지 않게 한다.
- 최초 실행의 `--workspace`는 기존 폴더를 명시한다. 기존 데이터 영역을 다른 Workspace에 연결하는 충돌은 거절하며 자동으로 바꾸지 않는다.
- 첫 범위에서 `--data-dir` / `--workspace`를 생략할 수 있는 조건이 없다면 사용법과 설정 부족을 명확히 안내한다. 간단한 기본 실행을 위해 사용자 홈·전역 설정을 암묵적으로 생성하지 않는다. 향후 제품 기본 경로는 별도 승인된 저장·설치 정책으로 정한다.
- `--port`는 기존 의미를 유지한다. 지정 포트 충돌 시 다른 포트로 조용히 이동하거나 점유 프로세스를 종료하지 않는다. 명시적인 `--port 0`을 지원하면 실제 배정 주소를 출력하고 동일 discovery 계약에 기록한다.
- 현재 `--acp` / `--codex-path` 등의 역할을 유지하고 도움말에 표시한다. `--web-ui`만으로 AI 사용 가능 상태를 약속하지 않는다. `status`에서 UI 제공 여부와 AI 실행 capability를 별도로 보여준다.
- 옵션·환경변수·향후 설정 파일에 같은 값이 존재한다면 우선순위를 문서화하고, 실행에 적용된 비밀이 아닌 값을 확인할 수 있게 한다. 범용 설정 시스템을 이 작업의 선행조건으로 만들지는 않는다.

예시 — **구현 후 제공하려는 사용 형태이며 현재 실행 가능한 명령으로 안내하지 않는다.**

```powershell
# 기존 standalone 인증 요구를 충족한 환경에서 실행한다.
# AI까지 사용하려면 기존 Codex 환경과 --acp 설정이 필요하다.
worknaru daemon start --foreground --data-dir .worknaru-dev --workspace C:\Projects\sample --port 4310 --acp

# 앞 실행을 정상 종료한 뒤, 같은 Daemon에 Web UI 제공과 브라우저 열기를 요청한다.
worknaru daemon start --foreground --data-dir .worknaru-dev --workspace C:\Projects\sample --port 4310 --acp --web-ui --open

# 실행 중인 대상은 별도 터미널에서 조회·종료한다.
worknaru daemon status --data-dir .worknaru-dev --json
worknaru daemon stop --data-dir .worknaru-dev
```

## 3. `--web-ui`의 정확한 의미

[Paseo 공식 Web UI 안내][p-web]의 참고점은 **Daemon 패키지에 포함된 정적 Web UI를 API/WebSocket과 같은 HTTP origin에서 선택적으로 제공한다**는 것이다. 별도 개발 서버를 띄우는 옵션이나 브라우저 열기 옵션으로 설명하지 않

sample.title: web/matches: confirm/reject pending match form + idempotency-keyed resolve (M4.3 FR9, FR10, NFR1, NFR3)
sample.body:
Part of #1924
Depends on: #1926

Milestone M4.3 (Product: #1562), capability **C9**. Delivers **FR9**, **FR10**, **NFR1**, **NFR3**.

## Summary

Add the confirm/reject write path to the pending-matches page built in #1926: a per-match form that calls the **exact same** `store.MatchStore.Resolve` method `resolve_pending_match`'s mutate step calls (`audience_score_system/mcp/tools/matches.go`), including the optional `video_script_id` override, gated by `store.CanWrite`, carrying a server-generated idempotency key.

Depends on #1926 because the form is rendered per pending-match row on the page that task creates; nothing here is landable before that page is on trunk.

No new store method, migration, or schema change (plan Out of scope).

## Scaffold

Minimal — the package, `BUILD.bazel`, and views already exist from #1926. Two pieces of new plumbing:

- `newIdempotencyKey()` in `audience_score_system/web/matches/matches.go` — server-generated (`uuid.NewString()`), minted **once at render time**, never client-generated and never derived from form content. Copy the contract (and doc comment intent) from `web/research/research.go`'s `newIdempotencyKey`.
- `authorizeWrite(w, r) (person *store.Person, ch store.Channel, ok bool)` — the shared parse + authorization preamble for this package's POST handler, structurally identical to `web/research/research.go`'s `authorizeWrite`: signed-in `Person` (401), parse `{id}` (400), Channel load (404 on `pgx.ErrNoRows`), then `store.CanWrite(ctx, h.store.Roles(), channelID, person.ID)` re-derived **fresh from Postgres on this request** (403 when false) — never from session state, a hidden field, or which button was rendered (**NFR3**).

## Implementation

**Route:** `POST /channels/{id}/matches/{matchID}/resolve`, registered in `audience_score_system/web/main.go` next to #1926's GET route, behind `a.auth.RequireSignedIn`.

**Form (in `views.templ`, one per pending-match row):**

- `confirm` — confirm and reject submit buttons resolving to a boolean (`confirm=true` / `confirm=false`), matching `ResolvePendingMatchInput.Confirm`.
- `video_script_id` — optional override select, **confirm only**. Options come from `store.VideoScriptStore.ListByChannel(ctx, channelID)` (already exists; no new store method) — **no status filter**, because `Resolve` deliberately applies none: a human may confirm against **any** script on the Channel including an `archived` one (FR40's archive/match interaction note, FR44). Default selection is the matcher's best guess when the match has one. This is the **primary** resolution path for an undated script, which can never auto-link.
- `idempotency_key` — hidden input, value from `newIdempotencyKey()`, minted at render time of the page (FR10). Two separate GETs of the page mint two different keys.
- Render the whole form only when `canWrite` is true. That omission is **presentation only** — the server-side `authorizeWrite` check is what rejects a forged POST (document this in the view's doc comment, as `web/research`'s views do).

**`HandleResolve`:**

1. `authorizeWrite` preamble (returns immediately when `ok` is false).
2. Parse `{matchID}` (400 on malformed). Load via `store.MatchStore.GetByID` (404 on `pgx.ErrNoRows`).
3. **Channel guard, mirroring `resolvePendingMatchMutate` exactly:** load the match's video with `store.SyncStore.GetByID(ctx, m.SyncedVideoID)` and 404 when `video.ChannelID != channelID`. A match that exists but belongs to a different Channel must 404 exactly like an unknown match (same rule `research.HandleSaveVerdict` applies to a cross-Channel Idea).
4. `r.ParseForm()`; reject `video_script_id` set with `confirm=false` (400, re-render with an error), matching `resolve_pending_match`'s `"video_script_id may only be set when confirm is true"`. When set, validate the script exists and is on the match's Channel — existence + Channel membership **only**, no status filter (see above).
5. **FR10 / NFR1 — idempotency.** `MatchStore.Resolve` carries no key parameter of its own (unlike `VerdictStore.Append` / `VideoScriptStore.Propose`, which M4.1/M4.2's web forms could pass one straight through), so this handler is the **first** `web` write path that must use `store.Idempotency` directly: wrap the `Resolve` call in `h.store.Idempotency().Do(ctx, toolName, person.ID, key, fingerprint, fn)`, mirroring `server.RunIdempotent` (`audience_score_system/mcp/server/idempotency.go`) without importing `mcp/server` (a `web` package must not depend on the MCP server layer — reimplement the small call, do not re-export it).
   - `toolName` is a package-level constant, `"web:resolve_pending_match"`, deliberately namespaced apart from MCP's `"resolve_pending_match"` so the two surfaces cannot collide in `mcp_idempotency`'s `(tool_name, person_id, idempotency_key)` primary key (migration 002). Document the choice in a comment.
   - `fingerprint` is a stable string over the request's meaningful inputs (`matchID`, `confirm`, `video_script_id`), so a *different* request replaying the same key surfaces `store.ErrIdempotencyConflict` rather than a stale replay.
   - Replay with the same key + same fingerprint → no-op returning the original result (redirect as success, no second state change).
   - `store.ErrIdempotencyConflict` → re-render with a conflict error (409-shaped), never a silent state flip.
   - `store.ErrMatchNotPending` (already-resolved match, or a request with no/again-different key) → re-render the page with an explanatory error, **never** a silent second resolution. Assert this is surfaced, not swallowed.
6. Success → `http.StatusSeeOther` redirect back to `/channels/{id}/matches` (post-redirect-get, so a browser refresh re-GETs rather than re-POSTs).
7. Validation-failure re-renders carry the **same** `idempotency_key` the failed POST carried, so a corrected resubmit is still the same logical write — the contract `web/research`'s `noteFormData`/`verdictFormData` already document.

## Testing

Extend `audience_score_system

sample.title: CredentialVault whole-file rewrites silently lose a concurrent write from another process
sample.body:
`CredentialVault::save` re-encrypts the entire vault from the calling instance's in-memory map, so two writers that each read before either wrote leave only the second one's entries on disk.
The first write disappears with no error raised anywhere — and over HTTP, after the route has already answered `200`.

#3640 made a single write atomic (per-process staging file plus `rename`), which stops a torn file, but it does not serialise two writers: both rewrites are individually atomic and the second still erases the first.

## Why the kernel's in-process lock does not cover it

The kernel holds one cached `CredentialVault` behind an `RwLock`, but that is not the only writer:

- `KernelOAuthProvider` opens its own `CredentialVault` instance, outside that lock, for the `mcp-oauth:*` entries.
- `librefang vault set` and `librefang vault rotate-key` run in a separate process entirely.

## The window is wide, not theoretical

Each read-modify-write cycle pays an Argon2id at `m=19456 KiB, t=2` on the reload and again on the save, so a cycle is hundreds of milliseconds long.
Overlapping cycles are the normal case rather than a rare interleaving.

## Three paths rewrite the whole file

- `set`.
- `remove`, which additionally un-deletes an entry another writer added since this instance read.
- `rewrap_with_new_key`, which is the worst of the three: once it completes the old key no longer opens the file, so an entry it dropped cannot be recovered by retrying with the old key.

## Impact

An operator storing a `GITHUB_TOKEN` over HTTP drops every OAuth client secret and token stored since the kernel first unlocked, dropping the affected MCP servers back to `NeedsAuth`.

## Suggested fix

An advisory lock on a `vault.enc.lock` sidecar, taken by every whole-file rewrite, with the file re-read inside it.
A sidecar rather than `vault.enc` itself, because `save` replaces the vault by `rename`: a lock taken on the file object ends up held against an inode no other writer is looking at any more.

sample.title: Add staged Programme review and accountable decisions
sample.body:
## Parent, priority, and dependencies

Native child of [#48](https://github.com/martonpornoi/maru/issues/48).
Owns the delivery checklist item **Add staged review, moderation, and accountable decisions** and the review portion of integrated acceptance: independent reviewers exercise field ceilings, conflict/recusal, moderation, and accountable decision states.

**Next Programme priority**, after merged #57, #59, #61, #63, #66, and #64.
Successors are separate children for the accepted-item adapter and Programme-owned host/co-host relationships, followed by Scheduling. This issue does not own those successors.

This is a bounded planning/execution specification, not a request to start implementation immediately or activate Programme Operations.

## Problem and current workflow

Applications now owns immutable, contributor-acknowledged Programme proposal revisions, preview-first import, and Department ownership continuity. Programme owns a dormant private item/readiness foundation. There is no Programme review or decision workflow joining them: generic Applications review and target seams intentionally reject Programme proposals.

A Programme coordinator needs attributable, privacy-aware assessment of exactly what the lead submitted. Independent reviewers need assigned work, bounded information, conflicts/recusal, and rubric evidence. A moderator and final decision maker need an inspectable rationale and decision history. Proposal contributors need deliberately recipient-visible decisions without access to private reviewer material.

## Bounded outcome

Define and implement the Applications-owned staged review and accountable-decision kernel against one exact submitted proposal revision. Reuse Applications' existing ownership and evidence vocabulary; do not create a second form engine or move private reviews into Programme.

Before implementation, refine PRG-003 and PRG-004 and the relevant module/page contracts for the concrete stage, rubric, independence, anonymization, recusal, decision, revision-request, and recipient-acknowledgement semantics. Record any new architectural decision as an ADR; explicitly extend or supersede affected ADR 0082 fences rather than silently removing them. Do not invent numerical quorum or scoring policy in code without an explicit contract.

## Acceptance boundary

- [ ] Review configuration is bounded and versioned: stage order, rubric fields, assigned reviewers, independence, optional anonymization, permitted discussion, and moderation are explicit. A review binds the exact submitted seal, relevant policy versions, and reviewer assignment, never a moving latest-answer view.
- [ ] Conflicts of interest and recusal are attributable and enforced. Removed, recused, stale, foreign-tenant, wrong-Department, and unassigned reviewers cannot read protected work or append scores. Moderator and final-decision authority do not arise merely from proposal collaboration or account existence.
- [ ] Independent scoring, discussion, and moderation retain immutable evidence and directly inspectable rationale. Reviewer, moderator, decision-maker, and contributor projections have explicit field ceilings; anonymization is a documented projection policy, not a claim that free-text content can never identify its author.
- [ ] Accept, reject, wait-list, and request-revision decisions have explicit allowed transitions, expected versions, retry semantics, accountable actors, and retained predecessors. Reopening, withdrawal, a newer seal, collaborator responses, Department retirement, and concurrent decisions cannot silently change what was reviewed or accepted.
- [ ] Templated decision content has canonical recipient-visible history and purpose-scoped acknowledgement where the contracted policy requires it. Private scores, reviewer discussion, conflict details, or identities are not disclosed implicitly. This child does not claim email delivery or mount a general Communications workspace.
- [ ] The Applications decision retains enough typed, exact-revision evidence for the later accepted-item adapter. An accept decision here creates no Programme item, host, occurrence, Shift, target record, or public rendition. The generic legacy Programme target and adapter fences stay closed; later conversion must prove exactly-once behavior separately.
- [ ] Every command reauthorizes at the appropriate lock boundary and couples state, idempotent receipt, minimized audit, event, and outbox evidence atomically. Sensitive reads are audited before disclosure. Failure and retry do not leave partial success or reveal private values.
- [ ] Current adoption manifests, root roles, routes, navigation, APIs, delivery handlers, and runtime writer privileges remain unchanged unless a separately accepted contract explicitly authorizes a change. The kernel stays dormant; neither current profile gains Programme authority.
- [ ] Focused unit and real PostgreSQL tests cover the policy/role/state matrix, object and field isolation, exact-revision binding, stale writes, replay, withdrawal/reopening/decision races, recusal, Department-retirement continuity, evidence rollback, retained history, and excluded-module side effects. Migration, populated downgrade, runtime-role/readiness, and recovery behavior are tested where schema changes require them. Reuse the established test harness without relaxing coverage or replacing real concurrency/commit tests with rollback-only cases.
- [ ] Requirements, owning module and page contracts, operations/recovery documentation, CURRENT.md, and an append-only checkpoint describe the exact result and its remaining boundaries. Final integrated browser acceptance stays open in #48; kernel tests alone do not satisfy it. Exact-head local certification and protected PR acceptance are required for delivery.

## Explicit non-goals

- Accepted-item conversion, host/co-host authority, readiness expansion, Scheduling, interactive timetable editing, staffing, releases, public outputs, or on-si

sample.title: BUG — Agent OS backlog audit can stop mid-execution after partial inventory instead of completing authorized reconciliation
sample.body:
## Summary
During the explicitly authorized 2026-09-05 Agent OS bug-backlog label reconciliation mission, ChatGPT began governance review and live GitHub inventory, reacquired open issues and #1919, and then stopped progressing before completing the audit, mutations, readback validation, and final report. The repository owner had to explicitly say: `Why do you stop working? Log the bug and finish the task.`

## Observed behavior
1. Repository owner authorized a finite, governed backlog-state and label-reconciliation task.
2. ChatGPT read the required governance and began the live GitHub audit.
3. It established partial facts (180 open issues, initial bug candidates, stale examples, #1919 state).
4. It emitted progress narration but did not continue through the remaining inventory, evidence reconciliation, label mutations, readback verification, or required final report.
5. No genuine authorization/governance blocker had been identified that justified returning control to the user.

## Expected behavior
For a finite already-authorized Agent OS audit/reconciliation mission, intermediate inventory or diagnostic progress must not become a terminal stop. The execution loop should continue until one of these occurs:
- the mission is completed and the required final report is returned; or
- a genuine authorization, capability, currentness, safety, or material-decision blocker prevents further progress.

If one candidate is ambiguous or blocked, preserve that evidence and continue through all other tractable candidates rather than terminating the parent mission.

## Relationship to existing lessons/issues
This is a recurrence of the broader Agent OS learned rule that implementation/review work must not stop merely after diagnosis or partial progress. Deduplicate carefully against #1873 and other continuation issues before implementation; if an existing canonical issue fully owns this exact audit/reconciliation premature-stop seam, mark this issue duplicate rather than creating parallel architecture.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reproduce a multi-phase authorized GitHub audit where partial inventory completes but substantial phases remain.
- [ ] Intermediate progress reporting does not terminate execution.
- [ ] One ambiguous/blocked candidate does not terminate processing of independent candidates.
- [ ] Execution continues through authorized mutations and required readback checks when no genuine blocker exists.
- [ ] The required final report is always produced, including files changed, tests run, docs updated, unresolved blockers, handoff recommendations, and remaining risks.
- [ ] No automatic broadening of authorization is introduced.
- [ ] Regression coverage includes the 2026-09-05 bug-backlog reconciliation shape: governance -> full inventory -> evidence reconciliation -> label mutation -> readback -> validation queries -> final report.

## Authorization boundary
Issue creation records this execution-continuation defect only. It does not authorize repository implementation, workflow/protected-setting changes, credentials/IAM, production/external changes, merge, or issue closure.

## Required report
Include files/systems changed, tests run, docs updated, exact reproduction, root cause, unresolved blockers, handoff recommendations, and remaining risks.

sample.title: [FEATURE] Address HACS default-listing feedback for the embedded integration
sample.body:
### What would you like to see?

Address the feedback on [hacs/default#8968](https://github.com/hacs/default/pull/8968) so the embedded HA-MCP integration can be reconsidered for HACS default listing.

This issue records the proposed direction, what source investigation established, and the questions still needing decisions. It is not a finalized implementation plan or a claim that HACS has approved these proposals.

**Scope and constraints**

- Target the embedded installation. Avoid intentional behavior changes to standalone, Docker, stdio, or Home Assistant app (add-on) installations.
- Prefer the smallest maintainable changes that preserve the existing toolset and connection options.
- Apply safer network/authentication defaults to **new installations**. Do not require existing users to migrate, reconfigure working connections, or adopt the new defaults merely because they update.
- Preserve existing effective settings, including installations that never explicitly saved values and currently inherit defaults. Any internal compatibility handling needed for that should be transparent to users.
- Packaging and credential changes need their own compatibility decisions. Do not assume a mandatory migration, forced credential replacement, or automatic account deletion is approved by this issue.
- If satisfying an item requires unacceptable breakage or a disproportionate redesign, discuss that tradeoff before implementation. Remaining a HACS custom repository is an acceptable outcome.

### Why do you need this?

The default-listing submission was closed because of the combination of network/authentication defaults, anonymous redirects, runtime server installation and updates, automatic administrator/token provisioning, secret logging, and dependencies on HACS internals.

The integration already works as a custom repository. The objective is to address the specific review concerns while retaining its functionality and making it suitable for another default-listing review. The reviewer invited a fresh submission after those concerns are addressed. The follow-up questions on the original PR have not received a maintainer answer as of this investigation.

### Additional context

Source investigation used HA-MCP master at [`ea6c907b`](https://github.com/homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp/tree/ea6c907b443a946150d6b20d6d147fe704095ff6). The numbered items below correspond to the review.

#### 1. Webhook/authentication defaults and direct-port binding

**Established:** The webhook currently defaults to enabled with `none` authentication, and the direct listener defaults to `0.0.0.0`. The existing “Remote access via webhook” checkbox disables webhook registration entirely; it does not merely disable WAN access. That also removes LAN access through the webhook URL.

Binding the direct listener to `127.0.0.1` prevents other LAN devices from connecting directly to port 9584. It does not prevent HA from forwarding an enabled webhook to that listener. The sidebar settings proxy and Assist/LLM bridge also use internal loopback access.

| Configuration | Available connection paths |
| --- | --- |
| Loopback, webhook disabled | Internal sidebar and Assist/LLM bridge |
| Loopback, webhook enabled | HA webhook, including remote access where HA provides it |
| LAN binding, webhook disabled | Direct LAN access through port 9584, plus internal consumers |
| LAN binding, webhook enabled | Direct access and the HA webhook |

**Proposed direction:** Default new installations to webhook disabled and loopback binding. Keep the existing authentication choices available as explicit opt-ins. Consider replacing the checkbox with a single webhook dropdown: Disabled, Secret URL (`none`), Home Assistant authentication, and Legacy OAuth. The existing stored enable/auth settings could remain internally if that reduces change scope.

Put webhook/authentication and direct LAN access controls together at the top of configuration, preferably available during initial setup. Clearly explain which option enables LAN connections and which enables access through HA. Do not make users discover these requirements after setup.

**Questions to resolve:**

- Is an independent LAN-only webhook option needed? HA supports `local_only=True`, but this integration does not currently pass it. This is distinct from both disabling the webhook and binding the direct port to loopback.
- If LAN-only webhook support is added, how should the separately registered OAuth endpoints be restricted? The webhook's local-only flag does not automatically cover those views. Proxy behavior also needs validation.
- The reviewer explicitly offered webhook off or `ha_auth` as acceptable defaults. Default `none` with WAN disabled was proposed in the PR follow-up but has not been accepted.
- Confirm that preserving existing configurations while changing fresh-install defaults meets the review expectation.

#### 2. Restore an administrator-editable redirect allowlist for `none` mode

**Established:** The anonymous auto-approval endpoint accepts spec-valid redirect destinations without requiring the webhook secret or a login. This supports the open-redirect concern in the review. It does not, by itself, demonstrate access to HA or theft of an HA token: the OAuth token issued by this compatibility flow is cosmetic in `none` mode.

**Proposed direction:** Restore exact callback matching specifically in the embedded `none`-mode auto-approval flow. Ship a small verified default list and let administrators add/remove callback URLs in Configure. Preserve existing URI validation and provide a useful rejection message explaining how to add a legitimate callback.

The earlier implementation in [#1976](https://github.com/homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp/pull/1976) provides a starting point. Restore the narrow check within the current OAuth code rather than reverting subsequent fixes. Keep this scoped so unrelated install methods and authenticated OAuth flows do not acquire new restrictions accidentall

sample.title: JSON body property constraints (format, pattern, length, bounds, enum, const, type) are not constructible as negative request cases
sample.body:
## Summary

Negative request cases cannot violate a constraint declared on a JSON body property. `Internal/Negative/BodyTargets` offers four categories — `additionalProperty`, `mediaTypeMismatch`, `partContentTypeMismatch` and `jsonBody` (malformed syntax) — and none of them touches a property's own schema. `format`, `pattern`, `minLength`/`maxLength`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `enum`, `const` and `type` on a body property are therefore never exercised by a generated case, while the same keywords on a parameter are (see #93 for the parameter side).

Split out of #93, where it was listed as "related, lower priority".

## Where

`src/Internal/Negative/BodyTargets.php` — public surface:

```
 25: additionalProperty()
 44: mediaTypeMismatch()
 82: partContentTypeMismatch()
165: jsonBody()
```

`ContractSuite::negativeCases()` wires exactly those four body categories plus the seven parameter categories from `ParameterTargets`.

## Impact

On the same 28-operation document as in #93, the two properties carrying the strictest constraints — `email` (`format: email`) and `token` (`pattern: ^[0-9a-f]{64}$`) — are both JSON body properties, so no generated case ever sends an invalid value for either. The `422` behaviour for both had to be covered by hand-written tests.

## The response side already does this

`Internal/Negative/ResponseTargets::bodyWitness(Operation, int $status, string $kind)` walks the top-level properties of the JSON response body (or the scalar root as `$`) and builds a witness for `type`, `enum`, `const`, `boundary`, `length` and `pattern` through the shared `SchemaProbe` / `PatternWitness`. `NegativeResponseCaseArbitrary` then overwrites that one property in an otherwise valid body and records `misuse = {kind, location: 'body', name: <property>}`.

The request side needs the mirror image:

- a `BodyTargets::bodyWitness(Operation, string $kind)` (or equivalent) over the required JSON request body's top-level properties, reusing `SchemaProbe` and `PatternWitness` — the witness rules (nullable / `not` / union types / `format` support) are the same as for responses, plus `format`, which the response side does not offer yet;
- one `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary` mutation per kind that overwrites the targeted property in the generated valid body and records `misuse = {kind, location: 'body', name: <property>}` — the `misuse.kind` union already contains every needed value;
- registration in `ContractSuite::negativeCases()`, which is enough for `OperationProperty` and `OperationCoverage` to pick the categories up.

## Scope notes

- Required JSON body, top-level properties only — the same scope as the response side. Nested properties, `items`, and combinators are a later step.
- `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and `multipart/form-data` bodies are out of scope here; they have their own wire encoding and deserve a separate look once the JSON case exists.
- `checkNegative()`'s pre-transport precondition (`validateRequest()` must be invalid) already covers body property schemas in `openapi-contract`, so no contract change is needed.
- Every kind must be recorded in the zoo (`tests/Support/ZooContracts.php`) and the recorded corpus in `openapi-contract` rewritten, per the corpus rule in `AGENTS.md`.
- Documentation to update: `llms.txt`, `README.md`, `README.ru.md`, the `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary` docblocks, `CHANGELOG.md` (`## Unreleased`, minor).

## Environment

- `rasuvaeff/property-testing-openapi` v0.11.0
- `rasuvaeff/openapi-contract` v0.10.0

sample.title: Pin mini.nvim test dependencies and fail clearly on bootstrap errors
sample.body:
Both test bootstraps shallow-clone mini.nvim's current default branch when the dependency directory is absent. Fresh machines can therefore run different test-framework revisions for the same plugin commit. Clone failure is not checked before requiring mini.test.

**Priority:** P2 — Address after the immediate data-preservation fixes.

**Scope**

Record one shared mini.nvim revision for unit and E2E tests and provide a deterministic bootstrap/update path. Verify an existing checkout matches the required revision instead of silently accepting arbitrary cached state. Detect clone/checkout failure and report an actionable error before collecting tests. Coordinate simultaneous fresh bootstraps without deleting unrelated user data.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Fresh unit and E2E runs resolve the same recorded mini.nvim commit.
- [ ] An existing stale/mismatched checkout is handled deterministically with a clear diagnostic or controlled refresh.
- [ ] Clone/checkout failure exits nonzero with the failed operation identified.
- [ ] Concurrent bootstrap attempts cannot leave a partially initialized dependency accepted as valid.
- [ ] Offline reruns work with a valid matching dependency cache.
- [ ] Document how to update the pinned revision and exercise successful, failed, and cached bootstrap paths.

**Code and verification context**

[Unit bootstrap](https://github.com/wadackel/eda.nvim/blob/c0083dc2250747d52a1063598309e8fd58654b10/tests/minit.lua#L3); [E2E bootstrap](https://github.com/wadackel/eda.nvim/blob/c0083dc2250747d52a1063598309e8fd58654b10/tests/e2e_minit.lua#L3); [Dependency setup guidance](https://github.com/wadackel/eda.nvim/blob/c0083dc2250747d52a1063598309e8fd58654b10/AGENTS.md#L44).

**Related work**

- Coordinate cache/bootstrap behavior with https://github.com/wadackel/eda.nvim/issues/77.

sample.title: AGENTS.md: sync the searxng and blocky customDNS guidance with the live config
sample.body:
Doc drift introduced by #3631 and not corrected there. Found by review-context on PR #3644.

## Problem

AGENTS.md still describes the `search` blocky `customDNS` pin as live and load-bearing. #3631 removed that pin. Two places are wrong:

1. **The "Count of unlabelled routes: zero" table**, `home/searxng` row. It says two internal paths replace the public record — the headscale pin and the blocky `customDNS` pin — and that "Both are load-bearing — removing either breaks a client class." Only the headscale pin remains. The blocky pin is gone, and the LAN client class it served is gone with it, deliberately.

2. **The blocky `customDNS` section** should state the live pin set: `unifi`, `traefik`, `longhorn`, `auth`. It should not present the searxng pin as an example to copy — that framing is what propagated the mistake #3631 corrected.

This now also contradicts the route comments corrected in #3644, so the repository disagrees with itself.

## Related correction, same area

The tier model changed after those sections were written. A blocky pin is a **tier-2** mechanism: it gives a LAN path to a break-glass service. A tier-3 service has no pin and no LAN path by design. Worth one sentence linking the pin rule to the tier model in #3635, so the two are not read as separate rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [functional] The `home/searxng` row no longer describes a blocky `customDNS` pin as one of its resolution paths.
- [ ] [functional] That row states the headscale split entry plus `extra_records` pin as the only internal path, and that the LAN path was removed deliberately in #3631.
- [ ] [functional] The blocky `customDNS` section names the live pin set as `unifi`, `traefik`, `longhorn`, `auth`.
- [ ] [functional] No section presents the searxng blocky pin as a pattern to copy.
- [ ] [functional] One sentence links the break-glass pin rule to the tier model in #3635.
- [ ] [edge-case] The existing guidance that removing a pin removes a client class is retained where it is still true — for a tier-2 service.
- [ ] [functional] No file other than AGENTS.md is modified.

sample.body:
# [Ola 8.07] feat-srs-requirements-ola8 — Append REQ-048..052 to docs/SRS/REQUIREMENTS.md

> Ola 8 — SRS documentation: 5 new requirements for curation + introspection + privacy + compute.
> Labels: `ola8`, `wave-8`

---

## Current State (MEDIBLE)

- File: `docs/SRS/REQUIREMENTS.md` EXISTS
- Last REQ added: REQ-047 (RTK Kernel CLI Proxy, 2026-09-05)
- Run `grep -c "^## REQ-" docs/SRS/REQUIREMENTS.md` to get current count
- Run `tail -20 docs/SRS/REQUIREMENTS.md` to see footer note pattern
- File size: run `wc -l docs/SRS/REQUIREMENTS.md`

## Desired State (DELTA)

Append 5 new requirements sections BEFORE the final `---` footer (maintain exact file format). Add in this order:

### REQ-048: HumanChallenge → Curation → Training Pipeline
```
## REQ-048: HumanChallenge → Curation → Training Pipeline

**Status:** Planned | **Wave:** 8 | **Module:** humanchallenge, data_commons
**SRS Reference:** IEEE 830 §3.2

### Description
Verified HumanChallenge events must flow through a human curation gate before feeding
the TrainingExporter. A CurationVote (Accept/Reject/Refine) with explicit training consent
gates which challenge responses become training data. Minimum thresholds: 10 eligible votes,
70% fact-verified, 60% training-eligible before export is allowed.

### Requirements
- REQ-048.1: System SHALL require explicit `training_eligible: true` on CurationVote for inclusion
- REQ-048.2: System SHALL block export unless CurationGate::check_readiness() returns is_ready=true
- REQ-048.3: CurationVote SHALL store domain_tags for mini-expert segment routing
- REQ-048.4: All curation votes SHALL be stored locally (Privacy P4) unless user upgrades consent
```

### REQ-049: Human Introspection Mode (LLM as Guide)
```
## REQ-049: Human Introspection Mode (LLM as Guide)

**Status:** Planned | **Wave:** 8 | **Module:** humanchallenge/introspection
**SRS Reference:** IEEE 830 §3.3

### Description
Xavier SHALL provide a structured human introspection mode where the LLM acts as a
professional guide (not answer-giver) using 6 evidence-based techniques. The human
produces insights; the LLM facilitates depth through targeted questions.

### Requirements
- REQ-049.1: System SHALL support 6 IntrospectionTechniques: Socratic, FiveWhys, PreMortem, SteelManning, FirstPrinciples, PatternRecognition
- REQ-049.2: IntrospectionSession SHALL auto-select technique based on ChallengeType
- REQ-049.3: FiveWhys technique SHALL auto-complete after 5 human turns
- REQ-049.4: Completed sessions SHALL extract human insights for optional training inclusion
- REQ-049.5: LLM guide prompts SHALL be generated locally — no external LLM API required for the guide scaffolding
```

### REQ-050: Privacy Pipeline P2/P3/P4
```
## REQ-050: Privacy Pipeline P2/P3/P4

**Status:** Planned | **Wave:** 8 | **Module:** data_commons/privacy
**SRS Reference:** IEEE 830 §3.4 (Privacy Requirements)

### Description
All training data exports SHALL pass through a PrivacyPipeline with three levels:
P4 (local only, no processing), P2 (PII scrubbing for on-prem sharing), P3 (DP + scrubbing for external/Colab).

### Requirements
- REQ-050.1: P4 data SHALL never leave the local node without explicit user upgrade
- REQ-050.2: P2 exports SHALL scrub: emails, file paths, API keys, passwords
- REQ-050.3: P3 exports SHALL add Laplace differential privacy noise (epsilon=1.0) on confidence scores
- REQ-050.4: k-anonymity check (k>=3) SHALL be enforced on P3 exports — export rejected if k<3
- REQ-050.5: Privacy audit report SHALL be included in every TrainingBundle manifest
```

### REQ-051: Enterprise ComputeProvider with ZDR
```
## REQ-051: Enterprise ComputeProvider with ZDR (Zero Data Retention)

**Status:** Planned | **Wave:** 8 | **Module:** enterprise/compute
**SRS Reference:** IEEE 830 §3.5 (Enterprise Requirements)

### Description
Enterprise users SHALL have access to ComputeProvider abstraction (Local, ColabPro, RunPod,
VastAI, LambdaLabs) with cryptographically verifiable Zero Data Retention audit trail.

### Requirements
- REQ-051.1: ZdrAuditEntry SHALL include pre/post volume hashes signed by the provider
- REQ-051.2: Xavier SHALL verify ZdrAuditEntry::verify() before marking a TrainingJob as ZDR-compliant
- REQ-051.3: ColabPro provider SHALL require explicit Google OAuth token (not stored in plaintext)
- REQ-051.4: Enterprise plan SHALL have access to RunPod and LambdaLabs providers
- REQ-051.5: Free/Pro plans SHALL only access Local compute provider
```

### REQ-052: Informed Consent for P3 Export
```
## REQ-052: Informed Consent for P3 (Colab) Training Export

**Status:** Planned | **Wave:** 8 | **Module:** panel-ui, humanchallenge
**SRS Reference:** IEEE 830 §3.6 (User Consent Requirements)

### Description
Before any P3-level export (Google Colab, external compute), the system SHALL present
a consent dialog explaining the privacy implications and requiring explicit user confirmation.

### Requirements
- REQ-052.1: P3 export SHALL be blocked until user explicitly confirms consent
- REQ-052.2: Consent dialog SHALL clearly state: "Google will process your anonymized dataset"
- REQ-052.3: Consent SHALL be recorded in the audit log with timestamp and user identity hash
- REQ-052.4: Consent can be revoked at any time — revocation blocks future P3 exports until re-confirmed
```

Also append to the footer note:
```
*WAVE-8 2026-09-12: REQ-048..052 added (HumanChallenge curation pipeline, introspection mode, privacy pipeline, enterprise ZDR, informed consent). Module: humanchallenge + data_commons + enterprise + panel-ui.*
```

1. search: "IEEE 830 SRS requirements specification format 2024"
2. search: "differential privacy epsilon parameter training data 2024"
3. search: "k-anonymity minimum threshold best practices 2024"

1. Run `tail -30 docs/SRS/REQUIREMENTS.md` — understand the footer note format and final `---` position
2. Run `grep -c '^## REQ-' docs/SRS/REQUIREMENTS.md` —
